sub_sqls: SELECT p.STATUS AS port_status, p.DEVICE_OWNER AS device_owner, COUNT(p.ID) AS port_count, MIN(sa.UPDATED_AT) AS earliest_standard_attr_update FROM PORTS p JOIN STANDARDATTRIBUTES sa ON sa.ID = p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID WHERE sa.RESOURCE_TYPE = 'ports' GROUP BY p.STATUS, p.DEVICE_OWNER;

SELECT e.NETWORK_ID, e.IS_DEFAULT, n.TENANT_ID, n.NAME, n.STATUS, n.ADMIN_STATE_UP, n.MTU, n.STANDARD_ATTR_ID, MIN(n.MTU) OVER (PARTITION BY n.TENANT_ID ORDER BY n.TENANT_ID) AS window_column FROM EXTERNALNETWORKS e JOIN NETWORKS n ON e.NETWORK_ID = n.ID WHERE e.IS_DEFAULT = 0;

WITH inner_cte AS (SELECT p.STATUS AS port_status, p.DEVICE_OWNER AS device_owner, COUNT(p.ID) AS port_count, MIN(sa.UPDATED_AT) AS earliest_standard_attr_update FROM PORTS p JOIN STANDARDATTRIBUTES sa ON sa.ID = p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID WHERE sa.RESOURCE_TYPE = 'ports' GROUP BY p.STATUS, p.DEVICE_OWNER), avg_cte AS (SELECT AVG(port_count) AS avg_port_count FROM inner_cte) SELECT i.port_status, i.device_owner, i.port_count, i.earliest_standard_attr_update, (i.port_count - a.avg_port_count) AS deviation_from_avg_port_count FROM inner_cte i CROSS JOIN avg_cte a;

WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT e.NETWORK_ID, e.IS_DEFAULT, n.TENANT_ID, n.NAME, n.STATUS, n.ADMIN_STATE_UP, n.MTU, n.STANDARD_ATTR_ID, MIN(n.MTU) OVER (PARTITION BY n.TENANT_ID ORDER BY n.TENANT_ID) AS window_column FROM EXTERNALNETWORKS e JOIN NETWORKS n ON e.NETWORK_ID = n.ID WHERE e.IS_DEFAULT = 0 ) SELECT inner_cte.NETWORK_ID, inner_cte.IS_DEFAULT, inner_cte.TENANT_ID, inner_cte.NAME, inner_cte.STATUS, inner_cte.ADMIN_STATE_UP, inner_cte.MTU, inner_cte.STANDARD_ATTR_ID, inner_cte.window_column, tenant_counts.total_default_external_networks, avg_counts.avg_default_external_networks_per_tenant FROM inner_cte JOIN ( SELECT TENANT_ID, COUNT(NETWORK_ID) AS total_default_external_networks FROM inner_cte GROUP BY TENANT_ID ) AS tenant_counts ON inner_cte.TENANT_ID = tenant_counts.TENANT_ID JOIN ( SELECT AVG(cnt) AS avg_default_external_networks_per_tenant FROM ( SELECT COUNT(NETWORK_ID) AS cnt FROM inner_cte GROUP BY TENANT_ID ) AS sub ) AS avg_counts ON 1 = 1;

question: For each port status that (among ports bound with VIF type 'ovs') has a minimum admin_state_up and an average standard_attr_id greater than the overall average standard_attr_id across all 'ovs'-bound ports, what are the status, that minimum admin_state_up, that average standard_attr_id, and (for the same status among ports that have both a security group port binding and a port security binding) the coefficient of variation (using STDDEV only and never STDDEV_POP) of standard_attr_id and the total number of distinct security groups involved? Do not return any rounded answers.
sql: WITH q1 AS ( WITH inner_cte AS (SELECT MIN(p.ADMIN_STATE_UP) AS min_admin_state_up, AVG(p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID) AS avg_standard_attr_id FROM PORTS p JOIN ML2_PORT_BINDINGS b ON p.ID = b.PORT_ID WHERE b.VIF_TYPE = 'ovs' GROUP BY p.STATUS) SELECT p.STATUS AS port_status, inner_cte.min_admin_state_up, inner_cte.avg_standard_attr_id FROM inner_cte JOIN PORTS p ON p.STATUS = p.STATUS JOIN ML2_PORT_BINDINGS b ON p.ID = b.PORT_ID WHERE b.VIF_TYPE = 'ovs' GROUP BY p.STATUS, inner_cte.min_admin_state_up, inner_cte.avg_standard_attr_id HAVING inner_cte.avg_standard_attr_id > ( SELECT AVG(p2.STANDARD_ATTR_ID) FROM PORTS p2 JOIN ML2_PORT_BINDINGS b2 ON p2.ID = b2.PORT_ID WHERE b2.VIF_TYPE = 'ovs' ) ), q2 AS ( WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT p.status, STDDEV(p.standard_attr_id) / NULLIF(AVG(p.standard_attr_id), 0) AS coefficient_of_variation FROM securitygroupportbindings AS sgpb JOIN ports AS p ON sgpb.port_id = p.id JOIN portsecuritybindings AS psb ON p.id = psb.port_id GROUP BY p.status HAVING AVG(p.standard_attr_id) > 0 ORDER BY coefficient_of_variation DESC ) SELECT CASE WHEN LAG(status) OVER (ORDER BY status_sort, status) = status THEN NULL ELSE status END AS status, coefficient_of_variation, distinct_security_groups FROM ( SELECT CASE WHEN GROUPING(i.status) = 1 THEN 'zzz' ELSE i.status END AS status_sort, CASE WHEN GROUPING(i.status) = 1 THEN 'TOTAL' ELSE i.status END AS status, AVG(i.coefficient_of_variation) AS coefficient_of_variation, COUNT(DISTINCT sgpb.security_group_id) AS distinct_security_groups FROM inner_cte i JOIN ports p ON p.status = i.status JOIN securitygroupportbindings sgpb ON sgpb.port_id = p.id JOIN portsecuritybindings psb ON psb.port_id = p.id GROUP BY i.status WITH ROLLUP ) AS tbltmp ORDER BY status_sort, status ) SELECT q1.port_status, q1.min_admin_state_up, q1.avg_standard_attr_id, q2.coefficient_of_variation, q2.distinct_security_groups FROM q1 JOIN q2 ON q2.status = q1.port_status;
sub_questions: For each port status, what are the minimum admin_state_up value and the average standard_attr_id for ports that are bound with VIF type 'ovs'?

For each port status, show the status and the coefficient of variation of the ports’ standard attribute IDs, considering only ports that have a security group port binding and a port security binding.

For each port status, which statuses have a minimum admin_state_up value and an average standard_attr_id (considering only ports bound with VIF type 'ovs') such that their average standard_attr_id is greater than the overall average standard_attr_id across all 'ovs'-bound ports?

For each port status, list the status, the coefficient of variation of the ports’ standard attribute IDs, and the total number of distinct security groups involved. Do not repeat the status if it is the same as the previous row. Include a final TOTAL row across all statuses, considering only ports that have both a security group port binding and a port security binding.
sub_sqls: SELECT MIN(p.ADMIN_STATE_UP) AS min_admin_state_up, AVG(p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID) AS avg_standard_attr_id FROM PORTS p JOIN ML2_PORT_BINDINGS b ON p.ID = b.PORT_ID WHERE b.VIF_TYPE = 'ovs' GROUP BY p.STATUS;

SELECT p.status, STDDEV(p.standard_attr_id) / NULLIF(AVG(p.standard_attr_id), 0) AS coefficient_of_variation FROM securitygroupportbindings AS sgpb JOIN ports AS p ON sgpb.port_id = p.id JOIN portsecuritybindings AS psb ON p.id = psb.port_id GROUP BY p.status HAVING AVG(p.standard_attr_id) > 0 ORDER BY coefficient_of_variation DESC;

WITH inner_cte AS (SELECT MIN(p.ADMIN_STATE_UP) AS min_admin_state_up, AVG(p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID) AS avg_standard_attr_id FROM PORTS p JOIN ML2_PORT_BINDINGS b ON p.ID = b.PORT_ID WHERE b.VIF_TYPE = 'ovs' GROUP BY p.STATUS) SELECT p.STATUS AS port_status, inner_cte.min_admin_state_up, inner_cte.avg_standard_attr_id FROM inner_cte JOIN PORTS p ON p.STATUS = p.STATUS JOIN ML2_PORT_BINDINGS b ON p.ID = b.PORT_ID WHERE b.VIF_TYPE = 'ovs' GROUP BY p.STATUS, inner_cte.min_admin_state_up, inner_cte.avg_standard_attr_id HAVING inner_cte.avg_standard_attr_id > ( SELECT AVG(p2.STANDARD_ATTR_ID) FROM PORTS p2 JOIN ML2_PORT_BINDINGS b2 ON p2.ID = b2.PORT_ID WHERE b2.VIF_TYPE = 'ovs' );

WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT p.status, STDDEV(p.standard_attr_id) / NULLIF(AVG(p.standard_attr_id), 0) AS coefficient_of_variation FROM securitygroupportbindings AS sgpb JOIN ports AS p ON sgpb.port_id = p.id JOIN portsecuritybindings AS psb ON p.id = psb.port_id GROUP BY p.status HAVING AVG(p.standard_attr_id) > 0 ORDER BY coefficient_of_variation DESC ) SELECT CASE WHEN LAG(status) OVER (ORDER BY status_sort, status) = status THEN NULL ELSE status END AS status, coefficient_of_variation, distinct_security_groups FROM ( SELECT CASE WHEN GROUPING(i.status) = 1 THEN 'zzz' ELSE i.status END AS status_sort, CASE WHEN GROUPING(i.status) = 1 THEN 'TOTAL' ELSE i.status END AS status, AVG(i.coefficient_of_variation) AS coefficient_of_variation, COUNT(DISTINCT sgpb.security_group_id) AS distinct_security_groups FROM inner_cte i JOIN ports p ON p.status = i.status JOIN securitygroupportbindings sgpb ON sgpb.port_id = p.id JOIN portsecuritybindings psb ON psb.port_id = p.id GROUP BY i.status WITH ROLLUP ) AS tbltmp ORDER BY status_sort, status;

question: For ACTIVE networks that are shared via an RBAC action of 'access_as_shared', list the network name, status, admin_state_up, RBAC action, and RBAC target tenant (including the dense-rank value from the ACTIVE-network RBAC/MTU view), along with the network MTU and its deviation from the average MTU across all ACTIVE networks; also include each related shared subnet’s name and CIDR, the running sum of subnet standard attribute IDs within each IP-version group ordered by standard attribute ID, plus the total number of such shared subnets per RBAC target tenant and the average of those totals across all target tenants. Do not return any rounded answers.
sql: WITH shared_subnets AS ( WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT s.NAME AS subnet_name, s.CIDR AS subnet_cidr, n.TARGET_TENANT AS rbac_target_tenant, SUM(s.STANDARD_ATTR_ID) OVER (PARTITION BY s.IP_VERSION ORDER BY s.STANDARD_ATTR_ID) AS window_column FROM SUBNETS AS s JOIN NETWORKRBACS AS n ON n.OBJECT_ID = s.NETWORK_ID WHERE n.ACTION = 'access_as_shared' ) SELECT i.subnet_name, i.subnet_cidr, i.rbac_target_tenant, i.window_column, tgt_counts.total_shared_subnets, avg_counts.avg_shared_subnets_per_target FROM inner_cte AS i JOIN ( SELECT rbac_target_tenant, COUNT(*) AS total_shared_subnets FROM inner_cte GROUP BY rbac_target_tenant ) AS tgt_counts ON tgt_counts.rbac_target_tenant = i.rbac_target_tenant JOIN ( SELECT AVG(total_shared_subnets) AS avg_shared_subnets_per_target FROM ( SELECT rbac_target_tenant, COUNT(*) AS total_shared_subnets FROM inner_cte GROUP BY rbac_target_tenant ) AS per_target ) AS avg_counts ), active_network_rbac_mtu AS ( WITH inner_cte AS (SELECT n.name, n.status, n.admin_state_up, r.action, r.target_tenant, DENSE_RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY n.id ORDER BY n.id) AS window_column FROM networksecuritybindings b JOIN networks n ON b.network_id = n.id JOIN networkrbacs r ON n.id = r.object_id WHERE n.status = 'ACTIVE'), ActiveNetworkMTU AS ( SELECT n.id AS network_id, n.mtu FROM networks n WHERE n.status = 'ACTIVE' ), AverageActiveMTU AS ( SELECT AVG(mtu) AS avg_mtu FROM ActiveNetworkMTU ) SELECT i.name, i.status, i.admin_state_up, i.action, i.target_tenant, i.window_column, anm.mtu, (anm.mtu - aam.avg_mtu) AS deviation_from_avg_mtu FROM inner_cte i JOIN networks n ON n.name = i.name AND n.status = i.status AND n.admin_state_up = i.admin_state_up JOIN ActiveNetworkMTU anm ON anm.network_id = n.id CROSS JOIN AverageActiveMTU aam ), active_shared_networks AS ( SELECT n.id AS network_id, n.name AS network_name, n.status AS network_status, n.admin_state_up, r.action AS rbac_action, r.target_tenant AS rbac_target_tenant FROM networks n JOIN networkrbacs r ON r.object_id = n.id WHERE n.status = 'ACTIVE' AND r.action = 'access_as_shared' ) SELECT asn.network_name, asn.network_status, asn.admin_state_up, asn.rbac_action, asn.rbac_target_tenant, anrm.window_column AS network_dense_rank_within_id, anrm.mtu, anrm.deviation_from_avg_mtu, ss.subnet_name, ss.subnet_cidr, ss.window_column AS running_sum_subnet_standard_attr_id_within_ip_version, ss.total_shared_subnets, ss.avg_shared_subnets_per_target FROM active_shared_networks asn JOIN active_network_rbac_mtu anrm ON anrm.name = asn.network_name AND anrm.status = asn.network_status AND anrm.admin_state_up = asn.admin_state_up AND anrm.action = asn.rbac_action AND anrm.target_tenant = asn.rbac_target_tenant JOIN networkrbacs r2 ON r2.object_id = asn.network_id AND r2.action = 'access_as_shared' AND r2.target_tenant = asn.rbac_target_tenant JOIN subnets s ON s.network_id = asn.network_id JOIN shared_subnets ss ON ss.subnet_name = s.name AND ss.subnet_cidr = s.cidr AND ss.rbac_target_tenant = asn.rbac_target_tenant ORDER BY asn.rbac_target_tenant, asn.network_name, ss.subnet_name;
sub_questions: For subnets whose network has a RBAC action of 'access_as_shared', list the subnet name, its CIDR, the RBAC target tenant, and the running sum of subnet standard attribute IDs within each IP version group ordered by standard attribute ID.

Show each network’s name, status, and admin_state_up together with the RBAC action and target tenant for that network, plus a dense rank within each network (partitioned by network ID and ordered by network ID). Only include networks that are ACTIVE.

For subnets whose network has a RBAC action of 'access_as_shared', list the subnet name, its CIDR, the RBAC target tenant, the running sum of subnet standard attribute IDs within each IP version group ordered by standard attribute ID, along with the total number of such shared subnets per RBAC target tenant and the average of those totals across all target tenants.

For each ACTIVE network, show the network name, status, admin_state_up, RBAC action, and RBAC target tenant (including a dense rank within each network by network ID), and also include the deviation of that network’s MTU from the average MTU across all ACTIVE networks.
sub_sqls: SELECT s.NAME AS subnet_name, s.CIDR AS subnet_cidr, n.TARGET_TENANT AS rbac_target_tenant, SUM(s.STANDARD_ATTR_ID) OVER ( PARTITION BY s.IP_VERSION ORDER BY s.STANDARD_ATTR_ID ) AS window_column FROM SUBNETS AS s JOIN NETWORKRBACS AS n ON n.OBJECT_ID = s.NETWORK_ID WHERE n.ACTION = 'access_as_shared';

SELECT n.name, n.status, n.admin_state_up, r.action, r.target_tenant, DENSE_RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY n.id ORDER BY n.id) AS window_column FROM networksecuritybindings b JOIN networks n ON b.network_id = n.id JOIN networkrbacs r ON n.id = r.object_id WHERE n.status = 'ACTIVE'

WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT s.NAME AS subnet_name, s.CIDR AS subnet_cidr, n.TARGET_TENANT AS rbac_target_tenant, SUM(s.STANDARD_ATTR_ID) OVER (PARTITION BY s.IP_VERSION ORDER BY s.STANDARD_ATTR_ID) AS window_column FROM SUBNETS AS s JOIN NETWORKRBACS AS n ON n.OBJECT_ID = s.NETWORK_ID WHERE n.ACTION = 'access_as_shared' ) SELECT i.subnet_name, i.subnet_cidr, i.rbac_target_tenant, i.window_column, tgt_counts.total_shared_subnets, avg_counts.avg_shared_subnets_per_target FROM inner_cte AS i JOIN ( SELECT rbac_target_tenant, COUNT(*) AS total_shared_subnets FROM inner_cte GROUP BY rbac_target_tenant ) AS tgt_counts ON tgt_counts.rbac_target_tenant = i.rbac_target_tenant JOIN ( SELECT AVG(total_shared_subnets) AS avg_shared_subnets_per_target FROM ( SELECT rbac_target_tenant, COUNT(*) AS total_shared_subnets FROM inner_cte GROUP BY rbac_target_tenant ) AS per_target ) AS avg_counts;

WITH inner_cte AS (SELECT n.name, n.status, n.admin_state_up, r.action, r.target_tenant, DENSE_RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY n.id ORDER BY n.id) AS window_column FROM networksecuritybindings b JOIN networks n ON b.network_id = n.id JOIN networkrbacs r ON n.id = r.object_id WHERE n.status = 'ACTIVE'), ActiveNetworkMTU AS ( SELECT n.id AS network_id, n.mtu FROM networks n WHERE n.status = 'ACTIVE' ), AverageActiveMTU AS ( SELECT AVG(mtu) AS avg_mtu FROM ActiveNetworkMTU ) SELECT i.name, i.status, i.admin_state_up, i.action, i.target_tenant, i.window_column, anm.mtu, (anm.mtu - aam.avg_mtu) AS deviation_from_avg_mtu FROM inner_cte i JOIN networks n ON n.name = i.name AND n.status = i.status AND n.admin_state_up = i.admin_state_up JOIN ActiveNetworkMTU anm ON anm.network_id = n.id CROSS JOIN AverageActiveMTU aam;

question: For DOWN ports that belong to security groups whose count of DOWN ports is above the average across security groups, list each port’s ID, tenant ID, MAC address, security group ID, and its rank within that security group (ordered by port ID), along with the security group’s DOWN-port count; also include, for the same tenant, the tenant’s port-security rollup metrics for admin status = 'Up' (total ports, total port security bindings, and total times port security is enabled). Do not return any rounded answers.
sql: WITH down_ports_ranked AS ( WITH inner_cte AS (SELECT p.id AS port_id, p.tenant_id, p.mac_address, sgpb.security_group_id, RANK() OVER ( PARTITION BY sgpb.security_group_id ORDER BY p.id ) AS window_column FROM SECURITYGROUPPORTBINDINGS AS sgpb JOIN PORTS AS p ON sgpb.port_id = p.id JOIN PORTSECURITYBINDINGS AS psb ON p.id = psb.port_id WHERE p.status = 'DOWN'), sg_counts AS ( SELECT security_group_id, COUNT(*) AS down_ports FROM inner_cte GROUP BY security_group_id ) SELECT i.port_id, i.tenant_id, i.mac_address, i.security_group_id, i.window_column, c.down_ports FROM inner_cte AS i JOIN sg_counts AS c ON i.security_group_id = c.security_group_id WHERE c.down_ports > (SELECT AVG(down_ports) FROM sg_counts) ), tenant_admin_rollup AS ( WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT p.id AS port_id, p.tenant_id, p.mac_address, COUNT(psb.port_id) AS binding_count, SUM(CASE WHEN psb.port_security_enabled THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS port_security_enabled_total FROM ports p JOIN portsecuritybindings psb ON p.id = psb.port_id WHERE p.admin_state_up = 1 GROUP BY p.id, p.tenant_id, p.mac_address ), TenantPortSecurityRollup AS ( SELECT p.tenant_id, CASE WHEN p.admin_state_up = 1 THEN 'Up' ELSE 'Down' END AS admin_status, COUNT(DISTINCT p.id) AS total_ports, COALESCE(SUM(inner_cte.binding_count), 0) AS total_bindings, COALESCE(SUM(inner_cte.port_security_enabled_total), 0) AS total_port_security_enabled FROM ports p LEFT JOIN inner_cte ON p.id = inner_cte.port_id GROUP BY p.tenant_id, admin_status ) SELECT CASE WHEN GROUPING(tenant_id) = 1 THEN 'GRAND TOTAL' ELSE tenant_id END AS tenant_id, CASE WHEN GROUPING(admin_status) = 1 AND GROUPING(tenant_id) = 0 THEN 'SUBTOTAL' WHEN GROUPING(admin_status) = 1 AND GROUPING(tenant_id) = 1 THEN 'GRAND TOTAL' ELSE admin_status END AS admin_status, SUM(total_ports) AS total_ports, SUM(total_bindings) AS total_bindings, SUM(total_port_security_enabled) AS total_port_security_enabled FROM TenantPortSecurityRollup GROUP BY tenant_id, admin_status WITH ROLLUP ) SELECT dpr.port_id, dpr.tenant_id, dpr.mac_address, dpr.security_group_id, dpr.window_column AS port_rank_within_security_group_by_port_id, dpr.down_ports AS down_ports_in_security_group, tar.admin_status, tar.total_ports, tar.total_bindings, tar.total_port_security_enabled FROM down_ports_ranked AS dpr JOIN tenant_admin_rollup AS tar ON dpr.tenant_id = tar.tenant_id WHERE tar.admin_status = 'Up';
sub_questions: For ports that are DOWN, show the port ID, tenant ID, MAC address, the security group ID from the security-group-to-port binding, and the rank of each port within its security group when ordered by port ID.

For each port that is administratively up, list the port ID, tenant ID, MAC address, the number of port security bindings on that port, and the total number of times port security is enabled across those bindings.

For ports that are DOWN, show the port ID, tenant ID, MAC address, the security group ID from the security-group-to-port binding, and the rank of each port within its security group when ordered by port ID. Then, return only those security groups whose number of DOWN ports is greater than the average number of DOWN ports per security group.

For each tenant and port administrative status, list the tenant ID, the port admin status label ('Up' or 'Down'), the total number of ports, the total number of port security bindings on those ports, and the total number of times port security is enabled across those bindings. Include subtotals per tenant and a grand total.
sub_sqls: SELECT p.id AS port_id, p.tenant_id, p.mac_address, sgpb.security_group_id, RANK() OVER ( PARTITION BY sgpb.security_group_id ORDER BY p.id ) AS window_column FROM SECURITYGROUPPORTBINDINGS AS sgpb JOIN PORTS AS p ON sgpb.port_id = p.id JOIN PORTSECURITYBINDINGS AS psb ON p.id = psb.port_id WHERE p.status = 'DOWN';

SELECT p.id AS port_id, p.tenant_id, p.mac_address, COUNT(psb.port_id) AS binding_count, SUM(CASE WHEN psb.port_security_enabled THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS port_security_enabled_total FROM ports p JOIN portsecuritybindings psb ON p.id = psb.port_id WHERE p.admin_state_up = 1 GROUP BY p.id, p.tenant_id, p.mac_address;

WITH inner_cte AS (SELECT p.id AS port_id, p.tenant_id, p.mac_address, sgpb.security_group_id, RANK() OVER ( PARTITION BY sgpb.security_group_id ORDER BY p.id ) AS window_column FROM SECURITYGROUPPORTBINDINGS AS sgpb JOIN PORTS AS p ON sgpb.port_id = p.id JOIN PORTSECURITYBINDINGS AS psb ON p.id = psb.port_id WHERE p.status = 'DOWN'), sg_counts AS ( SELECT security_group_id, COUNT(*) AS down_ports FROM inner_cte GROUP BY security_group_id ) SELECT i.port_id, i.tenant_id, i.mac_address, i.security_group_id, i.window_column, c.down_ports FROM inner_cte AS i JOIN sg_counts AS c ON i.security_group_id = c.security_group_id WHERE c.down_ports > (SELECT AVG(down_ports) FROM sg_counts);

WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT p.id AS port_id, p.tenant_id, p.mac_address, COUNT(psb.port_id) AS binding_count, SUM(CASE WHEN psb.port_security_enabled THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS port_security_enabled_total FROM ports p JOIN portsecuritybindings psb ON p.id = psb.port_id WHERE p.admin_state_up = 1 GROUP BY p.id, p.tenant_id, p.mac_address ), TenantPortSecurityRollup AS ( SELECT p.tenant_id, CASE WHEN p.admin_state_up = 1 THEN 'Up' ELSE 'Down' END AS admin_status, COUNT(DISTINCT p.id) AS total_ports, COALESCE(SUM(inner_cte.binding_count), 0) AS total_bindings, COALESCE(SUM(inner_cte.port_security_enabled_total), 0) AS total_port_security_enabled FROM ports p LEFT JOIN inner_cte ON p.id = inner_cte.port_id GROUP BY p.tenant_id, admin_status ) SELECT CASE WHEN GROUPING(tenant_id) = 1 THEN 'GRAND TOTAL' ELSE tenant_id END AS tenant_id, CASE WHEN GROUPING(admin_status) = 1 AND GROUPING(tenant_id) = 0 THEN 'SUBTOTAL' WHEN GROUPING(admin_status) = 1 AND GROUPING(tenant_id) = 1 THEN 'GRAND TOTAL' ELSE admin_status END AS admin_status, SUM(total_ports) AS total_ports, SUM(total_bindings) AS total_bindings, SUM(total_port_security_enabled) AS total_port_security_enabled FROM TenantPortSecurityRollup GROUP BY tenant_id, admin_status WITH ROLLUP;

question: For ports that are administratively up and also have status DOWN, list the port ID, tenant ID, and MAC address, along with (1) the number of port security bindings on the port, the total number of times port security is enabled across those bindings, and that enabled total’s deviation from the average enabled total across all administratively up ports, and (2) the running sum of the port’s standard attribute ID within its security group plus the security group’s total DOWN-port count and that count’s deviation from the average DOWN-port count across all security groups. Do not return any rounded answers.
sql: WITH q1 AS ( WITH inner_cte AS (SELECT p.id AS port_id, p.tenant_id, p.mac_address, COUNT(psb.port_id) AS binding_count, SUM(CASE WHEN psb.port_security_enabled THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS port_security_enabled_total FROM ports p JOIN portsecuritybindings psb ON p.id = psb.port_id WHERE p.admin_state_up = 1 GROUP BY p.id, p.tenant_id, p.mac_address), avg_cte AS ( SELECT AVG(port_security_enabled_total) AS avg_enabled_total FROM inner_cte ) SELECT i.port_id, i.tenant_id, i.mac_address, i.binding_count, i.port_security_enabled_total, (i.port_security_enabled_total - a.avg_enabled_total) AS deviation_from_avg_enabled_total FROM inner_cte i CROSS JOIN avg_cte a ), q2 AS ( WITH inner_cte AS (SELECT p.ID AS port_id, p.TENANT_ID AS tenant_id, p.MAC_ADDRESS AS mac_address, SUM(p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID) OVER ( PARTITION BY sgpb.SECURITY_GROUP_ID ORDER BY p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID ) AS window_column FROM SECURITYGROUPPORTBINDINGS AS sgpb JOIN PORTS AS p ON sgpb.PORT_ID = p.ID JOIN PORTSECURITYBINDINGS AS psb ON p.ID = psb.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN'), SecurityGroupDownCounts AS ( SELECT sgpb.SECURITY_GROUP_ID AS security_group_id, COUNT(*) AS down_ports_in_group FROM SECURITYGROUPPORTBINDINGS AS sgpb JOIN PORTS AS p ON sgpb.PORT_ID = p.ID JOIN PORTSECURITYBINDINGS AS psb ON p.ID = psb.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' GROUP BY sgpb.SECURITY_GROUP_ID ), AverageDownCounts AS ( SELECT AVG(down_ports_in_group) AS avg_down_ports_in_group FROM SecurityGroupDownCounts ) SELECT i.port_id, i.tenant_id, i.mac_address, i.window_column, sgdc.down_ports_in_group, (sgdc.down_ports_in_group - adc.avg_down_ports_in_group) AS deviation_from_avg_down_ports FROM inner_cte AS i JOIN SECURITYGROUPPORTBINDINGS AS sgpb ON sgpb.PORT_ID = i.port_id JOIN SecurityGroupDownCounts AS sgdc ON sgdc.security_group_id = sgpb.SECURITY_GROUP_ID CROSS JOIN AverageDownCounts AS adc ) SELECT q1.port_id, q1.tenant_id, q1.mac_address, q1.binding_count, q1.port_security_enabled_total, q1.deviation_from_avg_enabled_total, q2.window_column, q2.down_ports_in_group, q2.deviation_from_avg_down_ports FROM q1 JOIN q2 ON q1.port_id = q2.port_id AND q1.tenant_id = q2.tenant_id AND q1.mac_address = q2.mac_address;

sub_sqls: SELECT p.id AS port_id, p.tenant_id, p.mac_address, COUNT(psb.port_id) AS binding_count, SUM(CASE WHEN psb.port_security_enabled THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS port_security_enabled_total FROM ports p JOIN portsecuritybindings psb ON p.id = psb.port_id WHERE p.admin_state_up = 1 GROUP BY p.id, p.tenant_id, p.mac_address;

SELECT p.ID AS port_id, p.TENANT_ID AS tenant_id, p.MAC_ADDRESS AS mac_address, SUM(p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID) OVER ( PARTITION BY sgpb.SECURITY_GROUP_ID ORDER BY p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID ) AS window_column FROM SECURITYGROUPPORTBINDINGS AS sgpb JOIN PORTS AS p ON sgpb.PORT_ID = p.ID JOIN PORTSECURITYBINDINGS AS psb ON p.ID = psb.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN';

WITH inner_cte AS (SELECT p.id AS port_id, p.tenant_id, p.mac_address, COUNT(psb.port_id) AS binding_count, SUM(CASE WHEN psb.port_security_enabled THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS port_security_enabled_total FROM ports p JOIN portsecuritybindings psb ON p.id = psb.port_id WHERE p.admin_state_up = 1 GROUP BY p.id, p.tenant_id, p.mac_address), avg_cte AS ( SELECT AVG(port_security_enabled_total) AS avg_enabled_total FROM inner_cte ) SELECT i.port_id, i.tenant_id, i.mac_address, i.binding_count, i.port_security_enabled_total, (i.port_security_enabled_total - a.avg_enabled_total) AS deviation_from_avg_enabled_total FROM inner_cte i CROSS JOIN avg_cte a;

WITH inner_cte AS (SELECT p.ID AS port_id, p.TENANT_ID AS tenant_id, p.MAC_ADDRESS AS mac_address, SUM(p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID) OVER ( PARTITION BY sgpb.SECURITY_GROUP_ID ORDER BY p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID ) AS window_column FROM SECURITYGROUPPORTBINDINGS AS sgpb JOIN PORTS AS p ON sgpb.PORT_ID = p.ID JOIN PORTSECURITYBINDINGS AS psb ON p.ID = psb.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN'), SecurityGroupDownCounts AS ( SELECT sgpb.SECURITY_GROUP_ID AS security_group_id, COUNT(*) AS down_ports_in_group FROM SECURITYGROUPPORTBINDINGS AS sgpb JOIN PORTS AS p ON sgpb.PORT_ID = p.ID JOIN PORTSECURITYBINDINGS AS psb ON p.ID = psb.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' GROUP BY sgpb.SECURITY_GROUP_ID ), AverageDownCounts AS ( SELECT AVG(down_ports_in_group) AS avg_down_ports_in_group FROM SecurityGroupDownCounts ) SELECT i.port_id, i.tenant_id, i.mac_address, i.window_column, sgdc.down_ports_in_group, (sgdc.down_ports_in_group - adc.avg_down_ports_in_group) AS deviation_from_avg_down_ports FROM inner_cte AS i JOIN SECURITYGROUPPORTBINDINGS AS sgpb ON sgpb.PORT_ID = i.port_id JOIN SecurityGroupDownCounts AS sgdc ON sgdc.security_group_id = sgpb.SECURITY_GROUP_ID CROSS JOIN AverageDownCounts AS adc;

question: On host "drive-59", how many distinct tenants have ports there, how many of those tenants are classified as HIGH_USER based on their count of DOWN ports with port security enabled versus the cross-tenant average benchmark, and how many of those tenants have any port security enabled (also report the overall total number of DOWN ports with port security enabled across all tenants)? Do not return any rounded answers. Classify each tenant as 'HIGH_USER' (at least 50% more than average), 'LOW_USER' (at least 50% less than average), or 'AVERAGE_USER'.
sql: WITH q1 AS ( WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT COUNT(*) AS down_ports_with_port_security_enabled FROM PORTS p JOIN PORTSECURITYBINDINGS psb ON p.ID = psb.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' AND psb.PORT_SECURITY_ENABLED = 1 ), TenantDownSecurePorts AS ( SELECT p.TENANT_ID, COUNT(*) AS down_secure_ports FROM PORTS p JOIN PORTSECURITYBINDINGS psb ON p.ID = psb.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' AND psb.PORT_SECURITY_ENABLED = 1 GROUP BY p.TENANT_ID ), AverageDownSecurePorts AS ( SELECT AVG(down_secure_ports) AS avg_down_secure_ports FROM TenantDownSecurePorts ) SELECT tdsp.TENANT_ID, tdsp.down_secure_ports, adsp.avg_down_secure_ports AS benchmark, CASE WHEN tdsp.down_secure_ports > adsp.avg_down_secure_ports * 1.5 THEN 'HIGH_USER' WHEN tdsp.down_secure_ports < adsp.avg_down_secure_ports * 0.5 THEN 'LOW_USER' ELSE 'AVERAGE_USER' END AS user_category, inner_cte.down_ports_with_port_security_enabled AS overall_down_secure_ports FROM TenantDownSecurePorts tdsp CROSS JOIN AverageDownSecurePorts adsp CROSS JOIN inner_cte ), q2 AS ( WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT b.PORT_ID, p.TENANT_ID, p.MAC_ADDRESS, SUM(p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID) OVER ( PARTITION BY b.VIF_TYPE ORDER BY p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID ) AS window_column FROM ML2_PORT_BINDINGS AS b JOIN PORTS AS p ON b.PORT_ID = p.ID JOIN PORTSECURITYBINDINGS AS psb ON p.ID = psb.PORT_ID WHERE b.HOST = 'drive-59' ) SELECT i.TENANT_ID, COUNT(DISTINCT i.PORT_ID) AS total_ports, CASE WHEN COUNT(DISTINCT psb.PORT_ID) > 0 THEN 'Yes' ELSE 'No' END AS has_port_security_enabled FROM inner_cte AS i LEFT JOIN PORTSECURITYBINDINGS AS psb ON i.PORT_ID = psb.PORT_ID GROUP BY i.TENANT_ID ORDER BY total_ports DESC ) SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT q2.TENANT_ID) AS tenants_on_drive_59, COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN q1.user_category = 'HIGH_USER' THEN q2.TENANT_ID END) AS high_user_tenants_on_drive_59, COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN q2.has_port_security_enabled = 'Yes' THEN q2.TENANT_ID END) AS tenants_on_drive_59_with_port_security_enabled, MAX(q1.overall_down_secure_ports) AS overall_down_secure_ports FROM q2 JOIN q1 ON q2.TENANT_ID = q1.TENANT_ID;
sub_questions: How many ports are in status 'DOWN' and have port security enabled (as indicated by the port security binding)?
For ports on host "drive-59", show the port ID, tenant ID, MAC address, and a running sum of the port standard attribute IDs within each VIF type group ordered by standard attribute ID.

For each tenant, report the number of ports that are in status 'DOWN' and have port security enabled, the average of that count across all tenants as a benchmark, and classify each tenant as 'HIGH_USER' (at least 50% more than average), 'LOW_USER' (at least 50% less than average), or 'AVERAGE_USER'.
For ports on host "drive-59", list each tenant ID with the total number of distinct ports found there, and indicate whether that tenant has any ports with port security enabled.
sub_sqls: SELECT COUNT(*) AS down_ports_with_port_security_enabled FROM PORTS p JOIN PORTSECURITYBINDINGS psb ON p.ID = psb.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' AND psb.PORT_SECURITY_ENABLED = 1;

SELECT b.PORT_ID, p.TENANT_ID, p.MAC_ADDRESS, SUM(p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID) OVER ( PARTITION BY b.VIF_TYPE ORDER BY p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID ) AS window_column FROM ML2_PORT_BINDINGS AS b JOIN PORTS AS p ON b.PORT_ID = p.ID JOIN PORTSECURITYBINDINGS AS psb ON p.ID = psb.PORT_ID WHERE b.HOST = 'drive-59';

WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT COUNT(*) AS down_ports_with_port_security_enabled FROM PORTS p JOIN PORTSECURITYBINDINGS psb ON p.ID = psb.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' AND psb.PORT_SECURITY_ENABLED = 1 ), TenantDownSecurePorts AS ( SELECT p.TENANT_ID, COUNT(*) AS down_secure_ports FROM PORTS p JOIN PORTSECURITYBINDINGS psb ON p.ID = psb.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' AND psb.PORT_SECURITY_ENABLED = 1 GROUP BY p.TENANT_ID ), AverageDownSecurePorts AS ( SELECT AVG(down_secure_ports) AS avg_down_secure_ports FROM TenantDownSecurePorts ) SELECT tdsp.TENANT_ID, tdsp.down_secure_ports, adsp.avg_down_secure_ports AS benchmark, CASE WHEN tdsp.down_secure_ports > adsp.avg_down_secure_ports * 1.5 THEN 'HIGH_USER' WHEN tdsp.down_secure_ports < adsp.avg_down_secure_ports * 0.5 THEN 'LOW_USER' ELSE 'AVERAGE_USER' END AS user_category, inner_cte.down_ports_with_port_security_enabled AS overall_down_secure_ports FROM TenantDownSecurePorts tdsp CROSS JOIN AverageDownSecurePorts adsp CROSS JOIN inner_cte;

WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT b.PORT_ID, p.TENANT_ID, p.MAC_ADDRESS, SUM(p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID) OVER ( PARTITION BY b.VIF_TYPE ORDER BY p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID ) AS window_column FROM ML2_PORT_BINDINGS AS b JOIN PORTS AS p ON b.PORT_ID = p.ID JOIN PORTSECURITYBINDINGS AS psb ON p.ID = psb.PORT_ID WHERE b.HOST = 'drive-59' ) SELECT i.TENANT_ID, COUNT(DISTINCT i.PORT_ID) AS total_ports, CASE WHEN COUNT(DISTINCT psb.PORT_ID) > 0 THEN 'Yes' ELSE 'No' END AS has_port_security_enabled FROM inner_cte AS i LEFT JOIN PORTSECURITYBINDINGS AS psb ON i.PORT_ID = psb.PORT_ID GROUP BY i.TENANT_ID ORDER BY total_ports DESC;

question: For ports that are both (a) bound to a security group with admin_state_up = 1 and (b) in status DOWN, list the port ID, tenant ID, port name, host, VIF type, allocated IP address, and the row number ordered by IP address (with a window frame of 2 preceding rows and 1 following row), along with the port’s security group binding count, total DNS record count, deviation of its security group binding count from the average across all admin_state_up = 1 security-group-bound ports, and (for that tenant) the total number of DOWN ports plus the average DOWN-port count across all tenants. Do not return any rounded answers.
sql: WITH sg_dns_stats AS (WITH inner_cte AS (SELECT p.id AS port_id, p.tenant_id, p.name AS port_name, COUNT(sgpb.security_group_id) AS security_group_binding_count, SUM(CASE WHEN pd.port_id IS NULL THEN 0 ELSE 1 END) AS dns_record_count FROM SECURITYGROUPPORTBINDINGS sgpb JOIN PORTS p ON sgpb.port_id = p.id LEFT JOIN PORTDNSES pd ON p.id = pd.port_id WHERE p.admin_state_up = 1 GROUP BY p.id, p.tenant_id, p.name), avg_cte AS ( SELECT AVG(security_group_binding_count) AS avg_sg_binding_count FROM inner_cte ) SELECT i.port_id, i.tenant_id, i.port_name, i.security_group_binding_count, i.dns_record_count, (i.security_group_binding_count - a.avg_sg_binding_count) AS deviation_from_avg_sg_binding_count FROM inner_cte i CROSS JOIN avg_cte a), down_port_details AS (WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT p.ID AS port_id, p.TENANT_ID AS tenant_id, b.HOST AS host, b.VIF_TYPE AS vif_type, ia.IP_ADDRESS AS ip_address, ROW_NUMBER() OVER ( ORDER BY ia.IP_ADDRESS ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND 1 FOLLOWING ) AS window_column FROM ML2_PORT_BINDINGS b JOIN PORTS p ON b.PORT_ID = p.ID JOIN IPALLOCATIONS ia ON p.ID = ia.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' ) SELECT inner_cte.port_id, inner_cte.tenant_id, inner_cte.host, inner_cte.vif_type, inner_cte.ip_address, inner_cte.window_column, tenant_counts.total_down_ports, avg_down.avg_down_port_count FROM inner_cte JOIN ( SELECT tenant_id, COUNT(port_id) AS total_down_ports FROM inner_cte GROUP BY tenant_id ) AS tenant_counts ON inner_cte.tenant_id = tenant_counts.tenant_id JOIN ( SELECT AVG(down_port_count) AS avg_down_port_count FROM ( SELECT COUNT(port_id) AS down_port_count FROM inner_cte GROUP BY tenant_id ) AS sub ) AS avg_down ON 1 = 1) SELECT d.port_id, d.tenant_id, s.port_name, d.host, d.vif_type, d.ip_address, d.window_column, s.security_group_binding_count, s.dns_record_count, s.deviation_from_avg_sg_binding_count, d.total_down_ports, d.avg_down_port_count FROM down_port_details d JOIN sg_dns_stats s ON d.port_id = s.port_id WHERE s.tenant_id = d.tenant_id;
sub_questions: For each port that is bound to a security group and has admin_state_up = 1, list the port ID, tenant ID, port name, and the number of security group bindings for that port along with the total number of DNS records associated with the port.

For ports whose status is DOWN, list the port ID, tenant ID, host, VIF type, and allocated IP address, and assign row numbers ordered by IP address using a window frame of 2 preceding rows and 1 following row.

For each port that is bound to a security group and has admin_state_up = 1, list the port ID, tenant ID, port name, the number of security group bindings for that port, the total number of DNS records associated with the port, and the deviation of that port’s security group binding count from the average security group binding count across all such ports.

For ports whose status is DOWN, list the port ID, tenant ID, host, VIF type, allocated IP address, and the row number ordered by IP address (using a window frame of 2 preceding rows and 1 following row), and also show for each tenant the total number of DOWN ports along with the average DOWN-port count across all tenants.
sub_sqls: SELECT p.id AS port_id, p.tenant_id, p.name AS port_name, COUNT(sgpb.security_group_id) AS security_group_binding_count, SUM(CASE WHEN pd.port_id IS NULL THEN 0 ELSE 1 END) AS dns_record_count FROM SECURITYGROUPPORTBINDINGS sgpb JOIN PORTS p ON sgpb.port_id = p.id LEFT JOIN PORTDNSES pd ON p.id = pd.port_id WHERE p.admin_state_up = 1 GROUP BY p.id, p.tenant_id, p.name;

SELECT p.ID AS port_id, p.TENANT_ID AS tenant_id, b.HOST AS host, b.VIF_TYPE AS vif_type, ia.IP_ADDRESS AS ip_address, ROW_NUMBER() OVER ( ORDER BY ia.IP_ADDRESS ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND 1 FOLLOWING ) AS window_column FROM ML2_PORT_BINDINGS b JOIN PORTS p ON b.PORT_ID = p.ID JOIN IPALLOCATIONS ia ON p.ID = ia.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN';

WITH inner_cte AS (SELECT p.id AS port_id, p.tenant_id, p.name AS port_name, COUNT(sgpb.security_group_id) AS security_group_binding_count, SUM(CASE WHEN pd.port_id IS NULL THEN 0 ELSE 1 END) AS dns_record_count FROM SECURITYGROUPPORTBINDINGS sgpb JOIN PORTS p ON sgpb.port_id = p.id LEFT JOIN PORTDNSES pd ON p.id = pd.port_id WHERE p.admin_state_up = 1 GROUP BY p.id, p.tenant_id, p.name), avg_cte AS ( SELECT AVG(security_group_binding_count) AS avg_sg_binding_count FROM inner_cte ) SELECT i.port_id, i.tenant_id, i.port_name, i.security_group_binding_count, i.dns_record_count, (i.security_group_binding_count - a.avg_sg_binding_count) AS deviation_from_avg_sg_binding_count FROM inner_cte i CROSS JOIN avg_cte a;

WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT p.ID AS port_id, p.TENANT_ID AS tenant_id, b.HOST AS host, b.VIF_TYPE AS vif_type, ia.IP_ADDRESS AS ip_address, ROW_NUMBER() OVER ( ORDER BY ia.IP_ADDRESS ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND 1 FOLLOWING ) AS window_column FROM ML2_PORT_BINDINGS b JOIN PORTS p ON b.PORT_ID = p.ID JOIN IPALLOCATIONS ia ON p.ID = ia.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' ) SELECT inner_cte.port_id, inner_cte.tenant_id, inner_cte.host, inner_cte.vif_type, inner_cte.ip_address, inner_cte.window_column, tenant_counts.total_down_ports, avg_down.avg_down_port_count FROM inner_cte JOIN ( SELECT tenant_id, COUNT(port_id) AS total_down_ports FROM inner_cte GROUP BY tenant_id ) AS tenant_counts ON inner_cte.tenant_id = tenant_counts.tenant_id JOIN ( SELECT AVG(down_port_count) AS avg_down_port_count FROM ( SELECT COUNT(port_id) AS down_port_count FROM inner_cte GROUP BY tenant_id ) AS sub ) AS avg_down ON 1 = 1;

question: For tenants classified as HIGH_USER based on having at least 50% more DOWN ports than the average tenant, list each DOWN port’s port ID, tenant ID, host, VIF type, allocated IP address, and its row number ordered by IP address (using a window frame of 2 preceding rows and 1 following row). Also include the tenant’s total DOWN ports, the average DOWN-port benchmark, and—when available for the same port—the MAC address plus the port’s IP-allocation count and subnet-id row count from administratively up ports with IP allocations, along with the tenant’s total number of administratively up ports that have at least one IP allocation (restricted to tenants/ports with status DOWN). Do not return any rounded answers. Classify the tenant as 'HIGH_USER' (at least 50% more than average), 'LOW_USER' (at least 50% less than average), or 'AVERAGE_USER'.
sql: WITH down_ports AS (WITH inner_cte AS (SELECT p.ID AS port_id, p.TENANT_ID AS tenant_id, b.HOST AS host, b.VIF_TYPE AS vif_type, ia.IP_ADDRESS AS ip_address, ROW_NUMBER() OVER ( ORDER BY ia.IP_ADDRESS ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND 1 FOLLOWING ) AS window_column FROM ML2_PORT_BINDINGS b JOIN PORTS p ON b.PORT_ID = p.ID JOIN IPALLOCATIONS ia ON p.ID = ia.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN'), TenantDownPorts AS ( SELECT tenant_id, COUNT(DISTINCT port_id) AS total_down_ports FROM inner_cte GROUP BY tenant_id ), AverageDownPorts AS ( SELECT AVG(total_down_ports) AS avg_down_ports FROM TenantDownPorts ) SELECT i.port_id, i.tenant_id, i.host, i.vif_type, i.ip_address, i.window_column, tdp.total_down_ports, adp.avg_down_ports AS benchmark, CASE WHEN tdp.total_down_ports > adp.avg_down_ports * 1.5 THEN 'HIGH_USER' WHEN tdp.total_down_ports < adp.avg_down_ports * 0.5 THEN 'LOW_USER' ELSE 'AVERAGE_USER' END AS user_category FROM inner_cte i JOIN TenantDownPorts tdp ON i.tenant_id = tdp.tenant_id CROSS JOIN AverageDownPorts adp), admin_up_ipalloc_rollup AS (WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT p.id AS port_id, p.tenant_id, p.mac_address, COUNT(ia.ip_address) AS ip_allocation_count, SUM(CASE WHEN ia.subnet_id IS NOT NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS subnet_id_rows FROM ports p JOIN portsecuritybindings psb ON psb.port_id = p.id JOIN ipallocations ia ON ia.port_id = p.id WHERE p.admin_state_up = 1 AND ia.ip_address IS NOT NULL GROUP BY p.id, p.tenant_id, p.mac_address ) SELECT CASE WHEN LAG(tenant_id) OVER (ORDER BY tenant_id_sort, tenant_id, port_id) = tenant_id THEN NULL ELSE tenant_id END AS tenant_id, port_id, mac_address, ip_allocation_count, subnet_id_rows FROM ( SELECT CASE WHEN GROUPING(inner_cte.tenant_id) = 1 THEN 'zzz' ELSE inner_cte.tenant_id END AS tenant_id_sort, CASE WHEN GROUPING(inner_cte.tenant_id) = 1 THEN 'TOTAL' ELSE inner_cte.tenant_id END AS tenant_id, CASE WHEN GROUPING(inner_cte.port_id) = 1 THEN NULL ELSE inner_cte.port_id END AS port_id, CASE WHEN GROUPING(inner_cte.port_id) = 1 THEN NULL ELSE inner_cte.mac_address END AS mac_address, SUM(inner_cte.ip_allocation_count) AS ip_allocation_count, SUM(inner_cte.subnet_id_rows) AS subnet_id_rows FROM inner_cte GROUP BY inner_cte.tenant_id, inner_cte.port_id, inner_cte.mac_address WITH ROLLUP ) AS tbltmp ORDER BY tenant_id_sort, tenant_id, port_id), TenantAdminUpTotals AS ( SELECT p.tenant_id, COUNT(DISTINCT p.id) AS total_admin_up_ports_with_ip FROM ports p JOIN ipallocations ia ON ia.port_id = p.id WHERE p.admin_state_up = 1 AND ia.ip_address IS NOT NULL AND p.status = 'DOWN' GROUP BY p.tenant_id ) SELECT dp.tenant_id, dp.port_id, dp.host, dp.vif_type, dp.ip_address, dp.window_column, dp.total_down_ports, dp.benchmark, dp.user_category, aui.mac_address, aui.ip_allocation_count, aui.subnet_id_rows, tat.total_admin_up_ports_with_ip FROM down_ports dp LEFT JOIN admin_up_ipalloc_rollup aui ON aui.port_id = dp.port_id LEFT JOIN TenantAdminUpTotals tat ON tat.tenant_id = dp.tenant_id WHERE dp.user_category = 'HIGH_USER' ORDER BY dp.total_down_ports DESC, dp.tenant_id, dp.ip_address;

For each port that is administratively up and has at least one IP allocation, list the port ID, tenant ID, MAC address, the number of IP allocations on that port, and the total number of distinct subnets those IP allocations belong to.

sub_sqls: SELECT p.ID AS port_id, p.TENANT_ID AS tenant_id, b.HOST AS host, b.VIF_TYPE AS vif_type, ia.IP_ADDRESS AS ip_address, ROW_NUMBER() OVER ( ORDER BY ia.IP_ADDRESS ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND 1 FOLLOWING ) AS window_column FROM ML2_PORT_BINDINGS b JOIN PORTS p ON b.PORT_ID = p.ID JOIN IPALLOCATIONS ia ON p.ID = ia.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN';

SELECT p.id AS port_id, p.tenant_id, p.mac_address, COUNT(ia.ip_address) AS ip_allocation_count, SUM(CASE WHEN ia.subnet_id IS NOT NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS subnet_id_rows FROM ports p JOIN portsecuritybindings psb ON psb.port_id = p.id JOIN ipallocations ia ON ia.port_id = p.id WHERE p.admin_state_up = 1 AND ia.ip_address IS NOT NULL GROUP BY p.id, p.tenant_id, p.mac_address;

WITH inner_cte AS (SELECT p.ID AS port_id, p.TENANT_ID AS tenant_id, b.HOST AS host, b.VIF_TYPE AS vif_type, ia.IP_ADDRESS AS ip_address, ROW_NUMBER() OVER ( ORDER BY ia.IP_ADDRESS ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND 1 FOLLOWING ) AS window_column FROM ML2_PORT_BINDINGS b JOIN PORTS p ON b.PORT_ID = p.ID JOIN IPALLOCATIONS ia ON p.ID = ia.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN'), TenantDownPorts AS ( SELECT tenant_id, COUNT(DISTINCT port_id) AS total_down_ports FROM inner_cte GROUP BY tenant_id ), AverageDownPorts AS ( SELECT AVG(total_down_ports) AS avg_down_ports FROM TenantDownPorts ) SELECT i.port_id, i.tenant_id, i.host, i.vif_type, i.ip_address, i.window_column, tdp.total_down_ports, adp.avg_down_ports AS benchmark, CASE WHEN tdp.total_down_ports > adp.avg_down_ports * 1.5 THEN 'HIGH_USER' WHEN tdp.total_down_ports < adp.avg_down_ports * 0.5 THEN 'LOW_USER' ELSE 'AVERAGE_USER' END AS user_category FROM inner_cte i JOIN TenantDownPorts tdp ON i.tenant_id = tdp.tenant_id CROSS JOIN AverageDownPorts adp;

WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT p.id AS port_id, p.tenant_id, p.mac_address, COUNT(ia.ip_address) AS ip_allocation_count, SUM(CASE WHEN ia.subnet_id IS NOT NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS subnet_id_rows FROM ports p JOIN portsecuritybindings psb ON psb.port_id = p.id JOIN ipallocations ia ON ia.port_id = p.id WHERE p.admin_state_up = 1 AND ia.ip_address IS NOT NULL GROUP BY p.id, p.tenant_id, p.mac_address ) SELECT CASE WHEN LAG(tenant_id) OVER (ORDER BY tenant_id_sort, tenant_id, port_id) = tenant_id THEN NULL ELSE tenant_id END AS tenant_id, port_id, mac_address, ip_allocation_count, subnet_id_rows FROM ( SELECT CASE WHEN GROUPING(inner_cte.tenant_id) = 1 THEN 'zzz' ELSE inner_cte.tenant_id END AS tenant_id_sort, CASE WHEN GROUPING(inner_cte.tenant_id) = 1 THEN 'TOTAL' ELSE inner_cte.tenant_id END AS tenant_id, CASE WHEN GROUPING(inner_cte.port_id) = 1 THEN NULL ELSE inner_cte.port_id END AS port_id, CASE WHEN GROUPING(inner_cte.port_id) = 1 THEN NULL ELSE inner_cte.mac_address END AS mac_address, SUM(inner_cte.ip_allocation_count) AS ip_allocation_count, SUM(inner_cte.subnet_id_rows) AS subnet_id_rows FROM inner_cte GROUP BY inner_cte.tenant_id, inner_cte.port_id, inner_cte.mac_address WITH ROLLUP ) AS tbltmp ORDER BY tenant_id_sort, tenant_id, port_id;

question: For the top 10 security groups with the most DOWN ports, list each security group’s ID, its total number of DOWN ports, and whether any of those DOWN ports belong to a tenant that has more than one DOWN port; additionally, for the DOWN port status, include the variance of STANDARD_ATTR_ID (considering only ports with an IP allocation and a non-null STANDARD_ATTR_ID), the total number of distinct ports in that status, and whether any of those ports have floating IPs. Do not return any rounded answers.
sql: WITH PortStatusVariance AS ( WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT p.STATUS, VARIANCE(p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID) AS standard_attr_id_variance FROM PORTS AS p JOIN IPALLOCATIONS AS ia ON p.ID = ia.PORT_ID WHERE p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID IS NOT NULL GROUP BY p.STATUS ORDER BY standard_attr_id_variance DESC ) SELECT i.STATUS, i.standard_attr_id_variance, COUNT(DISTINCT p2.ID) AS total_ports, CASE WHEN COUNT(DISTINCT f.ID) > 0 THEN 'Yes' ELSE 'No' END AS has_floating_ips FROM inner_cte i JOIN PORTS p2 ON p2.STATUS = i.STATUS JOIN IPALLOCATIONS ia2 ON ia2.PORT_ID = p2.ID LEFT JOIN FLOATINGIPS f ON f.FIXED_PORT_ID = p2.ID WHERE p2.STANDARD_ATTR_ID IS NOT NULL GROUP BY i.STATUS, i.standard_attr_id_variance ORDER BY i.standard_attr_id_variance DESC LIMIT 10 ), TopSecurityGroupsDownPorts AS ( WITH inner_cte AS (SELECT p.id AS port_id, p.tenant_id, p.mac_address, sgpb.security_group_id, RANK() OVER ( PARTITION BY sgpb.security_group_id ORDER BY p.id ) AS window_column FROM SECURITYGROUPPORTBINDINGS AS sgpb JOIN PORTS AS p ON sgpb.port_id = p.id JOIN PORTSECURITYBINDINGS AS psb ON p.id = psb.port_id WHERE p.status = 'DOWN') SELECT inner_cte.security_group_id, COUNT(DISTINCT inner_cte.port_id) AS total_down_ports, CASE WHEN COUNT(DISTINCT t.tenant_id) > 0 THEN 'Yes' ELSE 'No' END AS has_tenant_with_multiple_down_ports FROM inner_cte LEFT JOIN (SELECT tenant_id FROM inner_cte GROUP BY tenant_id HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT port_id) > 1) AS t ON inner_cte.tenant_id = t.tenant_id GROUP BY inner_cte.security_group_id ORDER BY total_down_ports DESC LIMIT 10 ) SELECT tsg.security_group_id, tsg.total_down_ports, tsg.has_tenant_with_multiple_down_ports, psv.STATUS AS port_status, psv.standard_attr_id_variance, psv.total_ports, psv.has_floating_ips FROM TopSecurityGroupsDownPorts tsg JOIN SECURITYGROUPPORTBINDINGS sgpb ON sgpb.SECURITY_GROUP_ID = tsg.security_group_id JOIN PORTS p ON p.ID = sgpb.PORT_ID JOIN PortStatusVariance psv ON psv.STATUS = p.STATUS WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' ORDER BY tsg.total_down_ports DESC, psv.standard_attr_id_variance DESC;

question: For the top 3 networks with the most subnets among RBAC entries where the action is 'access_as_shared', show each network (with its subnet count) and each subnet’s tenant ID, along with (on those same networks) the number of DOWN ports whose standard attribute ID is greater than the average standard attribute ID for DOWN ports in the same resource type, and the average of their running-sum standard attribute ID window values. Do not return any rounded answers.
sql: WITH down_ports_windowed AS ( WITH inner_cte AS (SELECT p.ID AS port_id, p.TENANT_ID AS tenant_id, p.MAC_ADDRESS AS mac_address, SUM(sa.ID) OVER ( PARTITION BY sa.RESOURCE_TYPE ORDER BY sa.ID ) AS window_column FROM PORTS p JOIN STANDARDATTRIBUTES sa ON sa.ID = p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN'), ResourceTypeAverages AS (SELECT sa.RESOURCE_TYPE, AVG(sa.ID) AS avg_standard_attr_id FROM PORTS p JOIN STANDARDATTRIBUTES sa ON sa.ID = p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' GROUP BY sa.RESOURCE_TYPE) SELECT i.port_id, i.tenant_id, i.mac_address, i.window_column FROM inner_cte i JOIN PORTS p2 ON p2.ID = i.port_id JOIN STANDARDATTRIBUTES sa2 ON sa2.ID = p2.STANDARD_ATTR_ID WHERE sa2.ID > (SELECT avg_standard_attr_id FROM ResourceTypeAverages rta WHERE rta.RESOURCE_TYPE = sa2.RESOURCE_TYPE) ), top_shared_network_subnets AS ( WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT n.OBJECT_ID AS network_id, COUNT(*) AS subnet_count FROM NETWORKRBACS AS n JOIN SUBNETS AS s ON n.OBJECT_ID = s.NETWORK_ID WHERE n.ACTION = 'access_as_shared' GROUP BY n.OBJECT_ID ORDER BY COUNT(*) DESC LIMIT 3 ) SELECT CASE WHEN LAG(inner_cte.network_id) OVER (ORDER BY inner_cte.network_id) = inner_cte.network_id THEN NULL ELSE inner_cte.network_id END AS network_id, inner_cte.subnet_count, s.TENANT_ID AS subnet_tenant_id FROM inner_cte JOIN SUBNETS AS s ON s.NETWORK_ID = inner_cte.network_id ORDER BY inner_cte.network_id, s.TENANT_ID ), down_ports_on_top_shared_networks AS ( SELECT dpw.port_id, dpw.tenant_id, dpw.mac_address, dpw.window_column, tsn.network_id, tsn.subnet_count, tsn.subnet_tenant_id FROM down_ports_windowed dpw JOIN PORTS p ON p.ID = dpw.port_id JOIN top_shared_network_subnets tsn ON tsn.network_id = p.NETWORK_ID ) SELECT dptsn.network_id, dptsn.subnet_count, dptsn.subnet_tenant_id, COUNT(DISTINCT dptsn.port_id) AS down_port_count, AVG(dptsn.window_column) AS avg_down_port_running_sum_standard_attr_ids FROM down_ports_on_top_shared_networks dptsn GROUP BY dptsn.network_id, dptsn.subnet_count, dptsn.subnet_tenant_id ORDER BY dptsn.subnet_count DESC, dptsn.network_id, dptsn.subnet_tenant_id;

question: How many of the top 10 port statuses (ranked by the coefficient of variation (using STDDEV only and never STDDEV_POP) of ports’ standard attribute IDs, considering only ports that have both a security group port binding and a port security binding) are DOWN, how many of those DOWN statuses have any floating IPs allocated, and how many rows in the DOWN-and-security-group breakdown (by device owner, including subtotals) correspond to port status DOWN? Do not return any rounded answers.
sql: WITH q1 AS ( WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT p.status, STDDEV(p.standard_attr_id) / NULLIF(AVG(p.standard_attr_id), 0) AS coefficient_of_variation FROM securitygroupportbindings AS sgpb JOIN ports AS p ON sgpb.port_id = p.id JOIN portsecuritybindings AS psb ON p.id = psb.port_id GROUP BY p.status HAVING AVG(p.standard_attr_id) > 0 ORDER BY coefficient_of_variation DESC ) SELECT i.status, i.coefficient_of_variation, CASE WHEN COUNT(DISTINCT f.id) > 0 THEN 'Yes' ELSE 'No' END AS has_floating_ips FROM inner_cte i JOIN ports p ON p.status = i.status JOIN securitygroupportbindings sgpb ON sgpb.port_id = p.id JOIN portsecuritybindings psb ON psb.port_id = p.id LEFT JOIN floatingips f ON f.fixed_port_id = p.id GROUP BY i.status, i.coefficient_of_variation ORDER BY i.coefficient_of_variation DESC LIMIT 10 ), q2 AS ( WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT p.STATUS AS port_status, p.DEVICE_OWNER AS device_owner, COUNT(DISTINCT p.ID) AS port_count, MIN(p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID) AS min_standard_attr_id FROM PORTS p JOIN SECURITYGROUPPORTBINDINGS spb ON p.ID = spb.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' GROUP BY p.STATUS, p.DEVICE_OWNER ) SELECT CASE WHEN LAG(port_status) OVER (ORDER BY port_status_sort, port_status, device_owner) = port_status THEN NULL ELSE port_status END AS port_status, device_owner, port_count, min_standard_attr_id FROM ( SELECT CASE WHEN GROUPING(port_status) = 1 THEN 'zzz' ELSE port_status END AS port_status_sort, CASE WHEN GROUPING(device_owner) = 1 THEN 'TOTAL' ELSE device_owner END AS device_owner, port_status, SUM(port_count) AS port_count, MIN(min_standard_attr_id) AS min_standard_attr_id FROM inner_cte GROUP BY port_status, device_owner WITH ROLLUP ) AS tbltmp ORDER BY port_status_sort, port_status, device_owner ) SELECT (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM q1 WHERE status = 'DOWN') AS top10_statuses_with_high_cv_that_are_down_count, (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM q1 WHERE status = 'DOWN' AND has_floating_ips = 'Yes') AS top10_down_statuses_with_floating_ips_count, (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM q2 WHERE port_status = 'DOWN') AS down_status_rows_in_down_security_group_breakdown_count ;

question: For each tenant that (1) has ports in DOWN status and (2) also has administratively up ports with port security bindings, show the tenant ID, the tenant’s total number of DOWN ports, the average DOWN-port count across all tenants, and the average deviation (across that tenant’s administratively up ports) of port-security-enabled totals from the overall average enabled total across all administratively up ports. Do not return any rounded answers.
sql: WITH down_ports_by_tenant AS ( WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT p.ID AS port_id, p.TENANT_ID AS tenant_id, p.NAME AS port_name, p.NETWORK_ID AS network_id, p.MAC_ADDRESS AS mac_address, p.DEVICE_OWNER AS device_owner, ia.IP_ADDRESS AS ip_address, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY p.NETWORK_ID ORDER BY p.ID) AS window_column FROM PORTS p JOIN IPALLOCATIONS ia ON p.ID = ia.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' ) SELECT inner_cte.tenant_id AS ports_tenant_id, COUNT(inner_cte.port_id) AS total_down_ports, avg_ports.avg_down_port_count FROM inner_cte JOIN ( SELECT AVG(down_port_count) AS avg_down_port_count FROM ( SELECT COUNT(port_id) AS down_port_count FROM inner_cte GROUP BY tenant_id ) AS sub ) AS avg_ports GROUP BY inner_cte.tenant_id, avg_ports.avg_down_port_count ), admin_up_port_security AS ( WITH inner_cte AS (SELECT p.id AS port_id, p.tenant_id, p.mac_address, COUNT(psb.port_id) AS binding_count, SUM(CASE WHEN psb.port_security_enabled THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS port_security_enabled_total FROM ports p JOIN portsecuritybindings psb ON p.id = psb.port_id WHERE p.admin_state_up = 1 GROUP BY p.id, p.tenant_id, p.mac_address), avg_cte AS ( SELECT AVG(port_security_enabled_total) AS avg_enabled_total FROM inner_cte ) SELECT i.port_id, i.tenant_id, i.mac_address, i.binding_count, i.port_security_enabled_total, (i.port_security_enabled_total - a.avg_enabled_total) AS deviation_from_avg_enabled_total FROM inner_cte i CROSS JOIN avg_cte a ) SELECT aps.tenant_id, dpt.total_down_ports, dpt.avg_down_port_count, AVG(aps.deviation_from_avg_enabled_total) AS avg_deviation_from_avg_enabled_total_across_admin_up_ports FROM admin_up_port_security aps JOIN down_ports_by_tenant dpt ON aps.tenant_id = dpt.ports_tenant_id GROUP BY aps.tenant_id, dpt.total_down_ports, dpt.avg_down_port_count ORDER BY dpt.total_down_ports DESC, aps.tenant_id;

SELECT p.id AS port_id, p.tenant_id, p.mac_address, COUNT(psb.port_id) AS binding_count, SUM(CASE WHEN psb.port_security_enabled THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS port_security_enabled_total FROM ports p JOIN portsecuritybindings psb ON p.id = psb.port_id WHERE p.admin_state_up = 1 GROUP BY p.id, p.tenant_id, p.mac_address;

WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT p.ID AS port_id, p.TENANT_ID AS tenant_id, p.NAME AS port_name, p.NETWORK_ID AS network_id, p.MAC_ADDRESS AS mac_address, p.DEVICE_OWNER AS device_owner, ia.IP_ADDRESS AS ip_address, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY p.NETWORK_ID ORDER BY p.ID) AS window_column FROM PORTS p JOIN IPALLOCATIONS ia ON p.ID = ia.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' ) SELECT inner_cte.tenant_id AS ports_tenant_id, COUNT(inner_cte.port_id) AS total_down_ports, avg_ports.avg_down_port_count FROM inner_cte JOIN ( SELECT AVG(down_port_count) AS avg_down_port_count FROM ( SELECT COUNT(port_id) AS down_port_count FROM inner_cte GROUP BY tenant_id ) AS sub ) AS avg_ports GROUP BY inner_cte.tenant_id, avg_ports.avg_down_port_count;

WITH inner_cte AS (SELECT p.id AS port_id, p.tenant_id, p.mac_address, COUNT(psb.port_id) AS binding_count, SUM(CASE WHEN psb.port_security_enabled THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS port_security_enabled_total FROM ports p JOIN portsecuritybindings psb ON p.id = psb.port_id WHERE p.admin_state_up = 1 GROUP BY p.id, p.tenant_id, p.mac_address), avg_cte AS ( SELECT AVG(port_security_enabled_total) AS avg_enabled_total FROM inner_cte ) SELECT i.port_id, i.tenant_id, i.mac_address, i.binding_count, i.port_security_enabled_total, (i.port_security_enabled_total - a.avg_enabled_total) AS deviation_from_avg_enabled_total FROM inner_cte i CROSS JOIN avg_cte a;

question: List the tenant ID for tenants who are either in the top 10 by number of DOWN ports or in the top 10 by number of non-default external networks (IS_DEFAULT = 0), showing the reason for inclusion, the corresponding count (DOWN ports or non-default external networks), and a Yes/No flag indicating whether they have any DOWN ports with standard attribute resource type 'ports' or (for non-default external networks) whether any of those networks have at least one RBAC entry. Do not return any rounded answers.
sql: WITH DownPortTenants AS ( WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT p.ID AS port_id, p.TENANT_ID AS tenant_id, p.MAC_ADDRESS AS mac_address, SUM(sa.ID) OVER ( PARTITION BY sa.RESOURCE_TYPE ORDER BY sa.ID ) AS window_column FROM PORTS p JOIN STANDARDATTRIBUTES sa ON sa.ID = p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' ) SELECT i.tenant_id, COUNT(DISTINCT i.port_id) AS total_down_ports, CASE WHEN COUNT(DISTINCT sa2.ID) > 0 THEN 'Yes' ELSE 'No' END AS has_ports_resource_type FROM inner_cte i LEFT JOIN PORTS p2 ON p2.ID = i.port_id LEFT JOIN STANDARDATTRIBUTES sa2 ON sa2.ID = p2.STANDARD_ATTR_ID AND sa2.RESOURCE_TYPE = 'ports' GROUP BY i.tenant_id ORDER BY total_down_ports DESC LIMIT 10 ), NonDefaultExternalNetworkTenants AS ( WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT n.NAME, dense_rank() OVER ( ORDER BY r.ACTION ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW ) AS window_column FROM EXTERNALNETWORKS e JOIN NETWORKS n ON e.NETWORK_ID = n.ID JOIN NETWORKRBACS r ON n.ID = r.OBJECT_ID WHERE e.IS_DEFAULT = 0 ) SELECT n.TENANT_ID, COUNT(DISTINCT n.ID) AS total_nondefault_external_networks, CASE WHEN COUNT(DISTINCT r.ID) > 0 THEN 'Yes' ELSE 'No' END AS has_any_rbac FROM EXTERNALNETWORKS e JOIN NETWORKS n ON e.NETWORK_ID = n.ID LEFT JOIN NETWORKRBACS r ON n.ID = r.OBJECT_ID JOIN inner_cte ic ON ic.NAME = n.NAME WHERE e.IS_DEFAULT = 0 GROUP BY n.TENANT_ID ORDER BY total_nondefault_external_networks DESC LIMIT 10 ), CombinedTopTenants AS ( SELECT dpt.tenant_id AS tenant_id, 'Top DOWN Ports' AS reason, dpt.total_down_ports AS metric_count, dpt.has_ports_resource_type AS flag FROM DownPortTenants dpt UNION ALL SELECT ndent.tenant_id AS tenant_id, 'Top Non-default External Networks' AS reason, ndent.total_nondefault_external_networks AS metric_count, ndent.has_any_rbac AS flag FROM NonDefaultExternalNetworkTenants ndent ) SELECT tenant_id, reason, metric_count, flag FROM CombinedTopTenants ORDER BY tenant_id, reason;
sub_questions: For ports whose status is DOWN, show the port ID, tenant ID, and MAC address, along with the running sum of the standard attribute IDs within each resource type group ordered by standard attribute ID.

For networks that are marked as default external networks (IS_DEFAULT = 0), list the network name and the dense rank of each network when ordered by the RBAC action, using a window frame of the current row and the 2 preceding rows.

From the top 10 tenants with the highest number of DOWN ports, display each tenant's ID, total number of DOWN ports, and whether they have any DOWN ports whose standard attribute resource type is 'ports'.

From the top 10 tenants that own the most non-default external networks (IS_DEFAULT = 0), show each tenant ID, the total number of such networks, and whether any of those networks have at least one RBAC entry. Use the non-default external network listing with its dense-rank-by-action window as the inner CTE.
sub_sqls: SELECT p.ID AS port_id, p.TENANT_ID AS tenant_id, p.MAC_ADDRESS AS mac_address, SUM(sa.ID) OVER ( PARTITION BY sa.RESOURCE_TYPE ORDER BY sa.ID ) AS window_column FROM PORTS p JOIN STANDARDATTRIBUTES sa ON sa.ID = p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN';

SELECT n.NAME, dense_rank() OVER ( ORDER BY r.ACTION ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW ) AS window_column FROM EXTERNALNETWORKS e JOIN NETWORKS n ON e.NETWORK_ID = n.ID JOIN NETWORKRBACS r ON n.ID = r.OBJECT_ID WHERE e.IS_DEFAULT = 0;

WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT p.ID AS port_id, p.TENANT_ID AS tenant_id, p.MAC_ADDRESS AS mac_address, SUM(sa.ID) OVER ( PARTITION BY sa.RESOURCE_TYPE ORDER BY sa.ID ) AS window_column FROM PORTS p JOIN STANDARDATTRIBUTES sa ON sa.ID = p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' ) SELECT i.tenant_id, COUNT(DISTINCT i.port_id) AS total_down_ports, CASE WHEN COUNT(DISTINCT sa2.ID) > 0 THEN 'Yes' ELSE 'No' END AS has_ports_resource_type FROM inner_cte i LEFT JOIN PORTS p2 ON p2.ID = i.port_id LEFT JOIN STANDARDATTRIBUTES sa2 ON sa2.ID = p2.STANDARD_ATTR_ID AND sa2.RESOURCE_TYPE = 'ports' GROUP BY i.tenant_id ORDER BY total_down_ports DESC LIMIT 10;

WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT n.NAME, dense_rank() OVER ( ORDER BY r.ACTION ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW ) AS window_column FROM EXTERNALNETWORKS e JOIN NETWORKS n ON e.NETWORK_ID = n.ID JOIN NETWORKRBACS r ON n.ID = r.OBJECT_ID WHERE e.IS_DEFAULT = 0 ) SELECT n.TENANT_ID, COUNT(DISTINCT n.ID) AS total_nondefault_external_networks, CASE WHEN COUNT(DISTINCT r.ID) > 0 THEN 'Yes' ELSE 'No' END AS has_any_rbac FROM EXTERNALNETWORKS e JOIN NETWORKS n ON e.NETWORK_ID = n.ID LEFT JOIN NETWORKRBACS r ON n.ID = r.OBJECT_ID JOIN inner_cte ic ON ic.NAME = n.NAME WHERE e.IS_DEFAULT = 0 GROUP BY n.TENANT_ID ORDER BY total_nondefault_external_networks DESC LIMIT 10;

question: How many distinct tenants have DOWN ports with IP allocations, and among those tenants how many are categorized as HIGH_USER based on having at least 50% more DOWN ports than the average across tenants with DOWN ports? Do not return any rounded answers. Categorize each tenant as 'HIGH_USER' (at least 50% more than average), 'LOW_USER' (at least 50% less than average), or 'AVERAGE_USER'.
sql: WITH down_port_ip_details AS ( WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT p.ID AS port_id, p.TENANT_ID AS tenant_id, b.HOST AS host, b.VIF_TYPE AS vif_type, ia.IP_ADDRESS AS ip_address, ROW_NUMBER() OVER ( ORDER BY ia.IP_ADDRESS ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND 1 FOLLOWING ) AS window_column FROM ML2_PORT_BINDINGS b JOIN PORTS p ON b.PORT_ID = p.ID JOIN IPALLOCATIONS ia ON p.ID = ia.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' ), HostCounts AS ( SELECT host, COUNT(DISTINCT ip_address) AS down_allocated_ips FROM inner_cte GROUP BY host ), AverageHostCounts AS ( SELECT AVG(down_allocated_ips) AS avg_down_allocated_ips FROM HostCounts ) SELECT i.port_id, i.tenant_id, i.host, i.vif_type, i.ip_address, i.window_column, hc.down_allocated_ips, (hc.down_allocated_ips - ahc.avg_down_allocated_ips) AS deviation_from_avg FROM inner_cte i JOIN HostCounts hc ON i.host = hc.host CROSS JOIN AverageHostCounts ahc ), tenant_down_port_benchmark AS ( WITH inner_cte AS (SELECT p.NAME, p.NETWORK_ID, p.MAC_ADDRESS, p.ADMIN_STATE_UP, p.STATUS, p.DEVICE_OWNER, s.SECURITY_GROUP_ID, MIN(p.ADMIN_STATE_UP) OVER ( ORDER BY p.ID ROWS BETWEEN 3 PRECEDING AND 1 FOLLOWING ) AS window_column FROM PORTS AS p JOIN SECURITYGROUPPORTBINDINGS AS s ON p.ID = s.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN'), TenantDownPorts AS (SELECT p.tenant_id, COUNT(p.id) AS total_down_ports FROM PORTS AS p JOIN inner_cte AS ic ON ic.MAC_ADDRESS = p.MAC_ADDRESS GROUP BY p.tenant_id), AverageDownPorts AS (SELECT AVG(total_down_ports) AS avg_down_ports FROM TenantDownPorts) SELECT tdp.tenant_id, tdp.total_down_ports, adp.avg_down_ports AS benchmark, CASE WHEN tdp.total_down_ports > adp.avg_down_ports * 1.5 THEN 'HIGH_USER' WHEN tdp.total_down_ports < adp.avg_down_ports * 0.5 THEN 'LOW_USER' ELSE 'AVERAGE_USER' END AS user_category FROM TenantDownPorts AS tdp CROSS JOIN AverageDownPorts AS adp ) SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT dpipd.tenant_id) AS tenants_with_down_port_ip_allocations, COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN tdpb.user_category = 'HIGH_USER' THEN tdpb.tenant_id END) AS high_user_tenants_among_down_port_tenants FROM down_port_ip_details dpipd JOIN tenant_down_port_benchmark tdpb ON dpipd.tenant_id = tdpb.tenant_id;

For each tenant that has ports in DOWN status, list the tenant ID, the number of DOWN ports, the average number of DOWN ports across all such tenants as a benchmark, and categorize each tenant as 'HIGH_USER' (at least 50% more than average), 'LOW_USER' (at least 50% less than average), or 'AVERAGE_USER'.
sub_sqls: SELECT p.ID AS port_id, p.TENANT_ID AS tenant_id, b.HOST AS host, b.VIF_TYPE AS vif_type, ia.IP_ADDRESS AS ip_address, ROW_NUMBER() OVER ( ORDER BY ia.IP_ADDRESS ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND 1 FOLLOWING ) AS window_column FROM ML2_PORT_BINDINGS b JOIN PORTS p ON b.PORT_ID = p.ID JOIN IPALLOCATIONS ia ON p.ID = ia.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN';

SELECT p.NAME, p.NETWORK_ID, p.MAC_ADDRESS, p.ADMIN_STATE_UP, p.STATUS, p.DEVICE_OWNER, s.SECURITY_GROUP_ID, MIN(p.ADMIN_STATE_UP) OVER ( ORDER BY p.ID ROWS BETWEEN 3 PRECEDING AND 1 FOLLOWING ) AS window_column FROM PORTS AS p JOIN SECURITYGROUPPORTBINDINGS AS s ON p.ID = s.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN';

WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT p.ID AS port_id, p.TENANT_ID AS tenant_id, b.HOST AS host, b.VIF_TYPE AS vif_type, ia.IP_ADDRESS AS ip_address, ROW_NUMBER() OVER ( ORDER BY ia.IP_ADDRESS ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND 1 FOLLOWING ) AS window_column FROM ML2_PORT_BINDINGS b JOIN PORTS p ON b.PORT_ID = p.ID JOIN IPALLOCATIONS ia ON p.ID = ia.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' ), HostCounts AS ( SELECT host, COUNT(DISTINCT ip_address) AS down_allocated_ips FROM inner_cte GROUP BY host ), AverageHostCounts AS ( SELECT AVG(down_allocated_ips) AS avg_down_allocated_ips FROM HostCounts ) SELECT i.port_id, i.tenant_id, i.host, i.vif_type, i.ip_address, i.window_column, hc.down_allocated_ips, (hc.down_allocated_ips - ahc.avg_down_allocated_ips) AS deviation_from_avg FROM inner_cte i JOIN HostCounts hc ON i.host = hc.host CROSS JOIN AverageHostCounts ahc;

WITH inner_cte AS (SELECT p.NAME, p.NETWORK_ID, p.MAC_ADDRESS, p.ADMIN_STATE_UP, p.STATUS, p.DEVICE_OWNER, s.SECURITY_GROUP_ID, MIN(p.ADMIN_STATE_UP) OVER ( ORDER BY p.ID ROWS BETWEEN 3 PRECEDING AND 1 FOLLOWING ) AS window_column FROM PORTS AS p JOIN SECURITYGROUPPORTBINDINGS AS s ON p.ID = s.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN'), TenantDownPorts AS (SELECT p.tenant_id, COUNT(p.id) AS total_down_ports FROM PORTS AS p JOIN inner_cte AS ic ON ic.MAC_ADDRESS = p.MAC_ADDRESS GROUP BY p.tenant_id), AverageDownPorts AS (SELECT AVG(total_down_ports) AS avg_down_ports FROM TenantDownPorts) SELECT tdp.tenant_id, tdp.total_down_ports, adp.avg_down_ports AS benchmark, CASE WHEN tdp.total_down_ports > adp.avg_down_ports * 1.5 THEN 'HIGH_USER' WHEN tdp.total_down_ports < adp.avg_down_ports * 0.5 THEN 'LOW_USER' ELSE 'AVERAGE_USER' END AS user_category FROM TenantDownPorts AS tdp CROSS JOIN AverageDownPorts AS adp;

question: For each RBAC action, show the action (with repeated action labels suppressed and including a grand TOTAL row), the average/variance/standard deviation (using STDDEV only and never STDDEV_POP) of subnet IP version considering only IPv4 subnets on networks referenced by RBAC entries, the total number of distinct subnets involved, and—when the action is specifically 'access_as_shared'—also show the variance of subnet IP version across IPv4 vs IPv6 plus the average of that variance across all 'access_as_shared' RBAC actions. Do not return any rounded answers.
sql: WITH q1 AS ( WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT n.ACTION, AVG(s.IP_VERSION) AS avg_ip_version, VARIANCE(s.IP_VERSION) AS ip_version_variance, STDDEV(s.IP_VERSION) AS ip_version_stddev FROM NETWORKRBACS AS n JOIN SUBNETS AS s ON n.OBJECT_ID = s.NETWORK_ID WHERE s.IP_VERSION = 4 GROUP BY n.ACTION ORDER BY ip_version_variance DESC ) SELECT CASE WHEN LAG(action) OVER (ORDER BY action_sort, action) = action THEN NULL ELSE action END AS action, avg_ip_version, ip_version_variance, ip_version_stddev, distinct_subnets FROM ( SELECT CASE WHEN GROUPING(i.action) = 1 THEN 'zzz' ELSE i.action END AS action_sort, CASE WHEN GROUPING(i.action) = 1 THEN 'TOTAL' ELSE i.action END AS action, MAX(i.avg_ip_version) AS avg_ip_version, MAX(i.ip_version_variance) AS ip_version_variance, MAX(i.ip_version_stddev) AS ip_version_stddev, COUNT(DISTINCT s.id) AS distinct_subnets FROM inner_cte i JOIN NETWORKRBACS n ON n.action = i.action JOIN SUBNETS s ON s.network_id = n.object_id WHERE s.ip_version = 4 GROUP BY i.action WITH ROLLUP ) AS tbltmp ORDER BY action_sort, action ), q2 AS ( WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT n.ACTION, VARIANCE(s.IP_VERSION) AS ip_version_variance FROM NETWORKRBACS AS n JOIN SUBNETS AS s ON n.OBJECT_ID = s.NETWORK_ID WHERE n.ACTION = 'access_as_shared' GROUP BY n.ACTION ORDER BY ip_version_variance DESC ) SELECT inner_cte.ACTION, inner_cte.ip_version_variance, avg_stats.avg_ip_version_variance FROM inner_cte JOIN ( SELECT AVG(ip_version_variance) AS avg_ip_version_variance FROM inner_cte ) AS avg_stats ) SELECT q1.action, q1.avg_ip_version, q1.ip_version_variance AS ipv4_only_ip_version_variance, q1.ip_version_stddev, q1.distinct_subnets, q2.ip_version_variance AS access_as_shared_ip_version_variance_ipv4_vs_ipv6, q2.avg_ip_version_variance AS avg_access_as_shared_ip_version_variance FROM q1 LEFT JOIN q2 ON q1.action = q2.action ORDER BY CASE WHEN q1.action = 'TOTAL' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END, q1.action;
sub_questions: For each RBAC action, show the average, variance, and standard deviation of the subnet IP version (4 or 6) across subnets whose network is referenced by an RBAC entry.

For each RBAC action, show the action name and the variance of the subnet IP version (IPv4 vs IPv6) across the subnets on the network that the RBAC entry refers to, considering only RBAC entries with action = 'access_as_shared'.

For each RBAC action, list the action, the average/variance/standard deviation of the subnet IP version (considering only IPv4 subnets) for subnets whose network is referenced by an RBAC entry, and the total number of distinct subnets involved. Do not repeat the action if it is the same as the previous row, and include a grand total row across all actions.

For each RBAC action (considering only entries with action = 'access_as_shared'), show the action name, the variance of the subnet IP version (IPv4 vs IPv6) across the subnets on the referenced network, along with the average of that IP-version variance across all such RBAC actions.
sub_sqls: SELECT n.ACTION, AVG(s.IP_VERSION) AS avg_ip_version, VARIANCE(s.IP_VERSION) AS ip_version_variance, STDDEV(s.IP_VERSION) AS ip_version_stddev FROM NETWORKRBACS AS n JOIN SUBNETS AS s ON n.OBJECT_ID = s.NETWORK_ID WHERE s.IP_VERSION = 4 GROUP BY n.ACTION ORDER BY ip_version_variance DESC;

SELECT n.ACTION, VARIANCE(s.IP_VERSION) AS ip_version_variance FROM NETWORKRBACS AS n JOIN SUBNETS AS s ON n.OBJECT_ID = s.NETWORK_ID WHERE n.ACTION = 'access_as_shared' GROUP BY n.ACTION ORDER BY ip_version_variance DESC;

WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT n.ACTION, AVG(s.IP_VERSION) AS avg_ip_version, VARIANCE(s.IP_VERSION) AS ip_version_variance, STDDEV(s.IP_VERSION) AS ip_version_stddev FROM NETWORKRBACS AS n JOIN SUBNETS AS s ON n.OBJECT_ID = s.NETWORK_ID WHERE s.IP_VERSION = 4 GROUP BY n.ACTION ORDER BY ip_version_variance DESC ) SELECT CASE WHEN LAG(action) OVER (ORDER BY action_sort, action) = action THEN NULL ELSE action END AS action, avg_ip_version, ip_version_variance, ip_version_stddev, distinct_subnets FROM ( SELECT CASE WHEN GROUPING(i.action) = 1 THEN 'zzz' ELSE i.action END AS action_sort, CASE WHEN GROUPING(i.action) = 1 THEN 'TOTAL' ELSE i.action END AS action, MAX(i.avg_ip_version) AS avg_ip_version, MAX(i.ip_version_variance) AS ip_version_variance, MAX(i.ip_version_stddev) AS ip_version_stddev, COUNT(DISTINCT s.id) AS distinct_subnets FROM inner_cte i JOIN NETWORKRBACS n ON n.action = i.action JOIN SUBNETS s ON s.network_id = n.object_id WHERE s.ip_version = 4 GROUP BY i.action WITH ROLLUP ) AS tbltmp ORDER BY action_sort, action;

WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT n.ACTION, VARIANCE(s.IP_VERSION) AS ip_version_variance FROM NETWORKRBACS AS n JOIN SUBNETS AS s ON n.OBJECT_ID = s.NETWORK_ID WHERE n.ACTION = 'access_as_shared' GROUP BY n.ACTION ORDER BY ip_version_variance DESC ) SELECT inner_cte.ACTION, inner_cte.ip_version_variance, avg_stats.avg_ip_version_variance FROM inner_cte JOIN ( SELECT AVG(ip_version_variance) AS avg_ip_version_variance FROM inner_cte ) AS avg_stats;

question: Show port status coefficient-of-variation (CoV) results for ports that have both a security group port binding and a port security binding by combining (1) the top 10 statuses with the highest CoV including whether any of those ports have floating IPs allocated, and (2) all statuses with their CoV plus the overall average CoV across statuses, labeling each row with the reason/source of inclusion. Do not return any rounded answers.
sql: WITH Top10PortStatusCoV AS ( WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT p.status, STDDEV(p.standard_attr_id) / NULLIF(AVG(p.standard_attr_id), 0) AS coefficient_of_variation FROM securitygroupportbindings AS sgpb JOIN ports AS p ON sgpb.port_id = p.id JOIN portsecuritybindings AS psb ON p.id = psb.port_id GROUP BY p.status HAVING AVG(p.standard_attr_id) > 0 ORDER BY coefficient_of_variation DESC ) SELECT i.status, i.coefficient_of_variation, CASE WHEN COUNT(DISTINCT f.id) > 0 THEN 'Yes' ELSE 'No' END AS has_floating_ips FROM inner_cte i JOIN ports p ON p.status = i.status JOIN securitygroupportbindings sgpb ON sgpb.port_id = p.id JOIN portsecuritybindings psb ON psb.port_id = p.id LEFT JOIN floatingips f ON f.fixed_port_id = p.id GROUP BY i.status, i.coefficient_of_variation ORDER BY i.coefficient_of_variation DESC LIMIT 10 ), AllStatusCoVWithAvg AS ( WITH inner_cte AS (SELECT p.status, STDDEV(p.standard_attr_id) / NULLIF(AVG(p.standard_attr_id), 0) AS coefficient_of_variation FROM securitygroupportbindings AS sgpb JOIN ports AS p ON sgpb.port_id = p.id JOIN portsecuritybindings AS psb ON p.id = psb.port_id GROUP BY p.status HAVING AVG(p.standard_attr_id) > 0 ORDER BY coefficient_of_variation DESC) SELECT inner_cte.status, inner_cte.coefficient_of_variation, avg_cov.avg_coefficient_of_variation FROM inner_cte JOIN ( SELECT AVG(coefficient_of_variation) AS avg_coefficient_of_variation FROM inner_cte ) AS avg_cov ON 1 = 1 ORDER BY inner_cte.coefficient_of_variation DESC ), CombinedStatusCoV AS ( SELECT t.status, t.coefficient_of_variation, a.avg_coefficient_of_variation, t.has_floating_ips, 'Top 10 CoV Statuses (with Floating IP flag)' AS reason FROM Top10PortStatusCoV t JOIN AllStatusCoVWithAvg a ON a.status = t.status UNION ALL SELECT a.status, a.coefficient_of_variation, a.avg_coefficient_of_variation, NULL AS has_floating_ips, 'All Statuses (with overall average CoV)' AS reason FROM AllStatusCoVWithAvg a ) SELECT status, coefficient_of_variation, avg_coefficient_of_variation, has_floating_ips, reason FROM CombinedStatusCoV ORDER BY reason, coefficient_of_variation DESC, status;
