sub_sqls: SELECT p.status, STDDEV(p.standard_attr_id) / NULLIF(AVG(p.standard_attr_id), 0) AS coefficient_of_variation FROM securitygroupportbindings AS sgpb JOIN ports AS p ON sgpb.port_id = p.id JOIN portsecuritybindings AS psb ON p.id = psb.port_id GROUP BY p.status HAVING AVG(p.standard_attr_id) > 0 ORDER BY coefficient_of_variation DESC;

SELECT p.status, STDDEV(p.standard_attr_id) / NULLIF(AVG(p.standard_attr_id), 0) AS coefficient_of_variation FROM securitygroupportbindings AS sgpb JOIN ports AS p ON sgpb.port_id = p.id JOIN portsecuritybindings AS psb ON p.id = psb.port_id GROUP BY p.status HAVING AVG(p.standard_attr_id) > 0 ORDER BY coefficient_of_variation DESC;

WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT p.status, STDDEV(p.standard_attr_id) / NULLIF(AVG(p.standard_attr_id), 0) AS coefficient_of_variation FROM securitygroupportbindings AS sgpb JOIN ports AS p ON sgpb.port_id = p.id JOIN portsecuritybindings AS psb ON p.id = psb.port_id GROUP BY p.status HAVING AVG(p.standard_attr_id) > 0 ORDER BY coefficient_of_variation DESC ) SELECT i.status, i.coefficient_of_variation, CASE WHEN COUNT(DISTINCT f.id) > 0 THEN 'Yes' ELSE 'No' END AS has_floating_ips FROM inner_cte i JOIN ports p ON p.status = i.status JOIN securitygroupportbindings sgpb ON sgpb.port_id = p.id JOIN portsecuritybindings psb ON psb.port_id = p.id LEFT JOIN floatingips f ON f.fixed_port_id = p.id GROUP BY i.status, i.coefficient_of_variation ORDER BY i.coefficient_of_variation DESC LIMIT 10;

WITH inner_cte AS (SELECT p.status, STDDEV(p.standard_attr_id) / NULLIF(AVG(p.standard_attr_id), 0) AS coefficient_of_variation FROM securitygroupportbindings AS sgpb JOIN ports AS p ON sgpb.port_id = p.id JOIN portsecuritybindings AS psb ON p.id = psb.port_id GROUP BY p.status HAVING AVG(p.standard_attr_id) > 0 ORDER BY coefficient_of_variation DESC) SELECT inner_cte.status, inner_cte.coefficient_of_variation, avg_cov.avg_coefficient_of_variation FROM inner_cte JOIN ( SELECT AVG(coefficient_of_variation) AS avg_coefficient_of_variation FROM inner_cte ) AS avg_cov ON 1 = 1 ORDER BY inner_cte.coefficient_of_variation DESC;

question: For the top 10 tenants with ports in DOWN status, show each tenant ID, the total number of distinct DOWN ports, whether any of those DOWN ports have at least one IP allocation, the total number of DOWN ports with port security enabled, and the average DOWN-and-port-secure port count across all tenants. Do not return any rounded answers.
sql: WITH down_ports_ipallocs AS ( WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT p.ID AS port_id, p.TENANT_ID AS tenant_id, b.HOST AS host, b.VIF_TYPE AS vif_type, ia.IP_ADDRESS AS ip_address, ROW_NUMBER() OVER ( ORDER BY ia.IP_ADDRESS ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND 1 FOLLOWING ) AS window_column FROM ML2_PORT_BINDINGS b JOIN PORTS p ON b.PORT_ID = p.ID JOIN IPALLOCATIONS ia ON p.ID = ia.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' ) SELECT inner_cte.tenant_id, COUNT(DISTINCT inner_cte.port_id) AS total_down_ports, CASE WHEN COUNT(DISTINCT inner_cte.ip_address) > 0 THEN 'Yes' ELSE 'No' END AS has_ip_allocations FROM inner_cte GROUP BY inner_cte.tenant_id ORDER BY total_down_ports DESC LIMIT 10 ), down_secure_ports_by_tenant AS ( WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT COUNT(*) AS down_ports_with_port_security_enabled FROM PORTS p JOIN PORTSECURITYBINDINGS psb ON p.ID = psb.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' AND psb.PORT_SECURITY_ENABLED = 1 ) SELECT p.tenant_id AS ports_tenant_id, COUNT(p.id) AS total_down_ports_with_port_security_enabled, avg_counts.avg_down_secure_port_count FROM ports p JOIN portsecuritybindings psb ON p.id = psb.port_id JOIN ( SELECT AVG(port_count) AS avg_down_secure_port_count FROM ( SELECT p2.tenant_id, COUNT(p2.id) AS port_count FROM ports p2 JOIN portsecuritybindings psb2 ON p2.id = psb2.port_id WHERE p2.status = 'DOWN' AND psb2.port_security_enabled = 1 GROUP BY p2.tenant_id ) AS sub ) AS avg_counts ON 1 = 1 CROSS JOIN inner_cte WHERE p.status = 'DOWN' AND psb.port_security_enabled = 1 GROUP BY p.tenant_id, avg_counts.avg_down_secure_port_count ) SELECT dpi.tenant_id, dpi.total_down_ports, dpi.has_ip_allocations, dsp.total_down_ports_with_port_security_enabled, dsp.avg_down_secure_port_count FROM down_ports_ipallocs dpi JOIN down_secure_ports_by_tenant dsp ON dsp.ports_tenant_id = dpi.tenant_id ORDER BY dpi.total_down_ports DESC;
sub_questions: For ports whose status is DOWN, list the port ID, tenant ID, host, VIF type, and allocated IP address, and assign row numbers ordered by IP address using a window frame of 2 preceding rows and 1 following row.
How many ports are in status 'DOWN' and have port security enabled (as indicated by the port security binding)?

Among tenants that have ports in DOWN status, show each tenant ID, the total number of distinct DOWN ports, and whether any of those DOWN ports have at least one IP allocation. Return only the top 10 tenants by total DOWN ports.

For each tenant, list the tenant ID, the total number of ports that are in status 'DOWN' and have port security enabled (as indicated by the port security binding), along with the average of that down-and-secure port count across all tenants.
sub_sqls: SELECT p.ID AS port_id, p.TENANT_ID AS tenant_id, b.HOST AS host, b.VIF_TYPE AS vif_type, ia.IP_ADDRESS AS ip_address, ROW_NUMBER() OVER ( ORDER BY ia.IP_ADDRESS ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND 1 FOLLOWING ) AS window_column FROM ML2_PORT_BINDINGS b JOIN PORTS p ON b.PORT_ID = p.ID JOIN IPALLOCATIONS ia ON p.ID = ia.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN';
SELECT COUNT(*) AS down_ports_with_port_security_enabled FROM PORTS p JOIN PORTSECURITYBINDINGS psb ON p.ID = psb.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' AND psb.PORT_SECURITY_ENABLED = 1;

WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT p.ID AS port_id, p.TENANT_ID AS tenant_id, b.HOST AS host, b.VIF_TYPE AS vif_type, ia.IP_ADDRESS AS ip_address, ROW_NUMBER() OVER ( ORDER BY ia.IP_ADDRESS ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND 1 FOLLOWING ) AS window_column FROM ML2_PORT_BINDINGS b JOIN PORTS p ON b.PORT_ID = p.ID JOIN IPALLOCATIONS ia ON p.ID = ia.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' ) SELECT inner_cte.tenant_id, COUNT(DISTINCT inner_cte.port_id) AS total_down_ports, CASE WHEN COUNT(DISTINCT inner_cte.ip_address) > 0 THEN 'Yes' ELSE 'No' END AS has_ip_allocations FROM inner_cte GROUP BY inner_cte.tenant_id ORDER BY total_down_ports DESC LIMIT 10;

WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT COUNT(*) AS down_ports_with_port_security_enabled FROM PORTS p JOIN PORTSECURITYBINDINGS psb ON p.ID = psb.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' AND psb.PORT_SECURITY_ENABLED = 1 ) SELECT p.tenant_id AS ports_tenant_id, COUNT(p.id) AS total_down_ports_with_port_security_enabled, avg_counts.avg_down_secure_port_count FROM ports p JOIN portsecuritybindings psb ON p.id = psb.port_id JOIN ( SELECT AVG(port_count) AS avg_down_secure_port_count FROM ( SELECT p2.tenant_id, COUNT(p2.id) AS port_count FROM ports p2 JOIN portsecuritybindings psb2 ON p2.id = psb2.port_id WHERE p2.status = 'DOWN' AND psb2.port_security_enabled = 1 GROUP BY p2.tenant_id ) AS sub ) AS avg_counts ON 1 = 1 CROSS JOIN inner_cte WHERE p.status = 'DOWN' AND psb.port_security_enabled = 1 GROUP BY p.tenant_id, avg_counts.avg_down_secure_port_count;

question: For ACTIVE networks that are also in the top 3 networks by subnet count among RBAC entries with action = 'access_as_shared', return the network ID, its subnet count and benchmark/category within the top-3 shared set, along with its total subnets and the overall ACTIVE-network benchmark (average + standard deviation (using STDDEV only and never STDDEV_POP)) and whether it is above that 1-standard-deviation threshold. Do not return any rounded answers. Categorize each network as 'ABOVE_BENCHMARK' (at least 50% more than the benchmark), 'BELOW_BENCHMARK' (at least 50% less than the benchmark), or 'NEAR_BENCHMARK'.
sql: WITH q1 AS ( WITH inner_cte AS (SELECT n.id AS network_id, SUM(1) AS total_subnets FROM NETWORKS AS n JOIN NETWORKRBACS AS r ON n.id = r.object_id JOIN SUBNETS AS s ON r.object_id = s.network_id WHERE n.status = 'ACTIVE' GROUP BY n.id HAVING SUM(1) > ( SELECT AVG(subnet_cnt) + STDDEV(subnet_cnt) FROM ( SELECT n2.id AS network_id, SUM(1) AS subnet_cnt FROM NETWORKS AS n2 JOIN NETWORKRBACS AS r2 ON n2.id = r2.object_id JOIN SUBNETS AS s2 ON r2.object_id = s2.network_id WHERE n2.status = 'ACTIVE' GROUP BY n2.id ) AS per_network )), benchmark_cte AS ( SELECT AVG(subnet_cnt) + STDDEV(subnet_cnt) AS benchmark_threshold FROM ( SELECT n2.id AS network_id, SUM(1) AS subnet_cnt FROM NETWORKS AS n2 JOIN NETWORKRBACS AS r2 ON n2.id = r2.object_id JOIN SUBNETS AS s2 ON r2.object_id = s2.network_id WHERE n2.status = 'ACTIVE' GROUP BY n2.id ) AS per_network ) SELECT i.network_id, i.total_subnets, b.benchmark_threshold AS benchmark, CASE WHEN i.total_subnets > b.benchmark_threshold THEN 'ABOVE_1STD' ELSE 'NOT_ABOVE_1STD' END AS subnet_usage_category FROM inner_cte i CROSS JOIN benchmark_cte b ), q2 AS ( WITH inner_cte AS (SELECT n.OBJECT_ID AS network_id, COUNT(*) AS subnet_count FROM NETWORKRBACS AS n JOIN SUBNETS AS s ON n.OBJECT_ID = s.NETWORK_ID WHERE n.ACTION = 'access_as_shared' GROUP BY n.OBJECT_ID ORDER BY COUNT(*) DESC LIMIT 3), AverageSubnets AS ( SELECT AVG(subnet_count) AS avg_subnet_count FROM inner_cte ) SELECT ic.network_id, ic.subnet_count, a.avg_subnet_count AS benchmark, CASE WHEN ic.subnet_count > a.avg_subnet_count * 1.5 THEN 'ABOVE_BENCHMARK' WHEN ic.subnet_count < a.avg_subnet_count * 0.5 THEN 'BELOW_BENCHMARK' ELSE 'NEAR_BENCHMARK' END AS subnet_category FROM inner_cte ic CROSS JOIN AverageSubnets a ) SELECT q2.network_id, q2.subnet_count, q2.benchmark AS top3_shared_benchmark, q2.subnet_category, q1.total_subnets AS active_total_subnets, q1.benchmark AS active_avg_plus_stddev_benchmark, q1.subnet_usage_category FROM q2 JOIN q1 ON q2.network_id = q1.network_id JOIN NETWORKS n ON n.id = q2.network_id WHERE n.status = 'ACTIVE' ORDER BY q2.subnet_count DESC;
sub_questions: For each network, return the network ID and the total number of subnets on that network, considering only ACTIVE networks, and only keeping networks whose total subnet count is more than one standard deviation above the mean subnet count across all ACTIVE networks.

List the top 3 networks that have the most subnets, considering only RBAC entries where the action is 'access_as_shared'. For each of these networks, return the network object ID and the number of subnets on that network.

For each ACTIVE network that has a subnet count more than one standard deviation above the mean subnet count across all ACTIVE networks, return the network ID, its total number of subnets, the overall benchmark threshold (average + standard deviation), and label the network as 'ABOVE_1STD' or 'NOT_ABOVE_1STD'.

For the top 3 networks that have the most subnets (considering only RBAC entries where the action is 'access_as_shared'), return the network object ID, the subnet count, the average subnet count across these top networks as a benchmark, and categorize each network as 'ABOVE_BENCHMARK' (at least 50% more than the benchmark), 'BELOW_BENCHMARK' (at least 50% less than the benchmark), or 'NEAR_BENCHMARK'.
sub_sqls: SELECT n.id AS network_id, SUM(1) AS total_subnets FROM NETWORKS AS n JOIN NETWORKRBACS AS r ON n.id = r.object_id JOIN SUBNETS AS s ON r.object_id = s.network_id WHERE n.status = 'ACTIVE' GROUP BY n.id HAVING SUM(1) > ( SELECT AVG(subnet_cnt) + STDDEV(subnet_cnt) FROM ( SELECT n2.id AS network_id, SUM(1) AS subnet_cnt FROM NETWORKS AS n2 JOIN NETWORKRBACS AS r2 ON n2.id = r2.object_id JOIN SUBNETS AS s2 ON r2.object_id = s2.network_id WHERE n2.status = 'ACTIVE' GROUP BY n2.id ) AS per_network );

SELECT n.OBJECT_ID AS network_id, COUNT(*) AS subnet_count FROM NETWORKRBACS AS n JOIN SUBNETS AS s ON n.OBJECT_ID = s.NETWORK_ID WHERE n.ACTION = 'access_as_shared' GROUP BY n.OBJECT_ID ORDER BY COUNT(*) DESC LIMIT 3;

WITH inner_cte AS (SELECT n.id AS network_id, SUM(1) AS total_subnets FROM NETWORKS AS n JOIN NETWORKRBACS AS r ON n.id = r.object_id JOIN SUBNETS AS s ON r.object_id = s.network_id WHERE n.status = 'ACTIVE' GROUP BY n.id HAVING SUM(1) > ( SELECT AVG(subnet_cnt) + STDDEV(subnet_cnt) FROM ( SELECT n2.id AS network_id, SUM(1) AS subnet_cnt FROM NETWORKS AS n2 JOIN NETWORKRBACS AS r2 ON n2.id = r2.object_id JOIN SUBNETS AS s2 ON r2.object_id = s2.network_id WHERE n2.status = 'ACTIVE' GROUP BY n2.id ) AS per_network )), benchmark_cte AS ( SELECT AVG(subnet_cnt) + STDDEV(subnet_cnt) AS benchmark_threshold FROM ( SELECT n2.id AS network_id, SUM(1) AS subnet_cnt FROM NETWORKS AS n2 JOIN NETWORKRBACS AS r2 ON n2.id = r2.object_id JOIN SUBNETS AS s2 ON r2.object_id = s2.network_id WHERE n2.status = 'ACTIVE' GROUP BY n2.id ) AS per_network ) SELECT i.network_id, i.total_subnets, b.benchmark_threshold AS benchmark, CASE WHEN i.total_subnets > b.benchmark_threshold THEN 'ABOVE_1STD' ELSE 'NOT_ABOVE_1STD' END AS subnet_usage_category FROM inner_cte i CROSS JOIN benchmark_cte b;

WITH inner_cte AS (SELECT n.OBJECT_ID AS network_id, COUNT(*) AS subnet_count FROM NETWORKRBACS AS n JOIN SUBNETS AS s ON n.OBJECT_ID = s.NETWORK_ID WHERE n.ACTION = 'access_as_shared' GROUP BY n.OBJECT_ID ORDER BY COUNT(*) DESC LIMIT 3), AverageSubnets AS ( SELECT AVG(subnet_count) AS avg_subnet_count FROM inner_cte ) SELECT ic.network_id, ic.subnet_count, a.avg_subnet_count AS benchmark, CASE WHEN ic.subnet_count > a.avg_subnet_count * 1.5 THEN 'ABOVE_BENCHMARK' WHEN ic.subnet_count < a.avg_subnet_count * 0.5 THEN 'BELOW_BENCHMARK' ELSE 'NEAR_BENCHMARK' END AS subnet_category FROM inner_cte ic CROSS JOIN AverageSubnets a;

question: For ACTIVE networks, list each network’s name, status, and admin_state_up together with its RBAC action and target tenant, including the number of distinct RBAC target tenants per network and the dense-rank value. Alongside those network RBAC rows, also show the rolled-up port summary (port status, device owner, number of ports, and earliest standard-attribute updated timestamp) considering only ports whose standard attribute resource type is 'ports', including subtotals per port status and a grand total. Do not return any rounded answers.
sql: WITH port_rollup AS ( WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT p.STATUS AS port_status, p.DEVICE_OWNER AS device_owner, COUNT(p.ID) AS port_count, MIN(sa.UPDATED_AT) AS earliest_standard_attr_update FROM PORTS p JOIN STANDARDATTRIBUTES sa ON sa.ID = p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID WHERE sa.RESOURCE_TYPE = 'ports' GROUP BY p.STATUS, p.DEVICE_OWNER ) SELECT CASE WHEN GROUPING(port_status) = 1 THEN 'GRAND TOTAL' ELSE port_status END AS port_status, CASE WHEN GROUPING(device_owner) = 1 AND GROUPING(port_status) = 0 THEN 'SUBTOTAL' ELSE device_owner END AS device_owner, SUM(port_count) AS port_count, MIN(earliest_standard_attr_update) AS earliest_standard_attr_update FROM inner_cte GROUP BY port_status, device_owner WITH ROLLUP ), active_network_rbac AS ( WITH inner_cte AS (SELECT n.name, n.status, n.admin_state_up, r.action, r.target_tenant, DENSE_RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY n.id ORDER BY n.id) AS window_column FROM networksecuritybindings b JOIN networks n ON b.network_id = n.id JOIN networkrbacs r ON n.id = r.object_id WHERE n.status = 'ACTIVE'), rbac_counts AS ( SELECT n.id AS network_id, COUNT(DISTINCT r.target_tenant) AS distinct_target_tenants FROM networksecuritybindings b JOIN networks n ON b.network_id = n.id JOIN networkrbacs r ON n.id = r.object_id WHERE n.status = 'ACTIVE' GROUP BY n.id ) SELECT i.name, i.status, i.admin_state_up, i.action, i.target_tenant, c.distinct_target_tenants, i.window_column FROM inner_cte i JOIN rbac_counts c ON c.network_id = (SELECT n2.id FROM networks n2 WHERE n2.name = i.name AND n2.status = i.status AND n2.admin_state_up = i.admin_state_up LIMIT 1) ) SELECT anr.name AS network_name, anr.status AS network_status, anr.admin_state_up, anr.action AS rbac_action, anr.target_tenant, anr.distinct_target_tenants, anr.window_column, pr.port_status, pr.device_owner, pr.port_count, pr.earliest_standard_attr_update FROM active_network_rbac anr CROSS JOIN port_rollup pr ORDER BY anr.name, anr.action, anr.target_tenant, pr.port_status, pr.device_owner;
sub_questions: For each port status and device owner, considering only ports whose standard attribute resource type is 'ports', return the number of ports and the earliest (minimum) standard attribute updated timestamp.

Show each network’s name, status, and admin_state_up together with the RBAC action and target tenant for that network, plus a dense rank within each network (partitioned by network ID and ordered by network ID). Only include networks that are ACTIVE.

For each port status and device owner, considering only ports whose standard attribute resource type is 'ports', show the port status, device owner, the number of ports, and the earliest standard attribute updated timestamp. Include subtotals per port status and a grand total.

For each ACTIVE network, show the network name, status, and admin_state_up along with the RBAC action and target tenant, and also report how many distinct RBAC target tenants exist per network (computed from the detailed rows), plus a dense rank within each network (partitioned by network ID and ordered by network ID).
sub_sqls: SELECT p.STATUS AS port_status, p.DEVICE_OWNER AS device_owner, COUNT(p.ID) AS port_count, MIN(sa.UPDATED_AT) AS earliest_standard_attr_update FROM PORTS p JOIN STANDARDATTRIBUTES sa ON sa.ID = p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID WHERE sa.RESOURCE_TYPE = 'ports' GROUP BY p.STATUS, p.DEVICE_OWNER;

SELECT n.name, n.status, n.admin_state_up, r.action, r.target_tenant, DENSE_RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY n.id ORDER BY n.id) AS window_column FROM networksecuritybindings b JOIN networks n ON b.network_id = n.id JOIN networkrbacs r ON n.id = r.object_id WHERE n.status = 'ACTIVE'

WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT p.STATUS AS port_status, p.DEVICE_OWNER AS device_owner, COUNT(p.ID) AS port_count, MIN(sa.UPDATED_AT) AS earliest_standard_attr_update FROM PORTS p JOIN STANDARDATTRIBUTES sa ON sa.ID = p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID WHERE sa.RESOURCE_TYPE = 'ports' GROUP BY p.STATUS, p.DEVICE_OWNER ) SELECT CASE WHEN GROUPING(port_status) = 1 THEN 'GRAND TOTAL' ELSE port_status END AS port_status, CASE WHEN GROUPING(device_owner) = 1 AND GROUPING(port_status) = 0 THEN 'SUBTOTAL' ELSE device_owner END AS device_owner, SUM(port_count) AS port_count, MIN(earliest_standard_attr_update) AS earliest_standard_attr_update FROM inner_cte GROUP BY port_status, device_owner WITH ROLLUP;

WITH inner_cte AS (SELECT n.name, n.status, n.admin_state_up, r.action, r.target_tenant, DENSE_RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY n.id ORDER BY n.id) AS window_column FROM networksecuritybindings b JOIN networks n ON b.network_id = n.id JOIN networkrbacs r ON n.id = r.object_id WHERE n.status = 'ACTIVE'), rbac_counts AS ( SELECT n.id AS network_id, COUNT(DISTINCT r.target_tenant) AS distinct_target_tenants FROM networksecuritybindings b JOIN networks n ON b.network_id = n.id JOIN networkrbacs r ON n.id = r.object_id WHERE n.status = 'ACTIVE' GROUP BY n.id ) SELECT i.name, i.status, i.admin_state_up, i.action, i.target_tenant, c.distinct_target_tenants, i.window_column FROM inner_cte i JOIN rbac_counts c ON c.network_id = (SELECT n2.id FROM networks n2 WHERE n2.name = i.name AND n2.status = i.status AND n2.admin_state_up = i.admin_state_up LIMIT 1);

question: For ports whose status is DOWN, list the port ID, tenant ID, host, VIF type, allocated IP address, and the row number ordered by IP address (using a window frame of 2 preceding rows and 1 following row). Also include, for each tenant, the total number of DOWN ports and the average DOWN-port count across all tenants, and additionally attach the DOWN status’s STANDARD_ATTR_ID variance (considering only ports with an IP allocation and a non-null standard attribute ID), the total number of distinct DOWN ports with IP allocations, and whether any of those DOWN ports have a floating IP allocated. Do not return any rounded answers.
sql: WITH q1 AS ( WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT p.STATUS, VARIANCE(p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID) AS standard_attr_id_variance FROM PORTS AS p JOIN IPALLOCATIONS AS ia ON p.ID = ia.PORT_ID WHERE p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID IS NOT NULL GROUP BY p.STATUS ORDER BY standard_attr_id_variance DESC ) SELECT i.STATUS, i.standard_attr_id_variance, COUNT(DISTINCT p2.ID) AS total_ports, CASE WHEN COUNT(DISTINCT f.ID) > 0 THEN 'Yes' ELSE 'No' END AS has_floating_ips FROM inner_cte i JOIN PORTS p2 ON p2.STATUS = i.STATUS JOIN IPALLOCATIONS ia2 ON ia2.PORT_ID = p2.ID LEFT JOIN FLOATINGIPS f ON f.FIXED_PORT_ID = p2.ID WHERE p2.STANDARD_ATTR_ID IS NOT NULL GROUP BY i.STATUS, i.standard_attr_id_variance ORDER BY i.standard_attr_id_variance DESC LIMIT 10 ), q2 AS ( WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT p.ID AS port_id, p.TENANT_ID AS tenant_id, b.HOST AS host, b.VIF_TYPE AS vif_type, ia.IP_ADDRESS AS ip_address, ROW_NUMBER() OVER ( ORDER BY ia.IP_ADDRESS ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND 1 FOLLOWING ) AS window_column FROM ML2_PORT_BINDINGS b JOIN PORTS p ON b.PORT_ID = p.ID JOIN IPALLOCATIONS ia ON p.ID = ia.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' ) SELECT inner_cte.port_id, inner_cte.tenant_id, inner_cte.host, inner_cte.vif_type, inner_cte.ip_address, inner_cte.window_column, tenant_counts.total_down_ports, avg_down.avg_down_port_count FROM inner_cte JOIN ( SELECT tenant_id, COUNT(port_id) AS total_down_ports FROM inner_cte GROUP BY tenant_id ) AS tenant_counts ON inner_cte.tenant_id = tenant_counts.tenant_id JOIN ( SELECT AVG(down_port_count) AS avg_down_port_count FROM ( SELECT COUNT(port_id) AS down_port_count FROM inner_cte GROUP BY tenant_id ) AS sub ) AS avg_down ON 1 = 1 ) SELECT q2.port_id, q2.tenant_id, q2.host, q2.vif_type, q2.ip_address, q2.window_column, q2.total_down_ports, q2.avg_down_port_count, q1.standard_attr_id_variance AS down_status_standard_attr_id_variance, q1.total_ports AS down_status_total_ports_with_ipalloc, q1.has_floating_ips AS down_status_has_any_floating_ips FROM q2 JOIN q1 ON q1.STATUS = 'DOWN';

sub_sqls: SELECT p.STATUS, VARIANCE(p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID) AS standard_attr_id_variance FROM PORTS AS p JOIN IPALLOCATIONS AS ia ON p.ID = ia.PORT_ID WHERE p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID IS NOT NULL GROUP BY p.STATUS ORDER BY standard_attr_id_variance DESC;

SELECT p.ID AS port_id, p.TENANT_ID AS tenant_id, b.HOST AS host, b.VIF_TYPE AS vif_type, ia.IP_ADDRESS AS ip_address, ROW_NUMBER() OVER ( ORDER BY ia.IP_ADDRESS ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND 1 FOLLOWING ) AS window_column FROM ML2_PORT_BINDINGS b JOIN PORTS p ON b.PORT_ID = p.ID JOIN IPALLOCATIONS ia ON p.ID = ia.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN';

WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT p.STATUS, VARIANCE(p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID) AS standard_attr_id_variance FROM PORTS AS p JOIN IPALLOCATIONS AS ia ON p.ID = ia.PORT_ID WHERE p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID IS NOT NULL GROUP BY p.STATUS ORDER BY standard_attr_id_variance DESC ) SELECT i.STATUS, i.standard_attr_id_variance, COUNT(DISTINCT p2.ID) AS total_ports, CASE WHEN COUNT(DISTINCT f.ID) > 0 THEN 'Yes' ELSE 'No' END AS has_floating_ips FROM inner_cte i JOIN PORTS p2 ON p2.STATUS = i.STATUS JOIN IPALLOCATIONS ia2 ON ia2.PORT_ID = p2.ID LEFT JOIN FLOATINGIPS f ON f.FIXED_PORT_ID = p2.ID WHERE p2.STANDARD_ATTR_ID IS NOT NULL GROUP BY i.STATUS, i.standard_attr_id_variance ORDER BY i.standard_attr_id_variance DESC LIMIT 10;

WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT p.ID AS port_id, p.TENANT_ID AS tenant_id, b.HOST AS host, b.VIF_TYPE AS vif_type, ia.IP_ADDRESS AS ip_address, ROW_NUMBER() OVER ( ORDER BY ia.IP_ADDRESS ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND 1 FOLLOWING ) AS window_column FROM ML2_PORT_BINDINGS b JOIN PORTS p ON b.PORT_ID = p.ID JOIN IPALLOCATIONS ia ON p.ID = ia.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' ) SELECT inner_cte.port_id, inner_cte.tenant_id, inner_cte.host, inner_cte.vif_type, inner_cte.ip_address, inner_cte.window_column, tenant_counts.total_down_ports, avg_down.avg_down_port_count FROM inner_cte JOIN ( SELECT tenant_id, COUNT(port_id) AS total_down_ports FROM inner_cte GROUP BY tenant_id ) AS tenant_counts ON inner_cte.tenant_id = tenant_counts.tenant_id JOIN ( SELECT AVG(down_port_count) AS avg_down_port_count FROM ( SELECT COUNT(port_id) AS down_port_count FROM inner_cte GROUP BY tenant_id ) AS sub ) AS avg_down ON 1 = 1;

question: Among IPv4 subnets, for the top 10 subnet names with the largest route-count range, list only those subnets whose DNS nameserver order variance is greater than the overall average DNS order variance across all IPv4 subnets, and show the subnet name, tenant ID, whether DHCP is enabled, the route-count range/variance/standard deviation (using STDDEV only and never STDDEV_POP), and the average and variance of DNS nameserver order values. Do not return any rounded answers.
sql: WITH RouteRangeTop10 AS ( WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT s.NAME AS subnet_name, MAX(route_count) - MIN(route_count) AS route_count_range, VARIANCE(route_count) AS route_count_variance, STDDEV(route_count) AS route_count_stddev FROM SUBNETS AS s JOIN ( SELECT sr.SUBNET_ID, COUNT(*) AS route_count FROM SUBNETROUTES AS sr GROUP BY sr.SUBNET_ID, sr.NEXTHOP ) AS route_stats ON s.ID = route_stats.SUBNET_ID WHERE s.IP_VERSION = 4 GROUP BY s.NAME ORDER BY route_count_range DESC ) SELECT inner_cte.subnet_name, inner_cte.route_count_range, inner_cte.route_count_variance, inner_cte.route_count_stddev, s.tenant_id, CASE WHEN s.enable_dhcp = 1 THEN 'Yes' ELSE 'No' END AS dhcp_enabled FROM inner_cte JOIN subnets s ON s.name = inner_cte.subnet_name WHERE s.ip_version = 4 ORDER BY inner_cte.route_count_range DESC LIMIT 10 ), HighDNSVarianceSubnets AS ( WITH inner_cte AS (SELECT s.NAME AS subnet_name, AVG(d.ORDER) AS avg_dns_order, VARIANCE(d.ORDER) AS dns_order_variance FROM SUBNETS AS s JOIN DNSNAMESERVERS AS d ON s.ID = d.SUBNET_ID WHERE s.IP_VERSION = 4 GROUP BY s.NAME ORDER BY dns_order_variance DESC) SELECT subnet_name, avg_dns_order, dns_order_variance FROM inner_cte WHERE dns_order_variance > (SELECT AVG(dns_order_variance) FROM inner_cte) ORDER BY dns_order_variance DESC ) SELECT rrt.subnet_name, rrt.tenant_id, rrt.dhcp_enabled, rrt.route_count_range, rrt.route_count_variance, rrt.route_count_stddev, hdv.avg_dns_order, hdv.dns_order_variance FROM RouteRangeTop10 rrt JOIN HighDNSVarianceSubnets hdv ON rrt.subnet_name = hdv.subnet_name ORDER BY rrt.route_count_range DESC, hdv.dns_order_variance DESC;
sub_questions: For each subnet name, show the range, variance, and standard deviation of the number of routes per subnet, considering only IPv4 subnets.
For each subnet (by subnet name), calculate the average and variance of the DNS nameserver order values for DNS entries associated with that subnet, considering only IPv4 subnets.

From the top 10 IPv4 subnet names with the largest route-count range, show each subnet name, the route-count range, variance, and standard deviation, along with the tenant ID and whether DHCP is enabled.

For each IPv4 subnet (by subnet name), compute the average and variance of DNS nameserver order values, and then return only those subnets whose DNS order variance is greater than the overall average DNS order variance across all IPv4 subnets.
sub_sqls: SELECT s.NAME AS subnet_name, MAX(route_count) - MIN(route_count) AS route_count_range, VARIANCE(route_count) AS route_count_variance, STDDEV(route_count) AS route_count_stddev FROM SUBNETS AS s JOIN ( SELECT sr.SUBNET_ID, COUNT(*) AS route_count FROM SUBNETROUTES AS sr GROUP BY sr.SUBNET_ID, sr.NEXTHOP ) AS route_stats ON s.ID = route_stats.SUBNET_ID WHERE s.IP_VERSION = 4 GROUP BY s.NAME ORDER BY route_count_range DESC;

SELECT s.NAME AS subnet_name, AVG(d.ORDER) AS avg_dns_order, VARIANCE(d.ORDER) AS dns_order_variance FROM SUBNETS AS s JOIN DNSNAMESERVERS AS d ON s.ID = d.SUBNET_ID WHERE s.IP_VERSION = 4 GROUP BY s.NAME ORDER BY dns_order_variance DESC;

WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT s.NAME AS subnet_name, MAX(route_count) - MIN(route_count) AS route_count_range, VARIANCE(route_count) AS route_count_variance, STDDEV(route_count) AS route_count_stddev FROM SUBNETS AS s JOIN ( SELECT sr.SUBNET_ID, COUNT(*) AS route_count FROM SUBNETROUTES AS sr GROUP BY sr.SUBNET_ID, sr.NEXTHOP ) AS route_stats ON s.ID = route_stats.SUBNET_ID WHERE s.IP_VERSION = 4 GROUP BY s.NAME ORDER BY route_count_range DESC ) SELECT inner_cte.subnet_name, inner_cte.route_count_range, inner_cte.route_count_variance, inner_cte.route_count_stddev, s.tenant_id, CASE WHEN s.enable_dhcp = 1 THEN 'Yes' ELSE 'No' END AS dhcp_enabled FROM inner_cte JOIN subnets s ON s.name = inner_cte.subnet_name WHERE s.ip_version = 4 ORDER BY inner_cte.route_count_range DESC LIMIT 10;

WITH inner_cte AS (SELECT s.NAME AS subnet_name, AVG(d.ORDER) AS avg_dns_order, VARIANCE(d.ORDER) AS dns_order_variance FROM SUBNETS AS s JOIN DNSNAMESERVERS AS d ON s.ID = d.SUBNET_ID WHERE s.IP_VERSION = 4 GROUP BY s.NAME ORDER BY dns_order_variance DESC) SELECT subnet_name, avg_dns_order, dns_order_variance FROM inner_cte WHERE dns_order_variance > (SELECT AVG(dns_order_variance) FROM inner_cte) ORDER BY dns_order_variance DESC;

question: List all ports that either (a) are in DOWN status (showing their port ID, tenant ID, port name, network ID, MAC address, device owner, allocated IP address, row number within each network by port ID, the network’s total DOWN allocated IPs, and that total’s deviation from the average across networks) or (b) are administratively up with port security binding statistics (showing port ID, tenant ID, MAC address, binding count, total enabled count, the average enabled benchmark, and the security category), and include a column indicating whether each row came from the DOWN-port set or the admin-up security set. Do not return any rounded answers. Categorize each port as 'HIGH_SECURITY' (at least 50% above average), 'LOW_SECURITY' (at least 50% below average), or 'AVERAGE_SECURITY'.
sql: WITH DownPorts AS (WITH inner_cte AS (SELECT p.ID AS port_id, p.TENANT_ID AS tenant_id, p.NAME AS port_name, p.NETWORK_ID AS network_id, p.MAC_ADDRESS AS mac_address, p.DEVICE_OWNER AS device_owner, ia.IP_ADDRESS AS ip_address, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY p.NETWORK_ID ORDER BY p.ID) AS window_column FROM PORTS p JOIN IPALLOCATIONS ia ON p.ID = ia.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN'), NetworkDownAllocations AS ( SELECT network_id, COUNT(DISTINCT ip_address) AS down_allocated_ips FROM inner_cte GROUP BY network_id ), AverageNetworkDownAllocations AS ( SELECT AVG(down_allocated_ips) AS avg_down_allocated_ips FROM NetworkDownAllocations ) SELECT i.port_id, i.tenant_id, i.port_name, i.network_id, i.mac_address, i.device_owner, i.ip_address, i.window_column, nda.down_allocated_ips, (nda.down_allocated_ips - anda.avg_down_allocated_ips) AS deviation_from_avg FROM inner_cte i JOIN NetworkDownAllocations nda ON i.network_id = nda.network_id CROSS JOIN AverageNetworkDownAllocations anda), AdminUpPortSecurity AS (WITH inner_cte AS (SELECT p.id AS port_id, p.tenant_id, p.mac_address, COUNT(psb.port_id) AS binding_count, SUM(CASE WHEN psb.port_security_enabled THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS port_security_enabled_total FROM ports p JOIN portsecuritybindings psb ON p.id = psb.port_id WHERE p.admin_state_up = 1 GROUP BY p.id, p.tenant_id, p.mac_address), AverageEnabled AS (SELECT AVG(port_security_enabled_total) AS avg_enabled FROM inner_cte) SELECT i.port_id, i.tenant_id, i.mac_address, i.binding_count, i.port_security_enabled_total, ae.avg_enabled AS benchmark, CASE WHEN i.port_security_enabled_total > ae.avg_enabled * 1.5 THEN 'HIGH_SECURITY' WHEN i.port_security_enabled_total < ae.avg_enabled * 0.5 THEN 'LOW_SECURITY' ELSE 'AVERAGE_SECURITY' END AS security_category FROM inner_cte i CROSS JOIN AverageEnabled ae), CombinedPorts AS ( SELECT dp.port_id, dp.tenant_id, dp.port_name, dp.network_id, dp.mac_address, dp.device_owner, dp.ip_address, dp.window_column, dp.down_allocated_ips, dp.deviation_from_avg, NULL AS binding_count, NULL AS port_security_enabled_total, NULL AS benchmark, NULL AS security_category, 'DOWN_PORT' AS inclusion_reason FROM DownPorts dp UNION ALL SELECT aus.port_id, aus.tenant_id, NULL AS port_name, NULL AS network_id, aus.mac_address, NULL AS device_owner, NULL AS ip_address, NULL AS window_column, NULL AS down_allocated_ips, NULL AS deviation_from_avg, aus.binding_count, aus.port_security_enabled_total, aus.benchmark, aus.security_category, 'ADMIN_UP_SECURITY' AS inclusion_reason FROM AdminUpPortSecurity aus ) SELECT * FROM CombinedPorts ORDER BY tenant_id, port_id;
sub_questions: For ports that are DOWN, list the port ID, tenant ID, port name, network ID, MAC address, device owner, and the allocated IP address, and assign row numbers within each network ordered by port ID.

For each port that is administratively up, list the port ID, tenant ID, MAC address, the number of port security bindings on that port, and the total number of times port security is enabled across those bindings.

For ports that are DOWN, list the port ID, tenant ID, port name, network ID, MAC address, device owner, allocated IP address, and the row number within each network ordered by port ID; additionally, for each network show the total number of DOWN port IP allocations and the deviation of that network’s total from the average total across all networks.

For each administratively up port, list the port ID, tenant ID, MAC address, the number of port security bindings on that port, the total number of times port security is enabled across those bindings, the average enabled count across all administratively up ports as a benchmark, and categorize each port as 'HIGH_SECURITY' (at least 50% above average), 'LOW_SECURITY' (at least 50% below average), or 'AVERAGE_SECURITY'.
sub_sqls: SELECT p.ID AS port_id, p.TENANT_ID AS tenant_id, p.NAME AS port_name, p.NETWORK_ID AS network_id, p.MAC_ADDRESS AS mac_address, p.DEVICE_OWNER AS device_owner, ia.IP_ADDRESS AS ip_address, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY p.NETWORK_ID ORDER BY p.ID) AS window_column FROM PORTS p JOIN IPALLOCATIONS ia ON p.ID = ia.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN';

SELECT p.id AS port_id, p.tenant_id, p.mac_address, COUNT(psb.port_id) AS binding_count, SUM(CASE WHEN psb.port_security_enabled THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS port_security_enabled_total FROM ports p JOIN portsecuritybindings psb ON p.id = psb.port_id WHERE p.admin_state_up = 1 GROUP BY p.id, p.tenant_id, p.mac_address;

WITH inner_cte AS (SELECT p.ID AS port_id, p.TENANT_ID AS tenant_id, p.NAME AS port_name, p.NETWORK_ID AS network_id, p.MAC_ADDRESS AS mac_address, p.DEVICE_OWNER AS device_owner, ia.IP_ADDRESS AS ip_address, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY p.NETWORK_ID ORDER BY p.ID) AS window_column FROM PORTS p JOIN IPALLOCATIONS ia ON p.ID = ia.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN'), NetworkDownAllocations AS ( SELECT network_id, COUNT(DISTINCT ip_address) AS down_allocated_ips FROM inner_cte GROUP BY network_id ), AverageNetworkDownAllocations AS ( SELECT AVG(down_allocated_ips) AS avg_down_allocated_ips FROM NetworkDownAllocations ) SELECT i.port_id, i.tenant_id, i.port_name, i.network_id, i.mac_address, i.device_owner, i.ip_address, i.window_column, nda.down_allocated_ips, (nda.down_allocated_ips - anda.avg_down_allocated_ips) AS deviation_from_avg FROM inner_cte i JOIN NetworkDownAllocations nda ON i.network_id = nda.network_id CROSS JOIN AverageNetworkDownAllocations anda;

WITH inner_cte AS (SELECT p.id AS port_id, p.tenant_id, p.mac_address, COUNT(psb.port_id) AS binding_count, SUM(CASE WHEN psb.port_security_enabled THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS port_security_enabled_total FROM ports p JOIN portsecuritybindings psb ON p.id = psb.port_id WHERE p.admin_state_up = 1 GROUP BY p.id, p.tenant_id, p.mac_address), AverageEnabled AS (SELECT AVG(port_security_enabled_total) AS avg_enabled FROM inner_cte) SELECT i.port_id, i.tenant_id, i.mac_address, i.binding_count, i.port_security_enabled_total, ae.avg_enabled AS benchmark, CASE WHEN i.port_security_enabled_total > ae.avg_enabled * 1.5 THEN 'HIGH_SECURITY' WHEN i.port_security_enabled_total < ae.avg_enabled * 0.5 THEN 'LOW_SECURITY' ELSE 'AVERAGE_SECURITY' END AS security_category FROM inner_cte i CROSS JOIN AverageEnabled ae;

question: List the network ID for all networks that either (1) are ACTIVE and have a subnet total more than one standard deviation (using STDDEV only and never STDDEV_POP) above the mean across ACTIVE networks, or (2) are among the top 3 networks by subnet count considering only RBAC entries with action = 'access_as_shared'. For each returned network, include the subnet metric (total/count), the corresponding benchmark value, the category label, and a reason indicating which rule included it. Do not return any rounded answers. Categorize each network as 'ABOVE_BENCHMARK' (at least 50% more than the benchmark), 'BELOW_BENCHMARK' (at least 50% less than the benchmark), or 'NEAR_BENCHMARK'.
sql: WITH Above1StdActiveNetworks AS ( WITH inner_cte AS (SELECT n.id AS network_id, SUM(1) AS total_subnets FROM NETWORKS AS n JOIN NETWORKRBACS AS r ON n.id = r.object_id JOIN SUBNETS AS s ON r.object_id = s.network_id WHERE n.status = 'ACTIVE' GROUP BY n.id HAVING SUM(1) > ( SELECT AVG(subnet_cnt) + STDDEV(subnet_cnt) FROM ( SELECT n2.id AS network_id, SUM(1) AS subnet_cnt FROM NETWORKS AS n2 JOIN NETWORKRBACS AS r2 ON n2.id = r2.object_id JOIN SUBNETS AS s2 ON r2.object_id = s2.network_id WHERE n2.status = 'ACTIVE' GROUP BY n2.id ) AS per_network )), benchmark_cte AS ( SELECT AVG(subnet_cnt) + STDDEV(subnet_cnt) AS benchmark_threshold FROM ( SELECT n2.id AS network_id, SUM(1) AS subnet_cnt FROM NETWORKS AS n2 JOIN NETWORKRBACS AS r2 ON n2.id = r2.object_id JOIN SUBNETS AS s2 ON r2.object_id = s2.network_id WHERE n2.status = 'ACTIVE' GROUP BY n2.id ) AS per_network ) SELECT i.network_id, i.total_subnets, b.benchmark_threshold AS benchmark, CASE WHEN i.total_subnets > b.benchmark_threshold THEN 'ABOVE_1STD' ELSE 'NOT_ABOVE_1STD' END AS subnet_usage_category FROM inner_cte i CROSS JOIN benchmark_cte b ), Top3SharedNetworks AS ( WITH inner_cte AS (SELECT n.OBJECT_ID AS network_id, COUNT(*) AS subnet_count FROM NETWORKRBACS AS n JOIN SUBNETS AS s ON n.OBJECT_ID = s.NETWORK_ID WHERE n.ACTION = 'access_as_shared' GROUP BY n.OBJECT_ID ORDER BY COUNT(*) DESC LIMIT 3), AverageSubnets AS ( SELECT AVG(subnet_count) AS avg_subnet_count FROM inner_cte ) SELECT ic.network_id, ic.subnet_count, a.avg_subnet_count AS benchmark, CASE WHEN ic.subnet_count > a.avg_subnet_count * 1.5 THEN 'ABOVE_BENCHMARK' WHEN ic.subnet_count < a.avg_subnet_count * 0.5 THEN 'BELOW_BENCHMARK' ELSE 'NEAR_BENCHMARK' END AS subnet_category FROM inner_cte ic CROSS JOIN AverageSubnets a ), CombinedNetworks AS ( SELECT a.network_id AS network_id, a.total_subnets AS subnet_metric, a.benchmark AS benchmark_value, a.subnet_usage_category AS category, 'ACTIVE_ABOVE_1STD' AS reason FROM Above1StdActiveNetworks a UNION ALL SELECT t.network_id AS network_id, t.subnet_count AS subnet_metric, t.benchmark AS benchmark_value, t.subnet_category AS category, 'TOP3_SHARED_BY_SUBNETS' AS reason FROM Top3SharedNetworks t ) SELECT network_id, subnet_metric, benchmark_value, category, reason FROM CombinedNetworks ORDER BY network_id, reason;
sub_questions: For each network, return the network ID and the total number of subnets on that network, considering only ACTIVE networks, and only keeping networks whose total subnet count is more than one standard deviation above the mean subnet count across all ACTIVE networks.

List the top 3 networks that have the most subnets, considering only RBAC entries where the action is 'access_as_shared'. For each of these networks, return the network object ID and the number of subnets on that network.

For each ACTIVE network that has a subnet count more than one standard deviation above the mean subnet count across all ACTIVE networks, return the network ID, its total number of subnets, the overall benchmark threshold (average + standard deviation), and label the network as 'ABOVE_1STD' or 'NOT_ABOVE_1STD'.

For the top 3 networks that have the most subnets (considering only RBAC entries where the action is 'access_as_shared'), return the network object ID, the subnet count, the average subnet count across these top networks as a benchmark, and categorize each network as 'ABOVE_BENCHMARK' (at least 50% more than the benchmark), 'BELOW_BENCHMARK' (at least 50% less than the benchmark), or 'NEAR_BENCHMARK'.
sub_sqls: SELECT n.id AS network_id, SUM(1) AS total_subnets FROM NETWORKS AS n JOIN NETWORKRBACS AS r ON n.id = r.object_id JOIN SUBNETS AS s ON r.object_id = s.network_id WHERE n.status = 'ACTIVE' GROUP BY n.id HAVING SUM(1) > ( SELECT AVG(subnet_cnt) + STDDEV(subnet_cnt) FROM ( SELECT n2.id AS network_id, SUM(1) AS subnet_cnt FROM NETWORKS AS n2 JOIN NETWORKRBACS AS r2 ON n2.id = r2.object_id JOIN SUBNETS AS s2 ON r2.object_id = s2.network_id WHERE n2.status = 'ACTIVE' GROUP BY n2.id ) AS per_network );

SELECT n.OBJECT_ID AS network_id, COUNT(*) AS subnet_count FROM NETWORKRBACS AS n JOIN SUBNETS AS s ON n.OBJECT_ID = s.NETWORK_ID WHERE n.ACTION = 'access_as_shared' GROUP BY n.OBJECT_ID ORDER BY COUNT(*) DESC LIMIT 3;

WITH inner_cte AS (SELECT n.id AS network_id, SUM(1) AS total_subnets FROM NETWORKS AS n JOIN NETWORKRBACS AS r ON n.id = r.object_id JOIN SUBNETS AS s ON r.object_id = s.network_id WHERE n.status = 'ACTIVE' GROUP BY n.id HAVING SUM(1) > ( SELECT AVG(subnet_cnt) + STDDEV(subnet_cnt) FROM ( SELECT n2.id AS network_id, SUM(1) AS subnet_cnt FROM NETWORKS AS n2 JOIN NETWORKRBACS AS r2 ON n2.id = r2.object_id JOIN SUBNETS AS s2 ON r2.object_id = s2.network_id WHERE n2.status = 'ACTIVE' GROUP BY n2.id ) AS per_network )), benchmark_cte AS ( SELECT AVG(subnet_cnt) + STDDEV(subnet_cnt) AS benchmark_threshold FROM ( SELECT n2.id AS network_id, SUM(1) AS subnet_cnt FROM NETWORKS AS n2 JOIN NETWORKRBACS AS r2 ON n2.id = r2.object_id JOIN SUBNETS AS s2 ON r2.object_id = s2.network_id WHERE n2.status = 'ACTIVE' GROUP BY n2.id ) AS per_network ) SELECT i.network_id, i.total_subnets, b.benchmark_threshold AS benchmark, CASE WHEN i.total_subnets > b.benchmark_threshold THEN 'ABOVE_1STD' ELSE 'NOT_ABOVE_1STD' END AS subnet_usage_category FROM inner_cte i CROSS JOIN benchmark_cte b;

WITH inner_cte AS (SELECT n.OBJECT_ID AS network_id, COUNT(*) AS subnet_count FROM NETWORKRBACS AS n JOIN SUBNETS AS s ON n.OBJECT_ID = s.NETWORK_ID WHERE n.ACTION = 'access_as_shared' GROUP BY n.OBJECT_ID ORDER BY COUNT(*) DESC LIMIT 3), AverageSubnets AS ( SELECT AVG(subnet_count) AS avg_subnet_count FROM inner_cte ) SELECT ic.network_id, ic.subnet_count, a.avg_subnet_count AS benchmark, CASE WHEN ic.subnet_count > a.avg_subnet_count * 1.5 THEN 'ABOVE_BENCHMARK' WHEN ic.subnet_count < a.avg_subnet_count * 0.5 THEN 'BELOW_BENCHMARK' ELSE 'NEAR_BENCHMARK' END AS subnet_category FROM inner_cte ic CROSS JOIN AverageSubnets a;

question: For the top 10 tenants with the highest number of administratively up ports that are bound to at least one security group, show the tenant ID, the total number of such ports, the total number of security group bindings across those ports, whether the tenant has any DNS records associated with those ports, and (for those same tenants) the total number of port security bindings and the total number of times port security is enabled across those bindings on administratively up ports. Do not return any rounded answers.
sql: WITH TenantTop10AdminUpPortsWithSGAndDNS AS ( WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT p.id AS port_id, p.tenant_id, p.name AS port_name, COUNT(sgpb.security_group_id) AS security_group_binding_count, SUM(CASE WHEN pd.port_id IS NULL THEN 0 ELSE 1 END) AS dns_record_count FROM SECURITYGROUPPORTBINDINGS sgpb JOIN PORTS p ON sgpb.port_id = p.id LEFT JOIN PORTDNSES pd ON p.id = pd.port_id WHERE p.admin_state_up = 1 GROUP BY p.id, p.tenant_id, p.name ) SELECT inner_cte.tenant_id, COUNT(DISTINCT inner_cte.port_id) AS total_ports, SUM(inner_cte.security_group_binding_count) AS total_security_group_bindings, CASE WHEN SUM(inner_cte.dns_record_count) > 0 THEN 'Yes' ELSE 'No' END AS has_dns_records FROM inner_cte GROUP BY inner_cte.tenant_id ORDER BY total_ports DESC LIMIT 10 ), AdminUpPortSecurityBindingDetailsWithRollup AS ( WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT p.id AS port_id, p.tenant_id, p.mac_address, COUNT(psb.port_id) AS binding_count, SUM(CASE WHEN psb.port_security_enabled THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS port_security_enabled_total FROM ports p JOIN portsecuritybindings psb ON p.id = psb.port_id WHERE p.admin_state_up = 1 GROUP BY p.id, p.tenant_id, p.mac_address ) SELECT CASE WHEN LAG(tenant_id) OVER (ORDER BY tenant_id_sort, tenant_id, port_id) = tenant_id THEN NULL ELSE tenant_id END AS tenant_id, port_id, mac_address, binding_count, port_security_enabled_total FROM ( SELECT CASE WHEN GROUPING(tenant_id) = 1 THEN 'zzz' ELSE tenant_id END AS tenant_id_sort, CASE WHEN GROUPING(tenant_id) = 1 THEN 'TOTAL' ELSE tenant_id END AS tenant_id, CASE WHEN GROUPING(tenant_id) = 1 THEN NULL ELSE port_id END AS port_id, CASE WHEN GROUPING(tenant_id) = 1 THEN NULL ELSE mac_address END AS mac_address, SUM(binding_count) AS binding_count, SUM(port_security_enabled_total) AS port_security_enabled_total FROM inner_cte GROUP BY tenant_id, port_id, mac_address WITH ROLLUP ) AS tbltmp ORDER BY tenant_id_sort, tenant_id, port_id ) SELECT t10.tenant_id, t10.total_ports, t10.total_security_group_bindings, t10.has_dns_records, SUM(psd.binding_count) AS total_port_security_bindings_on_admin_up_ports, SUM(psd.port_security_enabled_total) AS total_port_security_enabled_across_bindings FROM TenantTop10AdminUpPortsWithSGAndDNS t10 JOIN AdminUpPortSecurityBindingDetailsWithRollup psd ON psd.tenant_id = t10.tenant_id WHERE t10.total_ports > 0 GROUP BY t10.tenant_id, t10.total_ports, t10.total_security_group_bindings, t10.has_dns_records ORDER BY t10.total_ports DESC;
sub_questions: For each port that is bound to a security group and has admin_state_up = 1, list the port ID, tenant ID, port name, and the number of security group bindings for that port along with the total number of DNS records associated with the port.

For each port that is administratively up, list the port ID, tenant ID, MAC address, the number of port security bindings on that port, and the total number of times port security is enabled across those bindings.

From the top 10 tenants with the highest number of admin-state-up ports that are bound to at least one security group, show each tenant’s ID, total number of such ports, the total number of security group bindings across those ports, and whether the tenant has any DNS records associated with those ports.

For each administratively up port, list the port ID, tenant ID, MAC address, the number of port security bindings on that port, and the total number of times port security is enabled across those bindings. Do not repeat the tenant ID if it is the same as the previous row. Include subtotals for each tenant.
sub_sqls: SELECT p.id AS port_id, p.tenant_id, p.name AS port_name, COUNT(sgpb.security_group_id) AS security_group_binding_count, SUM(CASE WHEN pd.port_id IS NULL THEN 0 ELSE 1 END) AS dns_record_count FROM SECURITYGROUPPORTBINDINGS sgpb JOIN PORTS p ON sgpb.port_id = p.id LEFT JOIN PORTDNSES pd ON p.id = pd.port_id WHERE p.admin_state_up = 1 GROUP BY p.id, p.tenant_id, p.name;

SELECT p.id AS port_id, p.tenant_id, p.mac_address, COUNT(psb.port_id) AS binding_count, SUM(CASE WHEN psb.port_security_enabled THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS port_security_enabled_total FROM ports p JOIN portsecuritybindings psb ON p.id = psb.port_id WHERE p.admin_state_up = 1 GROUP BY p.id, p.tenant_id, p.mac_address;

WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT p.id AS port_id, p.tenant_id, p.name AS port_name, COUNT(sgpb.security_group_id) AS security_group_binding_count, SUM(CASE WHEN pd.port_id IS NULL THEN 0 ELSE 1 END) AS dns_record_count FROM SECURITYGROUPPORTBINDINGS sgpb JOIN PORTS p ON sgpb.port_id = p.id LEFT JOIN PORTDNSES pd ON p.id = pd.port_id WHERE p.admin_state_up = 1 GROUP BY p.id, p.tenant_id, p.name ) SELECT inner_cte.tenant_id, COUNT(DISTINCT inner_cte.port_id) AS total_ports, SUM(inner_cte.security_group_binding_count) AS total_security_group_bindings, CASE WHEN SUM(inner_cte.dns_record_count) > 0 THEN 'Yes' ELSE 'No' END AS has_dns_records FROM inner_cte GROUP BY inner_cte.tenant_id ORDER BY total_ports DESC LIMIT 10;

WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT p.id AS port_id, p.tenant_id, p.mac_address, COUNT(psb.port_id) AS binding_count, SUM(CASE WHEN psb.port_security_enabled THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS port_security_enabled_total FROM ports p JOIN portsecuritybindings psb ON p.id = psb.port_id WHERE p.admin_state_up = 1 GROUP BY p.id, p.tenant_id, p.mac_address ) SELECT CASE WHEN LAG(tenant_id) OVER (ORDER BY tenant_id_sort, tenant_id, port_id) = tenant_id THEN NULL ELSE tenant_id END AS tenant_id, port_id, mac_address, binding_count, port_security_enabled_total FROM ( SELECT CASE WHEN GROUPING(tenant_id) = 1 THEN 'zzz' ELSE tenant_id END AS tenant_id_sort, CASE WHEN GROUPING(tenant_id) = 1 THEN 'TOTAL' ELSE tenant_id END AS tenant_id, CASE WHEN GROUPING(tenant_id) = 1 THEN NULL ELSE port_id END AS port_id, CASE WHEN GROUPING(tenant_id) = 1 THEN NULL ELSE mac_address END AS mac_address, SUM(binding_count) AS binding_count, SUM(port_security_enabled_total) AS port_security_enabled_total FROM inner_cte GROUP BY tenant_id, port_id, mac_address WITH ROLLUP ) AS tbltmp ORDER BY tenant_id_sort, tenant_id, port_id;

question: For each IPv4 subnet (by subnet name), show the coefficient of variation (using STDDEV only and never STDDEV_POP) of DNS nameserver order values and its deviation from the average coefficient of variation (using STDDEV only and never STDDEV_POP) across all IPv4 subnets, along with the subnet’s IP allocation pool count range, variance, standard deviation (using STDDEV only and never STDDEV_POP), and the overall average pool count range (considering only subnets that have at least one DNS nameserver entry). Do not return any rounded answers.
sql: WITH cv_stats AS ( WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT s.name AS subnet_name, STDDEV(d.ORDER) / NULLIF(AVG(d.ORDER), 0) AS coefficient_of_variation FROM subnets AS s JOIN dnsnameservers AS d ON d.subnet_id = s.id JOIN ipallocationpools AS p ON p.subnet_id = s.id WHERE s.ip_version = 4 GROUP BY s.name HAVING AVG(d.ORDER) > 0 ORDER BY coefficient_of_variation DESC ), avg_cte AS ( SELECT AVG(coefficient_of_variation) AS avg_coefficient_of_variation FROM inner_cte ) SELECT i.subnet_name, i.coefficient_of_variation, (i.coefficient_of_variation - a.avg_coefficient_of_variation) AS deviation_from_avg FROM inner_cte i CROSS JOIN avg_cte a ORDER BY deviation_from_avg DESC ), pool_stats AS ( WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT s.name AS subnet_name, MAX(pool_count) - MIN(pool_count) AS pool_count_range, VARIANCE(pool_count) AS pool_count_variance, STDDEV(pool_count) AS pool_count_stddev FROM subnets AS s JOIN dnsnameservers AS d ON d.subnet_id = s.id JOIN ( SELECT s2.id AS subnet_id, COUNT(*) AS pool_count FROM subnets AS s2 JOIN ipallocationpools AS p ON p.subnet_id = s2.id GROUP BY s2.id, p.id ) AS pool_stats ON pool_stats.subnet_id = s.id GROUP BY s.name ORDER BY pool_count_range DESC ) SELECT inner_cte.subnet_name, inner_cte.pool_count_range, inner_cte.pool_count_variance, inner_cte.pool_count_stddev, avg_stats.avg_pool_count_range FROM inner_cte JOIN ( SELECT AVG(pool_count_range) AS avg_pool_count_range FROM inner_cte ) AS avg_stats ON 1 = 1 ORDER BY inner_cte.pool_count_range DESC ) SELECT cv_stats.subnet_name, cv_stats.coefficient_of_variation, cv_stats.deviation_from_avg, pool_stats.pool_count_range, pool_stats.pool_count_variance, pool_stats.pool_count_stddev, pool_stats.avg_pool_count_range FROM cv_stats JOIN pool_stats ON cv_stats.subnet_name = pool_stats.subnet_name ORDER BY cv_stats.deviation_from_avg DESC;

question: For ports with status = 'DOWN', show each port’s ID and tenant ID along with its host, VIF type, allocated IP address, and the row number ordered by IP address (using a window frame of 2 preceding rows and 1 following row). Also include the tenant’s total number of DOWN ports and the average DOWN-port count across all tenants, plus the port’s MAC address, the running sum of its standard attribute ID within its security group (ordered by standard attribute ID), the security group’s total number of DOWN ports, and that group’s deviation from the average DOWN-port count across all security groups. Do not return any rounded answers.
sql: WITH q1 AS ( WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT p.ID AS port_id, p.TENANT_ID AS tenant_id, b.HOST AS host, b.VIF_TYPE AS vif_type, ia.IP_ADDRESS AS ip_address, ROW_NUMBER() OVER ( ORDER BY ia.IP_ADDRESS ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND 1 FOLLOWING ) AS window_column FROM ML2_PORT_BINDINGS b JOIN PORTS p ON b.PORT_ID = p.ID JOIN IPALLOCATIONS ia ON p.ID = ia.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' ) SELECT inner_cte.port_id, inner_cte.tenant_id, inner_cte.host, inner_cte.vif_type, inner_cte.ip_address, inner_cte.window_column, tenant_counts.total_down_ports, avg_down.avg_down_port_count FROM inner_cte JOIN ( SELECT tenant_id, COUNT(port_id) AS total_down_ports FROM inner_cte GROUP BY tenant_id ) AS tenant_counts ON inner_cte.tenant_id = tenant_counts.tenant_id JOIN ( SELECT AVG(down_port_count) AS avg_down_port_count FROM ( SELECT COUNT(port_id) AS down_port_count FROM inner_cte GROUP BY tenant_id ) AS sub ) AS avg_down ON 1 = 1 ), q2 AS ( WITH inner_cte AS (SELECT p.ID AS port_id, p.TENANT_ID AS tenant_id, p.MAC_ADDRESS AS mac_address, SUM(p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID) OVER ( PARTITION BY sgpb.SECURITY_GROUP_ID ORDER BY p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID ) AS window_column FROM SECURITYGROUPPORTBINDINGS AS sgpb JOIN PORTS AS p ON sgpb.PORT_ID = p.ID JOIN PORTSECURITYBINDINGS AS psb ON p.ID = psb.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN'), SecurityGroupDownCounts AS ( SELECT sgpb.SECURITY_GROUP_ID AS security_group_id, COUNT(*) AS down_ports_in_group FROM SECURITYGROUPPORTBINDINGS AS sgpb JOIN PORTS AS p ON sgpb.PORT_ID = p.ID JOIN PORTSECURITYBINDINGS AS psb ON p.ID = psb.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' GROUP BY sgpb.SECURITY_GROUP_ID ), AverageDownCounts AS ( SELECT AVG(down_ports_in_group) AS avg_down_ports_in_group FROM SecurityGroupDownCounts ) SELECT i.port_id, i.tenant_id, i.mac_address, i.window_column, sgdc.down_ports_in_group, (sgdc.down_ports_in_group - adc.avg_down_ports_in_group) AS deviation_from_avg_down_ports FROM inner_cte AS i JOIN SECURITYGROUPPORTBINDINGS AS sgpb ON sgpb.PORT_ID = i.port_id JOIN SecurityGroupDownCounts AS sgdc ON sgdc.security_group_id = sgpb.SECURITY_GROUP_ID CROSS JOIN AverageDownCounts AS adc ) SELECT q1.port_id, q1.tenant_id, q1.host, q1.vif_type, q1.ip_address, q1.window_column AS ip_row_number_window, q1.total_down_ports AS tenant_total_down_ports, q1.avg_down_port_count AS avg_down_ports_per_tenant, q2.mac_address, q2.window_column AS security_group_running_sum_standard_attr_id, q2.down_ports_in_group, q2.deviation_from_avg_down_ports FROM q1 JOIN q2 ON q1.port_id = q2.port_id AND q1.tenant_id = q2.tenant_id ORDER BY q1.ip_address;

question: For each tenant whose ports that are bound to a security group and have admin_state_up = 1 have an average security-group binding count greater than 1, return the tenant ID, that average security-group binding count, the total DNS record count across those ports, the number of such ports, and whether the tenant has any DOWN ports with ML2 bindings (VIF type present in the DOWN-ports windowed results). Do not return any rounded answers.
sql: WITH sg_bound_admin_up_ports AS (WITH inner_cte AS (SELECT p.id AS port_id, p.tenant_id, p.name AS port_name, COUNT(sgpb.security_group_id) AS security_group_binding_count, SUM(CASE WHEN pd.port_id IS NULL THEN 0 ELSE 1 END) AS dns_record_count FROM SECURITYGROUPPORTBINDINGS sgpb JOIN PORTS p ON sgpb.port_id = p.id LEFT JOIN PORTDNSES pd ON p.id = pd.port_id WHERE p.admin_state_up = 1 GROUP BY p.id, p.tenant_id, p.name), avg_cte AS ( SELECT AVG(security_group_binding_count) AS avg_sg_binding_count FROM inner_cte ) SELECT i.port_id, i.tenant_id, i.port_name, i.security_group_binding_count, i.dns_record_count, (i.security_group_binding_count - a.avg_sg_binding_count) AS deviation_from_avg_sg_binding_count FROM inner_cte i CROSS JOIN avg_cte a), down_ports_windowed_by_vif AS (WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT p.NAME, p.MAC_ADDRESS, p.ADMIN_STATE_UP, b.HOST, b.VIF_TYPE, AVG(p.ADMIN_STATE_UP) OVER ( PARTITION BY b.VIF_TYPE ORDER BY p.MAC_ADDRESS ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND 2 FOLLOWING ) AS window_column FROM PORTS AS p JOIN ML2_PORT_BINDINGS AS b ON p.ID = b.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' ORDER BY p.MAC_ADDRESS ) SELECT CASE WHEN LAG(vif_type) OVER (ORDER BY vif_type_sort, vif_type, mac_address) = vif_type THEN NULL ELSE vif_type END AS vif_type, name, mac_address, admin_state_up, host, window_column, down_ports_count, avg_window_column FROM ( SELECT CASE WHEN GROUPING(i.vif_type) = 1 THEN 'zzz' ELSE i.vif_type END AS vif_type_sort, CASE WHEN GROUPING(i.vif_type) = 1 THEN 'TOTAL' ELSE i.vif_type END AS vif_type, i.name, i.mac_address, i.admin_state_up, i.host, i.window_column, COUNT(*) AS down_ports_count, AVG(i.window_column) AS avg_window_column FROM inner_cte AS i GROUP BY i.vif_type, i.name, i.mac_address, i.admin_state_up, i.host, i.window_column WITH ROLLUP ) AS tbltmp ORDER BY vif_type_sort, vif_type, mac_address), tenant_sg_admin_up_summary AS ( SELECT p.tenant_id, AVG(sgpb.security_group_binding_count) AS avg_sg_binding_count_admin_up, SUM(sgpb.dns_record_count) AS total_dns_record_count_admin_up, COUNT(*) AS admin_up_sg_bound_port_count FROM sg_bound_admin_up_ports sgpb JOIN PORTS p ON p.id = sgpb.port_id WHERE p.admin_state_up = 1 GROUP BY p.tenant_id ) SELECT t.tenant_id, t.avg_sg_binding_count_admin_up, t.total_dns_record_count_admin_up, t.admin_up_sg_bound_port_count, CASE WHEN COUNT(DISTINCT d.vif_type) > 0 THEN 'Yes' ELSE 'No' END AS Has_Down_Ports_With_Bindings FROM tenant_sg_admin_up_summary t LEFT JOIN PORTS p ON p.tenant_id = t.tenant_id LEFT JOIN down_ports_windowed_by_vif d ON d.name = p.name WHERE t.avg_sg_binding_count_admin_up > 1 GROUP BY t.tenant_id, t.avg_sg_binding_count_admin_up, t.total_dns_record_count_admin_up, t.admin_up_sg_bound_port_count ORDER BY t.avg_sg_binding_count_admin_up DESC;

question: For the top 10 tenants by number of 'haproxy' load balancers (considering only load balancers whose highest admin_state_up is 1), return each tenant’s ID, their total number of qualifying load balancers, the average number of these qualifying 'haproxy' load balancers across all tenants, and whether the tenant has any qualifying load balancers currently operating ONLINE—restricted to tenants whose qualifying load balancer count is greater than the overall average. Do not return any rounded answers.
sql: WITH TopTenTenants AS ( WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT lb.name AS loadbalancer_name, MAX(lb.admin_state_up) AS max_admin_state_up, lb.operating_status FROM LBAAS_LOADBALANCERS lb JOIN PROVIDERRESOURCEASSOCIATIONS pra ON lb.id = pra.resource_id WHERE pra.provider_name = 'haproxy' GROUP BY lb.name, lb.operating_status HAVING MAX(lb.admin_state_up) = 1 ) SELECT lb.tenant_id, COUNT(DISTINCT lb.id) AS total_qualifying_loadbalancers, CASE WHEN COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN inner_cte.operating_status = 'ONLINE' THEN lb.id END) > 0 THEN 'Yes' ELSE 'No' END AS has_any_online FROM inner_cte JOIN LBAAS_LOADBALANCERS lb ON lb.name = inner_cte.loadbalancer_name AND lb.operating_status = inner_cte.operating_status GROUP BY lb.tenant_id ORDER BY total_qualifying_loadbalancers DESC LIMIT 10 ), TenantHaproxyCountsAndAverage AS ( WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT lb.name AS loadbalancer_name, MAX(lb.admin_state_up) AS max_admin_state_up, lb.operating_status FROM LBAAS_LOADBALANCERS lb JOIN PROVIDERRESOURCEASSOCIATIONS pra ON lb.id = pra.resource_id WHERE pra.provider_name = 'haproxy' GROUP BY lb.name, lb.operating_status HAVING MAX(lb.admin_state_up) = 1 ) SELECT lb.tenant_id AS tenant_id, COUNT(inner_cte.loadbalancer_name) AS total_haproxy_loadbalancers, avg_counts.avg_lb_count FROM inner_cte JOIN LBAAS_LOADBALANCERS lb ON lb.name = inner_cte.loadbalancer_name AND lb.operating_status = inner_cte.operating_status JOIN ( SELECT AVG(lb_count) AS avg_lb_count FROM ( SELECT lb2.tenant_id, COUNT(*) AS lb_count FROM ( SELECT lb.name AS loadbalancer_name, BY lb.name, lb.operating_status HAVING MAX(lb.admin_state_up) = 1 ) AS inner2 JOIN LBAAS_LOADBALANCERS lb2 ON lb2.name = inner2.loadbalancer_name AND lb2.operating_status = inner2.operating_status GROUP BY lb2.tenant_id ) AS sub ) AS avg_counts GROUP BY lb.tenant_id, avg_counts.avg_lb_count ) SELECT ttt.tenant_id, ttt.total_qualifying_loadbalancers, tha.avg_lb_count, ttt.has_any_online FROM question: For ports with status DOWN, which ports (matched by MAC address, host, and VIF type) appear in both (1) the IP-address-ordered row-number window output that also includes each tenant’s total DOWN-port count and the average DOWN-port count across tenants, and (2) the VIF-type-partitioned admin_state_up window-average output where the window average is above the overall average for that VIF type? Return the port ID, tenant ID, host, VIF type, allocated IP address, the IP-based window row number, the tenant’s total DOWN ports, the overall average DOWN-port count, plus the port name, MAC address, admin_state_up, and the admin_state_up window average. Do not return any rounded answers.
sql: WITH down_ports_ip_window AS ( WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT p.ID AS port_id, p.TENANT_ID AS tenant_id, b.HOST AS host, b.VIF_TYPE AS vif_type, ia.IP_ADDRESS AS ip_address, ROW_NUMBER() OVER ( ORDER BY ia.IP_ADDRESS ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND 1 FOLLOWING ) AS window_column FROM ML2_PORT_BINDINGS b JOIN PORTS p ON b.PORT_ID = p.ID JOIN IPALLOCATIONS ia ON p.ID = ia.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' ) SELECT inner_cte.port_id, inner_cte.tenant_id, inner_cte.host, inner_cte.vif_type, inner_cte.ip_address, inner_cte.window_column, tenant_counts.total_down_ports, avg_down.avg_down_port_count FROM inner_cte JOIN ( SELECT tenant_id, COUNT(port_id) AS total_down_ports FROM inner_cte GROUP BY tenant_id ) AS tenant_counts ON inner_cte.tenant_id = tenant_counts.tenant_id JOIN ( SELECT AVG(down_port_count) AS avg_down_port_count FROM ( SELECT COUNT(port_id) AS down_port_count FROM inner_cte GROUP BY tenant_id ) AS sub ) AS avg_down ON 1 = 1 ), down_ports_admin_window_filtered AS ( WITH inner_cte AS (SELECT p.NAME, p.MAC_ADDRESS, p.ADMIN_STATE_UP, b.HOST, b.VIF_TYPE, AVG(p.ADMIN_STATE_UP) OVER ( PARTITION BY b.VIF_TYPE ORDER BY p.MAC_ADDRESS ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND 2 FOLLOWING ) AS window_column FROM PORTS AS p JOIN ML2_PORT_BINDINGS AS b ON p.ID = b.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' ORDER BY p.MAC_ADDRESS), VifTypeAverages AS ( SELECT VIF_TYPE, AVG(window_column) AS avg_window_column FROM inner_cte GROUP BY VIF_TYPE ) SELECT i.NAME, i.MAC_ADDRESS, i.ADMIN_STATE_UP, i.HOST, i.VIF_TYPE, i.window_column FROM inner_cte i JOIN VifTypeAverages v ON i.VIF_TYPE = v.VIF_TYPE WHERE i.window_column > v.avg_window_column ORDER BY i.MAC_ADDRESS ) SELECT dipw.port_id, dipw.tenant_id, dipw.host, dipw.vif_type, dipw.ip_address, dipw.window_column AS ip_row_number_window, dipw.total_down_ports, dipw.avg_down_port_count, dapwf.NAME AS port_name, dapwf.MAC_ADDRESS, dapwf.ADMIN_STATE_UP, dapwf.window_column AS admin_state_up_window_avg FROM down_ports_ip_window dipw JOIN PORTS p ON p.ID = dipw.port_id JOIN down_ports_admin_window_filtered dapwf ON dapwf.MAC_ADDRESS = p.MAC_ADDRESS AND dapwf.HOST = dipw.host AND dapwf.VIF_TYPE = dipw.vif_type;

question: For ports that (1) are bound to a security group and have admin_state_up = 1 and (2) are also DOWN, list each port’s ID, tenant ID, port name, security-group binding count, DNS record count, and deviation from the average security-group binding count; additionally include the port MAC address, the running sum of standard attribute ID within its security group, and (for that tenant) the total number of DOWN ports, the average DOWN-port count benchmark across tenants, and the tenant’s usage category (HIGH_USER/LOW_USER/AVERAGE_USER). Do not return any rounded answers. Categorize each tenant as 'HIGH_USER' (at least 50% more than average), 'LOW_USER' (at least 50% less than average), or 'AVERAGE_USER'.
sql: WITH sg_admin_up_ports AS (WITH inner_cte AS (SELECT p.id AS port_id, p.tenant_id, p.name AS port_name, COUNT(sgpb.security_group_id) AS security_group_binding_count, SUM(CASE WHEN pd.port_id IS NULL THEN 0 ELSE 1 END) AS dns_record_count FROM SECURITYGROUPPORTBINDINGS sgpb JOIN PORTS p ON sgpb.port_id = p.id LEFT JOIN PORTDNSES pd ON p.id = pd.port_id WHERE p.admin_state_up = 1 GROUP BY p.id, p.tenant_id, p.name), avg_cte AS ( SELECT AVG(security_group_binding_count) AS avg_sg_binding_count FROM inner_cte ) SELECT i.port_id, i.tenant_id, i.port_name, i.security_group_binding_count, i.dns_record_count, (i.security_group_binding_count - a.avg_sg_binding_count) AS deviation_from_avg_sg_binding_count FROM inner_cte i CROSS JOIN avg_cte a), down_ports_tenant_benchmark AS (WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT p.ID AS port_id, p.TENANT_ID AS tenant_id, p.MAC_ADDRESS AS mac_address, SUM(p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID) OVER ( PARTITION BY sgpb.SECURITY_GROUP_ID ORDER BY p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID ) AS window_column FROM SECURITYGROUPPORTBINDINGS AS sgpb JOIN PORTS AS p ON sgpb.PORT_ID = p.ID JOIN PORTSECURITYBINDINGS AS psb ON p.ID = psb.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' ), TenantDownPorts AS ( SELECT tenant_id, COUNT(DISTINCT port_id) AS total_down_ports FROM inner_cte GROUP BY tenant_id ), AverageDownPorts AS ( SELECT AVG(total_down_ports) AS avg_down_ports FROM TenantDownPorts ) SELECT i.port_id, i.tenant_id, i.mac_address, i.window_column, tdp.total_down_ports, adp.avg_down_ports AS benchmark, CASE WHEN tdp.total_down_ports > adp.avg_down_ports * 1.5 THEN 'HIGH_USER' WHEN tdp.total_down_ports < adp.avg_down_ports * 0.5 THEN 'LOW_USER' ELSE 'AVERAGE_USER' END AS user_category FROM inner_cte i JOIN TenantDownPorts tdp ON i.tenant_id = tdp.tenant_id CROSS JOIN AverageDownPorts adp) SELECT sap.port_id, sap.tenant_id, sap.port_name, sap.security_group_binding_count, sap.dns_record_count, sap.deviation_from_avg_sg_binding_count, dptb.mac_address, dptb.window_column, dptb.total_down_ports, dptb.benchmark, dptb.user_category FROM sg_admin_up_ports sap JOIN down_ports_tenant_benchmark dptb ON sap.port_id = dptb.port_id WHERE sap.tenant_id IS NOT NULL;

question: For each of the top 10 port statuses (considering only ports that have an IP allocation and a non-null standard attribute ID) ranked by the variance of STANDARD_ATTR_ID, show the status, the STANDARD_ATTR_ID variance, the total number of distinct ports, whether any of those ports have a floating IP allocated, and—only when the status is DOWN—the number of distinct device owners with DOWN ports bound to a security group, the average and maximum DOWN-port counts per device owner, and how many of those device owners are categorized as HIGH_USER or LOW_USER versus the overall average benchmark. sql: WITH q1 AS ( WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT p.STATUS, VARIANCE(p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID) AS standard_attr_id_variance FROM PORTS AS p JOIN IPALLOCATIONS AS ia ON p.ID = ia.PORT_ID WHERE p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID IS NOT NULL GROUP BY p.STATUS ORDER BY standard_attr_id_variance DESC ) SELECT i.STATUS, i.standard_attr_id_variance, COUNT(DISTINCT p2.ID) AS total_ports, CASE WHEN COUNT(DISTINCT f.ID) > 0 THEN 'Yes' ELSE 'No' END AS has_floating_ips FROM inner_cte i JOIN PORTS p2 ON p2.STATUS = i.STATUS JOIN IPALLOCATIONS ia2 ON ia2.PORT_ID = p2.ID LEFT JOIN FLOATINGIPS f ON f.FIXED_PORT_ID = p2.ID WHERE p2.STANDARD_ATTR_ID IS NOT NULL GROUP BY i.STATUS, i.standard_attr_id_variance ORDER BY i.standard_attr_id_variance DESC LIMIT 10 ), q2 AS ( WITH inner_cte AS (SELECT p.STATUS AS port_status, p.DEVICE_OWNER AS device_owner, COUNT(DISTINCT p.ID) AS port_count, MIN(p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID) AS min_standard_attr_id FROM PORTS p JOIN SECURITYGROUPPORTBINDINGS spb ON p.ID = spb.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' GROUP BY p.STATUS, p.DEVICE_OWNER), AveragePorts AS ( SELECT AVG(port_count) AS avg_ports FROM inner_cte ) SELECT i.device_owner, i.port_count, i.min_standard_attr_id, ap.avg_ports AS benchmark, CASE WHEN i.port_count > ap.avg_ports * 1.5 THEN 'HIGH_USER' WHEN i.port_count < ap.avg_ports * 0.5 THEN 'LOW_USER' ELSE 'AVERAGE_USER' END AS user_category FROM inner_cte i CROSS JOIN AveragePorts ap ) SELECT q1.STATUS, q1.standard_attr_id_variance, q1.total_ports, q1.has_floating_ips, COUNT(DISTINCT q2.device_owner) AS down_device_owners_bound_to_sg, AVG(q2.port_count) AS avg_down_ports_per_device_owner, MAX(q2.port_count) AS max_down_ports_per_device_owner, COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN q2.user_category = 'HIGH_USER' THEN q2.device_owner END) AS high_user_device_owners, COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN q2.user_category = 'LOW_USER' THEN q2.device_owner END) AS low_user_device_owners FROM q1 LEFT JOIN q2 ON q1.STATUS = 'DOWN' GROUP BY q1.STATUS, q1.standard_attr_id_variance, q1.total_ports, q1.has_floating_ips ORDER BY q1.standard_attr_id_variance DESC;

WITH inner_cte AS (SELECT p.STATUS AS port_status, p.DEVICE_OWNER AS device_owner, COUNT(DISTINCT p.ID) AS port_count, MIN(p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID) AS min_standard_attr_id FROM PORTS p JOIN SECURITYGROUPPORTBINDINGS spb ON p.ID = spb.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' GROUP BY p.STATUS, p.DEVICE_OWNER), AveragePorts AS ( SELECT AVG(port_count) AS avg_ports FROM inner_cte ) SELECT i.device_owner, i.port_count, i.min_standard_attr_id, ap.avg_ports AS benchmark, CASE WHEN i.port_count > ap.avg_ports * 1.5 THEN 'HIGH_USER' WHEN i.port_count < ap.avg_ports * 0.5 THEN 'LOW_USER' ELSE 'AVERAGE_USER' END AS user_category FROM inner_cte i CROSS JOIN AveragePorts ap;

question: How many DOWN-status ports are on host "drive-59", and (equivalently) how many ports on host "drive-59" are also DOWN? Do not return any rounded answers.
sql: WITH down_ports AS ( WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT p.ID AS port_id, p.TENANT_ID AS tenant_id, b.HOST AS host, b.VIF_TYPE AS vif_type, ia.IP_ADDRESS AS ip_address, ROW_NUMBER() OVER ( ORDER BY ia.IP_ADDRESS ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND 1 FOLLOWING ) AS window_column FROM ML2_PORT_BINDINGS b JOIN PORTS p ON b.PORT_ID = p.ID JOIN IPALLOCATIONS ia ON p.ID = ia.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' ) SELECT CASE WHEN LAG(tenant_id) OVER (ORDER BY tenant_id_sort, ip_address, port_id) = tenant_id THEN NULL ELSE tenant_id END AS tenant_id, port_id, host, vif_type, ip_address, window_column, down_ports_total FROM ( SELECT CASE WHEN GROUPING(tenant_id) = 1 THEN 'zzz' ELSE tenant_id END AS tenant_id_sort, CASE WHEN GROUPING(tenant_id) = 1 THEN 'TOTAL' ELSE tenant_id END AS tenant_id, port_id, host, vif_type, ip_address, window_column, COUNT(*) AS down_ports_total FROM inner_cte GROUP BY tenant_id, port_id, host, vif_type, ip_address, window_column WITH ROLLUP ) AS tbltmp ORDER BY tenant_id_sort, ip_address, port_id ), drive59_ports AS ( WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT b.PORT_ID, p.TENANT_ID, p.MAC_ADDRESS, SUM(p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID) OVER ( PARTITION BY b.VIF_TYPE ORDER BY p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID ) AS window_column FROM ML2_PORT_BINDINGS AS b JOIN PORTS AS p ON b.PORT_ID = p.ID JOIN PORTSECURITYBINDINGS AS psb ON p.ID = psb.PORT_ID WHERE b.HOST = 'drive-59' ), VifTypeStats AS ( SELECT b.VIF_TYPE, COUNT(*) AS ports_in_vif_type, AVG(ic.window_column) AS avg_running_sum_in_vif_type FROM inner_cte ic JOIN ML2_PORT_BINDINGS b ON b.PORT_ID = ic.PORT_ID GROUP BY b.VIF_TYPE ) SELECT ic.PORT_ID, ic.TENANT_ID, ic.MAC_ADDRESS, ic.window_column AS running_sum_standard_attr_id, vts.ports_in_vif_type, (ic.window_column - vts.avg_running_sum_in_vif_type) AS deviation_from_avg_running_sum_in_vif_type FROM inner_cte ic JOIN ML2_PORT_BINDINGS b ON b.PORT_ID = ic.PORT_ID JOIN VifTypeStats vts ON vts.VIF_TYPE = b.VIF_TYPE ) SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT dp.port_id) AS down_ports_on_drive_59_count, COUNT(DISTINCT d59.PORT_ID) AS drive_59_ports_that_are_down_count FROM down_ports dp JOIN drive59_ports d59 ON d59.PORT_ID = dp.port_id WHERE dp.host = 'drive-59';

question: For IPv4 subnets whose DNS nameserver order range is greater than the average order range across all IPv4 subnets, return each subnet name along with its DNS nameserver order range, order variance, coefficient of variation (using STDDEV only and never STDDEV_POP) of the order values, and the deviation of that coefficient of variation (using STDDEV only and never STDDEV_POP) from the average coefficient of variation (using STDDEV only and never STDDEV_POP) across all IPv4 subnets. Do not return any rounded answers.
sql: WITH RangeVarianceSubnets AS ( WITH inner_cte AS (SELECT s.name AS subnet_name, MAX(d.ORDER) - MIN(d.ORDER) AS order_range, VARIANCE(d.ORDER) AS order_variance FROM SUBNETS AS s JOIN DNSNAMESERVERS AS d ON s.id = d.subnet_id WHERE s.ip_version = 4 GROUP BY s.name ORDER BY order_range DESC) SELECT subnet_name, order_range, order_variance FROM inner_cte WHERE order_range > (SELECT AVG(order_range) FROM inner_cte) ORDER BY order_range DESC ), CoeffVarDeviationSubnets AS ( WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT s.name AS subnet_name, STDDEV(d.ORDER) / NULLIF(AVG(d.ORDER), 0) AS coefficient_of_variation FROM subnets AS s JOIN dnsnameservers AS d ON d.subnet_id = s.id JOIN ipallocationpools AS p ON p.subnet_id = s.id WHERE s.ip_version = 4 GROUP BY s.name HAVING AVG(d.ORDER) > 0 ORDER BY coefficient_of_variation DESC ), avg_cte AS ( SELECT AVG(coefficient_of_variation) AS avg_coefficient_of_variation FROM inner_cte ) SELECT i.subnet_name, i.coefficient_of_variation, (i.coefficient_of_variation - a.avg_coefficient_of_variation) AS deviation_from_avg FROM inner_cte i CROSS JOIN avg_cte a ORDER BY deviation_from_avg DESC ) SELECT rvs.subnet_name, rvs.order_range, rvs.order_variance, cvd.coefficient_of_variation, cvd.deviation_from_avg FROM RangeVarianceSubnets rvs JOIN CoeffVarDeviationSubnets cvd ON rvs.subnet_name = cvd.subnet_name ORDER BY rvs.order_range DESC, cvd.deviation_from_avg DESC;

question: For each network whose number of ports that are both in status 'DOWN' and have port security enabled is greater than the average such count across all networks, list the network ID, that down-and-secure port count (and the overall total of down-and-secure ports), and also the maximum (within that network) of the range, variance, and standard deviation (using STDDEV only and never STDDEV_POP) of allowed address-pair counts per port (considering only ports that have at least one allowed address pair). Do not return any rounded answers.
sql: WITH DownSecureNetworks AS (WITH inner_cte AS (SELECT COUNT(*) AS down_ports_with_port_security_enabled FROM PORTS p JOIN PORTSECURITYBINDINGS psb ON p.ID = psb.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' AND psb.PORT_SECURITY_ENABLED = 1), NetworkDownSecureCounts AS (SELECT p.network_id, COUNT(*) AS down_secure_ports FROM PORTS p JOIN PORTSECURITYBINDINGS psb ON p.ID = psb.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' AND psb.PORT_SECURITY_ENABLED = 1 GROUP BY p.network_id), AvgDownSecure AS (SELECT AVG(down_secure_ports) AS avg_down_secure_ports FROM NetworkDownSecureCounts) SELECT ndsc.network_id, ndsc.down_secure_ports, (SELECT down_ports_with_port_security_enabled FROM inner_cte) AS total_down_secure_ports_overall FROM NetworkDownSecureCounts ndsc WHERE ndsc.down_secure_ports > (SELECT avg_down_secure_ports FROM AvgDownSecure)), AllowedAddressPairStatsByNetwork AS (WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT sgpb.SECURITY_GROUP_ID, MAX(port_pair_count) - MIN(port_pair_count) AS pair_count_range, VARIANCE(port_pair_count) AS pair_count_variance, STDDEV(port_pair_count) AS pair_count_stddev FROM SECURITYGROUPPORTBINDINGS AS sgpb JOIN ( SELECT p.ID AS port_id, COUNT(*) AS port_pair_count FROM PORTS AS p JOIN ALLOWEDADDRESSPAIRS AS aap ON p.ID = aap.PORT_ID GROUP BY p.ID ) AS port_stats ON sgpb.PORT_ID = port_stats.port_id GROUP BY sgpb.SECURITY_GROUP_ID ORDER BY pair_count_range DESC ) SELECT p.NETWORK_ID, MAX(inner_cte.pair_count_range) AS max_pair_count_range, MAX(inner_cte.pair_count_variance) AS max_pair_count_variance, MAX(inner_cte.pair_count_stddev) AS max_pair_count_stddev FROM inner_cte JOIN SECURITYGROUPPORTBINDINGS AS sgpb ON inner_cte.SECURITY_GROUP_ID = sgpb.SECURITY_GROUP_ID JOIN PORTS AS p ON sgpb.PORT_ID = p.ID GROUP BY p.NETWORK_ID), CombinedNetworkMetrics AS ( SELECT dsn.network_id, dsn.down_secure_ports, dsn.total_down_secure_ports_overall, aapsbn.max_pair_count_range, aapsbn.max_pair_count_variance, aapsbn.max_pair_count_stddev FROM DownSecureNetworks dsn JOIN AllowedAddressPairStatsByNetwork aapsbn ON dsn.network_id = aapsbn.network_id ) SELECT * FROM CombinedNetworkMetrics ORDER BY network_id;

question: For DOWN ports, show the port name, MAC address, admin_state_up flag, binding host, VIF type, and the 2-preceding/2-following window average of admin_state_up (partitioned by VIF type and ordered by MAC address), but only for rows whose window average is greater than the overall average window average for the same VIF type; also include the DOWN status’s STANDARD_ATTR_ID variance (computed among ports that have an IP allocation and a non-null standard attribute ID), the total number of distinct such ports, and whether any of them have floating IPs, considering only the top 10 statuses by that variance. Do not return any rounded answers.
sql: WITH q1 AS ( WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT p.STATUS, VARIANCE(p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID) AS standard_attr_id_variance FROM PORTS AS p JOIN IPALLOCATIONS AS ia ON p.ID = ia.PORT_ID WHERE p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID IS NOT NULL GROUP BY p.STATUS ORDER BY standard_attr_id_variance DESC ) SELECT i.STATUS, i.standard_attr_id_variance, COUNT(DISTINCT p2.ID) AS total_ports, CASE WHEN COUNT(DISTINCT f.ID) > 0 THEN 'Yes' ELSE 'No' END AS has_floating_ips FROM inner_cte i JOIN PORTS p2 ON p2.STATUS = i.STATUS JOIN IPALLOCATIONS ia2 ON ia2.PORT_ID = p2.ID LEFT JOIN FLOATINGIPS f ON f.FIXED_PORT_ID = p2.ID WHERE p2.STANDARD_ATTR_ID IS NOT NULL GROUP BY i.STATUS, i.standard_attr_id_variance ORDER BY i.standard_attr_id_variance DESC LIMIT 10 ), q2 AS ( WITH inner_cte AS (SELECT p.NAME, p.MAC_ADDRESS, p.ADMIN_STATE_UP, b.HOST, b.VIF_TYPE, AVG(p.ADMIN_STATE_UP) OVER ( PARTITION BY b.VIF_TYPE ORDER BY p.MAC_ADDRESS ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND 2 FOLLOWING ) AS window_column FROM PORTS AS p JOIN ML2_PORT_BINDINGS AS b ON p.ID = b.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' ORDER BY p.MAC_ADDRESS), VifTypeAverages AS ( SELECT VIF_TYPE, AVG(window_column) AS avg_window_column FROM inner_cte GROUP BY VIF_TYPE ) SELECT i.NAME, i.MAC_ADDRESS, i.ADMIN_STATE_UP, i.HOST, i.VIF_TYPE, i.window_column FROM inner_cte i JOIN VifTypeAverages v ON i.VIF_TYPE = v.VIF_TYPE WHERE i.window_column > v.avg_window_column ORDER BY i.MAC_ADDRESS ) SELECT q2.NAME, q2.MAC_ADDRESS, q2.ADMIN_STATE_UP, q2.HOST, q2.VIF_TYPE, q2.window_column, q1.standard_attr_id_variance, q1.total_ports, q1.has_floating_ips FROM q2 JOIN q1 ON q1.STATUS = 'DOWN' ORDER BY q1.standard_attr_id_variance DESC, q2.MAC_ADDRESS;
