sub_sqls: SELECT s.NAME, dense_rank() OVER ( ORDER BY sa.UPDATED_AT ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW ) AS window_column FROM SUBNETS AS s JOIN STANDARDATTRIBUTES AS sa ON sa.ID = s.STANDARD_ATTR_ID WHERE s.IP_VERSION = 4;

question: Among the load balancers associated with the provider named 'haproxy' whose highest admin_state_up value is 1, list the top 10 tenants by number of such load balancers, showing each tenant ID, the total number of qualifying load balancers, and whether any of those load balancers are currently operating ONLINE. Do not return any rounded answers.
sql: WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT lb.name AS loadbalancer_name, MAX(lb.admin_state_up) AS max_admin_state_up, lb.operating_status FROM LBAAS_LOADBALANCERS lb JOIN PROVIDERRESOURCEASSOCIATIONS pra ON lb.id = pra.resource_id WHERE pra.provider_name = 'haproxy' GROUP BY lb.name, lb.operating_status HAVING MAX(lb.admin_state_up) = 1 ) SELECT lb.tenant_id, COUNT(DISTINCT lb.id) AS total_qualifying_loadbalancers, CASE WHEN COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN inner_cte.operating_status = 'ONLINE' THEN lb.id END) > 0 THEN 'Yes' ELSE 'No' END AS has_any_online FROM inner_cte JOIN LBAAS_LOADBALANCERS lb ON lb.name = inner_cte.loadbalancer_name AND lb.operating_status = inner_cte.operating_status GROUP BY lb.tenant_id ORDER BY total_qualifying_loadbalancers DESC LIMIT 10;
sub_questions: For each load balancer that is associated with the provider named 'haproxy', return the load balancer name, the highest admin_state_up value, and the load balancer operating status, keeping only those groups where the highest admin_state_up value is 1.
sub_sqls: SELECT lb.name AS loadbalancer_name, MAX(lb.admin_state_up) AS max_admin_state_up, lb.operating_status FROM LBAAS_LOADBALANCERS lb JOIN PROVIDERRESOURCEASSOCIATIONS pra ON lb.id = pra.resource_id WHERE pra.provider_name = 'haproxy' GROUP BY lb.name, lb.operating_status HAVING MAX(lb.admin_state_up) = 1;

question: Among the top 3 networks that have the most subnets (considering only RBAC entries where the action is 'access_as_shared'), list each network object ID and its subnet count, and also show the tenant ID of each subnet on those networks. Do not repeat the network ID if it is the same as the previous row. Do not return any rounded answers.
sql: WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT n.OBJECT_ID AS network_id, COUNT(*) AS subnet_count FROM NETWORKRBACS AS n JOIN SUBNETS AS s ON n.OBJECT_ID = s.NETWORK_ID WHERE n.ACTION = 'access_as_shared' GROUP BY n.OBJECT_ID ORDER BY COUNT(*) DESC LIMIT 3 ) SELECT CASE WHEN LAG(inner_cte.network_id) OVER (ORDER BY inner_cte.network_id) = inner_cte.network_id THEN NULL ELSE inner_cte.network_id END AS network_id, inner_cte.subnet_count, s.TENANT_ID AS subnet_tenant_id FROM inner_cte JOIN SUBNETS AS s ON s.NETWORK_ID = inner_cte.network_id ORDER BY inner_cte.network_id, s.TENANT_ID;
sub_questions: List the top 3 networks that have the most subnets, considering only RBAC entries where the action is 'access_as_shared'. For each of these networks, return the network object ID and the number of subnets on that network.
sub_sqls: SELECT n.OBJECT_ID AS network_id, COUNT(*) AS subnet_count FROM NETWORKRBACS AS n JOIN SUBNETS AS s ON n.OBJECT_ID = s.NETWORK_ID WHERE n.ACTION = 'access_as_shared' GROUP BY n.OBJECT_ID ORDER BY COUNT(*) DESC LIMIT 3;

question: For each tenant, how many ports are in status 'DOWN' with port security enabled, and what is the deviation of that count from the average across all tenants? Do not return any rounded answers.
sql: WITH inner_cte AS (SELECT COUNT(*) AS down_ports_with_port_security_enabled FROM PORTS p JOIN PORTSECURITYBINDINGS psb ON p.ID = psb.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' AND psb.PORT_SECURITY_ENABLED = 1), TenantDownSecurePorts AS (SELECT p.TENANT_ID AS tenant_id, COUNT(*) AS down_secure_ports FROM PORTS p JOIN PORTSECURITYBINDINGS psb ON p.ID = psb.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' AND psb.PORT_SECURITY_ENABLED = 1 GROUP BY p.TENANT_ID), AverageTenantCounts AS (SELECT AVG(down_secure_ports) AS avg_down_secure_ports FROM TenantDownSecurePorts) SELECT tdsp.tenant_id, tdsp.down_secure_ports, (tdsp.down_secure_ports - atc.avg_down_secure_ports) AS deviation_from_avg, inner_cte.down_ports_with_port_security_enabled AS total_down_ports_with_port_security_enabled FROM TenantDownSecurePorts tdsp CROSS JOIN AverageTenantCounts atc CROSS JOIN inner_cte;
sub_questions: How many ports are in status 'DOWN' and have port security enabled (as indicated by the port security binding)?
sub_sqls: SELECT COUNT(*) AS down_ports_with_port_security_enabled FROM PORTS p JOIN PORTSECURITYBINDINGS psb ON p.ID = psb.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' AND psb.PORT_SECURITY_ENABLED = 1;

question: For each security group, show the security group ID, the range/variance/standard deviation (using STDDEV only and never STDDEV_POP) of the number of allowed address pairs per port (only counting ports that have at least one allowed address pair), also show the overall average of the security-group-level range as a benchmark, and categorize each security group as 'HIGH_SPREAD' (at least 50% above the benchmark), 'LOW_SPREAD' (at least 50% below the benchmark), or 'AVERAGE_SPREAD'. Do not return any rounded answers.
sql: WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT sgpb.SECURITY_GROUP_ID, MAX(port_pair_count) - MIN(port_pair_count) AS pair_count_range, VARIANCE(port_pair_count) AS pair_count_variance, STDDEV(port_pair_count) AS pair_count_stddev FROM SECURITYGROUPPORTBINDINGS AS sgpb JOIN ( SELECT p.ID AS port_id, COUNT(*) AS port_pair_count FROM PORTS AS p JOIN ALLOWEDADDRESSPAIRS AS aap ON p.ID = aap.PORT_ID GROUP BY p.ID ) AS port_stats ON sgpb.PORT_ID = port_stats.port_id GROUP BY sgpb.SECURITY_GROUP_ID ORDER BY pair_count_range DESC ), AverageRange AS ( SELECT AVG(pair_count_range) AS avg_pair_count_range FROM inner_cte ) SELECT ic.SECURITY_GROUP_ID, ic.pair_count_range, ic.pair_count_variance, ic.pair_count_stddev, ar.avg_pair_count_range AS benchmark, CASE WHEN ic.pair_count_range > ar.avg_pair_count_range * 1.5 THEN 'HIGH_SPREAD' WHEN ic.pair_count_range < ar.avg_pair_count_range * 0.5 THEN 'LOW_SPREAD' ELSE 'AVERAGE_SPREAD' END AS spread_category FROM inner_cte ic CROSS JOIN AverageRange ar;
sub_questions: For each security group, show the security group ID and the range, variance, and standard deviation of the number of allowed address pairs per port, considering only ports that have at least one allowed address pair.
sub_sqls: SELECT sgpb.SECURITY_GROUP_ID, MAX(port_pair_count) - MIN(port_pair_count) AS pair_count_range, VARIANCE(port_pair_count) AS pair_count_variance, STDDEV(port_pair_count) AS pair_count_stddev FROM SECURITYGROUPPORTBINDINGS AS sgpb JOIN ( SELECT p.ID AS port_id, COUNT(*) AS port_pair_count FROM PORTS AS p JOIN ALLOWEDADDRESSPAIRS AS aap ON p.ID = aap.PORT_ID GROUP BY p.ID ) AS port_stats ON sgpb.PORT_ID = port_stats.port_id GROUP BY sgpb.SECURITY_GROUP_ID ORDER BY pair_count_range DESC;

question: For each port status, report the minimum admin_state_up value and the average standard_attr_id for ports bound with VIF type 'ovs', and also show how each status’s average standard_attr_id deviates from the overall average standard_attr_id across all such ports. Do not return any rounded answers.
sql: WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT MIN(p.ADMIN_STATE_UP) AS min_admin_state_up, AVG(p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID) AS avg_standard_attr_id FROM PORTS p JOIN ML2_PORT_BINDINGS b ON p.ID = b.PORT_ID WHERE b.VIF_TYPE = 'ovs' GROUP BY p.STATUS ), overall_avg AS ( SELECT AVG(avg_standard_attr_id) AS overall_avg_standard_attr_id FROM inner_cte ) SELECT i.min_admin_state_up, i.avg_standard_attr_id, (i.avg_standard_attr_id - o.overall_avg_standard_attr_id) AS deviation_from_overall_avg_standard_attr_id FROM inner_cte i CROSS JOIN overall_avg o;
sub_questions: For each port status, what are the minimum admin_state_up value and the average standard_attr_id for ports that are bound with VIF type 'ovs'?
sub_sqls: SELECT MIN(p.ADMIN_STATE_UP) AS min_admin_state_up, AVG(p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID) AS avg_standard_attr_id FROM PORTS p JOIN ML2_PORT_BINDINGS b ON p.ID = b.PORT_ID WHERE b.VIF_TYPE = 'ovs' GROUP BY p.STATUS;

question: For each IPv4 subnet route, show the destination, next hop, subnet name and CIDR, and the allocation pool’s first and last IP (including the dense rank within each subnet as before). Also include, for each subnet, how many routes it has and the deviation of that subnet’s route count from the average route count across all IPv4 subnets. Do not return any rounded answers.
sql: WITH inner_cte AS (SELECT r.DESTINATION, r.NEXTHOP, s.NAME AS subnet_name, s.CIDR AS subnet_cidr, p.FIRST_IP, p.LAST_IP, DENSE_RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY r.SUBNET_ID ORDER BY r.SUBNET_ID) AS window_column FROM SUBNETROUTES r JOIN SUBNETS s ON r.SUBNET_ID = s.ID JOIN IPALLOCATIONPOOLS p ON s.ID = p.SUBNET_ID WHERE s.IP_VERSION = 4), SubnetRouteCounts AS ( SELECT s.id AS subnet_id, COUNT(r.destination) AS route_count FROM subnets s LEFT JOIN subnetroutes r ON r.subnet_id = s.id WHERE s.ip_version = 4 GROUP BY s.id ), AverageRouteCounts AS ( SELECT AVG(route_count) AS avg_route_count FROM SubnetRouteCounts ) SELECT ic.DESTINATION, ic.NEXTHOP, ic.subnet_name, ic.subnet_cidr, ic.FIRST_IP, ic.LAST_IP, ic.window_column, src.route_count, (src.route_count - arc.avg_route_count) AS deviation_from_avg_route_count FROM inner_cte ic JOIN subnets s ON s.cidr = ic.subnet_cidr AND s.name = ic.subnet_name JOIN SubnetRouteCounts src ON src.subnet_id = s.id CROSS JOIN AverageRouteCounts arc;
sub_questions: Show each subnet route’s destination and next hop together with the subnet name and CIDR, plus the allocation pool’s first and last IP. Also include a dense rank within each subnet (partitioned by subnet ID) ordered by the subnet ID. Only include IPv4 subnets.
sub_sqls: SELECT r.DESTINATION, r.NEXTHOP, s.NAME AS subnet_name, s.CIDR AS subnet_cidr, p.FIRST_IP, p.LAST_IP, DENSE_RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY r.SUBNET_ID ORDER BY r.SUBNET_ID) AS window_column FROM SUBNETROUTES r JOIN SUBNETS s ON r.SUBNET_ID = s.ID JOIN IPALLOCATIONPOOLS p ON s.ID = p.SUBNET_ID WHERE s.IP_VERSION = 4

question: Using the allowed address pairs on the port with ID `25d421c1-c76d-4c26-9550-9f871a1d5034`, return the allowed address pair MAC address, allowed address pair IP address, the port ID, the security group ID bound to that port, and the running average of the port’s standard attribute ID within each port (partitioned by port ID) ordered by the allowed address pair IP address. Also include the port’s tenant ID, the total number of ports owned by that tenant, the average number of ports across all tenants as a benchmark, and classify the tenant as 'HIGH_USER' (at least 50% more than average), 'LOW_USER' (at least 50% less than average), or 'AVERAGE_USER'. Do not return any rounded answers.
sql: WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT aap.MAC_ADDRESS AS allowed_mac_address, aap.IP_ADDRESS AS allowed_ip_address, p.ID AS port_id, sgpb.SECURITY_GROUP_ID AS security_group_id, AVG(p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID) OVER ( PARTITION BY p.ID ORDER BY aap.IP_ADDRESS ) AS window_column FROM SECURITYGROUPPORTBINDINGS AS sgpb JOIN PORTS AS p ON sgpb.PORT_ID = p.ID JOIN ALLOWEDADDRESSPAIRS AS aap ON p.ID = aap.PORT_ID WHERE p.ID = '25d421c1-c76d-4c26-9550-9f871a1d5034' ORDER BY aap.IP_ADDRESS ), TenantPorts AS ( SELECT p2.TENANT_ID AS tenant_id, COUNT(p2.ID) AS total_ports FROM PORTS AS p2 GROUP BY p2.TENANT_ID ), AveragePorts AS ( SELECT AVG(total_ports) AS avg_ports FROM TenantPorts ) SELECT i.allowed_mac_address, i.allowed_ip_address, i.port_id, i.security_group_id, i.window_column, p.TENANT_ID AS tenant_id, tp.total_ports, ap.avg_ports AS benchmark, CASE WHEN tp.total_ports > ap.avg_ports * 1.5 THEN 'HIGH_USER' WHEN tp.total_ports < ap.avg_ports * 0.5 THEN 'LOW_USER' ELSE 'AVERAGE_USER' END AS user_category FROM inner_cte AS i JOIN PORTS AS p ON p.ID = i.port_id JOIN TenantPorts AS tp ON tp.tenant_id = p.TENANT_ID CROSS JOIN AveragePorts AS ap ORDER BY i.allowed_ip_address;
sub_questions: For allowed address pairs on the port with ID `25d421c1-c76d-4c26-9550-9f871a1d5034`, show the allowed address pair MAC address, allowed address pair IP address, the port ID, the security group ID bound to that port, and the running average of the port’s standard attribute ID within each port (partitioned by port ID) ordered by the allowed address pair IP address.
sub_sqls: SELECT aap.MAC_ADDRESS AS allowed_mac_address, aap.IP_ADDRESS AS allowed_ip_address, p.ID AS port_id, sgpb.SECURITY_GROUP_ID AS security_group_id, AVG(p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID) OVER ( PARTITION BY p.ID ORDER BY aap.IP_ADDRESS ) AS window_column FROM SECURITYGROUPPORTBINDINGS AS sgpb JOIN PORTS AS p ON sgpb.PORT_ID = p.ID JOIN ALLOWEDADDRESSPAIRS AS aap ON p.ID = aap.PORT_ID WHERE p.ID = '25d421c1-c76d-4c26-9550-9f871a1d5034' ORDER BY aap.IP_ADDRESS;

question: For subnets whose network has a RBAC action of 'access_as_shared', show the IP version, a label indicating whether the subnet has DHCP enabled ('DHCP' if enabled, 'No DHCP' otherwise), and the number of matching subnets. Include subtotals per IP version and a grand total. Do not return any rounded answers.
sql: WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT s.NAME AS subnet_name, s.CIDR AS subnet_cidr, n.TARGET_TENANT AS rbac_target_tenant, SUM(s.STANDARD_ATTR_ID) OVER ( PARTITION BY s.IP_VERSION ORDER BY s.STANDARD_ATTR_ID ) AS window_column FROM SUBNETS AS s JOIN NETWORKRBACS AS n ON n.OBJECT_ID = s.NETWORK_ID WHERE n.ACTION = 'access_as_shared' ), SubnetSummary AS ( SELECT s.IP_VERSION AS ip_version, CASE WHEN s.ENABLE_DHCP = 1 THEN 'DHCP' ELSE 'No DHCP' END AS dhcp_status, COUNT(*) AS total_subnets FROM inner_cte i JOIN SUBNETS s ON s.NAME = i.subnet_name AND s.CIDR = i.subnet_cidr GROUP BY s.IP_VERSION, dhcp_status ) SELECT CASE WHEN GROUPING(ip_version) = 1 THEN 'GRAND TOTAL' ELSE CAST(ip_version AS CHAR) END AS ip_version, CASE WHEN GROUPING(dhcp_status) = 1 AND GROUPING(ip_version) = 0 THEN 'SUBTOTAL' ELSE dhcp_status END AS dhcp_status, SUM(total_subnets) AS total_subnets FROM SubnetSummary GROUP BY ip_version, dhcp_status WITH ROLLUP;
sub_questions: For subnets whose network has a RBAC action of 'access_as_shared', list the subnet name, its CIDR, the RBAC target tenant, and the running sum of subnet standard attribute IDs within each IP version group ordered by standard attribute ID.
sub_sqls: SELECT s.NAME AS subnet_name, s.CIDR AS subnet_cidr, n.TARGET_TENANT AS rbac_target_tenant, SUM(s.STANDARD_ATTR_ID) OVER ( PARTITION BY s.IP_VERSION ORDER BY s.STANDARD_ATTR_ID ) AS window_column FROM SUBNETS AS s JOIN NETWORKRBACS AS n ON n.OBJECT_ID = s.NETWORK_ID WHERE n.ACTION = 'access_as_shared';

question: For allowed address pairs on the port with ID `25d421c1-c76d-4c26-9550-9f871a1d5034`, show the allowed address pair MAC address, allowed address pair IP address, the port ID, the security group ID bound to that port, and the running average of the port’s standard attribute ID within each port (partitioned by port ID) ordered by the allowed address pair IP address, along with the total number of security group bindings on that port and the average number of security group bindings per port across all ports. question: For ports whose status is DOWN, list the port ID, tenant ID, and MAC address, along with the running sum of standard attribute IDs within each resource type group ordered by standard attribute ID; only include ports whose standard attribute ID is greater than the average standard attribute ID among DOWN ports for the same resource type. Do not return any rounded answers.
sql: WITH inner_cte AS (SELECT p.ID AS port_id, p.TENANT_ID AS tenant_id, p.MAC_ADDRESS AS mac_address, SUM(sa.ID) OVER ( PARTITION BY sa.RESOURCE_TYPE ORDER BY sa.ID ) AS window_column FROM PORTS p JOIN STANDARDATTRIBUTES sa ON sa.ID = p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN'), ResourceTypeAverages AS (SELECT sa.RESOURCE_TYPE, AVG(sa.ID) AS avg_standard_attr_id FROM PORTS p JOIN STANDARDATTRIBUTES sa ON sa.ID = p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' GROUP BY sa.RESOURCE_TYPE) SELECT i.port_id, i.tenant_id, i.mac_address, i.window_column FROM inner_cte i JOIN PORTS p2 ON p2.ID = i.port_id JOIN STANDARDATTRIBUTES sa2 ON sa2.ID = p2.STANDARD_ATTR_ID WHERE sa2.ID > (SELECT avg_standard_attr_id FROM ResourceTypeAverages rta WHERE rta.RESOURCE_TYPE = sa2.RESOURCE_TYPE);
sub_questions: For ports whose status is DOWN, show the port ID, tenant ID, and MAC address, along with the running sum of the standard attribute IDs within each resource type group ordered by standard attribute ID.
sub_sqls: SELECT p.ID AS port_id, p.TENANT_ID AS tenant_id, p.MAC_ADDRESS AS mac_address, SUM(sa.ID) OVER ( PARTITION BY sa.RESOURCE_TYPE ORDER BY sa.ID ) AS window_column FROM PORTS p JOIN STANDARDATTRIBUTES sa ON sa.ID = p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN';

question: For load balancers provided by “haproxy”, list only those whose bytes in are above the average bytes in across all “haproxy” load balancers; return the load balancer name, VIP address, bytes in, total connections, and the same row number window (ordered by load balancer name with a frame of 2 preceding and 1 following rows). Do not return any rounded answers.
sql: WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT lb.NAME AS loadbalancer_name, lb.VIP_ADDRESS AS vip_address, stats.BYTES_IN AS bytes_in, stats.TOTAL_CONNECTIONS AS total_connections, ROW_NUMBER() OVER ( ORDER BY lb.NAME ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND 1 FOLLOWING ) AS window_column FROM LBAAS_LOADBALANCER_STATISTICS AS stats JOIN LBAAS_LOADBALANCERS AS lb ON stats.LOADBALANCER_ID = lb.ID JOIN PROVIDERRESOURCEASSOCIATIONS AS pra ON lb.ID = pra.RESOURCE_ID WHERE pra.PROVIDER_NAME = 'haproxy' ), haproxy_avg AS ( SELECT AVG(stats2.BYTES_IN * 1.0) AS avg_bytes_in FROM LBAAS_LOADBALANCER_STATISTICS AS stats2 JOIN LBAAS_LOADBALANCERS AS lb2 ON stats2.LOADBALANCER_ID = lb2.ID JOIN PROVIDERRESOURCEASSOCIATIONS AS pra2 ON lb2.ID = pra2.RESOURCE_ID WHERE pra2.PROVIDER_NAME = 'haproxy' ) SELECT i.loadbalancer_name, i.vip_address, i.bytes_in, i.total_connections, i.window_column FROM inner_cte AS i CROSS JOIN haproxy_avg AS a WHERE i.bytes_in > a.avg_bytes_in ORDER BY i.loadbalancer_name;
sub_questions: For load balancers provided by “haproxy”, list the load balancer name, VIP address, bytes in, and total connections, and assign row numbers ordered by load balancer name using a window frame of 2 preceding and 1 following rows.
sub_sqls: SELECT lb.NAME AS loadbalancer_name, lb.VIP_ADDRESS AS vip_address, stats.BYTES_IN AS bytes_in, stats.TOTAL_CONNECTIONS AS total_connections, ROW_NUMBER() OVER ( ORDER BY lb.NAME ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND 1 FOLLOWING ) AS window_column FROM LBAAS_LOADBALANCER_STATISTICS AS stats JOIN LBAAS_LOADBALANCERS AS lb ON stats.LOADBALANCER_ID = lb.ID JOIN PROVIDERRESOURCEASSOCIATIONS AS pra ON lb.ID = pra.RESOURCE_ID WHERE pra.PROVIDER_NAME = 'haproxy';

question: Using the allowed address pairs on the port with ID `25d421c1-c76d-4c26-9550-9f871a1d5034`, list the allowed address pair MAC address, allowed address pair IP address, port ID, security group ID bound to that port, and the running average of the port’s standard attribute ID within each port (partitioned by port ID) ordered by the allowed address pair IP address; then return only those rows where the running average is greater than 0. sub_sqls: SELECT aap.MAC_ADDRESS AS allowed_mac_address, aap.IP_ADDRESS AS allowed_ip_address, p.ID AS port_id, sgpb.SECURITY_GROUP_ID AS security_group_id, AVG(p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID) OVER ( PARTITION BY p.ID ORDER BY aap.IP_ADDRESS ) AS window_column FROM SECURITYGROUPPORTBINDINGS AS sgpb JOIN PORTS AS p ON sgpb.PORT_ID = p.ID JOIN ALLOWEDADDRESSPAIRS AS aap ON p.ID = aap.PORT_ID WHERE p.ID = '25d421c1-c76d-4c26-9550-9f871a1d5034' ORDER BY aap.IP_ADDRESS;

question: For each load balancer operating status, show the operating status, the total number of load balancers associated with the “haproxy” provider (only keeping statuses where this count is greater than 1), the average of these per-status totals as a benchmark, and categorize each status as 'HIGH_COUNT' (at least 50% above average), 'LOW_COUNT' (at least 50% below average), or 'AVERAGE_COUNT'. Do not return any rounded answers.
sql: WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT lb.OPERATING_STATUS, COUNT(*) AS total_loadbalancers FROM LBAAS_LOADBALANCERS AS lb JOIN PROVIDERRESOURCEASSOCIATIONS AS pra ON lb.ID = pra.RESOURCE_ID WHERE pra.PROVIDER_NAME = 'haproxy' GROUP BY lb.OPERATING_STATUS HAVING COUNT(*) > 1 ), avg_cte AS ( SELECT AVG(total_loadbalancers) AS avg_loadbalancers FROM inner_cte ) SELECT i.OPERATING_STATUS, i.total_loadbalancers, a.avg_loadbalancers AS benchmark, CASE WHEN i.total_loadbalancers > a.avg_loadbalancers * 1.5 THEN 'HIGH_COUNT' WHEN i.total_loadbalancers < a.avg_loadbalancers * 0.5 THEN 'LOW_COUNT' ELSE 'AVERAGE_COUNT' END AS count_category FROM inner_cte i CROSS JOIN avg_cte a;
sub_questions: For each load balancer operating status, show the operating status and the total number of load balancers that are associated with the “haproxy” provider, only including statuses where the total count of such load balancers is greater than 1.
sub_sqls: SELECT lb.OPERATING_STATUS, COUNT(*) AS total_loadbalancers FROM LBAAS_LOADBALANCERS AS lb JOIN PROVIDERRESOURCEASSOCIATIONS AS pra ON lb.ID = pra.RESOURCE_ID WHERE pra.PROVIDER_NAME = 'haproxy' GROUP BY lb.OPERATING_STATUS HAVING COUNT(*) > 1;

question: For each ACTIVE network, show the network name, its total number of security bindings, the average number of security bindings across all ACTIVE networks as a benchmark, and categorize the network as 'HIGH_BINDINGS' (at least 50% more than average), 'LOW_BINDINGS' (at least 50% less than average), or 'AVERAGE_BINDINGS'. Only include networks that have more than 1 security binding. Do not return any rounded answers.
sql: WITH inner_cte AS (SELECT n.name AS network_name, SUM(1) AS total_security_bindings FROM NETWORKS n JOIN NETWORKSECURITYBINDINGS nsb ON n.id = nsb.network_id WHERE n.status = 'ACTIVE' GROUP BY n.name HAVING SUM(1) > 1), AverageBindings AS ( SELECT AVG(total_security_bindings) AS avg_bindings FROM inner_cte ) SELECT ic.network_name, ic.total_security_bindings, ab.avg_bindings AS benchmark, CASE WHEN ic.total_security_bindings > ab.avg_bindings * 1.5 THEN 'HIGH_BINDINGS' WHEN ic.total_security_bindings < ab.avg_bindings * 0.5 THEN 'LOW_BINDINGS' ELSE 'AVERAGE_BINDINGS' END AS bindings_category FROM inner_cte ic CROSS JOIN AverageBindings ab;
sub_questions: For each network, show the network name and calculate the total number of security bindings for networks that are ACTIVE and have more than 1 security binding in total.
sub_sqls: SELECT n.name AS network_name, SUM(1) AS total_security_bindings FROM NETWORKS n JOIN NETWORKSECURITYBINDINGS nsb ON n.id = nsb.network_id WHERE n.status = 'ACTIVE' GROUP BY n.name HAVING SUM(1) > 1;

question: For each subnet name and its gateway IP, find the maximum IP version among subnets whose network has a RBAC action of 'access_as_shared', keep only groups where that maximum IP version is greater than 3, and also report how many such subnet name/gateway IP groups exist in total along with each group’s deviation from that overall average maximum IP version. Do not return any rounded answers.
sql: WITH inner_cte AS (SELECT s.name, MAX(s.ip_version) AS max_ip_version, s.gateway_ip FROM NETWORKRBACS n JOIN SUBNETS s ON n.object_id = s.network_id WHERE n.action = 'access_as_shared' GROUP BY s.name, s.gateway_ip HAVING MAX(s.ip_version) > 3), avg_cte AS (SELECT AVG(max_ip_version) AS avg_max_ip_version, COUNT(*) AS total_groups FROM inner_cte) SELECT i.name, i.gateway_ip, i.max_ip_version, a.total_groups, (i.max_ip_version - a.avg_max_ip_version) AS deviation_from_avg_max_ip_version FROM inner_cte i CROSS JOIN avg_cte a;
sub_questions: For each subnet name and its gateway IP, find the maximum IP version among subnets whose network has a RBAC action of 'access_as_shared', and only keep subnet name/gateway IP groups where that maximum IP version is greater than 3.
sub_sqls: SELECT s.name, MAX(s.ip_version) AS max_ip_version, s.gateway_ip FROM NETWORKRBACS n JOIN SUBNETS s ON n.object_id = s.network_id WHERE n.action = 'access_as_shared' GROUP BY s.name, s.gateway_ip HAVING MAX(s.ip_version) > 3;

question: For each port status and device owner, considering only ports whose standard attribute resource type is 'ports', list the port status, device owner, number of ports, and earliest standard attribute updated timestamp, but only include groups where at least 80% of the ports have ADMIN_STATE_UP = 1. Do not return any rounded answers.
sql: WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT p.STATUS AS port_status, p.DEVICE_OWNER AS device_owner, COUNT(p.ID) AS port_count, MIN(sa.UPDATED_AT) AS earliest_standard_attr_update FROM PORTS p JOIN STANDARDATTRIBUTES sa ON sa.ID = p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID WHERE sa.RESOURCE_TYPE = 'ports' GROUP BY p.STATUS, p.DEVICE_OWNER ), AdminUpUtilization AS ( SELECT p.STATUS AS port_status, p.DEVICE_OWNER AS device_owner, SUM(CASE WHEN p.ADMIN_STATE_UP = 1 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS admin_up_ports, COUNT(p.ID) AS total_ports FROM PORTS p JOIN STANDARDATTRIBUTES sa ON sa.ID = p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID WHERE sa.RESOURCE_TYPE = 'ports' GROUP BY p.STATUS, p.DEVICE_OWNER ) SELECT i.port_status, i.device_owner, i.port_count, i.earliest_standard_attr_update FROM inner_cte i JOIN AdminUpUtilization a ON a.port_status = i.port_status AND a.device_owner = i.device_owner WHERE a.total_ports > 0 AND (a.admin_up_ports * 1.0 / a.total_ports) >= 0.80;
sub_questions: For each port status and device owner, considering only ports whose standard attribute resource type is 'ports', return the number of ports and the earliest (minimum) standard attribute updated timestamp.
sub_sqls: SELECT p.STATUS AS port_status, p.DEVICE_OWNER AS device_owner, COUNT(p.ID) AS port_count, MIN(sa.UPDATED_AT) AS earliest_standard_attr_update FROM PORTS p JOIN STANDARDATTRIBUTES sa ON sa.ID = p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID WHERE sa.RESOURCE_TYPE = 'ports' GROUP BY p.STATUS, p.DEVICE_OWNER;

question: For each subnet (by subnet name) that has at least one DNS nameserver entry, show the range, variance, and standard deviation (using STDDEV only and never STDDEV_POP) of the number of IP allocation pools per subnet, and also include the overall average number of IP allocation pools per subnet across all such subnets. Do not return any rounded answers.
sql: WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT s.name AS subnet_name, MAX(pool_count) - MIN(pool_count) AS pool_count_range, VARIANCE(pool_count) AS pool_count_variance, STDDEV(pool_count) AS pool_count_stddev FROM subnets AS s JOIN dnsnameservers AS d ON d.subnet_id = s.id JOIN ( SELECT s2.id AS subnet_id, COUNT(*) AS pool_count FROM subnets AS s2 JOIN ipallocationpools AS p ON p.subnet_id = s2.id GROUP BY s2.id, p.id ) AS pool_stats ON pool_stats.subnet_id = s.id GROUP BY s.name ORDER BY pool_count_range DESC ) SELECT inner_cte.subnet_name, inner_cte.pool_count_range, inner_cte.pool_count_variance, inner_cte.pool_count_stddev, avg_stats.avg_pool_count_range FROM inner_cte JOIN ( SELECT AVG(pool_count_range) AS avg_pool_count_range FROM inner_cte ) AS avg_stats ON 1 = 1 ORDER BY inner_cte.pool_count_range DESC;
sub_questions: For each subnet (by subnet name), show the range, variance, and standard deviation of the number of IP allocation pools per subnet, considering only subnets that have at least one DNS nameserver entry.
sub_sqls: SELECT s.name AS subnet_name, MAX(pool_count) - MIN(pool_count) AS pool_count_range, VARIANCE(pool_count) AS pool_count_variance, STDDEV(pool_count) AS pool_count_stddev FROM subnets AS s JOIN dnsnameservers AS d ON d.subnet_id = s.id JOIN ( SELECT s2.id AS subnet_id, COUNT(*) AS pool_count FROM subnets AS s2 JOIN ipallocationpools AS p ON p.subnet_id = s2.id GROUP BY s2.id, p.id ) AS pool_stats ON pool_stats.subnet_id = s.id GROUP BY s.name ORDER BY pool_count_range DESC;

question: For each port status and device owner (considering only DOWN ports that are bound to a security group), return the number of distinct ports and the minimum standard attribute ID, along with the overall average of these per-(status, owner) port counts across all such groups. Do not return any rounded answers.
sql: WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT p.STATUS AS port_status, p.DEVICE_OWNER AS device_owner, COUNT(DISTINCT p.ID) AS port_count, MIN(p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID) AS min_standard_attr_id FROM PORTS p JOIN SECURITYGROUPPORTBINDINGS spb ON p.ID = spb.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' GROUP BY p.STATUS, p.DEVICE_OWNER ) SELECT inner_cte.port_status, inner_cte.device_owner, inner_cte.port_count, inner_cte.min_standard_attr_id, avg_counts.avg_port_count FROM inner_cte JOIN ( SELECT AVG(port_count) AS avg_port_count FROM inner_cte ) AS avg_counts;
sub_questions: For each port status and device owner, considering only ports that are bound to a security group, return the number of distinct ports and the minimum standard attribute ID.
sub_sqls: SELECT p.STATUS AS port_status, p.DEVICE_OWNER AS device_owner, COUNT(DISTINCT p.ID) AS port_count, MIN(p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID) AS min_standard_attr_id FROM PORTS p JOIN SECURITYGROUPPORTBINDINGS spb ON p.ID = spb.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' GROUP BY p.STATUS, p.DEVICE_OWNER;

question: For each tenant, list each ACTIVE load balancer’s name, VIP address, total connections, and bytes in, along with the tenant’s average total connections across its ACTIVE load balancers as a benchmark, and categorize each load balancer as 'HIGH_CONN' (at least 50% above the tenant average), 'LOW_CONN' (at least 50% below the tenant average), or 'AVG_CONN'. Do not return any rounded answers.
sql: WITH inner_cte AS (SELECT lb.NAME, lb.VIP_ADDRESS, stats.TOTAL_CONNECTIONS, stats.BYTES_IN, DENSE_RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY lb.TENANT_ID ORDER BY lb.ID) AS window_column FROM LBAAS_LOADBALANCERS AS lb JOIN LBAAS_LOADBALANCER_STATISTICS AS stats ON lb.ID = stats.LOADBALANCER_ID WHERE lb.PROVISIONING_STATUS = 'ACTIVE'), tenant_avg AS ( SELECT lb.TENANT_ID, AVG(stats.TOTAL_CONNECTIONS) AS avg_total_connections FROM LBAAS_LOADBALANCERS AS lb JOIN LBAAS_LOADBALANCER_STATISTICS AS stats ON lb.ID = stats.LOADBALANCER_ID WHERE lb.PROVISIONING_STATUS = 'ACTIVE' GROUP BY lb.TENANT_ID ) SELECT lb.TENANT_ID, i.NAME, i.VIP_ADDRESS, i.TOTAL_CONNECTIONS, i.BYTES_IN, i.window_column, ta.avg_total_connections AS benchmark, CASE WHEN i.TOTAL_CONNECTIONS > ta.avg_total_connections * 1.5 THEN 'HIGH_CONN' WHEN i.TOTAL_CONNECTIONS < ta.avg_total_connections * 0.5 THEN 'LOW_CONN' ELSE 'AVG_CONN' END AS connection_category FROM inner_cte AS i JOIN LBAAS_LOADBALANCERS AS lb ON lb.NAME = i.NAME AND lb.VIP_ADDRESS = i.VIP_ADDRESS JOIN tenant_avg AS ta ON ta.TENANT_ID = lb.TENANT_ID;
sub_questions: Show each load balancer’s name, VIP address, total connections, and bytes in, and include a dense rank within each tenant ordered by the load balancer ID, considering only load balancers that are ACTIVE.
sub_sqls: SELECT lb.NAME, lb.VIP_ADDRESS, stats.TOTAL_CONNECTIONS, stats.BYTES_IN, DENSE_RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY lb.TENANT_ID ORDER BY lb.ID) AS window_column FROM LBAAS_LOADBALANCERS AS lb JOIN LBAAS_LOADBALANCER_STATISTICS AS stats ON lb.ID = stats.LOADBALANCER_ID WHERE lb.PROVISIONING_STATUS = 'ACTIVE'

question: For each tenant, list the tenant ID, the total number of administratively up ports that have at least one IP allocation, the total number of IP allocations across those ports, the total number of subnet-id rows across those allocations, and also include the average number of such ports per tenant across all tenants. Do not return any rounded answers.
sql: WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT p.id AS port_id, p.tenant_id, p.mac_address, COUNT(ia.ip_address) AS ip_allocation_count, SUM(CASE WHEN ia.subnet_id IS NOT NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS subnet_id_rows FROM ports p JOIN portsecuritybindings psb ON psb.port_id = p.id JOIN ipallocations ia ON ia.port_id = p.id WHERE p.admin_state_up = 1 AND ia.ip_address IS NOT NULL GROUP BY p.id, p.tenant_id, p.mac_address ) SELECT inner_cte.tenant_id AS ports_tenant_id, COUNT(inner_cte.port_id) AS total_admin_up_ports_with_ip_allocations, SUM(inner_cte.ip_allocation_count) AS total_ip_allocations, SUM(inner_cte.subnet_id_rows) AS total_subnet_id_rows, avg_ports.avg_port_count AS avg_ports_per_tenant FROM inner_cte JOIN ( SELECT AVG(port_count) AS avg_port_count FROM ( SELECT COUNT(port_id) AS port_count FROM inner_cte GROUP BY tenant_id ) AS sub ) AS avg_ports GROUP BY inner_cte.tenant_id, avg_ports.avg_port_count;
sub_questions: For each port that is administratively up and has at least one IP allocation, list the port ID, tenant ID, MAC address, the number of IP allocations on that port, and the total number of distinct subnets those IP allocations belong to.
sub_sqls: SELECT p.id AS port_id, p.tenant_id, p.mac_address, COUNT(ia.ip_address) AS ip_allocation_count, SUM(CASE WHEN ia.subnet_id IS NOT NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS subnet_id_rows FROM ports p JOIN portsecuritybindings psb ON psb.port_id = p.id JOIN ipallocations ia ON ia.port_id = p.id WHERE p.admin_state_up = 1 AND ia.ip_address IS NOT NULL GROUP BY p.id, p.tenant_id, p.mac_address;

question: Among ACTIVE networks that have an RBAC rule with the action set to 'access_as_shared', how many distinct target tenants are granted access per network, and which networks have more than 2 target tenants? Do not return any rounded answers.
sql: WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT COUNT(*) AS active_shared_rbac_networks FROM NETWORKS n JOIN NETWORKRBACS r ON n.ID = r.OBJECT_ID WHERE n.STATUS = 'ACTIVE' AND r.ACTION = 'access_as_shared' ) SELECT n.ID AS network_id, n.NAME AS network_name, COUNT(DISTINCT r.TARGET_TENANT) AS distinct_target_tenants FROM NETWORKS n JOIN NETWORKRBACS r ON n.ID = r.OBJECT_ID CROSS JOIN inner_cte WHERE n.STATUS = 'ACTIVE' AND r.ACTION = 'access_as_shared' GROUP BY n.ID, n.NAME HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT r.TARGET_TENANT) > 2;
sub_questions: How many ACTIVE networks have an RBAC rule with the action set to 'access_as_shared'?
sub_sqls: SELECT COUNT(*) AS active_shared_rbac_networks FROM NETWORKS n JOIN NETWORKRBACS r ON n.ID = r.OBJECT_ID WHERE n.STATUS = 'ACTIVE' AND r.ACTION = 'access_as_shared';

question: For ports that are bound to the security group ID 0008e629-5619-41e0-b86c-4eecfeaacb6c, list only those ports whose standard attribute ID running sum within each network (ordered by standard attribute ID) is above the average running sum for that same network; show the port ID, port status, allocated IP address, network ID, the running sum, and the network’s average running sum. Do not return any rounded answers.
sql: WITH inner_cte AS (SELECT p.ID AS port_id, p.STATUS AS port_status, ia.IP_ADDRESS AS ip_address, SUM(p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID) OVER ( PARTITION BY p.NETWORK_ID ORDER BY p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID ) AS window_column FROM SECURITYGROUPPORTBINDINGS sgpb JOIN PORTS p ON sgpb.PORT_ID = p.ID JOIN IPALLOCATIONS ia ON p.ID = ia.PORT_ID WHERE sgpb.SECURITY_GROUP_ID = '0008e629-5619-41e0-b86c-4eecfeaacb6c'), NetworkAverages AS ( SELECT p.NETWORK_ID AS network_id, AVG(inner_cte.window_column) AS avg_window_column FROM inner_cte JOIN PORTS p ON inner_cte.port_id = p.ID GROUP BY p.NETWORK_ID ) SELECT inner_cte.port_id, inner_cte.port_status, inner_cte.ip_address, p.NETWORK_ID AS network_id, inner_cte.window_column, na.avg_window_column FROM inner_cte JOIN PORTS p ON inner_cte.port_id = p.ID JOIN NetworkAverages na ON p.NETWORK_ID = na.network_id WHERE inner_cte.window_column > na.avg_window_column;
sub_questions: For ports that are bound to the security group ID 0008e629-5619-41e0-b86c-4eecfeaacb6c, show the port ID, the port status, the allocated IP address, and the running sum of the port’s standard attribute ID within each network ordered by standard attribute ID.
sub_sqls: SELECT p.ID AS port_id, p.STATUS AS port_status, ia.IP_ADDRESS AS ip_address, SUM(p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID) OVER ( PARTITION BY p.NETWORK_ID ORDER BY p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID ) AS window_column FROM SECURITYGROUPPORTBINDINGS sgpb JOIN PORTS p ON sgpb.PORT_ID = p.ID JOIN IPALLOCATIONS ia ON p.ID = ia.PORT_ID WHERE sgpb.SECURITY_GROUP_ID = '0008e629-5619-41e0-b86c-4eecfeaacb6c';

question: Among the top 10 tenants ranked by the highest coefficient of variation (using STDDEV only and never STDDEV_POP) (standard deviation (using STDDEV only and never STDDEV_POP) divided by average) of allocated IP address string lengths for ports with port security enabled, show each tenant’s ID, the tenant’s coefficient of variation (using STDDEV only and never STDDEV_POP), and whether the tenant has any ports in each port status. Do not return any rounded answers.
sql: WITH inner_cte AS (SELECT p.status, STDDEV(LENGTH(ia.ip_address)) / NULLIF(AVG(LENGTH(ia.ip_address)), 0) AS coefficient_of_variation FROM portsecuritybindings psb JOIN ports p ON psb.port_id = p.id JOIN ipallocations ia ON p.id = ia.port_id WHERE psb.port_security_enabled = 1 GROUP BY p.status HAVING AVG(LENGTH(ia.ip_address)) > 0 ORDER BY coefficient_of_variation DESC) SELECT p.tenant_id, STDDEV(LENGTH(ia.ip_address)) / NULLIF(AVG(LENGTH(ia.ip_address)), 0) AS tenant_coefficient_of_variation, CASE WHEN SUM(CASE WHEN p.status = 'ACTIVE' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) > 0 THEN 'Yes' ELSE 'No' END AS has_active_ports, CASE WHEN SUM(CASE WHEN p.status = 'DOWN' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) > 0 THEN 'Yes' ELSE 'No' END AS has_down_ports, CASE WHEN SUM(CASE WHEN p.status = 'BUILD' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) > 0 THEN 'Yes' ELSE 'No' END AS has_build_ports FROM portsecuritybindings psb JOIN ports p ON psb.port_id = p.id JOIN ipallocations ia ON p.id = ia.port_id JOIN inner_cte ic ON ic.status = p.status WHERE psb.port_security_enabled = 1 GROUP BY p.tenant_id HAVING AVG(LENGTH(ia.ip_address)) > 0 ORDER BY tenant_coefficient_of_variation DESC LIMIT 10;
sub_questions: For each port status, show the status value and the coefficient of variation (standard deviation divided by average) of the length of the allocated IP address strings for ports that have port security enabled.
sub_sqls: SELECT p.status, STDDEV(LENGTH(ia.ip_address)) / NULLIF(AVG(LENGTH(ia.ip_address)), 0) AS coefficient_of_variation FROM portsecuritybindings psb JOIN ports p ON psb.port_id = p.id JOIN ipallocations ia ON p.id = ia.port_id WHERE psb.port_security_enabled = 1 GROUP BY p.status HAVING AVG(LENGTH(ia.ip_address)) > 0 ORDER BY coefficient_of_variation DESC;

question: For each RBAC action, show the action name, the standard deviation (using STDDEV only and never STDDEV_POP) of the IP version numbers of DHCP-enabled subnets on the referenced network, and also include the overall average of these per-action standard deviation (using STDDEV only and never STDDEV_POP)s across all actions (considering only actions that have more than 5 matching subnets). Do not return any rounded answers.
sql: WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT n.ACTION, STDDEV(s.IP_VERSION) AS ip_version_stddev FROM NETWORKRBACS AS n JOIN SUBNETS AS s ON n.OBJECT_ID = s.NETWORK_ID WHERE s.ENABLE_DHCP = 1 GROUP BY n.ACTION HAVING COUNT(*) > 5 ORDER BY ip_version_stddev DESC ) SELECT inner_cte.ACTION, inner_cte.ip_version_stddev, avg_stddevs.avg_ip_version_stddev FROM inner_cte JOIN ( SELECT AVG(ip_version_stddev) AS avg_ip_version_stddev FROM inner_cte ) AS avg_stddevs ORDER BY inner_cte.ip_version_stddev DESC;
sub_questions: For each RBAC action, show the action name and the standard deviation of the IP version numbers of subnets on the network that the RBAC entry refers to, considering only subnets with DHCP enabled and only actions that have more than 5 matching subnets.
sub_sqls: SELECT n.ACTION, STDDEV(s.IP_VERSION) AS ip_version_stddev FROM NETWORKRBACS AS n JOIN SUBNETS AS s ON n.OBJECT_ID = s.NETWORK_ID WHERE s.ENABLE_DHCP = 1 GROUP BY n.ACTION HAVING COUNT(*) > 5 ORDER BY ip_version_stddev DESC;

question: For ports whose status is DOWN, group the results by port status and port-security setting (PORT_SECURITY_ENABLED) and list the port status, a label of the port-security setting ('Enabled' if true, 'Disabled' otherwise), and the number of ports. Include subtotals per port status and a grand total. Do not return any rounded answers.
sql: WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT p.id AS port_id, dense_rank() OVER ( ORDER BY psb.port_security_enabled ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW ) AS window_column FROM ports AS p JOIN portsecuritybindings AS psb ON p.id = psb.port_id WHERE p.status = 'DOWN' ), PortSecurityRollup AS ( SELECT p.status, CASE WHEN psb.port_security_enabled = 1 THEN 'Enabled' ELSE 'Disabled' END AS port_security_status, COUNT(DISTINCT inner_cte.port_id) AS total_ports FROM inner_cte JOIN ports AS p ON inner_cte.port_id = p.id JOIN portsecuritybindings AS psb ON p.id = psb.port_id GROUP BY p.status, port_security_status ) SELECT CASE WHEN GROUPING(status) = 1 THEN 'GRAND TOTAL' ELSE status END AS status, CASE WHEN GROUPING(port_security_status) = 1 AND GROUPING(status) = 0 THEN 'SUBTOTAL' ELSE port_security_status END AS port_security_status, SUM(total_ports) AS total_ports FROM PortSecurityRollup GROUP BY status, port_security_status WITH ROLLUP;
sub_questions: For ports whose status is DOWN, list each port ID and the dense rank of that port when ordering by its port-security setting (PORT_SECURITY_ENABLED), using a window frame that includes the current row and the 2 preceding rows.
sub_sqls: SELECT p.id AS port_id, dense_rank() OVER ( ORDER BY psb.port_security_enabled ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW ) AS window_column FROM ports AS p JOIN portsecuritybindings AS psb ON p.id = psb.port_id WHERE p.status = 'DOWN';

question: List the top 10 port status and device owner combinations (restricted to DOWN ports that are bound to a security group), showing the distinct port count, the minimum standard attribute ID, and whether any of those ports appear in the security group port bindings table. Do not return any rounded answers.
sql: WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT p.STATUS AS port_status, p.DEVICE_OWNER AS device_owner, COUNT(DISTINCT p.ID) AS port_count, MIN(p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID) AS min_standard_attr_id FROM PORTS p JOIN SECURITYGROUPPORTBINDINGS spb ON p.ID = spb.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' GROUP BY p.STATUS, p.DEVICE_OWNER ) SELECT i.port_status, i.device_owner, i.port_count, i.min_standard_attr_id, CASE WHEN COUNT(DISTINCT spb2.PORT_ID) > 0 THEN 'Yes' ELSE 'No' END AS has_security_group_bound_ports FROM inner_cte i LEFT JOIN PORTS p2 ON p2.STATUS = i.port_status AND p2.DEVICE_OWNER = i.device_owner LEFT JOIN SECURITYGROUPPORTBINDINGS spb2 ON p2.ID = spb2.PORT_ID GROUP BY i.port_status, i.device_owner, i.port_count, i.min_standard_attr_id ORDER BY i.port_count DESC LIMIT 10;
sub_questions: For each port status and device owner, considering only ports that are bound to a security group, return the number of distinct ports and the minimum standard attribute ID.
sub_sqls: SELECT p.STATUS AS port_status, p.DEVICE_OWNER AS device_owner, COUNT(DISTINCT p.ID) AS port_count, MIN(p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID) AS min_standard_attr_id FROM PORTS p JOIN SECURITYGROUPPORTBINDINGS spb ON p.ID = spb.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' GROUP BY p.STATUS, p.DEVICE_OWNER;

question: For each RBAC action, show the average, variance, and standard deviation (using STDDEV only and never STDDEV_POP) of the subnet IP version (4 or 6) across subnets whose network is referenced by an RBAC entry, and also include the overall average of these per-action average IP versions across all actions. Do not return any rounded answers.
sql: WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT n.ACTION, AVG(s.IP_VERSION) AS avg_ip_version, VARIANCE(s.IP_VERSION) AS ip_version_variance, STDDEV(s.IP_VERSION) AS ip_version_stddev FROM NETWORKRBACS AS n JOIN SUBNETS AS s ON n.OBJECT_ID = s.NETWORK_ID WHERE s.IP_VERSION = 4 GROUP BY n.ACTION ORDER BY ip_version_variance DESC ) SELECT inner_cte.action, inner_cte.avg_ip_version, inner_cte.ip_version_variance, inner_cte.ip_version_stddev, overall_avg.avg_of_action_avg_ip_version FROM inner_cte JOIN ( SELECT AVG(avg_ip_version) AS avg_of_action_avg_ip_version FROM inner_cte ) AS overall_avg ON 1 = 1;
sub_questions: For each RBAC action, show the average, variance, and standard deviation of the subnet IP version (4 or 6) across subnets whose network is referenced by an RBAC entry.
sub_sqls: SELECT n.ACTION, AVG(s.IP_VERSION) AS avg_ip_version, VARIANCE(s.IP_VERSION) AS ip_version_variance, STDDEV(s.IP_VERSION) AS ip_version_stddev FROM NETWORKRBACS AS n JOIN SUBNETS AS s ON n.OBJECT_ID = s.NETWORK_ID WHERE s.IP_VERSION = 4 GROUP BY n.ACTION ORDER BY ip_version_variance DESC;

question: For each IPv4 subnet (by subnet name), show the subnet name, the average and variance of its DNS nameserver order values, along with the overall average of these per-subnet average DNS order values across all IPv4 subnets. Do not return any rounded answers.
sql: WITH inner_cte AS (SELECT s.NAME AS subnet_name, AVG(d.ORDER) AS avg_dns_order, VARIANCE(d.ORDER) AS dns_order_variance FROM SUBNETS AS s JOIN DNSNAMESERVERS AS d ON s.ID = d.SUBNET_ID WHERE s.IP_VERSION = 4 GROUP BY s.NAME ORDER BY dns_order_variance DESC) SELECT inner_cte.subnet_name, inner_cte.avg_dns_order, inner_cte.dns_order_variance, overall_avg.avg_of_subnet_avg_dns_order FROM inner_cte JOIN ( SELECT AVG(avg_dns_order) AS avg_of_subnet_avg_dns_order FROM inner_cte ) AS overall_avg ORDER BY inner_cte.dns_order_variance DESC;
sub_questions: For each subnet (by subnet name), calculate the average and variance of the DNS nameserver order values for DNS entries associated with that subnet, considering only IPv4 subnets.
sub_sqls: SELECT s.NAME AS subnet_name, AVG(d.ORDER) AS avg_dns_order, VARIANCE(d.ORDER) AS dns_order_variance FROM SUBNETS AS s JOIN DNSNAMESERVERS AS d ON s.ID = d.SUBNET_ID WHERE s.IP_VERSION = 4 GROUP BY s.NAME ORDER BY dns_order_variance DESC;

question: For each port status, show the status, the coefficient of variation (using STDDEV only and never STDDEV_POP) of the ports’ standard attribute IDs (considering only ports that have both a security group port binding and a port security binding), along with the average coefficient of variation (using STDDEV only and never STDDEV_POP) across all statuses. Do not return any rounded answers.
sql: WITH inner_cte AS (SELECT p.status, STDDEV(p.standard_attr_id) / NULLIF(AVG(p.standard_attr_id), 0) AS coefficient_of_variation FROM securitygroupportbindings AS sgpb JOIN ports AS p ON sgpb.port_id = p.id JOIN portsecuritybindings AS psb ON p.id = psb.port_id GROUP BY p.status HAVING AVG(p.standard_attr_id) > 0 ORDER BY coefficient_of_variation DESC) SELECT inner_cte.status, inner_cte.coefficient_of_variation, avg_cov.avg_coefficient_of_variation FROM inner_cte JOIN ( SELECT AVG(coefficient_of_variation) AS avg_coefficient_of_variation FROM inner_cte ) AS avg_cov ON 1 = 1 ORDER BY inner_cte.coefficient_of_variation DESC;
sub_questions: For each port status, show the status and the coefficient of variation of the ports’ standard attribute IDs, considering only ports that have a security group port binding and a port security binding.
sub_sqls: SELECT p.status, STDDEV(p.standard_attr_id) / NULLIF(AVG(p.standard_attr_id), 0) AS coefficient_of_variation FROM securitygroupportbindings AS sgpb JOIN ports AS p ON sgpb.port_id = p.id JOIN portsecuritybindings AS psb ON p.id = psb.port_id GROUP BY p.status HAVING AVG(p.standard_attr_id) > 0 ORDER BY coefficient_of_variation DESC;

question: For each VIF type among administratively up ports, list the VIF type, total number of such ports, the overall average number of such ports across VIF types as a benchmark, and categorize each VIF type as 'HIGH_USER' (at least 50% more than average), 'LOW_USER' (at least 50% less than average), or 'AVERAGE_USER'. Do not return any rounded answers.
sql: WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT b.PORT_ID, b.HOST, b.VIF_TYPE, b.VNIC_TYPE, p.TENANT_ID, p.NETWORK_ID, p.MAC_ADDRESS, p.STATUS, p.DEVICE_OWNER, AVG(p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID) OVER ( PARTITION BY b.VIF_TYPE ORDER BY p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND 2 FOLLOWING ) AS window_column FROM ML2_PORT_BINDINGS AS b JOIN PORTS AS p ON b.PORT_ID = p.ID JOIN PORTSECURITYBINDINGS AS psb ON p.ID = psb.PORT_ID WHERE p.ADMIN_STATE_UP = 1 ), VifTypePorts AS ( SELECT VIF_TYPE, COUNT(PORT_ID) AS total_ports FROM inner_cte GROUP BY VIF_TYPE ), AveragePorts AS ( SELECT AVG(total_ports) AS avg_ports FROM VifTypePorts ) SELECT vtp.VIF_TYPE, vtp.total_ports, ap.avg_ports AS benchmark, CASE WHEN vtp.total_ports > ap.avg_ports * 1.5 THEN 'HIGH_USER' WHEN vtp.total_ports < ap.avg_ports * 0.5 THEN 'LOW_USER' ELSE 'AVERAGE_USER' END AS user_category FROM VifTypePorts vtp CROSS JOIN AveragePorts ap;
sub_questions: For ports that are administratively up, show the port ID, host, VIF type, VNIC type, tenant ID, network ID, MAC address, status, device owner, and the average standard attribute ID in a window of 2 preceding and 2 following rows partitioned by VIF type and ordered by standard attribute ID.
sub_sqls: SELECT b.PORT_ID, b.HOST, b.VIF_TYPE, b.VNIC_TYPE, p.TENANT_ID, p.NETWORK_ID, p.MAC_ADDRESS, p.STATUS, p.DEVICE_OWNER, AVG(p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID) OVER ( PARTITION BY b.VIF_TYPE ORDER BY p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND 2 FOLLOWING ) AS window_column FROM ML2_PORT_BINDINGS AS b JOIN PORTS AS p ON b.PORT_ID = p.ID JOIN PORTSECURITYBINDINGS AS psb ON p.ID = psb.PORT_ID WHERE p.ADMIN_STATE_UP = 1;

question: For each port that is bound to a security group and has admin_state_up = 1, list the port ID, tenant ID, port name, the number of security group bindings for that port, the total number of DNS records associated with the port, and the deviation of that port’s security group binding count from the average security group binding count across all such ports. Do not return any rounded answers.
sql: WITH inner_cte AS (SELECT p.id AS port_id, p.tenant_id, p.name AS port_name, COUNT(sgpb.security_group_id) AS security_group_binding_count, SUM(CASE WHEN pd.port_id IS NULL THEN 0 ELSE 1 END) AS dns_record_count FROM SECURITYGROUPPORTBINDINGS sgpb JOIN PORTS p ON sgpb.port_id = p.id LEFT JOIN PORTDNSES pd ON p.id = pd.port_id WHERE p.admin_state_up = 1 GROUP BY p.id, p.tenant_id, p.name), avg_cte AS ( SELECT AVG(security_group_binding_count) AS avg_sg_binding_count FROM inner_cte ) SELECT i.port_id, i.tenant_id, i.port_name, i.security_group_binding_count, i.dns_record_count, (i.security_group_binding_count - a.avg_sg_binding_count) AS deviation_from_avg_sg_binding_count FROM inner_cte i CROSS JOIN avg_cte a;
sub_questions: For each port that is bound to a security group and has admin_state_up = 1, list the port ID, tenant ID, port name, and the number of security group bindings for that port along with the total number of DNS records associated with the port.
sub_sqls: SELECT p.id AS port_id, p.tenant_id, p.name AS port_name, COUNT(sgpb.security_group_id) AS security_group_binding_count, SUM(CASE WHEN pd.port_id IS NULL THEN 0 ELSE 1 END) AS dns_record_count FROM SECURITYGROUPPORTBINDINGS sgpb JOIN PORTS p ON sgpb.port_id = p.id LEFT JOIN PORTDNSES pd ON p.id = pd.port_id WHERE p.admin_state_up = 1 GROUP BY p.id, p.tenant_id, p.name;

question: For each subnet name, show the subnet name, the range and variance of allocation pool starting IP addresses (FIRST_IP) across that subnet’s IP allocation pools, and the number of allocation pools. Consider only routes whose next hop is 10.30.19.197/8, and include subtotals per subnet and a grand total. Do not return any rounded answers.
sql: WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT s.NAME AS subnet_name, MAX(p.FIRST_IP) - MIN(p.FIRST_IP) AS first_ip_range, VARIANCE(p.FIRST_IP) AS first_ip_variance FROM SUBNETROUTES r JOIN SUBNETS s ON r.SUBNET_ID = s.ID JOIN IPALLOCATIONPOOLS p ON s.ID = p.SUBNET_ID WHERE r.NEXTHOP = '10.30.19.197/8' GROUP BY s.NAME ORDER BY first_ip_range DESC ) SELECT CASE WHEN GROUPING(subnet_name) = 1 THEN 'GRAND TOTAL' ELSE subnet_name END AS subnet_name, SUM(first_ip_range) AS total_first_ip_range, AVG(first_ip_variance) AS avg_first_ip_variance, COUNT(*) AS contributing_subnet_rows FROM inner_cte GROUP BY subnet_name WITH ROLLUP;
sub_questions: For each subnet name, calculate the range and variance of the allocation pool starting IP addresses (FIRST_IP) across that subnet’s IP allocation pools, considering only routes whose next hop is 10.30.19.197/8.
sub_sqls: SELECT s.NAME AS subnet_name, MAX(p.FIRST_IP) - MIN(p.FIRST_IP) AS first_ip_range, VARIANCE(p.FIRST_IP) AS first_ip_variance FROM SUBNETROUTES r JOIN SUBNETS s ON r.SUBNET_ID = s.ID JOIN IPALLOCATIONPOOLS p ON s.ID = p.SUBNET_ID WHERE r.NEXTHOP = '10.30.19.197/8' GROUP BY s.NAME ORDER BY first_ip_range DESC;

question: For each port status, show the status, the variance of the standard attribute ID across ports that have an IP allocation, the overall average variance across all statuses as a benchmark, and categorize each status as 'HIGH_VARIANCE' (at least 50% above the benchmark), 'LOW_VARIANCE' (at least 50% below the benchmark), or 'AVERAGE_VARIANCE'. Do not return any rounded answers.
sql: WITH inner_cte AS (SELECT p.STATUS, VARIANCE(p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID) AS standard_attr_id_variance FROM PORTS AS p JOIN IPALLOCATIONS AS ia ON p.ID = ia.PORT_ID WHERE p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID IS NOT NULL GROUP BY p.STATUS ORDER BY standard_attr_id_variance DESC), AverageVariance AS ( SELECT AVG(standard_attr_id_variance) AS avg_variance FROM inner_cte ) SELECT i.STATUS, i.standard_attr_id_variance, av.avg_variance AS benchmark, CASE WHEN i.standard_attr_id_variance > av.avg_variance * 1.5 THEN 'HIGH_VARIANCE' WHEN i.standard_attr_id_variance < av.avg_variance * 0.5 THEN 'LOW_VARIANCE' ELSE 'AVERAGE_VARIANCE' END AS variance_category FROM inner_cte i CROSS JOIN AverageVariance av;
sub_questions: For each port status, show the status and the variance of the standard attribute ID across ports that have an IP allocation.
sub_sqls: SELECT p.STATUS, VARIANCE(p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID) AS standard_attr_id_variance FROM PORTS AS p JOIN IPALLOCATIONS AS ia ON p.ID = ia.PORT_ID WHERE p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID IS NOT NULL GROUP BY p.STATUS ORDER BY standard_attr_id_variance DESC;

question: Using the DOWN-port listing (port ID, tenant ID, host, VIF type, allocated IP address, and the row number ordered by IP address with a window frame of 2 preceding rows and 1 following row) as an inner result, return only the tenants whose number of DOWN ports is greater than the average number of DOWN ports per tenant, and show each qualifying tenant ID with its total DOWN-port count. Do not return any rounded answers.
sql: WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT p.ID AS port_id, p.TENANT_ID AS tenant_id, b.HOST AS host, b.VIF_TYPE AS vif_type, ia.IP_ADDRESS AS ip_address, ROW_NUMBER() OVER ( ORDER BY ia.IP_ADDRESS ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND 1 FOLLOWING ) AS window_column FROM ML2_PORT_BINDINGS b JOIN PORTS p ON b.PORT_ID = p.ID JOIN IPALLOCATIONS ia ON p.ID = ia.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' ), TenantDownPorts AS ( SELECT tenant_id, COUNT(port_id) AS total_down_ports FROM inner_cte GROUP BY tenant_id ) SELECT tenant_id, total_down_ports FROM TenantDownPorts WHERE total_down_ports > (SELECT AVG(total_down_ports) FROM TenantDownPorts);
sub_questions: For ports whose status is DOWN, list the port ID, tenant ID, host, VIF type, and allocated IP address, and assign row numbers ordered by IP address using a window frame of 2 preceding rows and 1 following row.
sub_sqls: SELECT p.ID AS port_id, p.TENANT_ID AS tenant_id, b.HOST AS host, b.VIF_TYPE AS vif_type, ia.IP_ADDRESS AS ip_address, ROW_NUMBER() OVER ( ORDER BY ia.IP_ADDRESS ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND 1 FOLLOWING ) AS window_column FROM ML2_PORT_BINDINGS b JOIN PORTS p ON b.PORT_ID = p.ID JOIN IPALLOCATIONS ia ON p.ID = ia.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN';

question: Considering only subnets with IP version 4 or 6, list the top 10 RBAC actions (ranked by the subnet IP version range) and show for each action: the action name, the average subnet IP version, the IP version range (max minus min), the variance of the subnet IP version, and whether any of the referenced subnets have DHCP enabled. Do not return any rounded answers.
sql: WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT n.ACTION AS rbac_action, AVG(s.IP_VERSION) AS avg_ip_version, MAX(s.IP_VERSION) - MIN(s.IP_VERSION) AS ip_version_range, VARIANCE(s.IP_VERSION) AS ip_version_variance FROM NETWORKRBACS AS n JOIN SUBNETS AS s ON n.OBJECT_ID = s.NETWORK_ID WHERE s.IP_VERSION IN (4, 6) GROUP BY n.ACTION ORDER BY ip_version_range DESC ) SELECT i.rbac_action, i.avg_ip_version, i.ip_version_range, i.ip_version_variance, CASE WHEN COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN s.ENABLE_DHCP = 1 THEN s.ID END) > 0 THEN 'Yes' ELSE 'No' END AS has_dhcp_enabled_subnet FROM inner_cte i JOIN NETWORKRBACS n ON n.ACTION = i.rbac_action JOIN SUBNETS s ON s.NETWORK_ID = n.OBJECT_ID AND s.IP_VERSION IN (4, 6) GROUP BY i.rbac_action, i.avg_ip_version, i.ip_version_range, i.ip_version_variance ORDER BY i.ip_version_range DESC LIMIT 10;
sub_questions: For each RBAC action, show the action name and compute the average, range (max minus min), and variance of the subnet IP version for subnets whose network is referenced by that RBAC entry.
sub_sqls: SELECT n.ACTION AS rbac_action, AVG(s.IP_VERSION) AS avg_ip_version, MAX(s.IP_VERSION) - MIN(s.IP_VERSION) AS ip_version_range, VARIANCE(s.IP_VERSION) AS ip_version_variance FROM NETWORKRBACS AS n JOIN SUBNETS AS s ON n.OBJECT_ID = s.NETWORK_ID WHERE s.IP_VERSION IN (4, 6) GROUP BY n.ACTION ORDER BY ip_version_range DESC;

question: For each RBAC action, list the action, the average/variance/standard deviation (using STDDEV only and never STDDEV_POP) of the subnet IP version (considering only IPv4 subnets) for subnets whose network is referenced by an RBAC entry, and the total number of distinct subnets involved. Do not repeat the action if it is the same as the previous row, and include a grand total row across all actions. Do not return any rounded answers.
sql: WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT n.ACTION, AVG(s.IP_VERSION) AS avg_ip_version, VARIANCE(s.IP_VERSION) AS ip_version_variance, STDDEV(s.IP_VERSION) AS ip_version_stddev FROM NETWORKRBACS AS n JOIN SUBNETS AS s ON n.OBJECT_ID = s.NETWORK_ID WHERE s.IP_VERSION = 4 GROUP BY n.ACTION ORDER BY ip_version_variance DESC ) SELECT CASE WHEN LAG(action) OVER (ORDER BY action_sort, action) = action THEN NULL ELSE action END AS action, avg_ip_version, ip_version_variance, ip_version_stddev, distinct_subnets FROM ( SELECT CASE WHEN GROUPING(i.action) = 1 THEN 'zzz' ELSE i.action END AS action_sort, CASE WHEN GROUPING(i.action) = 1 THEN 'TOTAL' ELSE i.action END AS action, MAX(i.avg_ip_version) AS avg_ip_version, MAX(i.ip_version_variance) AS ip_version_variance, MAX(i.ip_version_stddev) AS ip_version_stddev, COUNT(DISTINCT s.id) AS distinct_subnets FROM inner_cte i JOIN NETWORKRBACS n ON n.action = i.action JOIN SUBNETS s ON s.network_id = n.object_id WHERE s.ip_version = 4 GROUP BY i.action WITH ROLLUP ) AS tbltmp ORDER BY action_sort, action;
sub_questions: For each RBAC action, show the average, variance, and standard deviation of the subnet IP version (4 or 6) across subnets whose network is referenced by an RBAC entry.
sub_sqls: SELECT n.ACTION, AVG(s.IP_VERSION) AS avg_ip_version, VARIANCE(s.IP_VERSION) AS ip_version_variance, STDDEV(s.IP_VERSION) AS ip_version_stddev FROM NETWORKRBACS AS n JOIN SUBNETS AS s ON n.OBJECT_ID = s.NETWORK_ID WHERE s.IP_VERSION = 4 GROUP BY n.ACTION ORDER BY ip_version_variance DESC;

question: For the top 3 networks that have the most subnets (considering only RBAC entries where the action is 'access_as_shared'), return the network object ID, the subnet count, the average subnet count across these top networks as a benchmark, and categorize each network as 'ABOVE_BENCHMARK' (at least 50% more than the benchmark), 'BELOW_BENCHMARK' (at least 50% less than the benchmark), or 'NEAR_BENCHMARK'. Do not return any rounded answers.
sql: WITH inner_cte AS (SELECT n.OBJECT_ID AS network_id, COUNT(*) AS subnet_count FROM NETWORKRBACS AS n JOIN SUBNETS AS s ON n.OBJECT_ID = s.NETWORK_ID WHERE n.ACTION = 'access_as_shared' GROUP BY n.OBJECT_ID ORDER BY COUNT(*) DESC LIMIT 3), AverageSubnets AS ( SELECT AVG(subnet_count) AS avg_subnet_count FROM inner_cte ) SELECT ic.network_id, ic.subnet_count, a.avg_subnet_count AS benchmark, CASE WHEN ic.subnet_count > a.avg_subnet_count * 1.5 THEN 'ABOVE_BENCHMARK' WHEN ic.subnet_count < a.avg_subnet_count * 0.5 THEN 'BELOW_BENCHMARK' ELSE 'NEAR_BENCHMARK' END AS subnet_category FROM inner_cte ic CROSS JOIN AverageSubnets a;
sub_questions: List the top 3 networks that have the most subnets, considering only RBAC entries where the action is 'access_as_shared'. For each of these networks, return the network object ID and the number of subnets on that network.
sub_sqls: SELECT n.OBJECT_ID AS network_id, COUNT(*) AS subnet_count FROM NETWORKRBACS AS n JOIN SUBNETS AS s ON n.OBJECT_ID = s.NETWORK_ID WHERE n.ACTION = 'access_as_shared' GROUP BY n.OBJECT_ID ORDER BY COUNT(*) DESC LIMIT 3;

question: For IPv4 subnets, list the subnet name, tenant ID, network ID, IP version, CIDR, gateway IP, DHCP enabled flag, the allocation pool’s first and last IP, and the maximum subnet standard attribute ID considering the current row and the next 2 rows when ordered by subnet ID; only include rows where the allocation pool’s first IP is the minimum first IP for that subnet. Do not return any rounded answers.
sql: WITH inner_cte AS (SELECT s.NAME, s.TENANT_ID, s.NETWORK_ID, s.IP_VERSION, s.CIDR, s.GATEWAY_IP, s.ENABLE_DHCP, p.FIRST_IP, p.LAST_IP, MAX(s.STANDARD_ATTR_ID) OVER ( ORDER BY s.ID ROWS BETWEEN CURRENT ROW AND 2 FOLLOWING ) AS max_standard_attr_id_next2 FROM SUBNETS AS s JOIN IPALLOCATIONPOOLS AS p ON s.ID = p.SUBNET_ID WHERE s.IP_VERSION = 4) SELECT i.NAME, i.TENANT_ID, i.NETWORK_ID, i.IP_VERSION, i.CIDR, i.GATEWAY_IP, i.ENABLE_DHCP, i.FIRST_IP, i.LAST_IP, i.max_standard_attr_id_next2 FROM inner_cte AS i JOIN SUBNETS AS s2 ON s2.TENANT_ID = i.TENANT_ID JOIN IPALLOCATIONPOOLS AS p2 ON p2.SUBNET_ID = s2.ID WHERE i.FIRST_IP = ( SELECT MIN(p3.FIRST_IP) FROM IPALLOCATIONPOOLS AS p3 WHERE p3.SUBNET_ID = s2.ID );
sub_questions: For each subnet, show the subnet name, tenant ID, network ID, IP version, CIDR, gateway IP, DHCP enabled flag, the allocation pool’s first IP and last IP, and the maximum subnet standard attribute ID considering the current row and the next 2 rows when ordered by subnet ID.
sub_sqls: SELECT s.NAME, s.TENANT_ID, s.NETWORK_ID, s.IP_VERSION, s.CIDR, s.GATEWAY_IP, s.ENABLE_DHCP, p.FIRST_IP, p.LAST_IP, MAX(s.STANDARD_ATTR_ID) OVER ( ORDER BY s.ID ROWS BETWEEN CURRENT ROW AND 2 FOLLOWING ) AS max_standard_attr_id_next2 FROM SUBNETS AS s JOIN IPALLOCATIONPOOLS AS p ON s.ID = p.SUBNET_ID WHERE s.IP_VERSION = 4;

question: For each network status and whether the network is external or internal, show the network status, the external status label ('External' if the network appears in EXTERNALNETWORKS, 'Internal' otherwise), and compute both the variance and the standard deviation (using STDDEV only and never STDDEV_POP) of PORT_SECURITY_ENABLED across networks that have at least one security binding. Include subtotals per network status and a grand total. Do not return any rounded answers.
sql: WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT n.STATUS AS network_status, VARIANCE(nsb.PORT_SECURITY_ENABLED) AS port_security_enabled_variance, STDDEV(nsb.PORT_SECURITY_ENABLED) AS port_security_enabled_stddev FROM NETWORKS AS n JOIN NETWORKSECURITYBINDINGS AS nsb ON n.ID = nsb.NETWORK_ID GROUP BY n.STATUS ORDER BY port_security_enabled_variance DESC ), NetworkStatusExternal AS ( SELECT n.status, CASE WHEN en.network_id IS NOT NULL THEN 'External' ELSE 'Internal' END AS external_status, VARIANCE(nsb.PORT_SECURITY_ENABLED) AS port_security_enabled_variance, STDDEV(nsb.PORT_SECURITY_ENABLED) AS port_security_enabled_stddev FROM networks n JOIN networksecuritybindings nsb ON n.id = nsb.network_id LEFT JOIN externalnetworks en ON n.id = en.network_id GROUP BY n.status, external_status ) SELECT CASE WHEN GROUPING(nse.status) = 1 THEN 'GRAND TOTAL' ELSE nse.status END AS network_status, CASE WHEN GROUPING(nse.external_status) = 1 AND GROUPING(nse.status) = 0 THEN 'SUBTOTAL' ELSE nse.external_status END AS external_status, VARIANCE(nse.port_security_enabled_variance) AS port_security_enabled_variance, STDDEV(nse.port_security_enabled_stddev) AS port_security_enabled_stddev FROM NetworkStatusExternal nse CROSS JOIN inner_cte GROUP BY nse.status, nse.external_status WITH ROLLUP;
sub_questions: For each network status, show the status and compute both the variance and the standard deviation of the security group binding order (PORT_SECURITY_ENABLED) across networks that have at least one security binding.
sub_sqls: SELECT n.STATUS AS network_status, VARIANCE(nsb.PORT_SECURITY_ENABLED) AS port_security_enabled_variance, STDDEV(nsb.PORT_SECURITY_ENABLED) AS port_security_enabled_stddev FROM NETWORKS AS n JOIN NETWORKSECURITYBINDINGS AS nsb ON n.ID = nsb.NETWORK_ID GROUP BY n.STATUS ORDER BY port_security_enabled_variance DESC;

question: For load balancers that are ONLINE, show the load balancer ID, name, provider name, VIP address, and the rank of each load balancer within its provider group ordered by total connections, along with the deviation of each load balancer’s total connections from the average total connections of ONLINE load balancers within the same provider. Do not return any rounded answers.
sql: WITH inner_cte AS (SELECT lb.ID AS loadbalancer_id, lb.NAME AS loadbalancer_name, pra.PROVIDER_NAME AS provider_name, lb.VIP_ADDRESS AS vip_address, RANK() OVER ( PARTITION BY pra.PROVIDER_NAME ORDER BY stats.TOTAL_CONNECTIONS ) AS window_column FROM LBAAS_LOADBALANCER_STATISTICS AS stats JOIN LBAAS_LOADBALANCERS AS lb ON stats.LOADBALANCER_ID = lb.ID JOIN PROVIDERRESOURCEASSOCIATIONS AS pra ON lb.ID = pra.RESOURCE_ID WHERE lb.OPERATING_STATUS = 'ONLINE'), provider_avg AS ( SELECT pra.PROVIDER_NAME AS provider_name, AVG(stats.TOTAL_CONNECTIONS) AS avg_total_connections FROM LBAAS_LOADBALANCER_STATISTICS AS stats JOIN LBAAS_LOADBALANCERS AS lb ON stats.LOADBALANCER_ID = lb.ID JOIN PROVIDERRESOURCEASSOCIATIONS AS pra ON lb.ID = pra.RESOURCE_ID WHERE lb.OPERATING_STATUS = 'ONLINE' GROUP BY pra.PROVIDER_NAME ) SELECT i.loadbalancer_id, i.loadbalancer_name, i.provider_name, i.vip_address, i.window_column AS rank_within_provider_by_total_connections, (stats.TOTAL_CONNECTIONS - pa.avg_total_connections) AS deviation_from_provider_avg_total_connections FROM inner_cte i JOIN LBAAS_LOADBALANCER_STATISTICS AS stats ON stats.LOADBALANCER_ID = i.loadbalancer_id JOIN provider_avg pa ON pa.provider_name = i.provider_name;
sub_questions: For load balancers that are ONLINE, show the load balancer ID, name, provider name, VIP address, and the rank of each load balancer within its provider group ordered by total connections.
sub_sqls: SELECT lb.ID AS loadbalancer_id, lb.NAME AS loadbalancer_name, pra.PROVIDER_NAME AS provider_name, lb.VIP_ADDRESS AS vip_address, RANK() OVER ( PARTITION BY pra.PROVIDER_NAME ORDER BY stats.TOTAL_CONNECTIONS ) AS window_column FROM LBAAS_LOADBALANCER_STATISTICS AS stats JOIN LBAAS_LOADBALANCERS AS lb ON stats.LOADBALANCER_ID = lb.ID JOIN PROVIDERRESOURCEASSOCIATIONS AS pra ON lb.ID = pra.RESOURCE_ID WHERE lb.OPERATING_STATUS = 'ONLINE';

question: For each VIF type, find the VIF type and the highest windowed average of the admin_state_up flag (computed over 2 preceding and 2 following rows ordered by MAC address) among ports that are DOWN. Do not return any rounded answers.
sql: WITH inner_cte AS (SELECT p.NAME, p.MAC_ADDRESS, p.ADMIN_STATE_UP, b.HOST, b.VIF_TYPE, AVG(p.ADMIN_STATE_UP) OVER ( PARTITION BY b.VIF_TYPE ORDER BY p.MAC_ADDRESS ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND 2 FOLLOWING ) AS window_column FROM PORTS AS p JOIN ML2_PORT_BINDINGS AS b ON p.ID = b.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' ORDER BY p.MAC_ADDRESS) SELECT VIF_TYPE, MAX(window_column) AS max_windowed_avg_admin_state_up FROM inner_cte GROUP BY VIF_TYPE;
sub_questions: For ports that are DOWN, show the port name, MAC address, admin_state_up flag, binding host, VIF type, and the average admin_state_up in a window of 2 preceding and 2 following rows partitioned by VIF type and ordered by MAC address.
sub_sqls: SELECT p.NAME, p.MAC_ADDRESS, p.ADMIN_STATE_UP, b.HOST, b.VIF_TYPE, AVG(p.ADMIN_STATE_UP) OVER ( PARTITION BY b.VIF_TYPE ORDER BY p.MAC_ADDRESS ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND 2 FOLLOWING ) AS window_column FROM PORTS AS p JOIN ML2_PORT_BINDINGS AS b ON p.ID = b.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' ORDER BY p.MAC_ADDRESS;

question: For each RBAC action, show the average, variance, and standard deviation (using STDDEV only and never STDDEV_POP) of the subnet IP version (4 or 6) across subnets whose network is referenced by an RBAC entry, and also include the deviation of each action’s average IP version from the overall average across all actions. Do not return any rounded answers.
sql: WITH inner_cte AS (SELECT n.ACTION, AVG(s.IP_VERSION) AS avg_ip_version, VARIANCE(s.IP_VERSION) AS ip_version_variance, STDDEV(s.IP_VERSION) AS ip_version_stddev FROM NETWORKRBACS AS n JOIN SUBNETS AS s ON n.OBJECT_ID = s.NETWORK_ID WHERE s.IP_VERSION = 4 GROUP BY n.ACTION ORDER BY ip_version_variance DESC), overall_avg AS ( SELECT AVG(avg_ip_version) AS overall_avg_ip_version FROM inner_cte ) SELECT i.ACTION, i.avg_ip_version, i.ip_version_variance, i.ip_version_stddev, (i.avg_ip_version - o.overall_avg_ip_version) AS deviation_from_overall_avg FROM inner_cte i CROSS JOIN overall_avg o;
sub_questions: For each RBAC action, show the average, variance, and standard deviation of the subnet IP version (4 or 6) across subnets whose network is referenced by an RBAC entry.
sub_sqls: SELECT n.ACTION, AVG(s.IP_VERSION) AS avg_ip_version, VARIANCE(s.IP_VERSION) AS ip_version_variance, STDDEV(s.IP_VERSION) AS ip_version_stddev FROM NETWORKRBACS AS n JOIN SUBNETS AS s ON n.OBJECT_ID = s.NETWORK_ID WHERE s.IP_VERSION = 4 GROUP BY n.ACTION ORDER BY ip_version_variance DESC;

question: For each IPv4 subnet (by subnet name), return the coefficient of variation (using STDDEV only and never STDDEV_POP) of the DNS nameserver order values across all DNS nameservers on that subnet, along with the deviation of that coefficient from the average coefficient of variation (using STDDEV only and never STDDEV_POP) across all IPv4 subnets. Do not return any rounded answers.
sql: WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT s.name AS subnet_name, STDDEV(d.ORDER) / NULLIF(AVG(d.ORDER), 0) AS coefficient_of_variation FROM subnets AS s JOIN dnsnameservers AS d ON d.subnet_id = s.id JOIN ipallocationpools AS p ON p.subnet_id = s.id WHERE s.ip_version = 4 GROUP BY s.name HAVING AVG(d.ORDER) > 0 ORDER BY coefficient_of_variation DESC ), avg_cte AS ( SELECT AVG(coefficient_of_variation) AS avg_coefficient_of_variation FROM inner_cte ) SELECT i.subnet_name, i.coefficient_of_variation, (i.coefficient_of_variation - a.avg_coefficient_of_variation) AS deviation_from_avg FROM inner_cte i CROSS JOIN avg_cte a ORDER BY deviation_from_avg DESC;
sub_questions: For each subnet (by subnet name), return the coefficient of variation of the DNS nameserver order values across all DNS nameservers on that subnet, considering only IPv4 subnets.
sub_sqls: SELECT s.name AS subnet_name, STDDEV(d.ORDER) / NULLIF(AVG(d.ORDER), 0) AS coefficient_of_variation FROM subnets AS s JOIN dnsnameservers AS d ON d.subnet_id = s.id JOIN ipallocationpools AS p ON p.subnet_id = s.id WHERE s.ip_version = 4 GROUP BY s.name HAVING AVG(d.ORDER) > 0 ORDER BY coefficient_of_variation DESC;

question: For ACTIVE load balancers, list the load balancer name, VIP address, bytes in, total connections, provider name, and the dense rank within each tenant ordered by load balancer ID, but only include those whose total connections are greater than the average total connections for ACTIVE load balancers in the same provider. Do not return any rounded answers.
sql: WITH inner_cte AS (SELECT lb.NAME AS loadbalancer_name, lb.VIP_ADDRESS AS vip_address, stats.BYTES_IN AS bytes_in, stats.TOTAL_CONNECTIONS AS total_connections, pra.PROVIDER_NAME AS provider_name, DENSE_RANK() OVER ( PARTITION BY lb.TENANT_ID ORDER BY lb.ID ) AS window_column FROM LBAAS_LOADBALANCER_STATISTICS AS stats JOIN LBAAS_LOADBALANCERS AS lb ON stats.LOADBALANCER_ID = lb.ID JOIN PROVIDERRESOURCEASSOCIATIONS AS pra ON lb.ID = pra.RESOURCE_ID WHERE lb.PROVISIONING_STATUS = 'ACTIVE'), ProviderAverages AS ( SELECT provider_name, AVG(total_connections) AS avg_total_connections FROM inner_cte GROUP BY provider_name ) SELECT i.loadbalancer_name, i.vip_address, i.bytes_in, i.total_connections, i.provider_name, i.window_column FROM inner_cte i JOIN ProviderAverages pa ON i.provider_name = pa.provider_name WHERE i.total_connections > pa.avg_total_connections;
sub_questions: Show each load balancer’s name, VIP address, bytes in, total connections, and provider name, and include a dense rank within each tenant ordered by the load balancer ID, considering only load balancers that are ACTIVE.
sub_sqls: SELECT lb.NAME AS loadbalancer_name, lb.VIP_ADDRESS AS vip_address, stats.BYTES_IN AS bytes_in, stats.TOTAL_CONNECTIONS AS total_connections, pra.PROVIDER_NAME AS provider_name, DENSE_RANK() OVER ( PARTITION BY lb.TENANT_ID ORDER BY lb.ID ) AS window_column FROM LBAAS_LOADBALANCER_STATISTICS AS stats JOIN LBAAS_LOADBALANCERS AS lb ON stats.LOADBALANCER_ID = lb.ID JOIN PROVIDERRESOURCEASSOCIATIONS AS pra ON lb.ID = pra.RESOURCE_ID WHERE lb.PROVISIONING_STATUS = 'ACTIVE'

question: For each port status, show the status, the coefficient of variation (using STDDEV only and never STDDEV_POP) of the ports’ standard attribute IDs (only for ports that have both a security group port binding and a port security binding), the overall average coefficient of variation (using STDDEV only and never STDDEV_POP) across all statuses as a benchmark, and categorize each status as 'HIGH_VARIATION' (at least 50% above the benchmark), 'LOW_VARIATION' (at least 50% below the benchmark), or 'AVERAGE_VARIATION'. Do not return any rounded answers.
sql: WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT p.status, STDDEV(p.standard_attr_id) / NULLIF(AVG(p.standard_attr_id), 0) AS coefficient_of_variation FROM securitygroupportbindings AS sgpb JOIN ports AS p ON sgpb.port_id = p.id JOIN portsecuritybindings AS psb ON p.id = psb.port_id GROUP BY p.status HAVING AVG(p.standard_attr_id) > 0 ORDER BY coefficient_of_variation DESC ), avg_cv AS ( SELECT AVG(coefficient_of_variation) AS avg_coefficient_of_variation FROM inner_cte ) SELECT i.status, i.coefficient_of_variation, a.avg_coefficient_of_variation AS benchmark, CASE WHEN i.coefficient_of_variation > a.avg_coefficient_of_variation * 1.5 THEN 'HIGH_VARIATION' WHEN i.coefficient_of_variation < a.avg_coefficient_of_variation * 0.5 THEN 'LOW_VARIATION' ELSE 'AVERAGE_VARIATION' END AS variation_category FROM inner_cte i CROSS JOIN avg_cv a;
sub_questions: For each port status, show the status and the coefficient of variation of the ports’ standard attribute IDs, considering only ports that have a security group port binding and a port security binding.
sub_sqls: SELECT p.status, STDDEV(p.standard_attr_id) / NULLIF(AVG(p.standard_attr_id), 0) AS coefficient_of_variation FROM securitygroupportbindings AS sgpb JOIN ports AS p ON sgpb.port_id = p.id JOIN portsecuritybindings AS psb ON p.id = psb.port_id GROUP BY p.status HAVING AVG(p.standard_attr_id) > 0 ORDER BY coefficient_of_variation DESC;

question: For each port status and device owner (considering only DOWN ports that are bound to a security group), return the port status, device owner, number of distinct ports, and minimum standard attribute ID, but only include those (status, owner) groups whose distinct port count is greater than the average distinct port count across all such groups. Do not return any rounded answers.
sql: WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT p.STATUS AS port_status, p.DEVICE_OWNER AS device_owner, COUNT(DISTINCT p.ID) AS port_count, MIN(p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID) AS min_standard_attr_id FROM PORTS p JOIN SECURITYGROUPPORTBINDINGS spb ON p.ID = spb.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' GROUP BY p.STATUS, p.DEVICE_OWNER ) SELECT port_status, device_owner, port_count, min_standard_attr_id FROM inner_cte WHERE port_count > (SELECT AVG(port_count) FROM inner_cte);
sub_questions: For each port status and device owner, considering only ports that are bound to a security group, return the number of distinct ports and the minimum standard attribute ID.
sub_sqls: SELECT p.STATUS AS port_status, p.DEVICE_OWNER AS device_owner, COUNT(DISTINCT p.ID) AS port_count, MIN(p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID) AS min_standard_attr_id FROM PORTS p JOIN SECURITYGROUPPORTBINDINGS spb ON p.ID = spb.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' GROUP BY p.STATUS, p.DEVICE_OWNER;

question: For each subnet (by subnet name), show the range, variance, and standard deviation (using STDDEV only and never STDDEV_POP) of the number of IP allocation pools per subnet (considering only subnets that have at least one DNS nameserver entry), and also include the deviation of each subnet’s pool-count range from the average pool-count range across all such subnets. Do not return any rounded answers.
sql: WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT s.name AS subnet_name, MAX(pool_count) - MIN(pool_count) AS pool_count_range, VARIANCE(pool_count) AS pool_count_variance, STDDEV(pool_count) AS pool_count_stddev FROM subnets AS s JOIN dnsnameservers AS d ON d.subnet_id = s.id JOIN ( SELECT s2.id AS subnet_id, COUNT(*) AS pool_count FROM subnets AS s2 JOIN ipallocationpools AS p ON p.subnet_id = s2.id GROUP BY s2.id, p.id ) AS pool_stats ON pool_stats.subnet_id = s.id GROUP BY s.name ORDER BY pool_count_range DESC ), avg_ranges AS ( SELECT AVG(pool_count_range) AS avg_pool_count_range FROM inner_cte ) SELECT i.subnet_name, i.pool_count_range, i.pool_count_variance, i.pool_count_stddev, (i.pool_count_range - a.avg_pool_count_range) AS deviation_from_avg_pool_count_range FROM inner_cte i CROSS JOIN avg_ranges a ORDER BY i.pool_count_range DESC;
sub_questions: For each subnet (by subnet name), show the range, variance, and standard deviation of the number of IP allocation pools per subnet, considering only subnets that have at least one DNS nameserver entry.
sub_sqls: SELECT s.name AS subnet_name, MAX(pool_count) - MIN(pool_count) AS pool_count_range, VARIANCE(pool_count) AS pool_count_variance, STDDEV(pool_count) AS pool_count_stddev FROM subnets AS s JOIN dnsnameservers AS d ON d.subnet_id = s.id JOIN ( SELECT s2.id AS subnet_id, COUNT(*) AS pool_count FROM subnets AS s2 JOIN ipallocationpools AS p ON p.subnet_id = s2.id GROUP BY s2.id, p.id ) AS pool_stats ON pool_stats.subnet_id = s.id GROUP BY s.name ORDER BY pool_count_range DESC;

question: For each subnet name, report the minimum DNS nameserver order and the average IP version (considering only subnets where the IP version is 4 and the DNS nameserver address is 10.107.23.242/8), and also include the overall average of these per-subnet minimum DNS orders across all such subnets. Do not return any rounded answers.
sql: WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT MIN(t2.ORDER) AS min_dns_order, AVG(t1.IP_VERSION) AS avg_ip_version FROM SUBNETROUTES t0 JOIN SUBNETS t1 ON t0.SUBNET_ID = t1.ID JOIN DNSNAMESERVERS t2 ON t1.ID = t2.SUBNET_ID WHERE t1.IP_VERSION = 4 AND t2.ADDRESS = '10.107.23.242/8' GROUP BY t1.NAME ) SELECT inner_cte.min_dns_order, inner_cte.avg_ip_version, overall_avg.avg_min_dns_order FROM inner_cte JOIN ( SELECT AVG(min_dns_order) AS avg_min_dns_order FROM inner_cte ) AS overall_avg ON 1 = 1;
sub_questions: For each subnet name, what is the minimum DNS nameserver order and the average IP version, considering only subnets where the IP version is 4 and the DNS nameserver address is 10.107.23.242/8?
