sub_sqls: SELECT MIN(t2.ORDER) AS min_dns_order, AVG(t1.IP_VERSION) AS avg_ip_version FROM SUBNETROUTES t0 JOIN SUBNETS t1 ON t0.SUBNET_ID = t1.ID JOIN DNSNAMESERVERS t2 ON t1.ID = t2.SUBNET_ID WHERE t1.IP_VERSION = 4 AND t2.ADDRESS = '10.107.23.242/8' GROUP BY t1.NAME;

question: For each ACTIVE network, show the network name, status, and admin_state_up along with the RBAC action and target tenant, and also report how many distinct RBAC target tenants exist per network (computed from the detailed rows), plus a dense rank within each network (partitioned by network ID and ordered by network ID). Do not return any rounded answers.
sql: WITH inner_cte AS (SELECT n.name, n.status, n.admin_state_up, r.action, r.target_tenant, DENSE_RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY n.id ORDER BY n.id) AS window_column FROM networksecuritybindings b JOIN networks n ON b.network_id = n.id JOIN networkrbacs r ON n.id = r.object_id WHERE n.status = 'ACTIVE'), rbac_counts AS ( SELECT n.id AS network_id, COUNT(DISTINCT r.target_tenant) AS distinct_target_tenants FROM networksecuritybindings b JOIN networks n ON b.network_id = n.id JOIN networkrbacs r ON n.id = r.object_id WHERE n.status = 'ACTIVE' GROUP BY n.id ) SELECT i.name, i.status, i.admin_state_up, i.action, i.target_tenant, c.distinct_target_tenants, i.window_column FROM inner_cte i JOIN rbac_counts c ON c.network_id = (SELECT n2.id FROM networks n2 WHERE n2.name = i.name AND n2.status = i.status AND n2.admin_state_up = i.admin_state_up LIMIT 1);
sub_questions: Show each network’s name, status, and admin_state_up together with the RBAC action and target tenant for that network, plus a dense rank within each network (partitioned by network ID and ordered by network ID). Only include networks that are ACTIVE.
sub_sqls: SELECT n.name, n.status, n.admin_state_up, r.action, r.target_tenant, DENSE_RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY n.id ORDER BY n.id) AS window_column FROM networksecuritybindings b JOIN networks n ON b.network_id = n.id JOIN networkrbacs r ON n.id = r.object_id WHERE n.status = 'ACTIVE'

question: For each IPv4 subnet, show the subnet name, tenant ID, network ID, IP version, CIDR, gateway IP, DHCP enabled flag, the allocation pool’s first IP and last IP, and the maximum subnet standard attribute ID considering the current row and the next 2 rows when ordered by subnet ID; then return only those rows whose max_standard_attr_id_next2 is greater than the average of max_standard_attr_id_next2 for subnets with the same DHCP enabled flag. Do not return any rounded answers.
sql: WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT s.NAME, s.TENANT_ID, s.NETWORK_ID, s.IP_VERSION, s.CIDR, s.GATEWAY_IP, s.ENABLE_DHCP, p.FIRST_IP, p.LAST_IP, MAX(s.STANDARD_ATTR_ID) OVER ( ORDER BY s.ID ROWS BETWEEN CURRENT ROW AND 2 FOLLOWING ) AS max_standard_attr_id_next2 FROM SUBNETS AS s JOIN IPALLOCATIONPOOLS AS p ON s.ID = p.SUBNET_ID WHERE s.IP_VERSION = 4 ), DhcpAverages AS ( SELECT ENABLE_DHCP, AVG(max_standard_attr_id_next2) AS avg_max_next2 FROM inner_cte GROUP BY ENABLE_DHCP ) SELECT i.NAME, i.TENANT_ID, i.NETWORK_ID, i.IP_VERSION, i.CIDR, i.GATEWAY_IP, i.ENABLE_DHCP, i.FIRST_IP, i.LAST_IP, i.max_standard_attr_id_next2 FROM inner_cte i JOIN DhcpAverages d ON i.ENABLE_DHCP = d.ENABLE_DHCP WHERE i.max_standard_attr_id_next2 > d.avg_max_next2;
sub_questions: For each subnet, show the subnet name, tenant ID, network ID, IP version, CIDR, gateway IP, DHCP enabled flag, the allocation pool’s first IP and last IP, and the maximum subnet standard attribute ID considering the current row and the next 2 rows when ordered by subnet ID.
sub_sqls: SELECT s.NAME, s.TENANT_ID, s.NETWORK_ID, s.IP_VERSION, s.CIDR, s.GATEWAY_IP, s.ENABLE_DHCP, p.FIRST_IP, p.LAST_IP, MAX(s.STANDARD_ATTR_ID) OVER ( ORDER BY s.ID ROWS BETWEEN CURRENT ROW AND 2 FOLLOWING ) AS max_standard_attr_id_next2 FROM SUBNETS AS s JOIN IPALLOCATIONPOOLS AS p ON s.ID = p.SUBNET_ID WHERE s.IP_VERSION = 4;

question: For each port status, report the status and the maximum range (max minus min) of port security binding counts observed within any single network for ports in that status (considering only ports that have at least one port security binding). Do not return any rounded answers.
sql: WITH inner_cte AS (SELECT p.status, MAX(ps.binding_count) - MIN(ps.binding_count) AS binding_count_range, VARIANCE(ps.binding_count) AS binding_count_variance, STDDEV(ps.binding_count) AS binding_count_stddev FROM ports AS p JOIN ( SELECT p2.id AS port_id, COUNT(*) AS binding_count FROM ports AS p2 JOIN portsecuritybindings AS b ON p2.id = b.port_id GROUP BY p2.id ) AS ps ON p.id = ps.port_id GROUP BY p.status ORDER BY binding_count_range DESC), NetworkStatusRanges AS ( SELECT p.network_id, p.status, MAX(ps.binding_count) - MIN(ps.binding_count) AS network_binding_count_range FROM ports AS p JOIN ( SELECT p2.id AS port_id, COUNT(*) AS binding_count FROM ports AS p2 JOIN portsecuritybindings AS b ON p2.id = b.port_id GROUP BY p2.id ) AS ps ON p.id = ps.port_id GROUP BY p.network_id, p.status ) SELECT i.status, MAX(nsr.network_binding_count_range) AS max_network_binding_count_range FROM inner_cte AS i JOIN NetworkStatusRanges AS nsr ON i.status = nsr.status GROUP BY i.status ORDER BY max_network_binding_count_range DESC;
sub_questions: For each port status, report the status and the range, variance, and standard deviation of the number of port security bindings per port (considering only ports that have at least one port security binding).
sub_sqls: SELECT p.status, MAX(ps.binding_count) - MIN(ps.binding_count) AS binding_count_range, VARIANCE(ps.binding_count) AS binding_count_variance, STDDEV(ps.binding_count) AS binding_count_stddev FROM ports AS p JOIN ( SELECT p2.id AS port_id, COUNT(*) AS binding_count FROM ports AS p2 JOIN portsecuritybindings AS b ON p2.id = b.port_id GROUP BY p2.id ) AS ps ON p.id = ps.port_id GROUP BY p.status ORDER BY binding_count_range DESC;

question: For each tenant, list each ACTIVE load balancer’s name, VIP address, total connections, and bytes in, include a dense rank within the tenant ordered by load balancer ID, and also show the tenant’s average total connections across its ACTIVE load balancers. Do not return any rounded answers.
sql: WITH inner_cte AS (SELECT lb.NAME, lb.VIP_ADDRESS, stats.TOTAL_CONNECTIONS, stats.BYTES_IN, DENSE_RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY lb.TENANT_ID ORDER BY lb.ID) AS window_column FROM LBAAS_LOADBALANCERS AS lb JOIN LBAAS_LOADBALANCER_STATISTICS AS stats ON lb.ID = stats.LOADBALANCER_ID WHERE lb.PROVISIONING_STATUS = 'ACTIVE') SELECT inner_cte.NAME, inner_cte.VIP_ADDRESS, inner_cte.TOTAL_CONNECTIONS, inner_cte.BYTES_IN, inner_cte.window_column, tenant_avg.avg_total_connections FROM inner_cte JOIN ( SELECT lb.TENANT_ID, AVG(stats.TOTAL_CONNECTIONS) AS avg_total_connections FROM LBAAS_LOADBALANCERS AS lb JOIN LBAAS_LOADBALANCER_STATISTICS AS stats ON lb.ID = stats.LOADBALANCER_ID WHERE lb.PROVISIONING_STATUS = 'ACTIVE' GROUP BY lb.TENANT_ID ) AS tenant_avg ON tenant_avg.TENANT_ID = ( SELECT lb2.TENANT_ID FROM LBAAS_LOADBALANCERS AS lb2 WHERE lb2.VIP_ADDRESS = inner_cte.VIP_ADDRESS LIMIT 1 );
sub_questions: Show each load balancer’s name, VIP address, total connections, and bytes in, and include a dense rank within each tenant ordered by the load balancer ID, considering only load balancers that are ACTIVE.
sub_sqls: SELECT lb.NAME, lb.VIP_ADDRESS, stats.TOTAL_CONNECTIONS, stats.BYTES_IN, DENSE_RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY lb.TENANT_ID ORDER BY lb.ID) AS window_column FROM LBAAS_LOADBALANCERS AS lb JOIN LBAAS_LOADBALANCER_STATISTICS AS stats ON lb.ID = stats.LOADBALANCER_ID WHERE lb.PROVISIONING_STATUS = 'ACTIVE'

question: For hosts where more than 60% of their DOWN ports (with IP allocations) use the VIF type 'ovs', list the host name, total number of DOWN ports, number of DOWN ports using 'ovs', and the ovs share. Do not return any rounded answers.
sql: WITH inner_cte AS (SELECT p.ID AS port_id, p.TENANT_ID AS tenant_id, b.HOST AS host, b.VIF_TYPE AS vif_type, ia.IP_ADDRESS AS ip_address, ROW_NUMBER() OVER ( ORDER BY ia.IP_ADDRESS ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND 1 FOLLOWING ) AS window_column FROM ML2_PORT_BINDINGS b JOIN PORTS p ON b.PORT_ID = p.ID JOIN IPALLOCATIONS ia ON p.ID = ia.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN'), HostVifShare AS (SELECT host, COUNT(DISTINCT port_id) AS down_ports, SUM(CASE WHEN vif_type = 'ovs' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS ovs_down_ports FROM inner_cte GROUP BY host) SELECT host, down_ports, ovs_down_ports, (ovs_down_ports * 1.0 / down_ports) AS ovs_share FROM HostVifShare WHERE down_ports > 0 AND (ovs_down_ports * 1.0 / down_ports) > 0.60;
sub_questions: For ports whose status is DOWN, list the port ID, tenant ID, host, VIF type, and allocated IP address, and assign row numbers ordered by IP address using a window frame of 2 preceding rows and 1 following row.
sub_sqls: SELECT p.ID AS port_id, p.TENANT_ID AS tenant_id, b.HOST AS host, b.VIF_TYPE AS vif_type, ia.IP_ADDRESS AS ip_address, ROW_NUMBER() OVER ( ORDER BY ia.IP_ADDRESS ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND 1 FOLLOWING ) AS window_column FROM ML2_PORT_BINDINGS b JOIN PORTS p ON b.PORT_ID = p.ID JOIN IPALLOCATIONS ia ON p.ID = ia.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN';

question: For load balancers provided by “haproxy”, for each tenant find the tenant ID and the maximum total connections among that tenant’s load balancers, where the per-load-balancer totals come from the detailed list of load balancer name, VIP address, bytes in, total connections, and a row number ordered by load balancer name using a window frame of 2 preceding and 1 following rows. Do not return any rounded answers.
sql: WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT lb.NAME AS loadbalancer_name, lb.VIP_ADDRESS AS vip_address, stats.BYTES_IN AS bytes_in, stats.TOTAL_CONNECTIONS AS total_connections, ROW_NUMBER() OVER ( ORDER BY lb.NAME ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND 1 FOLLOWING ) AS window_column FROM LBAAS_LOADBALANCER_STATISTICS AS stats JOIN LBAAS_LOADBALANCERS AS lb ON stats.LOADBALANCER_ID = lb.ID JOIN PROVIDERRESOURCEASSOCIATIONS AS pra ON lb.ID = pra.RESOURCE_ID WHERE pra.PROVIDER_NAME = 'haproxy' ) SELECT lb.TENANT_ID AS tenant_id, MAX(inner_cte.total_connections) AS max_total_connections FROM inner_cte JOIN LBAAS_LOADBALANCERS AS lb ON lb.NAME = inner_cte.loadbalancer_name AND lb.VIP_ADDRESS = inner_cte.vip_address GROUP BY lb.TENANT_ID;
sub_questions: For load balancers provided by “haproxy”, list the load balancer name, VIP address, bytes in, and total connections, and assign row numbers ordered by load balancer name using a window frame of 2 preceding and 1 following rows.
sub_sqls: SELECT lb.NAME AS loadbalancer_name, lb.VIP_ADDRESS AS vip_address, stats.BYTES_IN AS bytes_in, stats.TOTAL_CONNECTIONS AS total_connections, ROW_NUMBER() OVER ( ORDER BY lb.NAME ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND 1 FOLLOWING ) AS window_column FROM LBAAS_LOADBALANCER_STATISTICS AS stats JOIN LBAAS_LOADBALANCERS AS lb ON stats.LOADBALANCER_ID = lb.ID JOIN PROVIDERRESOURCEASSOCIATIONS AS pra ON lb.ID = pra.RESOURCE_ID WHERE pra.PROVIDER_NAME = 'haproxy';

question: For each RBAC action, list the action name, the average/variance/standard deviation (using STDDEV only and never STDDEV_POP) of subnet IP version (restricted to IPv4 subnets) for subnets whose network is referenced by an RBAC entry, include the overall average IP version across all such actions as a benchmark, and categorize each action as 'HIGH_IPV4' (at least 10% above the benchmark), 'LOW_IPV4' (at least 10% below the benchmark), or 'AVERAGE_IPV4'. Do not return any rounded answers.
sql: WITH inner_cte AS (SELECT n.ACTION, AVG(s.IP_VERSION) AS avg_ip_version, VARIANCE(s.IP_VERSION) AS ip_version_variance, STDDEV(s.IP_VERSION) AS ip_version_stddev FROM NETWORKRBACS AS n JOIN SUBNETS AS s ON n.OBJECT_ID = s.NETWORK_ID WHERE s.IP_VERSION = 4 GROUP BY n.ACTION ORDER BY ip_version_variance DESC), OverallBenchmark AS ( SELECT AVG(avg_ip_version) AS benchmark_avg_ip_version FROM inner_cte ) SELECT i.ACTION, i.avg_ip_version, i.ip_version_variance, i.ip_version_stddev, ob.benchmark_avg_ip_version AS benchmark, CASE WHEN i.avg_ip_version > ob.benchmark_avg_ip_version * 1.10 THEN 'HIGH_IPV4' WHEN i.avg_ip_version < ob.benchmark_avg_ip_version * 0.90 THEN 'LOW_IPV4' ELSE 'AVERAGE_IPV4' END AS ipv4_category FROM inner_cte i CROSS JOIN OverallBenchmark ob;
sub_questions: For each RBAC action, show the average, variance, and standard deviation of the subnet IP version (4 or 6) across subnets whose network is referenced by an RBAC entry.
sub_sqls: SELECT n.ACTION, AVG(s.IP_VERSION) AS avg_ip_version, VARIANCE(s.IP_VERSION) AS ip_version_variance, STDDEV(s.IP_VERSION) AS ip_version_stddev FROM NETWORKRBACS AS n JOIN SUBNETS AS s ON n.OBJECT_ID = s.NETWORK_ID WHERE s.IP_VERSION = 4 GROUP BY n.ACTION ORDER BY ip_version_variance DESC;

question: Among the top 3 networks with the most subnets (considering only RBAC entries where the action is 'access_as_shared'), for each network return the network object ID, the number of subnets on that network, and the deviation of that subnet count from the average subnet count across these top 3 networks. Do not return any rounded answers.
sql: WITH inner_cte AS (SELECT n.OBJECT_ID AS network_id, COUNT(*) AS subnet_count FROM NETWORKRBACS AS n JOIN SUBNETS AS s ON n.OBJECT_ID = s.NETWORK_ID WHERE n.ACTION = 'access_as_shared' GROUP BY n.OBJECT_ID ORDER BY COUNT(*) DESC LIMIT 3), avg_cte AS ( SELECT AVG(subnet_count) AS avg_subnet_count FROM inner_cte ) SELECT i.network_id, i.subnet_count, (i.subnet_count - a.avg_subnet_count) AS deviation_from_avg FROM inner_cte i CROSS JOIN avg_cte a;
sub_questions: List the top 3 networks that have the most subnets, considering only RBAC entries where the action is 'access_as_shared'. For each of these networks, return the network object ID and the number of subnets on that network.
sub_sqls: SELECT n.OBJECT_ID AS network_id, COUNT(*) AS subnet_count FROM NETWORKRBACS AS n JOIN SUBNETS AS s ON n.OBJECT_ID = s.NETWORK_ID WHERE n.ACTION = 'access_as_shared' GROUP BY n.OBJECT_ID ORDER BY COUNT(*) DESC LIMIT 3;

question: For each subnet name and its gateway IP, show the subnet name, gateway IP, and the maximum IP version among subnets whose network has a RBAC action of 'access_as_shared'. Include subtotals per subnet name and a grand total, and only keep rows where the maximum IP version is greater than 3. Do not return any rounded answers.
sql: WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT s.name, MAX(s.ip_version) AS max_ip_version, s.gateway_ip FROM NETWORKRBACS n JOIN SUBNETS s ON n.object_id = s.network_id WHERE n.action = 'access_as_shared' GROUP BY s.name, s.gateway_ip HAVING MAX(s.ip_version) > 3 ) SELECT CASE WHEN GROUPING(name) = 1 THEN 'GRAND TOTAL' ELSE name END AS name, CASE WHEN GROUPING(gateway_ip) = 1 AND GROUPING(name) = 0 THEN 'SUBTOTAL' WHEN GROUPING(gateway_ip) = 1 AND GROUPING(name) = 1 THEN 'ALL' ELSE gateway_ip END AS gateway_ip, MAX(max_ip_version) AS max_ip_version FROM inner_cte GROUP BY name, gateway_ip WITH ROLLUP;
sub_questions: For each subnet name and its gateway IP, find the maximum IP version among subnets whose network has a RBAC action of 'access_as_shared', and only keep subnet name/gateway IP groups where that maximum IP version is greater than 3.
sub_sqls: SELECT s.name, MAX(s.ip_version) AS max_ip_version, s.gateway_ip FROM NETWORKRBACS n JOIN SUBNETS s ON n.object_id = s.network_id WHERE n.action = 'access_as_shared' GROUP BY s.name, s.gateway_ip HAVING MAX(s.ip_version) > 3;

question: For each IPv4 subnet that has more than 5 DNS nameserver entries, show the subnet name, the standard deviation (using STDDEV only and never STDDEV_POP) of the DNS nameserver order values for that subnet, and the deviation of that subnet’s order standard deviation (using STDDEV only and never STDDEV_POP) from the average order standard deviation (using STDDEV only and never STDDEV_POP) across all such subnets. Do not return any rounded answers.
sql: WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT s.name, STDDEV(d.ORDER) AS order_stddev FROM SUBNETS AS s JOIN DNSNAMESERVERS AS d ON s.id = d.subnet_id WHERE s.ip_version = 4 GROUP BY s.name HAVING COUNT(*) > 5 ORDER BY order_stddev DESC ), avg_cte AS ( SELECT AVG(order_stddev) AS avg_order_stddev FROM inner_cte ) SELECT i.name, i.order_stddev, (i.order_stddev - a.avg_order_stddev) AS deviation_from_avg_order_stddev FROM inner_cte i CROSS JOIN avg_cte a ORDER BY deviation_from_avg_order_stddev DESC;
sub_questions: For each subnet, show the subnet name and the standard deviation of the DNS nameserver order values for that subnet, considering only IPv4 subnets that have more than 5 DNS nameserver entries.
sub_sqls: SELECT s.name, STDDEV(d.ORDER) AS order_stddev FROM SUBNETS AS s JOIN DNSNAMESERVERS AS d ON s.id = d.subnet_id WHERE s.ip_version = 4 GROUP BY s.name HAVING COUNT(*) > 5 ORDER BY order_stddev DESC;

question: For each port status, list the status, the coefficient of variation (using STDDEV only and never STDDEV_POP) of the ports’ standard attribute IDs, and the total number of distinct security groups involved. Do not repeat the status if it is the same as the previous row. Include a final TOTAL row across all statuses, considering only ports that have both a security group port binding and a port security binding. Do not return any rounded answers.
sql: WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT p.status, STDDEV(p.standard_attr_id) / NULLIF(AVG(p.standard_attr_id), 0) AS coefficient_of_variation FROM securitygroupportbindings AS sgpb JOIN ports AS p ON sgpb.port_id = p.id JOIN portsecuritybindings AS psb ON p.id = psb.port_id GROUP BY p.status HAVING AVG(p.standard_attr_id) > 0 ORDER BY coefficient_of_variation DESC ) SELECT CASE WHEN LAG(status) OVER (ORDER BY status_sort, status) = status THEN NULL ELSE status END AS status, coefficient_of_variation, distinct_security_groups FROM ( SELECT CASE WHEN GROUPING(i.status) = 1 THEN 'zzz' ELSE i.status END AS status_sort, CASE WHEN GROUPING(i.status) = 1 THEN 'TOTAL' ELSE i.status END AS status, AVG(i.coefficient_of_variation) AS coefficient_of_variation, COUNT(DISTINCT sgpb.security_group_id) AS distinct_security_groups FROM inner_cte i JOIN ports p ON p.status = i.status JOIN securitygroupportbindings sgpb ON sgpb.port_id = p.id JOIN portsecuritybindings psb ON psb.port_id = p.id GROUP BY i.status WITH ROLLUP ) AS tbltmp ORDER BY status_sort, status;
sub_questions: For each port status, show the status and the coefficient of variation of the ports’ standard attribute IDs, considering only ports that have a security group port binding and a port security binding.
sub_sqls: SELECT p.status, STDDEV(p.standard_attr_id) / NULLIF(AVG(p.standard_attr_id), 0) AS coefficient_of_variation FROM securitygroupportbindings AS sgpb JOIN ports AS p ON sgpb.port_id = p.id JOIN portsecuritybindings AS psb ON p.id = psb.port_id GROUP BY p.status HAVING AVG(p.standard_attr_id) > 0 ORDER BY coefficient_of_variation DESC;

question: For ports on host "drive-59", list each tenant ID with the total number of distinct ports found there, and indicate whether that tenant has any ports with port security enabled. Do not return any rounded answers.
sql: WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT b.PORT_ID, p.TENANT_ID, p.MAC_ADDRESS, SUM(p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID) OVER ( PARTITION BY b.VIF_TYPE ORDER BY p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID ) AS window_column FROM ML2_PORT_BINDINGS AS b JOIN PORTS AS p ON b.PORT_ID = p.ID JOIN PORTSECURITYBINDINGS AS psb ON p.ID = psb.PORT_ID WHERE b.HOST = 'drive-59' ) SELECT i.TENANT_ID, COUNT(DISTINCT i.PORT_ID) AS total_ports, CASE WHEN COUNT(DISTINCT psb.PORT_ID) > 0 THEN 'Yes' ELSE 'No' END AS has_port_security_enabled FROM inner_cte AS i LEFT JOIN PORTSECURITYBINDINGS AS psb ON i.PORT_ID = psb.PORT_ID GROUP BY i.TENANT_ID ORDER BY total_ports DESC;
sub_questions: For ports on host "drive-59", show the port ID, tenant ID, MAC address, and a running sum of the port standard attribute IDs within each VIF type group ordered by standard attribute ID.
sub_sqls: SELECT b.PORT_ID, p.TENANT_ID, p.MAC_ADDRESS, SUM(p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID) OVER ( PARTITION BY b.VIF_TYPE ORDER BY p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID ) AS window_column FROM ML2_PORT_BINDINGS AS b JOIN PORTS AS p ON b.PORT_ID = p.ID JOIN PORTSECURITYBINDINGS AS psb ON p.ID = psb.PORT_ID WHERE b.HOST = 'drive-59';

question: For security groups whose geometric mean of the standard attribute IDs of their bound ports is greater than 1000 (considering only ports with a standard attribute ID greater than 0), list the security group ID and that geometric mean, ordered from highest to lowest. Do not return any rounded answers.
sql: WITH inner_cte AS (SELECT s.SECURITY_GROUP_ID, EXP(AVG(LN(p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID))) AS geometric_mean_standard_attr_id FROM PORTS AS p JOIN SECURITYGROUPPORTBINDINGS AS s ON p.ID = s.PORT_ID WHERE p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID > 0 GROUP BY s.SECURITY_GROUP_ID ORDER BY geometric_mean_standard_attr_id DESC) SELECT SECURITY_GROUP_ID, geometric_mean_standard_attr_id FROM inner_cte WHERE geometric_mean_standard_attr_id > 1000 ORDER BY geometric_mean_standard_attr_id DESC;
sub_questions: For each security group, show the security group ID and the geometric mean of the standard attribute IDs of the ports bound to that security group, considering only ports whose standard attribute ID is greater than 0.
sub_sqls: SELECT s.SECURITY_GROUP_ID, EXP(AVG(LN(p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID))) AS geometric_mean_standard_attr_id FROM PORTS AS p JOIN SECURITYGROUPPORTBINDINGS AS s ON p.ID = s.PORT_ID WHERE p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID > 0 GROUP BY s.SECURITY_GROUP_ID ORDER BY geometric_mean_standard_attr_id DESC;

question: For each subnet name, considering only subnets where the IP version is 4 and the DNS nameserver address is 10.107.23.242/8, list the subnet name along with the minimum DNS nameserver order and average IP version, but only include subnet names whose minimum DNS nameserver order is greater than 0. Do not return any rounded answers.
sql: WITH inner_cte AS (SELECT MIN(t2.ORDER) AS min_dns_order, AVG(t1.IP_VERSION) AS avg_ip_version FROM SUBNETROUTES t0 JOIN SUBNETS t1 ON t0.SUBNET_ID = t1.ID JOIN DNSNAMESERVERS t2 ON t1.ID = t2.SUBNET_ID WHERE t1.IP_VERSION = 4 AND t2.ADDRESS = '10.107.23.242/8' GROUP BY t1.NAME) SELECT min_dns_order, avg_ip_version FROM inner_cte WHERE min_dns_order > 0;
sub_questions: For each subnet name, what is the minimum DNS nameserver order and the average IP version, considering only subnets where the IP version is 4 and the DNS nameserver address is 10.107.23.242/8?
sub_sqls: SELECT MIN(t2.ORDER) AS min_dns_order, AVG(t1.IP_VERSION) AS avg_ip_version FROM SUBNETROUTES t0 JOIN SUBNETS t1 ON t0.SUBNET_ID = t1.ID JOIN DNSNAMESERVERS t2 ON t1.ID = t2.SUBNET_ID WHERE t1.IP_VERSION = 4 AND t2.ADDRESS = '10.107.23.242/8' GROUP BY t1.NAME;

question: For ports that are DOWN, show the port ID, tenant ID, and MAC address, along with the running sum of the port’s standard attribute ID within each security group (ordered by standard attribute ID). Also include, for each security group, the total number of DOWN ports and the deviation of that security group’s DOWN-port count from the average DOWN-port count across all security groups. Do not return any rounded answers.
sql: WITH inner_cte AS (SELECT p.ID AS port_id, p.TENANT_ID AS tenant_id, p.MAC_ADDRESS AS mac_address, SUM(p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID) OVER ( PARTITION BY sgpb.SECURITY_GROUP_ID ORDER BY p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID ) AS window_column FROM SECURITYGROUPPORTBINDINGS AS sgpb JOIN PORTS AS p ON sgpb.PORT_ID = p.ID JOIN PORTSECURITYBINDINGS AS psb ON p.ID = psb.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN'), SecurityGroupDownCounts AS ( SELECT sgpb.SECURITY_GROUP_ID AS security_group_id, COUNT(*) AS down_ports_in_group FROM SECURITYGROUPPORTBINDINGS AS sgpb JOIN PORTS AS p ON sgpb.PORT_ID = p.ID JOIN PORTSECURITYBINDINGS AS psb ON p.ID = psb.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' GROUP BY sgpb.SECURITY_GROUP_ID ), AverageDownCounts AS ( SELECT AVG(down_ports_in_group) AS avg_down_ports_in_group FROM SecurityGroupDownCounts ) SELECT i.port_id, i.tenant_id, i.mac_address, i.window_column, sgdc.down_ports_in_group, (sgdc.down_ports_in_group - adc.avg_down_ports_in_group) AS deviation_from_avg_down_ports FROM inner_cte AS i JOIN SECURITYGROUPPORTBINDINGS AS sgpb ON sgpb.PORT_ID = i.port_id JOIN SecurityGroupDownCounts AS sgdc ON sgdc.security_group_id = sgpb.SECURITY_GROUP_ID CROSS JOIN AverageDownCounts AS adc;
sub_questions: For ports that are DOWN, show the port ID, tenant ID, and MAC address, along with the running sum of the port’s standard attribute ID within each security group, ordered by standard attribute ID.
sub_sqls: SELECT p.ID AS port_id, p.TENANT_ID AS tenant_id, p.MAC_ADDRESS AS mac_address, SUM(p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID) OVER ( PARTITION BY sgpb.SECURITY_GROUP_ID ORDER BY p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID ) AS window_column FROM SECURITYGROUPPORTBINDINGS AS sgpb JOIN PORTS AS p ON sgpb.PORT_ID = p.ID JOIN PORTSECURITYBINDINGS AS psb ON p.ID = psb.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN';

question: For the top 10 tenants (among networks that are marked as default external networks) with the highest number of such networks, show each tenant's ID, total number of default external networks, and the minimum MTU observed for those networks within the tenant. Do not return any rounded answers.
sql: WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT e.NETWORK_ID, e.IS_DEFAULT, n.TENANT_ID, n.NAME, n.STATUS, n.ADMIN_STATE_UP, n.MTU, n.STANDARD_ATTR_ID, MIN(n.MTU) OVER (PARTITION BY n.TENANT_ID ORDER BY n.TENANT_ID) AS window_column FROM EXTERNALNETWORKS e JOIN NETWORKS n ON e.NETWORK_ID = n.ID WHERE e.IS_DEFAULT = 0 ) SELECT i.TENANT_ID, COUNT(DISTINCT i.NETWORK_ID) AS total_default_external_networks, MIN(i.MTU) AS min_mtu_in_tenant FROM inner_cte i GROUP BY i.TENANT_ID ORDER BY total_default_external_networks DESC LIMIT 10;
sub_questions: For networks that are marked as default external networks, show the network ID, whether it is default, the tenant ID, network name, status, admin state up flag, MTU, standard attribute ID, and the minimum MTU within each tenant (partitioned and ordered by tenant ID).

question: For each subnet name and its gateway IP, show the subnet name, gateway IP, and the maximum IP version among subnets whose network has a RBAC action of 'access_as_shared' and whose RBAC target tenant is public (i.e., `'*'`). Include subtotals per subnet name and a grand total across all returned rows, and only keep groups where that maximum IP version is greater than 3. Do not return any rounded answers.
sql: WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT s.name, MAX(s.ip_version) AS max_ip_version, s.gateway_ip FROM NETWORKRBACS n JOIN SUBNETS s ON n.object_id = s.network_id WHERE n.action = 'access_as_shared' AND n.target_tenant = '*' GROUP BY s.name, s.gateway_ip HAVING MAX(s.ip_version) > 3 ) SELECT CASE WHEN GROUPING(name) = 1 THEN 'GRAND TOTAL' ELSE name END AS name, CASE WHEN GROUPING(gateway_ip) = 1 AND GROUPING(name) = 0 THEN 'SUBTOTAL' WHEN GROUPING(gateway_ip) = 1 AND GROUPING(name) = 1 THEN 'ALL' ELSE gateway_ip END AS gateway_ip, MAX(max_ip_version) AS max_ip_version, COUNT(*) AS total_groups FROM inner_cte GROUP BY name, gateway_ip WITH ROLLUP;

question: For each RBAC action, list the action name, the variance of the subnet IP version (IPv4 vs IPv6) across the subnets on the network that the RBAC entry refers to (considering only RBAC entries with action = 'access_as_shared' and public access where target_tenant = '*'), and the total number of distinct subnets involved. sql: WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT n.ACTION, VARIANCE(s.IP_VERSION) AS ip_version_variance FROM NETWORKRBACS AS n JOIN SUBNETS AS s ON n.OBJECT_ID = s.NETWORK_ID WHERE n.ACTION = 'access_as_shared' AND n.TARGET_TENANT = '*' GROUP BY n.ACTION ORDER BY ip_version_variance DESC ) SELECT CASE WHEN LAG(action) OVER (ORDER BY action_sort, action) = action THEN NULL ELSE action END AS action, ip_version_variance, distinct_subnets FROM ( SELECT CASE WHEN GROUPING(i.action) = 1 THEN 'zzz' ELSE i.action END AS action_sort, CASE WHEN GROUPING(i.action) = 1 THEN 'TOTAL' ELSE i.action END AS action, i.ip_version_variance AS ip_version_variance, COUNT(DISTINCT s2.id) AS distinct_subnets FROM inner_cte i JOIN NETWORKRBACS n2 ON n2.action = i.action AND n2.action = 'access_as_shared' AND n2.target_tenant = '*' JOIN SUBNETS s2 ON s2.network_id = n2.object_id GROUP BY i.action, i.ip_version_variance WITH ROLLUP ) AS tbltmp ORDER BY action_sort, action;

question: Using the set of ports whose status is DOWN and whose device ID is `da811c75-0f9b-462c-b020-8ea55f6ca7c7`, show each port’s tenant ID, the number of such ports the tenant has, the average number of such ports per tenant as a benchmark, and classify each tenant as 'HIGH_USER' (at least 50% above average), 'LOW_USER' (at least 50% below average), or 'AVERAGE_USER'. sql: WITH inner_cte AS (SELECT p.id AS port_id, dense_rank() OVER ( ORDER BY psb.port_security_enabled ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW ) AS window_column FROM ports AS p JOIN portsecuritybindings AS psb ON p.id = psb.port_id WHERE p.status = 'DOWN' AND p.device_id IN ('da811c75-0f9b-462c-b020-8ea55f6ca7c7')), TenantPorts AS (SELECT p.tenant_id, COUNT(inner_cte.port_id) AS total_ports FROM inner_cte JOIN ports AS p ON p.id = inner_cte.port_id GROUP BY p.tenant_id), AveragePorts AS (SELECT AVG(total_ports) AS avg_ports FROM TenantPorts) SELECT tp.tenant_id, tp.total_ports, ap.avg_ports AS benchmark, CASE WHEN tp.total_ports > ap.avg_ports * 1.5 THEN 'HIGH_USER' WHEN tp.total_ports < ap.avg_ports * 0.5 THEN 'LOW_USER' ELSE 'AVERAGE_USER' END AS user_category FROM TenantPorts tp CROSS JOIN AveragePorts ap;

question: For each subnet name, report the subnet name, the range and variance of the allocation pool starting IP addresses (FIRST_IP) across that subnet’s IP allocation pools, and the number of distinct routes. Consider only routes whose next hop is 10.30.19.197/8 and only subnets with ID 012993ae-5d73-4aad-834b-e87a31e99d48. Include a subtotal row per subnet and a grand total row. Do not return any rounded answers.
sql: WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT s.NAME AS subnet_name, MAX(p.FIRST_IP) - MIN(p.FIRST_IP) AS first_ip_range, VARIANCE(p.FIRST_IP) AS first_ip_variance FROM SUBNETROUTES r JOIN SUBNETS s ON r.SUBNET_ID = s.ID JOIN IPALLOCATIONPOOLS p ON s.ID = p.SUBNET_ID WHERE r.NEXTHOP = '10.30.19.197/8' AND s.ID IN ('012993ae-5d73-4aad-834b-e87a31e99d48') GROUP BY s.NAME ORDER BY first_ip_range DESC ), RouteCounts AS ( SELECT s.NAME AS subnet_name, COUNT(DISTINCT r.DESTINATION) AS distinct_route_destinations FROM SUBNETROUTES r JOIN SUBNETS s ON r.SUBNET_ID = s.ID WHERE r.NEXTHOP = '10.30.19.197/8' AND s.ID IN ('012993ae-5d73-4aad-834b-e87a31e99d48') GROUP BY s.NAME ) SELECT CASE WHEN GROUPING(i.subnet_name) = 1 THEN 'GRAND TOTAL' ELSE i.subnet_name END AS subnet_name, CASE WHEN GROUPING(i.subnet_name) = 0 AND GROUPING(i.first_ip_range) = 1 THEN 'SUBTOTAL' ELSE CAST(i.first_ip_range AS CHAR) END AS first_ip_range, CASE WHEN GROUPING(i.subnet_name) = 0 AND GROUPING(i.first_ip_variance) = 1 THEN 'SUBTOTAL' ELSE CAST(i.first_ip_variance AS CHAR) END AS first_ip_variance, SUM(COALESCE(rc.distinct_route_destinations, 0)) AS distinct_route_destinations FROM inner_cte i LEFT JOIN RouteCounts rc ON rc.subnet_name = i.subnet_name GROUP BY i.subnet_name, i.first_ip_range, i.first_ip_variance WITH ROLLUP;

question: For each network name and RBAC action, show the maximum MTU among ACTIVE networks that have an RBAC entry (restricted to actions 'access_as_shared' or 'access_as_external') and only keep groups where that maximum MTU is greater than 8000; additionally, for each such group, report how many distinct target tenants are granted that RBAC action and the deviation of that count from the overall average distinct-target-tenant count across all returned groups. Do not return any rounded answers.
sql: WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT n.name AS network_name, r.action AS rbac_action, MAX(n.mtu) AS max_mtu FROM NETWORKSECURITYBINDINGS nsb JOIN NETWORKS n ON nsb.network_id = n.id JOIN NETWORKRBACS r ON n.id = r.object_id WHERE n.status = 'ACTIVE' AND r.action IN ('access_as_shared', 'access_as_external') GROUP BY n.name, r.action HAVING MAX(n.mtu) > 8000 ), TargetTenantCounts AS ( SELECT ic.network_name, ic.rbac_action, ic.max_mtu, COUNT(DISTINCT r.target_tenant) AS distinct_target_tenants FROM inner_cte ic JOIN NETWORKS n ON n.name = ic.network_name JOIN NETWORKRBACS r ON r.object_id = n.id AND r.action = ic.rbac_action GROUP BY ic.network_name, ic.rbac_action, ic.max_mtu ), AverageTargetTenantCounts AS ( SELECT AVG(distinct_target_tenants) AS avg_distinct_target_tenants FROM TargetTenantCounts ) SELECT ttc.network_name, ttc.rbac_action, ttc.max_mtu, ttc.distinct_target_tenants, (ttc.distinct_target_tenants - atc.avg_distinct_target_tenants) AS deviation_from_avg_distinct_target_tenants FROM TargetTenantCounts ttc CROSS JOIN AverageTargetTenantCounts atc;

question: For each IPv4 subnet (by subnet name), return the coefficient of variation (using STDDEV only and never STDDEV_POP) of the DNS nameserver order values across all DNS nameservers on that subnet (excluding subnets that belong to shared networks granted `access_as_shared` to `*` or to tenant `9f13bf11e06e4d81b44c8c3e62d4362b`), along with the deviation of that coefficient of variation (using STDDEV only and never STDDEV_POP) from the average coefficient of variation (using STDDEV only and never STDDEV_POP) across all such subnets. Do not return any rounded answers.
sql: WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT s.name AS subnet_name, STDDEV(d.order) / NULLIF(AVG(d.order), 0) AS coefficient_of_variation FROM subnets AS s JOIN dnsnameservers AS d ON d.subnet_id = s.id JOIN ipallocationpools AS p ON p.subnet_id = s.id JOIN networks AS n ON n.id = s.network_id WHERE s.ip_version = 4 AND n.id NOT IN ( SELECT r.object_id FROM networkrbacs AS r WHERE r.action = 'access_as_shared' AND (r.target_tenant = '*' OR r.target_tenant = '9f13bf11e06e4d81b44c8c3e62d4362b') ) GROUP BY s.name HAVING AVG(d.order) > 0 ORDER BY coefficient_of_variation DESC ), avg_cte AS ( SELECT AVG(coefficient_of_variation) AS avg_coefficient_of_variation FROM inner_cte ) SELECT i.subnet_name, i.coefficient_of_variation, (i.coefficient_of_variation - a.avg_coefficient_of_variation) AS deviation_from_avg_coefficient_of_variation FROM inner_cte i CROSS JOIN avg_cte a ORDER BY deviation_from_avg_coefficient_of_variation DESC;

sql: WITH inner_cte AS (SELECT p.NAME, p.NETWORK_ID, p.MAC_ADDRESS, p.ADMIN_STATE_UP, p.STATUS, p.DEVICE_OWNER, s.SECURITY_GROUP_ID, MIN(p.ADMIN_STATE_UP) OVER ( ORDER BY p.ID ROWS BETWEEN 3 PRECEDING AND 1 FOLLOWING ) AS window_column FROM PORTS AS p JOIN SECURITYGROUPPORTBINDINGS AS s ON p.ID = s.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' AND p.NETWORK_ID IN ('0a1d0a27-cffa-4de3-92c5-9d3fd3f2e74d')), TenantPortCounts AS (SELECT p.TENANT_ID, COUNT(*) AS total_ports FROM inner_cte ic JOIN PORTS p ON p.NETWORK_ID = ic.NETWORK_ID AND p.MAC_ADDRESS = ic.MAC_ADDRESS AND p.DEVICE_OWNER = ic.DEVICE_OWNER GROUP BY p.TENANT_ID), AveragePorts AS (SELECT AVG(total_ports) AS avg_ports FROM TenantPortCounts) SELECT tpc.TENANT_ID, tpc.total_ports, ap.avg_ports AS benchmark, CASE WHEN tpc.total_ports > ap.avg_ports * 1.5 THEN 'HIGH_USER' WHEN tpc.total_ports < ap.avg_ports * 0.5 THEN 'LOW_USER' ELSE 'AVERAGE_USER' END AS user_category FROM TenantPortCounts tpc CROSS JOIN AveragePorts ap;

question: For each IPv4 subnet (by subnet name), return the coefficient of variation (using STDDEV only and never STDDEV_POP) of the DNS nameserver order values across all DNS nameservers on that subnet, excluding subnets that belong to shared networks (i.e., networks granted `access_as_shared` to `*` or to tenant `9f13bf11e06e4d81b44c8c3e62d4362b`), but only include subnets whose coefficient of variation (using STDDEV only and never STDDEV_POP) is greater than the average coefficient of variation (using STDDEV only and never STDDEV_POP) across all such eligible IPv4 subnets. question: For each VIF type, what is the maximum of the per-status minimum admin_state_up values and the maximum of the per-status average standard_attr_id values for ports whose device_id is 'da811c75-0f9b-462c-b020-8ea55f6ca7c7'? Do not return any rounded answers.

question: For active networks that belong to tenant ID "98333a1a28e746fa8c629c83a818ad57", list the network ID, network name, tenant ID, admin_state_up flag, MTU, and the standard attribute updated_at timestamp, along with the average MTU across those networks as a benchmark, and categorize each network as 'HIGH_MTU' (at least 10% above average), 'LOW_MTU' (at least 10% below average), or 'AVERAGE_MTU'. Also assign row numbers within each tenant ordered by network name. Do not return any rounded answers.
sql: WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT n.ID AS network_id, n.NAME AS network_name, n.TENANT_ID AS tenant_id, n.ADMIN_STATE_UP AS admin_state_up, n.MTU AS mtu, sa.UPDATED_AT AS standard_attr_updated_at, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY n.TENANT_ID ORDER BY n.NAME) AS window_column FROM NETWORKS n JOIN STANDARDATTRIBUTES sa ON sa.ID = n.STANDARD_ATTR_ID WHERE n.STATUS = 'ACTIVE' AND n.TENANT_ID IN ('98333a1a28e746fa8c629c83a818ad57') ), AverageMtu AS ( SELECT AVG(mtu) AS avg_mtu FROM inner_cte ) SELECT ic.network_id, ic.network_name, ic.tenant_id, ic.admin_state_up, ic.mtu, ic.standard_attr_updated_at, ic.window_column, am.avg_mtu AS benchmark_mtu, CASE WHEN ic.mtu > am.avg_mtu * 1.1 THEN 'HIGH_MTU' WHEN ic.mtu < am.avg_mtu * 0.9 THEN 'LOW_MTU' ELSE 'AVERAGE_MTU' END AS mtu_category FROM inner_cte ic CROSS JOIN AverageMtu am;

question: For ports that are DOWN and belong to tenant ID `98333a1a28e746fa8c629c83a818ad57`, list only the ports whose running sum of the port’s standard attribute ID within each security group is greater than 100, showing the port ID, tenant ID, MAC address, security group ID, and the running sum, ordered by security group ID and standard attribute ID. Do not return any rounded answers.
sql: WITH inner_cte AS (SELECT p.ID AS port_id, p.TENANT_ID AS tenant_id, p.MAC_ADDRESS AS mac_address, SUM(p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID) OVER ( PARTITION BY sgpb.SECURITY_GROUP_ID ORDER BY p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID ) AS window_column FROM SECURITYGROUPPORTBINDINGS AS sgpb JOIN PORTS AS p ON sgpb.PORT_ID = p.ID JOIN PORTSECURITYBINDINGS AS psb ON p.ID = psb.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' AND p.TENANT_ID IN ('98333a1a28e746fa8c629c83a818ad57')) SELECT inner_cte.port_id, inner_cte.tenant_id, inner_cte.mac_address, sgpb.SECURITY_GROUP_ID AS security_group_id, inner_cte.window_column FROM inner_cte JOIN SECURITYGROUPPORTBINDINGS AS sgpb ON inner_cte.port_id = sgpb.PORT_ID WHERE inner_cte.window_column > 100 ORDER BY sgpb.SECURITY_GROUP_ID, inner_cte.window_column;

question: For each RBAC action, show the action name, the variance of the subnet IP version (IPv4 vs IPv6) across the subnets on the referenced network (only for RBAC entries with action = 'access_as_shared' and public access where target_tenant = '*'), also report the overall average of that variance across actions as a benchmark, and classify each action as 'HIGH_VARIANCE' (at least 50% above the average), 'LOW_VARIANCE' (at least 50% below the average), or 'AVERAGE_VARIANCE'. Do not return any rounded answers.
sql: WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT n.ACTION, VARIANCE(s.IP_VERSION) AS ip_version_variance FROM NETWORKRBACS AS n JOIN SUBNETS AS s ON n.OBJECT_ID = s.NETWORK_ID WHERE n.ACTION = 'access_as_shared' AND n.TARGET_TENANT = '*' GROUP BY n.ACTION ORDER BY ip_version_variance DESC ), avg_cte AS ( SELECT AVG(ip_version_variance) AS avg_ip_version_variance FROM inner_cte ) SELECT i.ACTION, i.ip_version_variance, a.avg_ip_version_variance AS benchmark, CASE WHEN i.ip_version_variance > a.avg_ip_version_variance * 1.5 THEN 'HIGH_VARIANCE' WHEN i.ip_version_variance < a.avg_ip_version_variance * 0.5 THEN 'LOW_VARIANCE' ELSE 'AVERAGE_VARIANCE' END AS variance_category FROM inner_cte i CROSS JOIN avg_cte a;

sub_questions: For each RBAC action, show the action name and the variance of the subnet IP version (IPv4 vs IPv6) across the subnets on the network that the RBAC entry refers to, considering only RBAC entries with action = 'access_as_shared' and with public access (i.e., target_tenant = '*').
sub_sqls: SELECT n.ACTION, VARIANCE(s.IP_VERSION) AS ip_version_variance FROM NETWORKRBACS AS n JOIN SUBNETS AS s ON n.OBJECT_ID = s.NETWORK_ID WHERE n.ACTION = 'access_as_shared' AND n.TARGET_TENANT = '*' GROUP BY n.ACTION ORDER BY ip_version_variance DESC;

question: For each IPv4 network ID, show the network’s highest route-count range (max minus min), highest variance, and highest standard deviation (using STDDEV only and never STDDEV_POP) observed among its subnets, considering only subnets whose ID is in ('012993ae-5d73-4aad-834b-e87a31e99d48'). Do not return any rounded answers.
sql: WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT s.NAME AS subnet_name, MAX(route_count) - MIN(route_count) AS route_count_range, VARIANCE(route_count) AS route_count_variance, STDDEV(route_count) AS route_count_stddev FROM SUBNETS AS s JOIN ( SELECT sr.SUBNET_ID, COUNT(*) AS route_count FROM SUBNETROUTES AS sr GROUP BY sr.SUBNET_ID, sr.NEXTHOP ) AS route_stats ON s.ID = route_stats.SUBNET_ID WHERE s.IP_VERSION = 4 AND s.ID IN ('012993ae-5d73-4aad-834b-e87a31e99d48') GROUP BY s.NAME ORDER BY route_count_range DESC ) SELECT s.NETWORK_ID AS network_id, MAX(inner_cte.route_count_range) AS max_route_count_range, MAX(inner_cte.route_count_variance) AS max_route_count_variance, MAX(inner_cte.route_count_stddev) AS max_route_count_stddev FROM inner_cte JOIN SUBNETS AS s ON s.NAME = inner_cte.subnet_name WHERE s.IP_VERSION = 4 AND s.ID IN ('012993ae-5d73-4aad-834b-e87a31e99d48') GROUP BY s.NETWORK_ID;

sub_questions: For each IPv4 subnet name, show the range, variance, and standard deviation of the number of routes per subnet, considering only subnets whose ID is in ('012993ae-5d73-4aad-834b-e87a31e99d48').
sub_sqls: SELECT s.NAME AS subnet_name, MAX(route_count) - MIN(route_count) AS route_count_range, VARIANCE(route_count) AS route_count_variance, STDDEV(route_count) AS route_count_stddev FROM SUBNETS AS s JOIN ( SELECT sr.SUBNET_ID, COUNT(*) AS route_count FROM SUBNETROUTES AS sr GROUP BY sr.SUBNET_ID, sr.NEXTHOP ) AS route_stats ON s.ID = route_stats.SUBNET_ID WHERE s.IP_VERSION = 4 AND s.ID IN ('012993ae-5d73-4aad-834b-e87a31e99d48') GROUP BY s.NAME ORDER BY route_count_range DESC;

question: For ports that are DOWN and belong to network ID `0a1d0a27-cffa-4de3-92c5-9d3fd3f2e74d`, list the port name, network ID, MAC address, admin state, status, device owner, bound security group ID, and the windowed minimum admin_state_up (3 preceding to 1 following ordered by port ID). Do not repeat the network ID if it is the same as the previous row, and include a subtotal row per network showing the total number of matching ports. Do not return any rounded answers.
sql: WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT p.NAME, p.NETWORK_ID, p.MAC_ADDRESS, p.ADMIN_STATE_UP, p.STATUS, p.DEVICE_OWNER, s.SECURITY_GROUP_ID, MIN(p.ADMIN_STATE_UP) OVER ( ORDER BY p.ID ROWS BETWEEN 3 PRECEDING AND 1 FOLLOWING ) AS window_column FROM PORTS AS p JOIN SECURITYGROUPPORTBINDINGS AS s ON p.ID = s.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' AND p.NETWORK_ID IN ('0a1d0a27-cffa-4de3-92c5-9d3fd3f2e74d') ) SELECT CASE WHEN LAG(network_id) OVER (ORDER BY network_id_sort, network_id, name, mac_address, security_group_id) = network_id THEN NULL ELSE network_id END AS network_id, name, mac_address, admin_state_up, status, device_owner, security_group_id, window_column, total_ports FROM ( SELECT CASE WHEN GROUPING(i.network_id) = 1 THEN 'zzz' ELSE i.network_id END AS network_id_sort, CASE WHEN GROUPING(i.network_id) = 1 THEN 'TOTAL' ELSE i.network_id END AS network_id, i.name, i.mac_address, i.admin_state_up, i.status, i.device_owner, i.security_group_id, i.window_column, COUNT(*) AS total_ports FROM inner_cte AS i GROUP BY i.network_id, i.name, i.mac_address, i.admin_state_up, i.status, i.device_owner, i.security_group_id, i.window_column WITH ROLLUP ) AS tbltmp ORDER BY network_id_sort, network_id, name, mac_address, security_group_id;

sub_questions: For ports that are DOWN and belong to network ID `0a1d0a27-cffa-4de3-92c5-9d3fd3f2e74d`, show the port name, network ID, MAC address, admin state, status, device owner, the bound security group ID, and the minimum admin_state_up value in a window of 3 preceding and 1 following row ordered by port ID.
sub_sqls: SELECT p.NAME, p.NETWORK_ID, p.MAC_ADDRESS, p.ADMIN_STATE_UP, p.STATUS, p.DEVICE_OWNER, s.SECURITY_GROUP_ID, MIN(p.ADMIN_STATE_UP) OVER ( ORDER BY p.ID ROWS BETWEEN 3 PRECEDING AND 1 FOLLOWING ) AS window_column FROM PORTS AS p JOIN SECURITYGROUPPORTBINDINGS AS s ON p.ID = s.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' AND p.NETWORK_ID IN ('0a1d0a27-cffa-4de3-92c5-9d3fd3f2e74d');

question: Among networks that are marked as default external networks (IS_DEFAULT = 0) and have the RBAC permission action set to 'access_as_external', show the top 10 tenants (by number of such networks) along with each tenant's ID, the total number of qualifying networks they own, and whether any of those networks have at least one RBAC entry targeting a specific tenant (i.e., TARGET_TENANT is not '*'). Do not return any rounded answers.
sql: WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT n.NAME, dense_rank() OVER ( ORDER BY r.ACTION ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW ) AS window_column FROM EXTERNALNETWORKS e JOIN NETWORKS n ON e.NETWORK_ID = n.ID JOIN NETWORKRBACS r ON n.ID = r.OBJECT_ID WHERE e.IS_DEFAULT = 0 AND r.ACTION = 'access_as_external' ) SELECT n.tenant_id, COUNT(DISTINCT n.id) AS total_qualifying_networks, CASE WHEN COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN r.target_tenant <> '*' THEN r.id END) > 0 THEN 'Yes' ELSE 'No' END AS has_targeted_rbac FROM inner_cte i JOIN networks n ON n.name = i.name JOIN externalnetworks e ON e.network_id = n.id JOIN networkrbacs r ON r.object_id = n.id WHERE e.is_default = 0 AND r.action = 'access_as_external' GROUP BY n.tenant_id ORDER BY total_qualifying_networks DESC LIMIT 10;

sub_sqls: SELECT n.NAME, dense_rank() OVER ( ORDER BY r.ACTION ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW ) AS window_column FROM EXTERNALNETWORKS e JOIN NETWORKS n ON e.NETWORK_ID = n.ID JOIN NETWORKRBACS r ON n.ID = r.OBJECT_ID WHERE e.IS_DEFAULT = 0 AND r.ACTION = 'access_as_external';

question: For each subnet name and its gateway IP, show the maximum IP version among subnets whose network has a RBAC action of 'access_as_shared' and whose RBAC target tenant is public (`'*'`), keeping only groups where that maximum IP version is greater than 3; also include, for each result row, the overall average of these per-(subnet name, gateway IP) maximum IP versions across all such groups. Do not return any rounded answers.
sql: WITH inner_cte AS (SELECT s.name, MAX(s.ip_version) AS max_ip_version, s.gateway_ip FROM NETWORKRBACS n JOIN SUBNETS s ON n.object_id = s.network_id WHERE n.action = 'access_as_shared' AND n.target_tenant = '*' GROUP BY s.name, s.gateway_ip HAVING MAX(s.ip_version) > 3) SELECT inner_cte.name, inner_cte.gateway_ip, inner_cte.max_ip_version, avg_maxes.avg_max_ip_version FROM inner_cte JOIN ( SELECT AVG(max_ip_version) AS avg_max_ip_version FROM inner_cte ) AS avg_maxes;
domain_knowledge: "public access" (wildcard) is predicated by "networkrbacs.target_tenant = '*'"
sub_questions: For each subnet name and its gateway IP, find the maximum IP version among subnets whose network has a RBAC action of 'access_as_shared' **and whose RBAC target tenant is public (i.e., `'*'`)**, and only keep subnet name/gateway IP groups where that maximum IP version is greater than 3.
sub_sqls: SELECT s.name, MAX(s.ip_version) AS max_ip_version, s.gateway_ip FROM NETWORKRBACS n JOIN SUBNETS s ON n.object_id = s.network_id WHERE n.action = 'access_as_shared' AND n.target_tenant = '*' GROUP BY s.name, s.gateway_ip HAVING MAX(s.ip_version) > 3;

question: For the top 3 publicly shared networks (RBAC action = 'access_as_shared' and target_tenant = '*') with the most subnets, list the network ID, subnet count, and the number of distinct subnet tenant IDs contributing subnets to that network. Do not repeat the network ID if it is the same as the previous row, and include a final TOTAL row across all returned networks. Do not return any rounded answers.
sql: WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT n.OBJECT_ID AS network_id, COUNT(*) AS subnet_count FROM NETWORKRBACS AS n JOIN SUBNETS AS s ON n.OBJECT_ID = s.NETWORK_ID WHERE n.ACTION = 'access_as_shared' AND n.TARGET_TENANT = '*' GROUP BY n.OBJECT_ID ORDER BY COUNT(*) DESC LIMIT 3 ) SELECT CASE WHEN LAG(network_id) OVER (ORDER BY network_id_sort, network_id) = network_id THEN NULL ELSE network_id END AS network_id, subnet_count, distinct_subnet_tenants FROM ( SELECT CASE WHEN GROUPING(i.network_id) = 1 THEN 'zzz' ELSE i.network_id END AS network_id_sort, CASE WHEN GROUPING(i.network_id) = 1 THEN 'TOTAL' ELSE i.network_id END AS network_id, SUM(i.subnet_count) AS subnet_count, COUNT(DISTINCT s.TENANT_ID) AS distinct_subnet_tenants FROM inner_cte i JOIN SUBNETS s ON s.NETWORK_ID = i.network_id GROUP BY i.network_id WITH ROLLUP ) AS tbltmp ORDER BY network_id_sort, network_id;
domain_knowledge: "public access" (wildcard) is predicated by "networkrbacs.target_tenant = '*'"
sub_questions: List the top 3 networks that have the most subnets, considering only RBAC entries where the action is 'access_as_shared' and the RBAC target tenant is public access (i.e., target_tenant = '*'). For each of these networks, return the network object ID and the number of subnets on that network.
sub_sqls: SELECT n.OBJECT_ID AS network_id, COUNT(*) AS subnet_count FROM NETWORKRBACS AS n JOIN SUBNETS AS s ON n.OBJECT_ID = s.NETWORK_ID WHERE n.ACTION = 'access_as_shared' AND n.TARGET_TENANT = '*' GROUP BY n.OBJECT_ID ORDER BY COUNT(*) DESC LIMIT 3;

question: For each IPv4 subnet (by subnet name), show the coefficient of variation (using STDDEV only and never STDDEV_POP) of the DNS nameserver order values across all DNS nameservers on that subnet (excluding subnets that belong to shared networks, i.e., networks granted `access_as_shared` to `*` or to tenant `9f13bf11e06e4d81b44c8c3e62d4362b`). Do not repeat the subnet name if it is the same as the previous row, and include a grand total row across all returned subnets. Do not return any rounded answers.
sql: WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT s.name AS subnet_name, STDDEV(d.order) / NULLIF(AVG(d.order), 0) AS coefficient_of_variation FROM subnets AS s JOIN dnsnameservers AS d ON d.subnet_id = s.id JOIN ipallocationpools AS p ON p.subnet_id = s.id JOIN networks AS n ON n.id = s.network_id WHERE s.ip_version = 4 AND n.id NOT IN ( SELECT r.object_id FROM networkrbacs AS r WHERE r.action = 'access_as_shared' AND (r.target_tenant = '*' OR r.target_tenant = '9f13bf11e06e4d81b44c8c3e62d4362b') ) GROUP BY s.name HAVING AVG(d.order) > 0 ORDER BY coefficient_of_variation DESC ) SELECT CASE WHEN LAG(subnet_name) OVER (ORDER BY subnet_name_sort, subnet_name) = subnet_name THEN NULL ELSE subnet_name END AS subnet_name, coefficient_of_variation FROM ( SELECT CASE WHEN GROUPING(subnet_name) = 1 THEN 'zzz' ELSE subnet_name END AS subnet_name_sort, CASE WHEN GROUPING(subnet_name) = 1 THEN 'TOTAL' ELSE subnet_name END AS subnet_name, AVG(coefficient_of_variation) AS coefficient_of_variation FROM inner_cte GROUP BY subnet_name WITH ROLLUP ) AS tbltmp ORDER BY subnet_name_sort, subnet_name;
domain_knowledge: "exclusion of shared networks" is predicated by "networks.id NOT IN (SELECT networkrbacs.object_id FROM networkrbacs WHERE networkrbacs.action = 'access_as_shared' AND (networkrbacs.target_tenant = '*' OR networkrbacs.target_tenant = '9f13bf11e06e4d81b44c8c3e62d4362b'))"
sub_questions: For each IPv4 subnet (by subnet name), return the coefficient of variation of the DNS nameserver order values across all DNS nameservers on that subnet, excluding subnets that belong to shared networks (i.e., networks granted `access_as_shared` to `*` or to tenant `9f13bf11e06e4d81b44c8c3e62d4362b`).
sub_sqls: SELECT s.name AS subnet_name, STDDEV(d.order) / NULLIF(AVG(d.order), 0) AS coefficient_of_variation FROM subnets AS s JOIN dnsnameservers AS d ON d.subnet_id = s.id JOIN ipallocationpools AS p ON p.subnet_id = s.id JOIN networks AS n ON n.id = s.network_id WHERE s.ip_version = 4 AND n.id NOT IN ( SELECT r.object_id FROM networkrbacs AS r WHERE r.action = 'access_as_shared' AND (r.target_tenant = '*' OR r.target_tenant = '9f13bf11e06e4d81b44c8c3e62d4362b') ) GROUP BY s.name HAVING AVG(d.order) > 0 ORDER BY coefficient_of_variation DESC;

question: For ports that are DOWN and belong to tenant ID '98333a1a28e746fa8c629c83a818ad57', list only those ports whose security group has more ports bound to it than the average number of ports per security group (computed across all security groups). Show the port ID, tenant ID, MAC address, the security group ID from the security-group-to-port binding, and the rank of each port within its security group when ordered by port ID. sql: WITH inner_cte AS (SELECT p.id AS port_id, p.tenant_id, p.mac_address, sgpb.security_group_id, RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY sgpb.security_group_id ORDER BY p.id) AS window_column FROM SECURITYGROUPPORTBINDINGS AS sgpb JOIN PORTS AS p ON sgpb.port_id = p.id JOIN PORTSECURITYBINDINGS AS psb ON p.id = psb.port_id WHERE p.status = 'DOWN' AND p.tenant_id IN ('98333a1a28e746fa8c629c83a818ad57')), SecurityGroupAverages AS (SELECT AVG(sg_port_count) AS avg_ports_per_sg FROM (SELECT sgpb2.security_group_id, COUNT(*) AS sg_port_count FROM SECURITYGROUPPORTBINDINGS AS sgpb2 JOIN PORTS AS p2 ON sgpb2.port_id = p2.id JOIN PORTSECURITYBINDINGS AS psb2 ON p2.id = psb2.port_id GROUP BY sgpb2.security_group_id) sg_counts) SELECT i.port_id, i.tenant_id, i.mac_address, i.security_group_id, i.window_column FROM inner_cte i JOIN (SELECT sgpb3.security_group_id, COUNT(*) AS total_ports_in_sg FROM SECURITYGROUPPORTBINDINGS AS sgpb3 JOIN PORTS AS p3 ON sgpb3.port_id = p3.id JOIN PORTSECURITYBINDINGS AS psb3 ON p3.id = psb3.port_id GROUP BY sgpb3.security_group_id) sg_totals ON sg_totals.security_group_id = i.security_group_id WHERE sg_totals.total_ports_in_sg > (SELECT avg_ports_per_sg FROM SecurityGroupAverages);

question: For the ACTIVE networks that have an RBAC permission action of 'access_as_shared', group results by network status and whether the network is “High Subnet Count” (its subnet total is more than one standard deviation (using STDDEV only and never STDDEV_POP) above the mean subnet count across all such ACTIVE shared networks) or “Normal Subnet Count” otherwise. Return the network status, the subnet-count category, and the number of networks in each group, including subtotals per status and a grand total. Do not return any rounded answers.
sql: WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT n.id AS network_id, SUM(1) AS total_subnets FROM NETWORKS AS n JOIN NETWORKRBACS AS r ON n.id = r.object_id JOIN SUBNETS AS s ON r.object_id = s.network_id WHERE n.status = 'ACTIVE' AND r.action = 'access_as_shared' GROUP BY n.id HAVING SUM(1) > ( SELECT AVG(subnet_cnt) + STDDEV(subnet_cnt) FROM ( SELECT n2.id AS network_id, SUM(1) AS subnet_cnt FROM NETWORKS AS n2 JOIN NETWORKRBACS AS r2 ON n2.id = r2.object_id JOIN SUBNETS AS s2 ON r2.object_id = s2.network_id WHERE n2.status = 'ACTIVE' AND r2.action = 'access_as_shared' GROUP BY n2.id ) AS per_network ) ), NetworkSubnetCategory AS ( SELECT n.status, CASE WHEN ic.network_id IS NOT NULL THEN 'High Subnet Count' ELSE 'Normal Subnet Count' END AS subnet_count_category, COUNT(DISTINCT n.id) AS total_networks FROM NETWORKS n JOIN NETWORKRBACS r ON n.id = r.object_id LEFT JOIN inner_cte ic ON n.id = ic.network_id WHERE n.status = 'ACTIVE' AND r.action = 'access_as_shared' GROUP BY n.status, subnet_count_category ) SELECT CASE WHEN GROUPING(status) = 1 THEN 'GRAND TOTAL' ELSE status END AS status, CASE WHEN GROUPING(subnet_count_category) = 1 AND GROUPING(status) = 0 THEN 'SUBTOTAL' ELSE subnet_count_category END AS subnet_count_category, SUM(total_networks) AS total_networks FROM NetworkSubnetCategory GROUP BY status, subnet_count_category WITH ROLLUP;

sql: WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT p.status, MAX(ps.binding_count) - MIN(ps.binding_count) AS binding_count_range, VARIANCE(ps.binding_count) AS binding_count_variance, STDDEV(ps.binding_count) AS binding_count_stddev FROM ports AS p JOIN ( SELECT p2.id AS port_id, COUNT(*) AS binding_count FROM ports AS p2 JOIN portsecuritybindings AS b ON p2.id = b.port_id WHERE p2.tenant_id IN ('17ea94ad74b64b9d92f4888336a598c7') GROUP BY p2.id ) AS ps ON p.id = ps.port_id GROUP BY p.status ORDER BY binding_count_range DESC ) SELECT inner_cte.status, inner_cte.binding_count_range, inner_cte.binding_count_variance, inner_cte.binding_count_stddev, avg_bindings.avg_binding_count FROM inner_cte JOIN ( SELECT AVG(binding_count) AS avg_binding_count FROM ( SELECT p2.id AS port_id, COUNT(*) AS binding_count FROM ports AS p2 JOIN portsecuritybindings AS b ON p2.id = b.port_id WHERE p2.tenant_id IN ('17ea94ad74b64b9d92f4888336a598c7') GROUP BY p2.id ) AS sub ) AS avg_bindings ON 1 = 1 ORDER BY inner_cte.binding_count_range DESC;

question: For each subnet name and its gateway IP, list the maximum IP version among subnets whose network has a RBAC action of 'access_as_shared' and whose RBAC target tenant is public (i.e., `'*'`), keeping only groups where that maximum IP version is greater than 3. sql: WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT s.name, MAX(s.ip_version) AS max_ip_version, s.gateway_ip FROM NETWORKRBACS n JOIN SUBNETS s ON n.object_id = s.network_id WHERE n.action = 'access_as_shared' AND n.target_tenant = '*' GROUP BY s.name, s.gateway_ip HAVING MAX(s.ip_version) > 3 ) SELECT CASE WHEN LAG(name) OVER (ORDER BY name, gateway_ip) = name THEN NULL ELSE name END AS name, max_ip_version, gateway_ip FROM inner_cte ORDER BY name, gateway_ip;

sql: WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT p.id AS port_id, p.tenant_id, p.mac_address, sgpb.security_group_id, RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY sgpb.security_group_id ORDER BY p.id) AS window_column FROM SECURITYGROUPPORTBINDINGS AS sgpb JOIN PORTS AS p ON sgpb.port_id = p.id JOIN PORTSECURITYBINDINGS AS psb ON p.id = psb.port_id WHERE p.status = 'DOWN' AND p.tenant_id IN ('98333a1a28e746fa8c629c83a818ad57') ) SELECT inner_cte.port_id, inner_cte.tenant_id, inner_cte.mac_address, inner_cte.security_group_id, inner_cte.window_column, tenant_down.total_down_ports_for_tenant, avg_down.avg_down_ports_per_tenant FROM inner_cte JOIN ( SELECT tenant_id, COUNT(*) AS total_down_ports_for_tenant FROM ports WHERE status = 'DOWN' GROUP BY tenant_id ) AS tenant_down ON inner_cte.tenant_id = tenant_down.tenant_id JOIN ( SELECT AVG(down_port_count) AS avg_down_ports_per_tenant FROM ( SELECT tenant_id, COUNT(*) AS down_port_count FROM ports WHERE status = 'DOWN' GROUP BY tenant_id ) AS sub ) AS avg_down ON 1 = 1;

question: Among the top 10 (port status, device owner) combinations with the highest number of ports—considering only ports whose standard attribute resource type is 'ports' and excluding shared networks (networks whose IDs appear in networkrbacs with action = 'access_as_shared' and target_tenant = '*' or '9f13bf11e06e4d81b44c8c3e62d4362b')—return the port status, device owner, total number of ports, the earliest (minimum) standard attribute updated timestamp, and whether any of those ports have a floating IP allocated. Do not return any rounded answers.
sql: WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT p.STATUS AS port_status, p.DEVICE_OWNER AS device_owner, COUNT(p.ID) AS port_count, MIN(sa.UPDATED_AT) AS earliest_standard_attr_update FROM PORTS p JOIN STANDARDATTRIBUTES sa ON sa.ID = p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID WHERE sa.RESOURCE_TYPE = 'ports' AND p.NETWORK_ID NOT IN ( SELECT networkrbacs.object_id FROM networkrbacs WHERE networkrbacs.action = 'access_as_shared' AND (networkrbacs.target_tenant = '*' OR networkrbacs.target_tenant = '9f13bf11e06e4d81b44c8c3e62d4362b') ) GROUP BY p.STATUS, p.DEVICE_OWNER ) SELECT i.port_status, i.device_owner, i.port_count, i.earliest_standard_attr_update, CASE WHEN COUNT(DISTINCT f.id) > 0 THEN 'Yes' ELSE 'No' END AS has_floating_ips FROM inner_cte i JOIN ports p ON p.status = i.port_status AND p.device_owner = i.device_owner JOIN standardattributes sa ON sa.id = p.standard_attr_id LEFT JOIN floatingips f ON p.id = f.fixed_port_id WHERE sa.resource_type = 'ports' AND p.network_id NOT IN ( SELECT networkrbacs.object_id FROM networkrbacs WHERE networkrbacs.action = 'access_as_shared' AND (networkrbacs.target_tenant = '*' OR networkrbacs.target_tenant = '9f13bf11e06e4d81b44c8c3e62d4362b') ) GROUP BY i.port_status, i.device_owner, i.port_count, i.earliest_standard_attr_update ORDER BY i.port_count DESC LIMIT 10;

question: For each port status, list the status value and the coefficient of variation (using STDDEV only and never STDDEV_POP) (standard deviation (using STDDEV only and never STDDEV_POP) divided by average) of the length of the allocated IP address strings for ports that have port security enabled, restricting to allocated IP addresses in ('10.150.64.113/8'). Do not repeat the status value if it is the same as the previous row. Also include a final TOTAL row across all statuses. Do not return any rounded answers.
sql: WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT p.status, STDDEV(LENGTH(ia.ip_address)) / NULLIF(AVG(LENGTH(ia.ip_address)), 0) AS coefficient_of_variation FROM portsecuritybindings psb JOIN ports p ON psb.port_id = p.id JOIN ipallocations ia ON p.id = ia.port_id WHERE psb.port_security_enabled = 1 AND ia.ip_address IN ('10.150.64.113/8') GROUP BY p.status HAVING AVG(LENGTH(ia.ip_address)) > 0 ORDER BY coefficient_of_variation DESC ) SELECT CASE WHEN LAG(status) OVER (ORDER BY status_sort, status) = status THEN NULL ELSE status END AS status, coefficient_of_variation FROM ( SELECT CASE WHEN GROUPING(status) = 1 THEN 'zzz' ELSE status END AS status_sort, CASE WHEN GROUPING(status) = 1 THEN 'TOTAL' ELSE status END AS status, AVG(coefficient_of_variation) AS coefficient_of_variation FROM inner_cte GROUP BY status WITH ROLLUP ) AS tbltmp ORDER BY status_sort, status;

question: Among the top 10 subnet name/gateway IP pairs (ranked by the maximum IP version) for subnets whose network has an RBAC action of 'access_as_shared' and whose RBAC target tenant is public (`'*'`), show the subnet name, gateway IP, that maximum IP version, and whether any of those subnets have DHCP enabled. sql: WITH inner_cte AS (SELECT s.name, MAX(s.ip_version) AS max_ip_version, s.gateway_ip FROM NETWORKRBACS n JOIN SUBNETS s ON n.object_id = s.network_id WHERE n.action = 'access_as_shared' AND n.target_tenant = '*' GROUP BY s.name, s.gateway_ip HAVING MAX(s.ip_version) > 3) SELECT i.name, i.gateway_ip, i.max_ip_version, CASE WHEN MAX(s.enable_dhcp) = 1 THEN 'Yes' ELSE 'No' END AS has_dhcp_enabled FROM inner_cte i JOIN SUBNETS s ON s.name = i.name AND s.gateway_ip = i.gateway_ip GROUP BY i.name, i.gateway_ip, i.max_ip_version ORDER BY i.max_ip_version DESC LIMIT 10;

question: For each IPv4 subnet (by subnet name), return the coefficient of variation (using STDDEV only and never STDDEV_POP) of the DNS nameserver order values across all DNS nameservers on that subnet (excluding subnets that belong to shared networks granted `access_as_shared` to `*` or to tenant `9f13bf11e06e4d81b44c8c3e62d4362b`), along with the overall average coefficient of variation (using STDDEV only and never STDDEV_POP) across all such subnets. sql: WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT p.status, STDDEV(LENGTH(ia.ip_address)) / NULLIF(AVG(LENGTH(ia.ip_address)), 0) AS coefficient_of_variation FROM portsecuritybindings psb JOIN ports p ON psb.port_id = p.id JOIN ipallocations ia ON p.id = ia.port_id WHERE psb.port_security_enabled = 1 AND ia.ip_address IN ('10.150.64.113/8') GROUP BY p.status HAVING AVG(LENGTH(ia.ip_address)) > 0 ORDER BY coefficient_of_variation DESC ), avg_cte AS ( SELECT AVG(coefficient_of_variation) AS avg_coefficient_of_variation FROM inner_cte ) SELECT i.status, i.coefficient_of_variation, (i.coefficient_of_variation - a.avg_coefficient_of_variation) AS deviation_from_avg_coefficient_of_variation FROM inner_cte i CROSS JOIN avg_cte a ORDER BY deviation_from_avg_coefficient_of_variation DESC;

sql: WITH inner_cte AS (SELECT n.name AS network_name, r.action AS rbac_action, MAX(n.mtu) AS max_mtu FROM NETWORKSECURITYBINDINGS nsb JOIN NETWORKS n ON nsb.network_id = n.id JOIN NETWORKRBACS r ON n.id = r.object_id WHERE n.status = 'ACTIVE' AND r.action IN ('access_as_shared', 'access_as_external') GROUP BY n.name, r.action HAVING MAX(n.mtu) > 8000) SELECT i.network_name, i.rbac_action, i.max_mtu, COUNT(DISTINCT r2.target_tenant) AS distinct_target_tenants FROM inner_cte i JOIN NETWORKS n2 ON n2.name = i.network_name JOIN NETWORKRBACS r2 ON r2.object_id = n2.id AND r2.action = i.rbac_action GROUP BY i.network_name, i.rbac_action, i.max_mtu;

"access_as_external" permission is predicated by "networkrbacs.action = 'access_as_external'"

question: Among the IPv4 subnets whose ID is in ('012993ae-5d73-4aad-834b-e87a31e99d48'), list the top 10 tenants (by total routes across those subnets) and show each tenant's ID, total number of routes, and the range, variance, and standard deviation (using STDDEV only and never STDDEV_POP) of routes per subnet for that tenant. sql: WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT s.NAME AS subnet_name, MAX(route_count) - MIN(route_count) AS route_count_range, VARIANCE(route_count) AS route_count_variance, STDDEV(route_count) AS route_count_stddev FROM SUBNETS AS s JOIN ( SELECT sr.SUBNET_ID, COUNT(*) AS route_count FROM SUBNETROUTES AS sr GROUP BY sr.SUBNET_ID, sr.NEXTHOP ) AS route_stats ON s.ID = route_stats.SUBNET_ID WHERE s.IP_VERSION = 4 AND s.ID IN ('012993ae-5d73-4aad-834b-e87a31e99d48') GROUP BY s.NAME ORDER BY route_count_range DESC ) SELECT s.TENANT_ID AS tenant_id, COUNT(sr.DESTINATION) AS total_routes, MAX(inner_cte.route_count_range) AS route_count_range, MAX(inner_cte.route_count_variance) AS route_count_variance, MAX(inner_cte.route_count_stddev) AS route_count_stddev FROM SUBNETS AS s JOIN SUBNETROUTES AS sr ON s.ID = sr.SUBNET_ID JOIN inner_cte ON inner_cte.subnet_name = s.NAME WHERE s.IP_VERSION = 4 AND s.ID IN ('012993ae-5d73-4aad-834b-e87a31e99d48') GROUP BY s.TENANT_ID ORDER BY total_routes DESC LIMIT 10;

sql: SELECT n.STATUS AS network_status, AVG(n.MTU) AS avg_mtu, MAX(n.MTU) - MIN(n.MTU) AS mtu_range, VARIANCE(n.MTU) AS mtu_variance FROM NETWORKS AS n JOIN NETWORKRBACS AS r ON n.ID = r.OBJECT_ID WHERE r.ACTION = 'access_as_shared' AND r.TARGET_TENANT = '*' AND n.MTU IS NOT NULL GROUP BY n.STATUS ORDER BY mtu_range DESC;
domain_knowledge: "public access" (wildcard) is predicated by "networkrbacs.target_tenant = '*'"

sql: SELECT p.id AS port_id, p.tenant_id, p.mac_address, COUNT(ia.ip_address) AS ip_allocation_count, COUNT(DISTINCT ia.subnet_id) AS distinct_subnet_count FROM ports p JOIN portsecuritybindings psb ON psb.port_id = p.id JOIN ipallocations ia ON ia.port_id = p.id WHERE p.admin_state_up = 1 AND ia.ip_address IS NOT NULL AND p.tenant_id IN ('17ea94ad74b64b9d92f4888336a598c7') GROUP BY p.id, p.tenant_id, p.mac_address;

question: For ports whose status is DOWN and whose tenant ID is in ('17ea94ad74b64b9d92f4888336a598c7'), show the port ID, tenant ID, and MAC address, along with the running sum of the standard attribute IDs within each resource type group ordered by standard attribute ID. Do not return any rounded answers.
sql: SELECT p.ID AS port_id, p.TENANT_ID AS tenant_id, p.MAC_ADDRESS AS mac_address, SUM(sa.ID) OVER (PARTITION BY sa.RESOURCE_TYPE ORDER BY sa.ID) AS window_column FROM PORTS p JOIN STANDARDATTRIBUTES sa ON sa.ID = p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' AND p.TENANT_ID IN ('17ea94ad74b64b9d92f4888336a598c7');

question: For the security group ID 0008e629-5619-41e0-b86c-4eecfeaacb6c, list only the networks where more than 50% of the ports bound to that security group are in DOWN status, returning the network ID, total bound ports, total DOWN ports, and the DOWN-to-total ratio.
sql: WITH inner_cte AS ( WITH Subq1 AS ( SELECT p.ID AS port_id, p.STATUS AS port_status, ia.IP_ADDRESS AS ip_address, SUM(p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID) OVER ( PARTITION BY p.NETWORK_ID ORDER BY p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID ) AS window_column FROM SECURITYGROUPPORTBINDINGS sgpb JOIN PORTS p ON sgpb.PORT_ID = p.ID JOIN IPALLOCATIONS ia ON p.ID = ia.PORT_ID WHERE sgpb.SECURITY_GROUP_ID = '0008e629-5619-41e0-b86c-4eecfeaacb6c' ), Subq2 AS ( SELECT p.id AS port_id, dense_rank() OVER ( ORDER BY psb.port_security_enabled ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW ) AS window_column FROM ports AS p JOIN portsecuritybindings AS psb ON p.id = psb.port_id WHERE p.status = 'DOWN' ), PortNetwork AS ( SELECT p.ID AS port_id, p.NETWORK_ID AS network_id FROM PORTS p JOIN SECURITYGROUPPORTBINDINGS sgpb ON sgpb.PORT_ID = p.ID WHERE sgpb.SECURITY_GROUP_ID = '0008e629-5619-41e0-b86c-4eecfeaacb6c' ) SELECT pn.network_id, COUNT(DISTINCT s1.port_id) AS total_ports_in_security_group, COUNT(DISTINCT s2.port_id) AS total_down_ports, ROUND( COUNT(DISTINCT s2.port_id) * 1.0 / NULLIF(COUNT(DISTINCT s1.port_id), 0), 2 ) AS down_port_ratio FROM PortNetwork pn LEFT JOIN Subq1 s1 ON s1.port_id = pn.port_id LEFT JOIN Subq2 s2 ON s2.port_id = pn.port_id GROUP BY pn.network_id ) SELECT network_id, total_ports_in_security_group, total_down_ports, down_port_ratio FROM inner_cte WHERE total_ports_in_security_group > 0 AND down_port_ratio > 0.50;

question: From the top 10 tenants (by number of qualifying subnets) where the qualifying subnets are IP version 4 and are on networks with an RBAC action of 'access_as_shared' (and whose subnet name/gateway IP group has a maximum IP version greater than 3), show each tenant’s ID, the total number of qualifying subnets, and whether they have any qualifying subnet whose maximum-IP-version-to-window-rank ratio (rounded to 2 decimals) is at least 2.00.
sql: WITH inner_cte AS ( WITH SubnetWindowRanks AS ( SELECT s.NAME, dense_rank() OVER ( ORDER BY sa.UPDATED_AT ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW ) AS window_column FROM SUBNETS AS s JOIN STANDARDATTRIBUTES AS sa ON sa.ID = s.STANDARD_ATTR_ID WHERE s.IP_VERSION = 4 ), SharedNetworkSubnetMaxIP AS ( SELECT s.name, MAX(s.ip_version) AS max_ip_version, s.gateway_ip FROM NETWORKRBACS n JOIN SUBNETS s ON n.object_id = s.network_id WHERE n.action = 'access_as_shared' GROUP BY s.name, s.gateway_ip HAVING MAX(s.ip_version) > 3 ) SELECT swr.NAME AS subnet_name, swr.window_column, sns.gateway_ip, sns.max_ip_version, ROUND(sns.max_ip_version / NULLIF(swr.window_column, 0), 2) AS max_ip_version_per_window_rank FROM SubnetWindowRanks swr JOIN SharedNetworkSubnetMaxIP sns ON sns.name = swr.NAME ORDER BY max_ip_version_per_window_rank DESC ) SELECT s.tenant_id, COUNT(DISTINCT s.id) AS total_qualifying_subnets, CASE WHEN SUM(CASE WHEN inner_cte.max_ip_version_per_window_rank >= 2.00 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) > 0 THEN 'Yes' ELSE 'No' END AS has_ratio_at_least_2 FROM inner_cte JOIN subnets s ON s.name = inner_cte.subnet_name AND s.gateway_ip = inner_cte.gateway_ip GROUP BY s.tenant_id ORDER BY total_qualifying_subnets DESC LIMIT 10;

question: For ports whose status is DOWN, list the port ID, tenant ID, host, VIF type, allocated IP address, and the row number ordered by IP address (using a window frame of 2 preceding rows and 1 following row), and also include the DOWN-status range, variance, and standard deviation (using STDDEV only and never STDDEV_POP) of the number of port security bindings per port (considering only ports that have at least one port security binding), along with the total number of DOWN ports per tenant and the average number of DOWN ports across all tenants. Do not return any rounded answers.
sql: WITH inner_cte AS (WITH DownPortsWithIPs AS (SELECT p.ID AS port_id, p.TENANT_ID AS tenant_id, b.HOST AS host, b.VIF_TYPE AS vif_type, ia.IP_ADDRESS AS ip_address, ROW_NUMBER() OVER ( ORDER BY ia.IP_ADDRESS ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND 1 FOLLOWING ) AS window_column FROM ML2_PORT_BINDINGS b JOIN PORTS p ON b.PORT_ID = p.ID JOIN IPALLOCATIONS ia ON p.ID = ia.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN'), PortStatusSecurityBindingStats AS (SELECT p.status, MAX(ps.binding_count) - MIN(ps.binding_count) AS binding_count_range, VARIANCE(ps.binding_count) AS binding_count_variance, STDDEV(ps.binding_count) AS binding_count_stddev FROM ports AS p JOIN ( SELECT p2.id AS port_id, COUNT(*) AS binding_count FROM ports AS p2 JOIN portsecuritybindings AS b ON p2.id = b.port_id GROUP BY p2.id ) AS ps ON p.id = ps.port_id GROUP BY p.status ORDER BY binding_count_range DESC) SELECT d.port_id, d.tenant_id, d.host, d.vif_type, d.ip_address, d.window_column, s.binding_count_range, s.binding_count_variance, s.binding_count_stddev FROM DownPortsWithIPs d JOIN PortStatusSecurityBindingStats s ON s.status = 'DOWN' ORDER BY d.ip_address), avg_down_ports AS ( SELECT AVG(down_port_count) AS avg_down_port_count FROM ( SELECT tenant_id, COUNT(*) AS down_port_count FROM ports WHERE status = 'DOWN' GROUP BY tenant_id ) AS sub ), tenant_down_counts AS ( SELECT tenant_id, COUNT(*) AS total_down_ports FROM ports WHERE status = 'DOWN' GROUP BY tenant_id ) SELECT i.port_id, i.tenant_id, i.host, i.vif_type, i.ip_address, i.window_column, i.binding_count_range, i.binding_count_variance, i.binding_count_stddev, tdc.total_down_ports, adp.avg_down_port_count FROM inner_cte i JOIN tenant_down_counts tdc ON tdc.tenant_id = i.tenant_id JOIN avg_down_ports adp ON 1 = 1 ORDER BY i.ip_address;

question: For ports whose status is DOWN, list the port ID, tenant ID, host, VIF type, allocated IP address, and the row number ordered by IP address (using a window frame of 2 preceding rows and 1 following row), along with the DOWN-status range, variance, and standard deviation (using STDDEV only and never STDDEV_POP) of the number of port security bindings per port (considering only ports that have at least one port security binding). Additionally, only keep ports whose tenant has more DOWN ports than the average number of DOWN ports per tenant, and show each port’s total DOWN-port count for its tenant. sql: WITH inner_cte AS (WITH DownPortsWithIPs AS (SELECT p.ID AS port_id, p.TENANT_ID AS tenant_id, b.HOST AS host, b.VIF_TYPE AS vif_type, ia.IP_ADDRESS AS ip_address, ROW_NUMBER() OVER ( ORDER BY ia.IP_ADDRESS ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND 1 FOLLOWING ) AS window_column FROM ML2_PORT_BINDINGS b JOIN PORTS p ON b.PORT_ID = p.ID JOIN IPALLOCATIONS ia ON p.ID = ia.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN'), PortStatusSecurityBindingStats AS (SELECT p.status, MAX(ps.binding_count) - MIN(ps.binding_count) AS binding_count_range, VARIANCE(ps.binding_count) AS binding_count_variance, STDDEV(ps.binding_count) AS binding_count_stddev FROM ports AS p JOIN ( SELECT p2.id AS port_id, COUNT(*) AS binding_count FROM ports AS p2 JOIN portsecuritybindings AS b ON p2.id = b.port_id GROUP BY p2.id ) AS ps ON p.id = ps.port_id GROUP BY p.status ORDER BY binding_count_range DESC) SELECT d.port_id, d.tenant_id, d.host, d.vif_type, d.ip_address, d.window_column, s.binding_count_range, s.binding_count_variance, s.binding_count_stddev FROM DownPortsWithIPs d JOIN PortStatusSecurityBindingStats s ON s.status = 'DOWN' ORDER BY d.ip_address), TenantDownPortCounts AS ( SELECT p.tenant_id, COUNT(*) AS down_port_count FROM ports p WHERE p.status = 'DOWN' GROUP BY p.tenant_id ), AvgDownPortsPerTenant AS ( SELECT AVG(down_port_count) AS avg_down_ports FROM TenantDownPortCounts ) SELECT i.port_id, i.tenant_id, i.host, i.vif_type, i.ip_address, i.window_column, i.binding_count_range, i.binding_count_variance, i.binding_count_stddev, t.down_port_count FROM inner_cte i JOIN TenantDownPortCounts t ON t.tenant_id = i.tenant_id WHERE t.down_port_count > (SELECT avg_down_ports FROM AvgDownPortsPerTenant) ORDER BY i.ip_address;

question: For ports that are DOWN and are also bound to the security group ID 0008e629-5619-41e0-b86c-4eecfeaacb6c, show the port ID, tenant ID, MAC address, port status, and allocated IP address, along with (1) the running sum of the port’s standard attribute ID within each security group (ordered by standard attribute ID) and (2) the running sum of the port’s standard attribute ID within each network (ordered by standard attribute ID). Additionally, for each tenant appearing in these results, include the total number of ports they own and the average number of ports across all tenants. Do not return any rounded answers.
sql: WITH inner_cte AS (WITH Subq1 AS ( SELECT p.ID AS port_id, p.TENANT_ID AS tenant_id, p.MAC_ADDRESS AS mac_address, SUM(p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID) OVER ( PARTITION BY sgpb.SECURITY_GROUP_ID ORDER BY p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID ) AS window_column FROM SECURITYGROUPPORTBINDINGS AS sgpb JOIN PORTS AS p ON sgpb.PORT_ID = p.ID JOIN PORTSECURITYBINDINGS AS psb ON p.ID = psb.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' ), Subq2 AS ( SELECT p.ID AS port_id, p.STATUS AS port_status, ia.IP_ADDRESS AS ip_address, SUM(p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID) OVER ( PARTITION BY p.NETWORK_ID ORDER BY p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID ) AS window_column FROM SECURITYGROUPPORTBINDINGS sgpb JOIN PORTS p ON sgpb.PORT_ID = p.ID JOIN IPALLOCATIONS ia ON p.ID = ia.PORT_ID WHERE sgpb.SECURITY_GROUP_ID = '0008e629-5619-41e0-b86c-4eecfeaacb6c' ) SELECT s1.port_id, s1.tenant_id, s1.mac_address, s2.port_status, s2.ip_address, s1.window_column AS running_sum_standard_attr_id_within_security_group, s2.window_column AS running_sum_standard_attr_id_within_network FROM Subq1 s1 JOIN Subq2 s2 ON s1.port_id = s2.port_id ORDER BY s1.port_id) SELECT i.port_id, i.tenant_id, i.mac_address, i.port_status, i.ip_address, i.running_sum_standard_attr_id_within_security_group, i.running_sum_standard_attr_id_within_network, COUNT(p_all.id) AS total_ports_for_tenant, avg_ports.avg_port_count AS avg_ports_across_all_tenants FROM inner_cte i JOIN ports p_all ON p_all.tenant_id = i.tenant_id JOIN (SELECT AVG(port_count) AS avg_port_count FROM (SELECT COUNT(id) AS port_count FROM ports GROUP BY tenant_id) AS sub) AS avg_ports GROUP BY i.port_id, i.tenant_id, i.mac_address, i.port_status, i.ip_address, i.running_sum_standard_attr_id_within_security_group, i.running_sum_standard_attr_id_within_network, avg_ports.avg_port_count ORDER BY i.port_id;
