WITH DownPortBindingsAndIPs AS ( SELECT p.ID AS port_id, p.TENANT_ID AS tenant_id, b.HOST AS host, b.VIF_TYPE AS vif_type, ia.IP_ADDRESS AS ip_address, ROW_NUMBER() OVER ( ORDER BY ia.IP_ADDRESS ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND 1 FOLLOWING ) AS window_column FROM ML2_PORT_BINDINGS b JOIN PORTS p ON b.PORT_ID = p.ID JOIN IPALLOCATIONS ia ON p.ID = ia.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' ), DownPortsWithSecurityGroups AS ( SELECT p.NAME, p.NETWORK_ID, p.MAC_ADDRESS, p.ADMIN_STATE_UP, p.STATUS, p.DEVICE_OWNER, s.SECURITY_GROUP_ID, MIN(p.ADMIN_STATE_UP) OVER ( ORDER BY p.ID ROWS BETWEEN 3 PRECEDING AND 1 FOLLOWING ) AS window_column FROM PORTS AS p JOIN SECURITYGROUPPORTBINDINGS AS s ON p.ID = s.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' ) SELECT dpbip.tenant_id, COUNT(DISTINCT dpbip.port_id) AS down_port_count, MIN(dpbip.ip_address) AS min_allocated_ip_address, CASE WHEN COUNT(DISTINCT dpsg.SECURITY_GROUP_ID) > 0 THEN 'Yes' ELSE 'No' END AS Has_Bound_Security_Groups FROM DownPortBindingsAndIPs dpbip JOIN PORTS p ON p.ID = dpbip.port_id JOIN DownPortsWithSecurityGroups dpsg ON dpsg.NETWORK_ID = p.NETWORK_ID AND dpsg.MAC_ADDRESS = p.MAC_ADDRESS AND dpsg.STATUS = p.STATUS WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' GROUP BY dpbip.tenant_id HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT dpbip.port_id) >= 2 ORDER BY down_port_count DESC, min_allocated_ip_address ASC;

question: For ports that are DOWN and are bound to security group ID 0008e629-5619-41e0-b86c-4eecfeaacb6c, group the results by port status and whether the port has an IP allocation (Has IP vs No IP). For each group, show the port status, the IP-allocation status, and the number of distinct ports. Include subtotals per port status and a grand total. Do not return any rounded answers.
sql: WITH inner_cte AS ( WITH q1 AS ( SELECT p.ID AS port_id, p.TENANT_ID AS tenant_id, p.MAC_ADDRESS AS mac_address, SUM(p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID) OVER ( PARTITION BY sgpb.SECURITY_GROUP_ID ORDER BY p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID ) AS window_column FROM SECURITYGROUPPORTBINDINGS AS sgpb JOIN PORTS AS p ON sgpb.PORT_ID = p.ID JOIN PORTSECURITYBINDINGS AS psb ON p.ID = psb.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' ), q2 AS ( SELECT p.ID AS port_id, p.STATUS AS port_status, ia.IP_ADDRESS AS ip_address, SUM(p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID) OVER ( PARTITION BY p.NETWORK_ID ORDER BY p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID ) AS window_column FROM SECURITYGROUPPORTBINDINGS sgpb JOIN PORTS p ON sgpb.PORT_ID = p.ID JOIN IPALLOCATIONS ia ON p.ID = ia.PORT_ID WHERE sgpb.SECURITY_GROUP_ID = '0008e629-5619-41e0-b86c-4eecfeaacb6c' ) SELECT q2.port_id, q1.tenant_id, q1.mac_address, q2.port_status, q2.ip_address, q1.window_column AS running_sum_standard_attr_id_within_security_group, q2.window_column AS running_sum_standard_attr_id_within_network FROM q2 JOIN q1 ON q2.port_id = q1.port_id ORDER BY q2.port_id ) , PortRollup AS ( SELECT ic.port_status, CASE WHEN ia.PORT_ID IS NOT NULL THEN 'Has IP' ELSE 'No IP' END AS ip_allocation_status, COUNT(DISTINCT ic.port_id) AS total_ports FROM inner_cte ic LEFT JOIN IPALLOCATIONS ia ON ia.PORT_ID = ic.port_id GROUP BY ic.port_status, ip_allocation_status ) SELECT CASE WHEN GROUPING(port_status) = 1 THEN 'GRAND TOTAL' ELSE port_status END AS port_status, CASE WHEN GROUPING(ip_allocation_status) = 1 AND GROUPING(port_status) = 0 THEN 'SUBTOTAL' ELSE ip_allocation_status END AS ip_allocation_status, SUM(total_ports) AS total_ports FROM PortRollup GROUP BY port_status, ip_allocation_status WITH ROLLUP;

question: For each port status and device owner where the standard attribute resource type is 'ports', list the port count, the earliest standard attribute updated timestamp, and the coefficient of variation (using STDDEV only and never STDDEV_POP) of standard attribute IDs (computed only from ports that have both a security group port binding and a port security binding), but return only those (status, device owner) groups whose port count is greater than the average port count among all device owners with the same port status. Do not return any rounded answers.
sql: WITH inner_cte AS ( WITH PortStatusOwnerStats AS ( SELECT p.STATUS AS port_status, p.DEVICE_OWNER AS device_owner, COUNT(p.ID) AS port_count, MIN(sa.UPDATED_AT) AS earliest_standard_attr_update FROM PORTS p JOIN STANDARDATTRIBUTES sa ON sa.ID = p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID WHERE sa.RESOURCE_TYPE = 'ports' GROUP BY p.STATUS, p.DEVICE_OWNER ), PortStatusVariation AS ( SELECT p.status, STDDEV(p.standard_attr_id) / NULLIF(AVG(p.standard_attr_id), 0) AS coefficient_of_variation FROM securitygroupportbindings AS sgpb JOIN ports AS p ON sgpb.port_id = p.id JOIN portsecuritybindings AS psb ON p.id = psb.port_id GROUP BY p.status HAVING AVG(p.standard_attr_id) > 0 ORDER BY coefficient_of_variation DESC ), CombinedPortStatusMetrics AS ( SELECT psos.port_status AS port_status, psos.device_owner AS device_owner, psos.port_count AS port_count, psos.earliest_standard_attr_update AS earliest_standard_attr_update, psv.coefficient_of_variation AS coefficient_of_variation FROM PortStatusOwnerStats psos JOIN PortStatusVariation psv ON psos.port_status = psv.status ) SELECT port_status, device_owner, port_count, earliest_standard_attr_update, coefficient_of_variation FROM CombinedPortStatusMetrics ORDER BY port_status, device_owner ), StatusAverages AS ( SELECT port_status, AVG(port_count) AS avg_ports_per_owner_in_status FROM inner_cte GROUP BY port_status ) SELECT i.port_status, i.device_owner, i.port_count, i.earliest_standard_attr_update, i.coefficient_of_variation FROM inner_cte i JOIN StatusAverages sa ON sa.port_status = i.port_status WHERE i.port_count > sa.avg_ports_per_owner_in_status ORDER BY i.port_status, i.device_owner;

WITH PortStatusOwnerStats AS ( SELECT p.STATUS AS port_status, p.DEVICE_OWNER AS device_owner, COUNT(p.ID) AS port_count, MIN(sa.UPDATED_AT) AS earliest_standard_attr_update FROM PORTS p JOIN STANDARDATTRIBUTES sa ON sa.ID = p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID WHERE sa.RESOURCE_TYPE = 'ports' GROUP BY p.STATUS, p.DEVICE_OWNER ), PortStatusVariation AS ( SELECT p.status, STDDEV(p.standard_attr_id) / NULLIF(AVG(p.standard_attr_id), 0) AS coefficient_of_variation FROM securitygroupportbindings AS sgpb JOIN ports AS p ON sgpb.port_id = p.id JOIN portsecuritybindings AS psb ON p.id = psb.port_id GROUP BY p.status HAVING AVG(p.standard_attr_id) > 0 ORDER BY coefficient_of_variation DESC ), CombinedPortStatusMetrics AS ( SELECT psos.port_status AS port_status, psos.device_owner AS device_owner, psos.port_count AS port_count, psos.earliest_standard_attr_update AS earliest_standard_attr_update, psv.coefficient_of_variation AS coefficient_of_variation FROM PortStatusOwnerStats psos JOIN PortStatusVariation psv ON psos.port_status = psv.status ) SELECT port_status, device_owner, port_count, earliest_standard_attr_update, coefficient_of_variation FROM CombinedPortStatusMetrics ORDER BY port_status, device_owner;

question: For IPv4 subnets, list each subnet route’s destination and next hop along with the subnet name and CIDR and the allocation pool’s first and last IP, include a dense rank within each subnet, and also show (per subnet name) the range and variance of the DNS nameserver order values configured for that subnet; additionally, compute the deviation of each subnet’s DNS order range from the average DNS order range across all IPv4 subnets. Do not return any rounded answers.
sql: WITH inner_cte AS (WITH DnsOrderStats AS ( SELECT s.name AS subnet_name, MAX(d.ORDER) - MIN(d.ORDER) AS order_range, VARIANCE(d.ORDER) AS order_variance FROM SUBNETS AS s JOIN DNSNAMESERVERS AS d ON s.id = d.subnet_id WHERE s.ip_version = 4 GROUP BY s.name ORDER BY order_range DESC ), SubnetRoutePoolDetails AS ( SELECT r.DESTINATION, r.NEXTHOP, s.NAME AS subnet_name, s.CIDR AS subnet_cidr, p.FIRST_IP, p.LAST_IP, DENSE_RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY r.SUBNET_ID ORDER BY r.SUBNET_ID) AS window_column FROM SUBNETROUTES r JOIN SUBNETS s ON r.SUBNET_ID = s.ID JOIN IPALLOCATIONPOOLS p ON s.ID = p.SUBNET_ID WHERE s.IP_VERSION = 4 ) SELECT srpd.subnet_name, srpd.subnet_cidr, srpd.DESTINATION, srpd.NEXTHOP, srpd.FIRST_IP, srpd.LAST_IP, srpd.window_column, dos.order_range, dos.order_variance FROM SubnetRoutePoolDetails srpd JOIN DnsOrderStats dos ON srpd.subnet_name = dos.subnet_name ORDER BY srpd.subnet_name, srpd.window_column, srpd.DESTINATION) , AvgDnsOrderRange AS (SELECT AVG(order_range) AS avg_order_range FROM inner_cte) SELECT i.subnet_name, i.subnet_cidr, i.DESTINATION, i.NEXTHOP, i.FIRST_IP, i.LAST_IP, i.window_column, i.order_range, i.order_variance, (i.order_range - a.avg_order_range) AS deviation_from_avg_order_range FROM inner_cte i CROSS JOIN AvgDnsOrderRange a ORDER BY i.subnet_name, i.window_column, i.DESTINATION;

WITH DnsOrderStats AS ( SELECT s.name AS subnet_name, MAX(d.ORDER) - MIN(d.ORDER) AS order_range, VARIANCE(d.ORDER) AS order_variance FROM SUBNETS AS s JOIN DNSNAMESERVERS AS d ON s.id = d.subnet_id WHERE s.ip_version = 4 GROUP BY s.name ORDER BY order_range DESC ), SubnetRoutePoolDetails AS ( SELECT r.DESTINATION, r.NEXTHOP, s.NAME AS subnet_name, s.CIDR AS subnet_cidr, p.FIRST_IP, p.LAST_IP, DENSE_RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY r.SUBNET_ID ORDER BY r.SUBNET_ID) AS window_column FROM SUBNETROUTES r JOIN SUBNETS s ON r.SUBNET_ID = s.ID JOIN IPALLOCATIONPOOLS p ON s.ID = p.SUBNET_ID WHERE s.IP_VERSION = 4 ) SELECT srpd.subnet_name, srpd.subnet_cidr, srpd.DESTINATION, srpd.NEXTHOP, srpd.FIRST_IP, srpd.LAST_IP, srpd.window_column, dos.order_range, dos.order_variance FROM SubnetRoutePoolDetails srpd JOIN DnsOrderStats dos ON srpd.subnet_name = dos.subnet_name ORDER BY srpd.subnet_name, srpd.window_column, srpd.DESTINATION;

question: For security groups whose number of DOWN ports is greater than the average number of DOWN ports per security group, list each security group ID along with (1) its count of DOWN ports (based on the security-group windowed standard-attribute running sum result) and (2) the total number of administratively up ports that have at least one IP allocation. Do not return any rounded answers.
sql: WITH inner_cte AS (WITH ip_allocations_admin_up AS (SELECT p.id AS port_id, p.tenant_id, p.mac_address, COUNT(ia.ip_address) AS ip_allocation_count, SUM(CASE WHEN ia.subnet_id IS NOT NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS subnet_id_rows FROM ports p JOIN portsecuritybindings psb ON psb.port_id = p.id JOIN ipallocations ia ON ia.port_id = p.id WHERE p.admin_state_up = 1 AND ia.ip_address IS NOT NULL GROUP BY p.id, p.tenant_id, p.mac_address), down_ports_window AS (SELECT p.ID AS port_id, p.TENANT_ID AS tenant_id, p.MAC_ADDRESS AS mac_address, SUM(p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID) OVER ( PARTITION BY sgpb.SECURITY_GROUP_ID ORDER BY p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID ) AS window_column FROM SECURITYGROUPPORTBINDINGS AS sgpb JOIN PORTS AS p ON sgpb.PORT_ID = p.ID JOIN PORTSECURITYBINDINGS AS psb ON p.ID = psb.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN') SELECT COUNT(*) AS admin_up_ports_with_ip_allocations_count, COUNT(DISTINCT dpw.port_id) AS down_ports_count FROM ip_allocations_admin_up iaau CROSS JOIN down_ports_window dpw), DownPortsPerSecurityGroup AS ( SELECT sgpb.security_group_id, COUNT(DISTINCT dpw.port_id) AS down_ports_in_sg, MAX(inner_cte.admin_up_ports_with_ip_allocations_count) AS admin_up_ports_with_ip_allocations_count FROM SECURITYGROUPPORTBINDINGS sgpb JOIN ( SELECT p.ID AS port_id, sgpb2.SECURITY_GROUP_ID AS security_group_id, SUM(p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID) OVER (PARTITION BY sgpb2.SECURITY_GROUP_ID ORDER BY p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID) AS window_column FROM SECURITYGROUPPORTBINDINGS AS sgpb2 JOIN PORTS AS p ON sgpb2.PORT_ID = p.ID JOIN PORTSECURITYBINDINGS AS psb ON p.ID = psb.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' ) dpw ON dpw.security_group_id = sgpb.security_group_id AND dpw.port_id = sgpb.port_id CROSS JOIN inner_cte GROUP BY sgpb.security_group_id ) SELECT security_group_id, down_ports_in_sg, admin_up_ports_with_ip_allocations_count FROM DownPortsPerSecurityGroup WHERE down_ports_in_sg > (SELECT AVG(down_ports_in_sg) FROM DownPortsPerSecurityGroup);

WITH ip_allocations_admin_up AS (SELECT p.id AS port_id, p.tenant_id, p.mac_address, COUNT(ia.ip_address) AS ip_allocation_count, SUM(CASE WHEN ia.subnet_id IS NOT NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS subnet_id_rows FROM ports p JOIN portsecuritybindings psb ON psb.port_id = p.id JOIN ipallocations ia ON ia.port_id = p.id WHERE p.admin_state_up = 1 AND ia.ip_address IS NOT NULL GROUP BY p.id, p.tenant_id, p.mac_address), down_ports_window AS (SELECT p.ID AS port_id, p.TENANT_ID AS tenant_id, p.MAC_ADDRESS AS mac_address, SUM(p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID) OVER ( PARTITION BY sgpb.SECURITY_GROUP_ID ORDER BY p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID ) AS window_column FROM SECURITYGROUPPORTBINDINGS AS sgpb JOIN PORTS AS p ON sgpb.PORT_ID = p.ID JOIN PORTSECURITYBINDINGS AS psb ON p.ID = psb.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN') SELECT COUNT(*) AS admin_up_ports_with_ip_allocations_count, COUNT(DISTINCT dpw.port_id) AS down_ports_count FROM ip_allocations_admin_up iaau CROSS JOIN down_ports_window dpw;

question: For active networks, using the per-tenant first network by name (row_number = 1) and the subnet on that network (by subnet name) that has at least one DNS nameserver entry, group the results by the network’s admin_state_up flag and an MTU bucket ('Jumbo' if MTU >= 9000, 'Standard' otherwise). For each group, show the admin_state_up flag, the MTU bucket, the number of distinct tenants, and the average subnet IP allocation pool count range, variance, and standard deviation (using STDDEV only and never STDDEV_POP). Include subtotals per admin_state_up and a grand total. Do not return any rounded answers.
sql: WITH inner_cte AS ( WITH SubnetPoolStats AS ( SELECT s.name AS subnet_name, MAX(pool_count) - MIN(pool_count) AS pool_count_range, VARIANCE(pool_count) AS pool_count_variance, STDDEV(pool_count) AS pool_count_stddev FROM subnets AS s JOIN dnsnameservers AS d ON d.subnet_id = s.id JOIN ( SELECT s2.id AS subnet_id, COUNT(*) AS pool_count FROM subnets AS s2 JOIN ipallocationpools AS p ON p.subnet_id = s2.id GROUP BY s2.id, p.id ) AS pool_stats ON pool_stats.subnet_id = s.id GROUP BY s.name ORDER BY pool_count_range DESC ), ActiveNetworks AS ( SELECT n.ID AS network_id, n.NAME AS network_name, n.TENANT_ID AS tenant_id, n.ADMIN_STATE_UP AS admin_state_up, n.MTU AS mtu, sa.UPDATED_AT AS standard_attr_updated_at, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY n.TENANT_ID ORDER BY n.NAME) AS window_column FROM NETWORKS n JOIN STANDARDATTRIBUTES sa ON sa.ID = n.STANDARD_ATTR_ID WHERE n.STATUS = 'ACTIVE' ) SELECT an.tenant_id, an.network_id, an.network_name, an.admin_state_up, an.mtu, an.standard_attr_updated_at, an.window_column, sps.subnet_name, sps.pool_count_range, sps.pool_count_variance, sps.pool_count_stddev FROM ActiveNetworks an JOIN subnets s ON s.network_id = an.network_id JOIN SubnetPoolStats sps ON sps.subnet_name = s.name WHERE an.window_column = 1 ORDER BY sps.pool_count_range DESC, an.tenant_id, an.network_name ), GroupedStats AS ( SELECT ic.admin_state_up, CASE WHEN ic.mtu >= 9000 THEN 'Jumbo' ELSE 'Standard' END AS mtu_bucket, COUNT(DISTINCT ic.tenant_id) AS distinct_tenants, AVG(ic.pool_count_range) AS avg_pool_count_range, AVG(ic.pool_count_variance) AS avg_pool_count_variance, AVG(ic.pool_count_stddev) AS avg_pool_count_stddev FROM inner_cte ic GROUP BY ic.admin_state_up, mtu_bucket ) SELECT CASE WHEN GROUPING(admin_state_up) = 1 THEN 'GRAND TOTAL' ELSE CAST(admin_state_up AS CHAR) END AS admin_state_up, CASE WHEN GROUPING(mtu_bucket) = 1 AND GROUPING(admin_state_up) = 0 THEN 'SUBTOTAL' WHEN GROUPING(mtu_bucket) = 1 AND GROUPING(admin_state_up) = 1 THEN 'GRAND TOTAL' ELSE mtu_bucket END AS mtu_bucket, SUM(distinct_tenants) AS distinct_tenants, AVG(avg_pool_count_range) AS avg_pool_count_range, AVG(avg_pool_count_variance) AS avg_pool_count_variance, AVG(avg_pool_count_stddev) AS avg_pool_count_stddev FROM GroupedStats GROUP BY admin_state_up, mtu_bucket WITH ROLLUP;

question: Among the top 10 tenant/VIF type combinations with the highest number of administratively-up ports (restricted to those where the administratively-up port windowed average standard attribute ID is greater than 0), display the tenant ID, VIF type, the number of distinct administratively-up ports, the number of distinct DOWN ports that have allocated IP addresses, and whether the tenant/VIF type has any DOWN ports with IPs. Do not return any rounded answers.
sql: WITH inner_cte AS (WITH AdminUpPorts AS ( SELECT b.PORT_ID, b.HOST, b.VIF_TYPE, b.VNIC_TYPE, p.TENANT_ID, p.NETWORK_ID, p.MAC_ADDRESS, p.STATUS, p.DEVICE_OWNER, AVG(p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID) OVER ( PARTITION BY b.VIF_TYPE ORDER BY p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND 2 FOLLOWING ) AS window_column FROM ML2_PORT_BINDINGS AS b JOIN PORTS AS p ON b.PORT_ID = p.ID JOIN PORTSECURITYBINDINGS AS psb ON p.ID = psb.PORT_ID WHERE p.ADMIN_STATE_UP = 1 ), DownPortsWithIPs AS ( SELECT p.ID AS port_id, p.TENANT_ID AS tenant_id, b.HOST AS host, b.VIF_TYPE AS vif_type, ia.IP_ADDRESS AS ip_address, ROW_NUMBER() OVER ( ORDER BY ia.IP_ADDRESS ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND 1 FOLLOWING ) AS window_column FROM ML2_PORT_BINDINGS b JOIN PORTS p ON b.PORT_ID = p.ID JOIN IPALLOCATIONS ia ON p.ID = ia.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' ) SELECT aup.TENANT_ID, aup.VIF_TYPE, COUNT(DISTINCT aup.PORT_ID) AS Admin_Up_Port_Count, COUNT(DISTINCT dpi.port_id) AS Down_Port_Count, CASE WHEN COUNT(DISTINCT dpi.port_id) > 0 THEN 'Yes' ELSE 'No' END AS Has_Down_Ports_With_IPs FROM AdminUpPorts aup LEFT JOIN DownPortsWithIPs dpi ON aup.TENANT_ID = dpi.tenant_id AND aup.VIF_TYPE = dpi.vif_type WHERE aup.window_column > 0 GROUP BY aup.TENANT_ID, aup.VIF_TYPE ORDER BY Admin_Up_Port_Count DESC, Down_Port_Count DESC) SELECT inner_cte.TENANT_ID, inner_cte.VIF_TYPE, inner_cte.Admin_Up_Port_Count, inner_cte.Down_Port_Count, inner_cte.Has_Down_Ports_With_IPs FROM inner_cte ORDER BY inner_cte.Admin_Up_Port_Count DESC, inner_cte.Down_Port_Count DESC LIMIT 10;

i.allowed_mac_address, i.allowed_ip_address, i.port_id, i.security_group_id, i.allowed_address_pairs_running_avg_standard_attr_id, i.HOST, i.VIF_TYPE, i.VNIC_TYPE, i.TENANT_ID, i.NETWORK_ID, i.MAC_ADDRESS, i.STATUS, i.DEVICE_OWNER, i.admin_up_ports_window_avg_standard_attr_id, nmsg.max_security_groups_on_any_port FROM inner_cte i JOIN NetworkMaxSecurityGroups nmsg ON i.NETWORK_ID = FROM SECURITYGROUPPORTBINDINGS AS sgpb JOIN PORTS AS p ON sgpb.port_id = p.id JOIN PORTSECURITYBINDINGS AS psb ON p.id = psb.port_id WHERE p.status = 'DOWN' ), subq2 AS ( SELECT p.NAME, p.NETWORK_ID, p.MAC_ADDRESS, p.ADMIN_STATE_UP, p.STATUS, p.DEVICE_OWNER, s.SECURITY_GROUP_ID, MIN(p.ADMIN_STATE_UP) OVER ( ORDER BY p.ID ROWS BETWEEN 3 PRECEDING AND 1 FOLLOWING ) AS window_column FROM PORTS AS p JOIN SECURITYGROUPPORTBINDINGS AS s ON p.ID = s.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' ) SELECT subq1.port_id, subq1.tenant_id, subq2.name AS port_name, subq2.network_id, subq1.mac_address, min_admin_state_up_in_3_preceding_1_following_by_port_id FROM subq1 JOIN subq2 ON subq1.security_group_id = subq2.security_group_id AND subq1.mac_address = subq2.mac_address ORDER BY subq1.security_group_id, subq1.window_column, subq1.port_id ) SELECT inner_cte.port_id, inner_cte.tenant_id, inner_cte.port_name, inner_cte.network_id, inner_cte.mac_address, inner_cte.admin_state_up, question: For each tenant and VIF type, among ports that are administratively up (and where the administratively-up port windowed average standard attribute ID is greater than 0), show the tenant ID, VIF type, the number of distinct administratively-up ports, the number of distinct DOWN ports that have allocated IP addresses, and whether the tenant/VIF type has any DOWN ports with IPs. Also include subtotals per tenant and a grand total across all tenants and VIF types. Do not return any rounded answers.
sql: WITH inner_cte AS (WITH AdminUpPorts AS ( SELECT b.PORT_ID, b.HOST, b.VIF_TYPE, b.VNIC_TYPE, p.TENANT_ID, p.NETWORK_ID, p.MAC_ADDRESS, p.STATUS, p.DEVICE_OWNER, AVG(p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID) OVER ( PARTITION BY b.VIF_TYPE ORDER BY p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND 2 FOLLOWING ) AS window_column FROM ML2_PORT_BINDINGS AS b JOIN PORTS AS p ON b.PORT_ID = p.ID JOIN PORTSECURITYBINDINGS AS psb ON p.ID = psb.PORT_ID WHERE p.ADMIN_STATE_UP = 1 ), DownPortsWithIPs AS ( SELECT p.ID AS port_id, p.TENANT_ID AS tenant_id, b.HOST AS host, b.VIF_TYPE AS vif_type, ia.IP_ADDRESS AS ip_address, ROW_NUMBER() OVER ( ORDER BY ia.IP_ADDRESS ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND 1 FOLLOWING ) AS window_column FROM ML2_PORT_BINDINGS b JOIN PORTS p ON b.PORT_ID = p.ID JOIN IPALLOCATIONS ia ON p.ID = ia.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' ) SELECT aup.TENANT_ID, aup.VIF_TYPE, COUNT(DISTINCT aup.PORT_ID) AS Admin_Up_Port_Count, COUNT(DISTINCT dpi.port_id) AS Down_Port_Count, CASE WHEN COUNT(DISTINCT dpi.port_id) > 0 THEN 'Yes' ELSE 'No' END AS Has_Down_Ports_With_IPs FROM AdminUpPorts aup LEFT JOIN DownPortsWithIPs dpi ON aup.TENANT_ID = dpi.tenant_id AND aup.VIF_TYPE = dpi.vif_type WHERE aup.window_column > 0 GROUP BY aup.TENANT_ID, aup.VIF_TYPE ORDER BY Admin_Up_Port_Count DESC, Down_Port_Count DESC) SELECT CASE WHEN GROUPING(TENANT_ID) = 1 THEN 'GRAND TOTAL' ELSE TENANT_ID END AS TENANT_ID, CASE WHEN GROUPING(VIF_TYPE) = 1 AND GROUPING(TENANT_ID) = 0 THEN 'SUBTOTAL' WHEN GROUPING(VIF_TYPE) = 1 AND GROUPING(TENANT_ID) = 1 THEN 'ALL' ELSE VIF_TYPE END AS VIF_TYPE, SUM(Admin_Up_Port_Count) AS Admin_Up_Port_Count, SUM(Down_Port_Count) AS Down_Port_Count, CASE WHEN SUM(Down_Port_Count) > 0 THEN 'Yes' ELSE 'No' END AS Has_Down_Ports_With_IPs FROM inner_cte GROUP BY TENANT_ID, VIF_TYPE WITH ROLLUP;

question: For the port status value 'DOWN', list the status-level variance of PORTS.STANDARD_ATTR_ID across ports that have an IP allocation, along with each port-binding host and that host’s variance of PORTS.STANDARD_ATTR_ID considering only DOWN ports that have an IP allocation; also include, for each host, the total number of DOWN ports with an IP allocation and the average of that host-level port count across all hosts. Do not return any rounded answers.
sql: WITH inner_cte AS (WITH PortStatusVariances AS ( SELECT p.STATUS, VARIANCE(p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID) AS standard_attr_id_variance FROM PORTS AS p JOIN IPALLOCATIONS AS ia ON p.ID = ia.PORT_ID WHERE p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID IS NOT NULL GROUP BY p.STATUS ORDER BY standard_attr_id_variance DESC ), DownPortHostVariances AS ( SELECT b.HOST, VARIANCE(p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID) AS standard_attr_id_variance FROM ML2_PORT_BINDINGS AS b JOIN PORTS AS p ON b.PORT_ID = p.ID JOIN IPALLOCATIONS AS ia ON p.ID = ia.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' AND ia.PORT_ID IS NOT NULL GROUP BY b.HOST ORDER BY standard_attr_id_variance DESC ) SELECT psv.STATUS, psv.standard_attr_id_variance AS status_standard_attr_id_variance, dhv.HOST, dhv.standard_attr_id_variance AS down_host_standard_attr_id_variance FROM PortStatusVariances AS psv JOIN DownPortHostVariances AS dhv ON psv.STATUS = 'DOWN' WHERE psv.standard_attr_id_variance IS NOT NULL ORDER BY psv.standard_attr_id_variance DESC, dhv.standard_attr_id_variance DESC) SELECT i.STATUS, i.status_standard_attr_id_variance, i.HOST, i.down_host_standard_attr_id_variance, host_counts.down_ports_with_ip_count, avg_host_counts.avg_down_ports_with_ip_count FROM inner_cte AS i JOIN ( SELECT b.HOST, COUNT(DISTINCT p.ID) AS down_ports_with_ip_count FROM ML2_PORT_BINDINGS AS b JOIN PORTS AS p ON b.PORT_ID = p.ID JOIN IPALLOCATIONS AS ia ON p.ID = ia.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' AND ia.PORT_ID IS NOT NULL GROUP BY b.HOST ) AS host_counts ON i.HOST = host_counts.HOST JOIN ( SELECT AVG(down_ports_with_ip_count) AS avg_down_ports_with_ip_count FROM ( SELECT b.HOST, COUNT(DISTINCT p.ID) AS down_ports_with_ip_count FROM ML2_PORT_BINDINGS AS b JOIN PORTS AS p ON b.PORT_ID = p.ID JOIN IPALLOCATIONS AS ia ON p.ID = ia.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' AND ia.PORT_ID IS NOT NULL GROUP BY b.HOST ) AS sub ) AS avg_host_counts ORDER BY i.status_standard_attr_id_variance DESC, i.down_host_standard_attr_id_variance DESC, host_counts.down_ports_with_ip_count DESC;

question: For each port status that appears both among ports with a security group port binding and a port security binding and among ports with an IP allocation (and a non-null standard attribute ID), show the status, the coefficient of variation (using STDDEV only and never STDDEV_POP) of standard attribute IDs, the variance of standard attribute IDs, the overall average coefficient of variation (using STDDEV only and never STDDEV_POP) across these statuses, and the deviation of each status’s coefficient of variation (using STDDEV only and never STDDEV_POP) from that overall average, ordered by the coefficient of variation (using STDDEV only and never STDDEV_POP) descending. Do not return any rounded answers.
sql: WITH inner_cte AS ( WITH sq1 AS ( SELECT p.status, STDDEV(p.standard_attr_id) / NULLIF(AVG(p.standard_attr_id), 0) AS coefficient_of_variation FROM securitygroupportbindings AS sgpb JOIN ports AS p ON sgpb.port_id = p.id JOIN portsecuritybindings AS psb ON p.id = psb.port_id GROUP BY p.status HAVING AVG(p.standard_attr_id) > 0 ORDER BY coefficient_of_variation DESC ), sq2 AS ( SELECT p.STATUS, VARIANCE(p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID) AS standard_attr_id_variance FROM PORTS AS p JOIN IPALLOCATIONS AS ia ON p.ID = ia.PORT_ID WHERE p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID IS NOT NULL GROUP BY p.STATUS ORDER BY standard_attr_id_variance DESC ) SELECT sq1.status, sq1.coefficient_of_variation, sq2.standard_attr_id_variance FROM sq1 JOIN sq2 ON sq1.status = sq2.status ORDER BY sq1.coefficient_of_variation DESC ), avg_stats AS (SELECT AVG(coefficient_of_variation) AS avg_coefficient_of_variation FROM inner_cte) SELECT i.status, i.coefficient_of_variation, i.standard_attr_id_variance, a.avg_coefficient_of_variation, (i.coefficient_of_variation - a.avg_coefficient_of_variation) AS deviation_from_avg_coefficient_of_variation FROM inner_cte i CROSS JOIN avg_stats a ORDER BY i.coefficient_of_variation DESC;

question: For each RBAC action that is access_as_shared, list the action along with (1) the variance of subnet IP version (IPv4 vs IPv6) across subnets on the referenced networks, and (2) the overall average, range (max minus min), and variance of subnet IP version (considering only subnets with IP version 4 or 6) for networks referenced by RBAC entries with that same action; additionally, include the global average of the per-action IP-version variance across all RBAC actions as a benchmark and label the shared action as HIGH_VARIANCE if it is at least 50% above the benchmark, LOW_VARIANCE if it is at least 50% below, otherwise AVERAGE_VARIANCE. Do not return any rounded answers.
sql: WITH inner_cte AS ( WITH RbacSharedIpVersionVariance AS ( SELECT n.ACTION, VARIANCE(s.IP_VERSION) AS ip_version_variance FROM NETWORKRBACS AS n JOIN SUBNETS AS s ON n.OBJECT_ID = s.NETWORK_ID WHERE n.ACTION = 'access_as_shared' GROUP BY n.ACTION ORDER BY ip_version_variance DESC ), RbacIpVersionStats AS ( SELECT n.ACTION AS rbac_action, AVG(s.IP_VERSION) AS avg_ip_version, MAX(s.IP_VERSION) - MIN(s.IP_VERSION) AS ip_version_range, VARIANCE(s.IP_VERSION) AS ip_version_variance FROM NETWORKRBACS AS n JOIN SUBNETS AS s ON n.OBJECT_ID = s.NETWORK_ID WHERE s.IP_VERSION IN (4, 6) GROUP BY n.ACTION ORDER BY ip_version_range DESC ) SELECT rs.ACTION AS rbac_action, rs.ip_version_variance AS shared_action_ip_version_variance, ris.avg_ip_version, ris.ip_version_range, ris.ip_version_variance AS overall_ip_version_variance FROM RbacSharedIpVersionVariance rs JOIN RbacIpVersionStats ris ON rs.ACTION = ris.rbac_action ORDER BY rs.ip_version_variance DESC ), AllActionIpVersionVariance AS ( SELECT n.ACTION, VARIANCE(s.IP_VERSION) AS ip_version_variance FROM NETWORKRBACS AS n JOIN SUBNETS AS s ON n.OBJECT_ID = s.NETWORK_ID WHERE s.IP_VERSION IN (4, 6) GROUP BY n.ACTION ), VarianceBenchmark AS ( SELECT AVG(ip_version_variance) AS avg_action_ip_version_variance FROM AllActionIpVersionVariance ) SELECT i.rbac_action, i.shared_action_ip_version_variance, i.avg_ip_version, i.ip_version_range, i.overall_ip_version_variance, vb.avg_action_ip_version_variance AS variance_benchmark, CASE WHEN i.shared_action_ip_version_variance > vb.avg_action_ip_version_variance * 1.5 THEN 'HIGH_VARIANCE' WHEN i.shared_action_ip_version_variance < vb.avg_action_ip_version_variance * 0.5 THEN 'LOW_VARIANCE' ELSE 'AVERAGE_VARIANCE' END AS variance_category FROM inner_cte i CROSS JOIN VarianceBenchmark vb;

question: For load balancers that are both provided by the 'haproxy' provider and have an operating status of ONLINE, list each load balancer’s name, ID, VIP address, provisioning status, operating status, the running average of the load balancer ID within its provider group ordered by load balancer name, its rank within the provider group ordered by total connections, the load balancer’s total connections, and the deviation of its total connections from the average total connections across all such load balancers. Do not return any rounded answers.
sql: WITH inner_cte AS ( WITH subq1 AS ( SELECT lb.NAME, lb.ID, lb.VIP_ADDRESS, lb.PROVISIONING_STATUS, lb.OPERATING_STATUS, AVG(lb.ID) OVER ( PARTITION BY pra.PROVIDER_NAME ORDER BY lb.NAME ) AS window_column FROM LBAAS_LOADBALANCERS AS lb JOIN PROVIDERRESOURCEASSOCIATIONS AS pra ON lb.ID = pra.RESOURCE_ID WHERE pra.PROVIDER_NAME = 'haproxy' ), subq2 AS ( SELECT lb.ID AS loadbalancer_id, lb.NAME AS loadbalancer_name, pra.PROVIDER_NAME AS provider_name, lb.VIP_ADDRESS AS vip_address, RANK() OVER ( PARTITION BY pra.PROVIDER_NAME ORDER BY stats.TOTAL_CONNECTIONS ) AS window_column FROM LBAAS_LOADBALANCER_STATISTICS AS stats JOIN LBAAS_LOADBALANCERS AS lb ON stats.LOADBALANCER_ID = lb.ID JOIN PROVIDERRESOURCEASSOCIATIONS AS pra ON lb.ID = pra.RESOURCE_ID WHERE lb.OPERATING_STATUS = 'ONLINE' ) SELECT s1.NAME AS load_balancer_name, s1.ID AS load_balancer_id, s1.VIP_ADDRESS AS vip_address, s1.PROVISIONING_STATUS AS provisioning_status, s1.OPERATING_STATUS AS operating_status, s1.window_column AS running_avg_loadbalancer_id_within_provider_ordered_by_name, s2.provider_name, s2.window_column AS rank_within_provider_by_total_connections FROM subq1 s1 JOIN subq2 s2 ON s1.ID = s2.loadbalancer_id ORDER BY s1.NAME ), AvgConnections AS ( SELECT AVG(stats.TOTAL_CONNECTIONS) AS avg_total_connections FROM inner_cte i JOIN LBAAS_LOADBALANCER_STATISTICS stats ON stats.LOADBALANCER_ID = i.load_balancer_id ) SELECT i.load_balancer_name, i.load_balancer_id, i.vip_address, i.provisioning_status, i.operating_status, i.running_avg_loadbalancer_id_within_provider_ordered_by_name, i.provider_name, i.rank_within_provider_by_total_connections, stats.TOTAL_CONNECTIONS AS total_connections, (stats.TOTAL_CONNECTIONS - ac.avg_total_connections) AS deviation_from_avg_total_connections FROM inner_cte i JOIN LBAAS_LOADBALANCER_STATISTICS stats ON stats.LOADBALANCER_ID = i.load_balancer_id CROSS JOIN AvgConnections ac ORDER BY i.load_balancer_name;

WITH subq1 AS ( SELECT lb.NAME, lb.ID, lb.VIP_ADDRESS, lb.PROVISIONING_STATUS, lb.OPERATING_STATUS, AVG(lb.ID) OVER ( PARTITION BY pra.PROVIDER_NAME ORDER BY lb.NAME ) AS window_column FROM LBAAS_LOADBALANCERS AS lb JOIN PROVIDERRESOURCEASSOCIATIONS AS pra ON lb.ID = pra.RESOURCE_ID WHERE pra.PROVIDER_NAME = 'haproxy' ), subq2 AS ( SELECT lb.ID AS loadbalancer_id, lb.NAME AS loadbalancer_name, pra.PROVIDER_NAME AS provider_name, lb.VIP_ADDRESS AS vip_address, RANK() OVER ( PARTITION BY pra.PROVIDER_NAME ORDER BY stats.TOTAL_CONNECTIONS ) AS window_column FROM LBAAS_LOADBALANCER_STATISTICS AS stats JOIN LBAAS_LOADBALANCERS AS lb ON stats.LOADBALANCER_ID = lb.ID JOIN PROVIDERRESOURCEASSOCIATIONS AS pra ON lb.ID = pra.RESOURCE_ID WHERE lb.OPERATING_STATUS = 'ONLINE' ) SELECT s1.NAME AS load_balancer_name, s1.ID AS load_balancer_id, s1.VIP_ADDRESS AS vip_address, s1.PROVISIONING_STATUS AS provisioning_status, s1.OPERATING_STATUS AS operating_status, s1.window_column AS running_avg_loadbalancer_id_within_provider_ordered_by_name, s2.provider_name, s2.window_column AS rank_within_provider_by_total_connections FROM subq1 s1 JOIN subq2 s2 ON s1.ID = s2.loadbalancer_id ORDER BY s1.NAME;

question: For ports that are DOWN and bound to host "drive-59", return the port name, MAC address, admin_state_up flag, host, VIF type, the 2-preceding/2-following window average of admin_state_up (partitioned by VIF type and ordered by MAC address), along with the port ID, tenant ID, and the running sum of standard attribute IDs within each VIF type group (ordered by standard attribute ID). Also include, for each tenant appearing in those results, the total number of ports they own and the average number of ports across all tenants. Do not return any rounded answers.
sql: WITH inner_cte AS ( WITH DownPortsWindow AS ( SELECT p.NAME, p.MAC_ADDRESS, p.ADMIN_STATE_UP, b.HOST, b.VIF_TYPE, AVG(p.ADMIN_STATE_UP) OVER ( PARTITION BY b.VIF_TYPE ORDER BY p.MAC_ADDRESS ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND 2 FOLLOWING ) AS window_column FROM PORTS AS p JOIN ML2_PORT_BINDINGS AS b ON p.ID = b.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' ORDER BY p.MAC_ADDRESS ), Drive59PortsRunningSum AS ( SELECT b.PORT_ID, p.TENANT_ID, p.MAC_ADDRESS, SUM(p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID) OVER ( PARTITION BY b.VIF_TYPE ORDER BY p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID ) AS window_column FROM ML2_PORT_BINDINGS AS b JOIN PORTS AS p ON b.PORT_ID = p.ID JOIN PORTSECURITYBINDINGS AS psb ON p.ID = psb.PORT_ID WHERE b.HOST = 'drive-59' ), DownDrive59PortDetails AS ( SELECT dpw.NAME, dpw.MAC_ADDRESS, dpw.ADMIN_STATE_UP, dpw.HOST, dpw.VIF_TYPE, dpw.window_column AS down_ports_avg_admin_state_up_window, d59.PORT_ID, d59.TENANT_ID, d59.window_column AS drive59_running_sum_standard_attr_id FROM DownPortsWindow dpw JOIN Drive59PortsRunningSum d59 ON dpw.MAC_ADDRESS = d59.MAC_ADDRESS WHERE dpw.HOST = 'drive-59' ) SELECT * FROM DownDrive59PortDetails ORDER BY VIF_TYPE, MAC_ADDRESS, PORT_ID ), avg_ports AS ( SELECT AVG(port_count) AS avg_port_count FROM ( SELECT COUNT(p2.ID) AS port_count FROM PORTS p2 GROUP BY p2.TENANT_ID ) AS sub ), tenant_port_counts AS ( SELECT p3.TENANT_ID, COUNT(p3.ID) AS total_ports FROM PORTS p3 GROUP BY p3.TENANT_ID ) SELECT i.*, tpc.total_ports, ap.avg_port_count FROM inner_cte i JOIN tenant_port_counts tpc ON i.TENANT_ID = tpc.TENANT_ID JOIN avg_ports ap ORDER BY i.VIF_TYPE, i.MAC_ADDRESS, i.PORT_ID;

question: For ACTIVE networks, list each network’s ID, name, tenant ID, admin_state_up flag, MTU, and standard-attribute updated_at timestamp, along with any DOWN ports on that network (port ID and MAC address), the port’s security group ID, the port’s rank within its security group (ordered by port ID), and the network’s row number within its tenant (ordered by network name). Also include, for each row, the deviation of that network’s MTU from the average MTU across all ACTIVE networks. Do not return any rounded answers.
sql: WITH inner_cte AS ( WITH q1 AS ( SELECT p.id AS port_id, p.tenant_id, p.mac_address, sgpb.security_group_id, RANK() OVER ( PARTITION BY sgpb.security_group_id ORDER BY p.id ) AS window_column FROM SECURITYGROUPPORTBINDINGS AS sgpb JOIN PORTS AS p ON sgpb.port_id = p.id JOIN PORTSECURITYBINDINGS AS psb ON p.id = psb.port_id WHERE p.status = 'DOWN' ), q2 AS ( SELECT n.ID AS network_id, n.NAME AS network_name, n.TENANT_ID AS tenant_id, n.ADMIN_STATE_UP AS admin_state_up, n.MTU AS mtu, sa.UPDATED_AT AS standard_attr_updated_at, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY n.TENANT_ID ORDER BY n.NAME) AS window_column FROM NETWORKS n JOIN STANDARDATTRIBUTES sa ON sa.ID = n.STANDARD_ATTR_ID WHERE n.STATUS = 'ACTIVE' ) SELECT q2.network_id, q2.network_name, q2.tenant_id, q2.admin_state_up, q2.mtu, q2.standard_attr_updated_at, q1.port_id, q1.mac_address, q1.security_group_id, q1.window_column AS port_rank_within_security_group, q2.window_column AS network_row_number_within_tenant FROM q2 JOIN PORTS p ON p.network_id = q2.network_id JOIN q1 ON q1.port_id = p.id AND q1.tenant_id = q2.tenant_id ORDER BY q2.tenant_id, q2.network_name, q1.security_group_id, q1.window_column, q1.port_id ), avg_active_mtu AS ( SELECT AVG(n.mtu) AS avg_mtu FROM NETWORKS n WHERE n.status = 'ACTIVE' ) SELECT i.network_id, i.network_name, i.tenant_id, i.admin_state_up, i.mtu, i.standard_attr_updated_at, i.port_id, i.mac_address, i.security_group_id, i.port_rank_within_security_group, i.network_row_number_within_tenant, (i.mtu - a.avg_mtu) AS deviation_from_avg_active_network_mtu FROM inner_cte i CROSS JOIN avg_active_mtu a;

question: For DOWN ports, list the port ID, tenant ID, port name, network ID, MAC address, device owner, allocated IP address, and the row number within each network (ordered by port ID), along with the DOWN-status range, variance, and standard deviation (using STDDEV only and never STDDEV_POP) of port security binding counts per port (considering only ports with at least one binding) and the total number of DOWN ports in the same network; additionally, include the number of allocated IP addresses in that port’s subnet and the deviation of that subnet’s allocated IP count from the average allocated IP count across all subnets. Do not return any rounded answers.
sql: WITH inner_cte AS (WITH DownPortsWithIPs AS ( SELECT p.ID AS port_id, p.TENANT_ID AS tenant_id, p.NAME AS port_name, p.NETWORK_ID AS network_id, p.MAC_ADDRESS AS mac_address, p.DEVICE_OWNER AS device_owner, ia.IP_ADDRESS AS ip_address, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY p.NETWORK_ID ORDER BY p.ID) AS window_column FROM PORTS p JOIN IPALLOCATIONS ia ON p.ID = ia.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' ), PortSecurityBindingStatsByStatus AS ( SELECT p.status, MAX(ps.binding_count) - MIN(ps.binding_count) AS binding_count_range, VARIANCE(ps.binding_count) AS binding_count_variance, STDDEV(ps.binding_count) AS binding_count_stddev FROM ports AS p JOIN ( SELECT p2.id AS port_id, COUNT(*) AS binding_count FROM ports AS p2 JOIN portsecuritybindings AS b ON p2.id = b.port_id GROUP BY p2.id ) AS ps ON p.id = ps.port_id GROUP BY p.status ORDER BY binding_count_range DESC ), DownPortCountsByNetwork AS ( SELECT network_id, COUNT(DISTINCT port_id) AS down_port_count FROM DownPortsWithIPs GROUP BY network_id ) SELECT d.port_id, d.tenant_id, d.port_name, d.network_id, d.mac_address, d.device_owner, d.ip_address, d.window_column, ps.status, ps.binding_count_range, ps.binding_count_variance, ps.binding_count_stddev, c.down_port_count FROM DownPortsWithIPs d JOIN PortSecurityBindingStatsByStatus ps ON ps.status = 'DOWN' JOIN DownPortCountsByNetwork c ON d.network_id = c.network_id ORDER BY d.network_id, d.window_column), SubnetAllocations AS ( SELECT ia.subnet_id, ia.network_id, COUNT(DISTINCT ia.ip_address) AS allocated_ips FROM ipallocations ia GROUP BY ia.subnet_id, ia.network_id ), AverageAllocations AS ( SELECT AVG(allocated_ips) AS avg_ips FROM SubnetAllocations ) SELECT i.port_id, i.tenant_id, i.port_name, i.network_id, i.mac_address, i.device_owner, i.ip_address, i.window_column, i.status, i.binding_count_range, i.binding_count_variance, i.binding_count_stddev, i.down_port_count, ia.subnet_id, sa.allocated_ips AS subnet_allocated_ips, (sa.allocated_ips - aa.avg_ips) AS subnet_deviation_from_avg_allocated_ips FROM inner_cte i JOIN ipallocations ia ON ia.port_id = i.port_id AND ia.ip_address = i.ip_address JOIN SubnetAllocations sa ON sa.subnet_id = ia.subnet_id AND sa.network_id = ia.network_id CROSS JOIN AverageAllocations aa ORDER BY i.network_id, i.window_column;

SELECT p.status, MAX(ps.binding_count) - MIN(ps.binding_count) AS binding_count_range, VARIANCE(ps.binding_count) AS binding_count_variance, STDDEV(ps.binding_count) AS binding_count_stddev FROM ports AS p JOIN ( SELECT p2.id AS port_id, COUNT(*) AS binding_count FROM ports AS p2 JOIN portsecuritybindings AS b ON p2.id = b.port_id GROUP BY p2.id ) AS ps ON p.id = ps.port_id GROUP BY p.status ORDER BY binding_count_range DESC;

WITH DownPortsWithIPs AS ( SELECT p.ID AS port_id, p.TENANT_ID AS tenant_id, p.NAME AS port_name, p.NETWORK_ID AS network_id, p.MAC_ADDRESS AS mac_address, p.DEVICE_OWNER AS device_owner, ia.IP_ADDRESS AS ip_address, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY p.NETWORK_ID ORDER BY p.ID) AS window_column FROM PORTS p JOIN IPALLOCATIONS ia ON p.ID = ia.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' ), PortSecurityBindingStatsByStatus AS ( SELECT p.status, MAX(ps.binding_count) - MIN(ps.binding_count) AS binding_count_range, VARIANCE(ps.binding_count) AS binding_count_variance, STDDEV(ps.binding_count) AS binding_count_stddev FROM ports AS p JOIN ( SELECT p2.id AS port_id, COUNT(*) AS binding_count FROM ports AS p2 JOIN portsecuritybindings AS b ON p2.id = b.port_id GROUP BY p2.id ) AS ps ON p.id = ps.port_id GROUP BY p.status ORDER BY binding_count_range DESC ), DownPortCountsByNetwork AS ( SELECT network_id, COUNT(DISTINCT port_id) AS down_port_count FROM DownPortsWithIPs GROUP BY network_id ) SELECT d.port_id, d.tenant_id, d.port_name, d.network_id, d.mac_address, d.device_owner, d.ip_address, d.window_column, ps.status, ps.binding_count_range, ps.binding_count_variance, ps.binding_count_stddev, c.down_port_count FROM DownPortsWithIPs d JOIN PortSecurityBindingStatsByStatus ps ON ps.status = 'DOWN' JOIN DownPortCountsByNetwork c ON d.network_id = c.network_id ORDER BY d.network_id, d.window_column;

question: Among IPv4 subnets whose network has an RBAC action of 'access_as_shared', show the top 10 RBAC target tenants by number of distinct shared subnets, along with each tenant’s shared subnet count and whether any of those shared subnets have DNS nameservers configured. Do not return any rounded answers.
sql: WITH inner_cte AS ( WITH Ipv4SubnetDnsOrderStats AS ( SELECT s.name AS subnet_name, MAX(d.ORDER) - MIN(d.ORDER) AS order_range, VARIANCE(d.ORDER) AS order_variance FROM SUBNETS AS s JOIN DNSNAMESERVERS AS d ON s.id = d.subnet_id WHERE s.ip_version = 4 GROUP BY s.name ORDER BY order_range DESC ), SharedNetworkSubnets AS ( SELECT s.NAME AS subnet_name, s.CIDR AS subnet_cidr, n.TARGET_TENANT AS rbac_target_tenant, SUM(s.STANDARD_ATTR_ID) OVER ( PARTITION BY s.IP_VERSION ORDER BY s.STANDARD_ATTR_ID ) AS window_column FROM SUBNETS AS s JOIN NETWORKRBACS AS n ON n.OBJECT_ID = s.NETWORK_ID WHERE n.ACTION = 'access_as_shared' ), CombinedSubnetInsights AS ( SELECT sns.subnet_name, sns.subnet_cidr, sns.rbac_target_tenant, sns.window_column, ids.order_range, ids.order_variance FROM SharedNetworkSubnets sns JOIN Ipv4SubnetDnsOrderStats ids ON ids.subnet_name = sns.subnet_name ) SELECT subnet_name, subnet_cidr, rbac_target_tenant, window_column, order_range, order_variance FROM CombinedSubnetInsights ORDER BY subnet_name ) SELECT i.rbac_target_tenant, COUNT(DISTINCT i.subnet_name) AS total_shared_subnets, CASE WHEN COUNT(DISTINCT d.subnet_id) > 0 THEN 'Yes' ELSE 'No' END AS has_any_dns_nameservers FROM inner_cte i LEFT JOIN SUBNETS s ON s.name = i.subnet_name AND s.cidr = i.subnet_cidr LEFT JOIN DNSNAMESERVERS d ON d.subnet_id = s.id GROUP BY i.rbac_target_tenant ORDER BY total_shared_subnets DESC LIMIT 10;

sub_sqls: SELECT s.name AS subnet_name, MAX(d.ORDER) - MIN(d.ORDER) AS order_range, VARIANCE(d.ORDER) AS order_variance FROM SUBNETS AS s JOIN DNSNAMESERVERS AS d ON s.id = d.subnet_id WHERE s.ip_version = 4 GROUP BY s.name ORDER BY order_range DESC;

SELECT s.NAME AS subnet_name, s.CIDR AS subnet_cidr, n.TARGET_TENANT AS rbac_target_tenant, SUM(s.STANDARD_ATTR_ID) OVER ( PARTITION BY s.IP_VERSION ORDER BY s.STANDARD_ATTR_ID ) AS window_column FROM SUBNETS AS s JOIN NETWORKRBACS AS n ON n.OBJECT_ID = s.NETWORK_ID WHERE n.ACTION = 'access_as_shared';

WITH Ipv4SubnetDnsOrderStats AS ( SELECT s.name AS subnet_name, MAX(d.ORDER) - MIN(d.ORDER) AS order_range, VARIANCE(d.ORDER) AS order_variance FROM SUBNETS AS s JOIN DNSNAMESERVERS AS d ON s.id = d.subnet_id WHERE s.ip_version = 4 GROUP BY s.name ORDER BY order_range DESC ), SharedNetworkSubnets AS ( SELECT s.NAME AS subnet_name, s.CIDR AS subnet_cidr, n.TARGET_TENANT AS rbac_target_tenant, SUM(s.STANDARD_ATTR_ID) OVER ( PARTITION BY s.IP_VERSION ORDER BY s.STANDARD_ATTR_ID ) AS window_column FROM SUBNETS AS s JOIN NETWORKRBACS AS n ON n.OBJECT_ID = s.NETWORK_ID WHERE n.ACTION = 'access_as_shared' ), CombinedSubnetInsights AS ( SELECT sns.subnet_name, sns.subnet_cidr, sns.rbac_target_tenant, sns.window_column, ids.order_range, ids.order_variance FROM SharedNetworkSubnets sns JOIN Ipv4SubnetDnsOrderStats ids ON ids.subnet_name = sns.subnet_name ) SELECT subnet_name, subnet_cidr, rbac_target_tenant, window_column, order_range, order_variance FROM CombinedSubnetInsights ORDER BY subnet_name;

question: For each VIF type, list the VIF type, the number of DOWN ports, the average of the per-port windowed average admin_state_up (2 preceding and 2 following rows partitioned by VIF type and ordered by MAC address), and the average (across the involved hosts) variance of port standard attribute IDs for DOWN ports that have an IP allocation; also include the overall average down_ports_count across VIF types as a benchmark and categorize each VIF type as 'HIGH_DOWN' (at least 50% more than average), 'LOW_DOWN' (at least 50% less than average), or 'AVERAGE_DOWN'. Do not return any rounded answers.
sql: WITH inner_cte AS (WITH DownPortsWindow AS ( SELECT p.NAME, p.MAC_ADDRESS, p.ADMIN_STATE_UP, b.HOST, b.VIF_TYPE, AVG(p.ADMIN_STATE_UP) OVER ( PARTITION BY b.VIF_TYPE ORDER BY p.MAC_ADDRESS ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND 2 FOLLOWING ) AS window_column FROM PORTS AS p JOIN ML2_PORT_BINDINGS AS b ON p.ID = b.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' ORDER BY p.MAC_ADDRESS ), HostStandardAttrVariance AS ( SELECT b.HOST, VARIANCE(p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID) AS standard_attr_id_variance FROM ML2_PORT_BINDINGS AS b JOIN PORTS AS p ON b.PORT_ID = p.ID JOIN IPALLOCATIONS AS ia ON p.ID = ia.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' AND ia.PORT_ID IS NOT NULL GROUP BY b.HOST ORDER BY standard_attr_id_variance DESC ) SELECT dpw.VIF_TYPE, COUNT(*) AS down_ports_count, AVG(dpw.window_column) AS avg_window_admin_state_up, AVG(hsav.standard_attr_id_variance) AS avg_standard_attr_id_variance_across_hosts FROM DownPortsWindow dpw JOIN HostStandardAttrVariance hsav ON dpw.HOST = hsav.HOST GROUP BY dpw.VIF_TYPE ORDER BY down_ports_count DESC), AverageDownPorts AS (SELECT AVG(down_ports_count) AS avg_down_ports_count FROM inner_cte) SELECT i.VIF_TYPE, i.down_ports_count, i.avg_window_admin_state_up, i.avg_standard_attr_id_variance_across_hosts, adp.avg_down_ports_count AS benchmark, CASE WHEN i.down_ports_count > adp.avg_down_ports_count * 1.5 THEN 'HIGH_DOWN' WHEN i.down_ports_count < adp.avg_down_ports_count * 0.5 THEN 'LOW_DOWN' ELSE 'AVERAGE_DOWN' END AS down_port_category FROM inner_cte i CROSS JOIN AverageDownPorts adp;

sub_sqls: SELECT p.NAME, p.MAC_ADDRESS, p.ADMIN_STATE_UP, b.HOST, b.VIF_TYPE, AVG(p.ADMIN_STATE_UP) OVER ( PARTITION BY b.VIF_TYPE ORDER BY p.MAC_ADDRESS ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND 2 FOLLOWING ) AS window_column FROM PORTS AS p JOIN ML2_PORT_BINDINGS AS b ON p.ID = b.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' ORDER BY p.MAC_ADDRESS;

SELECT b.HOST, VARIANCE(p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID) AS standard_attr_id_variance FROM ML2_PORT_BINDINGS AS b JOIN PORTS AS p ON b.PORT_ID = p.ID JOIN IPALLOCATIONS AS ia ON p.ID = ia.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' AND ia.PORT_ID IS NOT NULL GROUP BY b.HOST ORDER BY standard_attr_id_variance DESC;

WITH DownPortsWindow AS ( SELECT p.NAME, p.MAC_ADDRESS, p.ADMIN_STATE_UP, b.HOST, b.VIF_TYPE, AVG(p.ADMIN_STATE_UP) OVER ( PARTITION BY b.VIF_TYPE ORDER BY p.MAC_ADDRESS ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND 2 FOLLOWING ) AS window_column FROM PORTS AS p JOIN ML2_PORT_BINDINGS AS b ON p.ID = b.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' ORDER BY p.MAC_ADDRESS ), HostStandardAttrVariance AS ( SELECT b.HOST, VARIANCE(p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID) AS standard_attr_id_variance FROM ML2_PORT_BINDINGS AS b JOIN PORTS AS p ON b.PORT_ID = p.ID JOIN IPALLOCATIONS AS ia ON p.ID = ia.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' AND ia.PORT_ID IS NOT NULL GROUP BY b.HOST ORDER BY standard_attr_id_variance DESC ) SELECT dpw.VIF_TYPE, COUNT(*) AS down_ports_count, AVG(dpw.window_column) AS avg_window_admin_state_up, AVG(hsav.standard_attr_id_variance) AS avg_standard_attr_id_variance_across_hosts FROM DownPortsWindow dpw JOIN HostStandardAttrVariance hsav ON dpw.HOST = hsav.HOST GROUP BY dpw.VIF_TYPE ORDER BY down_ports_count DESC;

question: For external networks marked as default (IS_DEFAULT = 0), list each network’s ID, name, status, and admin_state_up along with (1) the average admin_state_up within the same status group ordered by network name and (2) the dense rank of the network ordered by RBAC action using a window frame of the current row and the 2 preceding rows; additionally, include the overall average of these per-network status-group averages across all returned networks. Do not return any rounded answers.
sql: WITH inner_cte AS (WITH default_external_network_rbac_rank AS ( SELECT n.NAME, dense_rank() OVER ( ORDER BY r.ACTION ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW ) AS window_column FROM EXTERNALNETWORKS e JOIN NETWORKS n ON e.NETWORK_ID = n.ID JOIN NETWORKRBACS r ON n.ID = r.OBJECT_ID WHERE e.IS_DEFAULT = 0 ), default_external_network_status_admin_avg AS ( SELECT e.NETWORK_ID, n.NAME, n.STATUS, n.ADMIN_STATE_UP, AVG(n.ADMIN_STATE_UP) OVER (PARTITION BY n.STATUS ORDER BY n.NAME) AS window_column FROM EXTERNALNETWORKS e JOIN NETWORKS n ON e.NETWORK_ID = n.ID WHERE e.IS_DEFAULT = 0 ) SELECT s.NETWORK_ID, s.NAME, s.STATUS, s.ADMIN_STATE_UP, s.window_column AS avg_admin_state_up_within_status_by_name, r.window_column AS dense_rank_by_rbac_action_with_2_preceding_frame FROM default_external_network_status_admin_avg s JOIN default_external_network_rbac_rank r ON s.NAME = r.NAME) SELECT i.NETWORK_ID, i.NAME, i.STATUS, i.ADMIN_STATE_UP, i.avg_admin_state_up_within_status_by_name, i.dense_rank_by_rbac_action_with_2_preceding_frame, overall_avg.overall_avg_of_status_group_avgs FROM inner_cte i JOIN ( SELECT AVG(avg_admin_state_up_within_status_by_name) AS overall_avg_of_status_group_avgs FROM inner_cte ) AS overall_avg ON 1 = 1;

For external networks that are marked as default (is_default = 0), list the network ID, the network name, status, admin_state_up flag, and the average admin_state_up within each status group ordered by network name.

SELECT e.NETWORK_ID, n.NAME, n.STATUS, n.ADMIN_STATE_UP, AVG(n.ADMIN_STATE_UP) OVER (PARTITION BY n.STATUS ORDER BY n.NAME) AS window_column FROM EXTERNALNETWORKS e JOIN NETWORKS n ON e.NETWORK_ID = n.ID WHERE e.IS_DEFAULT = 0;

WITH default_external_network_rbac_rank AS ( SELECT n.NAME, dense_rank() OVER ( ORDER BY r.ACTION ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW ) AS window_column FROM EXTERNALNETWORKS e JOIN NETWORKS n ON e.NETWORK_ID = n.ID JOIN NETWORKRBACS r ON n.ID = r.OBJECT_ID WHERE e.IS_DEFAULT = 0 ), default_external_network_status_admin_avg AS ( SELECT e.NETWORK_ID, n.NAME, n.STATUS, n.ADMIN_STATE_UP, AVG(n.ADMIN_STATE_UP) OVER (PARTITION BY n.STATUS ORDER BY n.NAME) AS window_column FROM EXTERNALNETWORKS e JOIN NETWORKS n ON e.NETWORK_ID = n.ID WHERE e.IS_DEFAULT = 0 ) SELECT s.NETWORK_ID, s.NAME, s.STATUS, s.ADMIN_STATE_UP, s.window_column AS avg_admin_state_up_within_status_by_name, r.window_column AS dense_rank_by_rbac_action_with_2_preceding_frame FROM default_external_network_status_admin_avg s JOIN default_external_network_rbac_rank r ON s.NAME = r.NAME;

question: Using the DOWN ports result set, group the rows by device owner and security group ID and list the device owner, security group ID, the number of DOWN ports, and the average (for DOWN status) coefficient of variation (using STDDEV only and never STDDEV_POP) of allocated IP address string lengths for ports with port security enabled. Include subtotals per device owner and a grand total. Do not return any rounded answers.
sql: WITH inner_cte AS (WITH PortStatusIPLenCV AS (SELECT p.status, STDDEV(LENGTH(ia.ip_address)) / NULLIF(AVG(LENGTH(ia.ip_address)), 0) AS coefficient_of_variation FROM portsecuritybindings psb JOIN ports p ON psb.port_id = p.id JOIN ipallocations ia ON p.id = ia.port_id WHERE psb.port_security_enabled = 1 GROUP BY p.status HAVING AVG(LENGTH(ia.ip_address)) > 0 ORDER BY coefficient_of_variation DESC), DownPortsWithSecurityGroup AS (SELECT p.NAME, p.NETWORK_ID, p.MAC_ADDRESS, p.ADMIN_STATE_UP, p.STATUS, p.DEVICE_OWNER, s.SECURITY_GROUP_ID, MIN(p.ADMIN_STATE_UP) OVER ( ORDER BY p.ID ROWS BETWEEN 3 PRECEDING AND 1 FOLLOWING ) AS window_column FROM PORTS AS p JOIN SECURITYGROUPPORTBINDINGS AS s ON p.ID = s.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN') SELECT d.NAME, d.NETWORK_ID, d.MAC_ADDRESS, d.ADMIN_STATE_UP, d.STATUS, d.DEVICE_OWNER, d.SECURITY_GROUP_ID, d.window_column, cv.coefficient_of_variation AS status_ip_length_coefficient_of_variation FROM DownPortsWithSecurityGroup d JOIN PortStatusIPLenCV cv ON d.STATUS = cv.status ORDER BY cv.coefficient_of_variation DESC, d.NAME) SELECT CASE WHEN GROUPING(device_owner) = 1 THEN 'GRAND TOTAL' ELSE device_owner END AS device_owner, CASE WHEN GROUPING(security_group_id) = 1 AND GROUPING(device_owner) = 0 THEN 'SUBTOTAL' ELSE security_group_id END AS security_group_id, COUNT(*) AS down_ports, AVG(status_ip_length_coefficient_of_variation) AS avg_down_status_ip_length_coefficient_of_variation FROM inner_cte GROUP BY device_owner, security_group_id WITH ROLLUP;
sub_questions: For each port status, show the status value and the coefficient of variation (standard deviation divided by average) of the length of the allocated IP address strings for ports that have port security enabled.

For ports that are DOWN, show the port name, network ID, MAC address, admin state, status, device owner, the bound security group ID, and the minimum admin_state_up value in a window of 3 preceding and 1 following row ordered by port ID.

For ports that are DOWN, list the port name, network ID, MAC address, admin state, status, device owner, the bound security group ID, and the minimum admin_state_up value in a window of 3 preceding and 1 following row ordered by port ID, and also include (for the DOWN status) the coefficient of variation (standard deviation divided by average) of the length of allocated IP address strings for ports that have port security enabled.
sub_sqls: SELECT p.status, STDDEV(LENGTH(ia.ip_address)) / NULLIF(AVG(LENGTH(ia.ip_address)), 0) AS coefficient_of_variation FROM portsecuritybindings psb JOIN ports p ON psb.port_id = p.id JOIN ipallocations ia ON p.id = ia.port_id WHERE psb.port_security_enabled = 1 GROUP BY p.status HAVING AVG(LENGTH(ia.ip_address)) > 0 ORDER BY coefficient_of_variation DESC;

SELECT p.NAME, p.NETWORK_ID, p.MAC_ADDRESS, p.ADMIN_STATE_UP, p.STATUS, p.DEVICE_OWNER, s.SECURITY_GROUP_ID, MIN(p.ADMIN_STATE_UP) OVER ( ORDER BY p.ID ROWS BETWEEN 3 PRECEDING AND 1 FOLLOWING ) AS window_column FROM PORTS AS p JOIN SECURITYGROUPPORTBINDINGS AS s ON p.ID = s.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN';

WITH PortStatusIPLenCV AS (SELECT p.status, STDDEV(LENGTH(ia.ip_address)) / NULLIF(AVG(LENGTH(ia.ip_address)), 0) AS coefficient_of_variation FROM portsecuritybindings psb JOIN ports p ON psb.port_id = p.id JOIN ipallocations ia ON p.id = ia.port_id WHERE psb.port_security_enabled = 1 GROUP BY p.status HAVING AVG(LENGTH(ia.ip_address)) > 0 ORDER BY coefficient_of_variation DESC), DownPortsWithSecurityGroup AS (SELECT p.NAME, p.NETWORK_ID, p.MAC_ADDRESS, p.ADMIN_STATE_UP, p.STATUS, p.DEVICE_OWNER, s.SECURITY_GROUP_ID, MIN(p.ADMIN_STATE_UP) OVER ( ORDER BY p.ID ROWS BETWEEN 3 PRECEDING AND 1 FOLLOWING ) AS window_column FROM PORTS AS p JOIN SECURITYGROUPPORTBINDINGS AS s ON p.ID = s.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN') SELECT d.NAME, d.NETWORK_ID, d.MAC_ADDRESS, d.ADMIN_STATE_UP, d.STATUS, d.DEVICE_OWNER, d.SECURITY_GROUP_ID, d.window_column, cv.coefficient_of_variation AS status_ip_length_coefficient_of_variation FROM DownPortsWithSecurityGroup d JOIN PortStatusIPLenCV cv ON d.STATUS = cv.status ORDER BY cv.coefficient_of_variation DESC, d.NAME;

question: Using the same DOWN-and-admin-up ports with ML2 bindings and port security binding stats, group the results by VIF type and show the VIF type, the number of distinct ports, and the total number of times port security is enabled across those ports. Include subtotals per VIF type and a grand total. Do not return any rounded answers.
sql: WITH inner_cte AS (WITH DownPortsWithBindings AS (SELECT p.ID AS port_id, p.NAME AS port_name, p.MAC_ADDRESS AS mac_address, b.HOST AS binding_host, b.VIF_TYPE AS vif_type, RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY p.STATUS ORDER BY p.ID) AS window_column FROM PORTS p JOIN ML2_PORT_BINDINGS b ON p.ID = b.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN'), AdminUpPortSecurityStats AS (SELECT p.id AS port_id, p.tenant_id, p.mac_address, COUNT(psb.port_id) AS binding_count, SUM(CASE WHEN psb.port_security_enabled THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS port_security_enabled_total FROM ports p JOIN portsecuritybindings psb ON p.id = psb.port_id WHERE p.admin_state_up = 1 GROUP BY p.id, p.tenant_id, p.mac_address) SELECT dpwb.port_id, dpwb.port_name, dpwb.mac_address, dpwb.binding_host, dpwb.vif_type, dpwb.window_column, aupss.tenant_id, aupss.binding_count, aupss.port_security_enabled_total FROM DownPortsWithBindings dpwb JOIN AdminUpPortSecurityStats aupss ON dpwb.port_id = aupss.port_id ORDER BY dpwb.window_column, dpwb.port_id) SELECT CASE WHEN GROUPING(vif_type) = 1 THEN 'GRAND TOTAL' ELSE vif_type END AS vif_type, COUNT(DISTINCT port_id) AS total_ports, SUM(port_security_enabled_total) AS total_port_security_enabled FROM inner_cte GROUP BY vif_type WITH ROLLUP;
sub_questions: For ports whose status is DOWN, show the port ID, port name, MAC address, the binding host, VIF type, and the rank of each port within its status group ordered by port ID.

For each port that is administratively up, list the port ID, tenant ID, MAC address, the number of port security bindings on that port, and the total number of times port security is enabled across those bindings.

For ports that are DOWN and also administratively up, show the port ID, port name, MAC address, binding host, VIF type, the port’s rank within the DOWN status group ordered by port ID, along with the tenant ID, the number of port security bindings on the port, and the total number of times port security is enabled across those bindings.
sub_sqls: SELECT p.ID AS port_id, p.NAME AS port_name, p.MAC_ADDRESS AS mac_address, b.HOST AS binding_host, b.VIF_TYPE AS vif_type, RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY p.STATUS ORDER BY p.ID) AS window_column FROM PORTS p JOIN ML2_PORT_BINDINGS b ON p.ID = b.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN';

SELECT p.id AS port_id, p.tenant_id, p.mac_address, COUNT(psb.port_id) AS binding_count, SUM(CASE WHEN psb.port_security_enabled THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS port_security_enabled_total FROM ports p JOIN portsecuritybindings psb ON p.id = psb.port_id WHERE p.admin_state_up = 1 GROUP BY p.id, p.tenant_id, p.mac_address;

WITH DownPortsWithBindings AS (SELECT p.ID AS port_id, p.NAME AS port_name, p.MAC_ADDRESS AS mac_address, b.HOST AS binding_host, b.VIF_TYPE AS vif_type, RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY p.STATUS ORDER BY p.ID) AS window_column FROM PORTS p JOIN ML2_PORT_BINDINGS b ON p.ID = b.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN'), AdminUpPortSecurityStats AS (SELECT p.id AS port_id, p.tenant_id, p.mac_address, COUNT(psb.port_id) AS binding_count, SUM(CASE WHEN psb.port_security_enabled THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS port_security_enabled_total FROM ports p JOIN portsecuritybindings psb ON p.id = psb.port_id WHERE p.admin_state_up = 1 GROUP BY p.id, p.tenant_id, p.mac_address) SELECT dpwb.port_id, dpwb.port_name, dpwb.mac_address, dpwb.binding_host, dpwb.vif_type, dpwb.window_column, aupss.tenant_id, aupss.binding_count, aupss.port_security_enabled_total FROM DownPortsWithBindings dpwb JOIN AdminUpPortSecurityStats aupss ON dpwb.port_id = aupss.port_id ORDER BY dpwb.window_column, dpwb.port_id;

question: For ACTIVE networks, show the network name, status, admin_state_up, RBAC action and target tenant (with the dense rank per network), along with any subnets whose network RBAC action is access_as_shared for the same target tenant (including subnet name, CIDR, and the running sum of subnet standard attribute IDs within each IP version group ordered by standard attribute ID). Also include, for each returned row, the deviation of the subnet’s running-sum value from the overall average running-sum value across all returned subnets. Do not return any rounded answers.
sql: WITH inner_cte AS ( WITH subnet_shared_rbac AS ( SELECT s.NAME AS subnet_name, s.CIDR AS subnet_cidr, n.TARGET_TENANT AS rbac_target_tenant, SUM(s.STANDARD_ATTR_ID) OVER ( PARTITION BY s.IP_VERSION ORDER BY s.STANDARD_ATTR_ID ) AS window_column FROM SUBNETS AS s JOIN NETWORKRBACS AS n ON n.OBJECT_ID = s.NETWORK_ID WHERE n.ACTION = 'access_as_shared' ), active_network_rbac AS ( SELECT n.name, n.status, n.admin_state_up, r.action, r.target_tenant, DENSE_RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY n.id ORDER BY n.id) AS window_column FROM networksecuritybindings b JOIN networks n ON b.network_id = n.id JOIN networkrbacs r ON n.id = r.object_id WHERE n.status = 'ACTIVE' ) SELECT anr.name AS network_name, anr.status AS network_status, anr.admin_state_up, anr.action AS rbac_action, anr.target_tenant AS rbac_target_tenant, anr.window_column AS network_dense_rank, ssr.subnet_name, ssr.subnet_cidr, ssr.window_column AS subnet_standard_attr_running_sum FROM active_network_rbac anr JOIN subnet_shared_rbac ssr ON ssr.rbac_target_tenant = anr.target_tenant AND anr.action = 'access_as_shared' ), avg_running_sum AS ( SELECT AVG(subnet_standard_attr_running_sum) AS avg_subnet_running_sum FROM inner_cte ) SELECT i.network_name, i.network_status, i.admin_state_up, i.rbac_action, i.rbac_target_tenant, i.network_dense_rank, i.subnet_name, i.subnet_cidr, i.subnet_standard_attr_running_sum, (i.subnet_standard_attr_running_sum - a.avg_subnet_running_sum) AS deviation_from_avg_running_sum FROM inner_cte i CROSS JOIN avg_running_sum a;
sub_questions: For subnets whose network has a RBAC action of 'access_as_shared', list the subnet name, its CIDR, the RBAC target tenant, and the running sum of subnet standard attribute IDs within each IP version group ordered by standard attribute ID.

Show each network’s name, status, and admin_state_up together with the RBAC action and target tenant for that network, plus a dense rank within each network (partitioned by network ID and ordered by network ID). Only include networks that are ACTIVE.

For ACTIVE networks, list the network name, status, admin_state_up, RBAC action and target tenant (with the dense rank per network), and also list any subnets whose network RBAC action is access_as_shared for the same target tenant, including the subnet name, CIDR, and the running sum of subnet standard attribute IDs within each IP version group ordered by standard attribute ID.
sub_sqls: SELECT s.NAME AS subnet_name, s.CIDR AS subnet_cidr, n.TARGET_TENANT AS rbac_target_tenant, SUM(s.STANDARD_ATTR_ID) OVER ( PARTITION BY s.IP_VERSION ORDER BY s.STANDARD_ATTR_ID ) AS window_column FROM SUBNETS AS s JOIN NETWORKRBACS AS n ON n.OBJECT_ID = s.NETWORK_ID WHERE n.ACTION = 'access_as_shared';

SELECT n.name, n.status, n.admin_state_up, r.action, r.target_tenant, DENSE_RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY n.id ORDER BY n.id) AS window_column FROM networksecuritybindings b JOIN networks n ON b.network_id = n.id JOIN networkrbacs r ON n.id = r.object_id WHERE n.status = 'ACTIVE'

WITH subnet_shared_rbac AS ( SELECT s.NAME AS subnet_name, s.CIDR AS subnet_cidr, n.TARGET_TENANT AS rbac_target_tenant, SUM(s.STANDARD_ATTR_ID) OVER ( PARTITION BY s.IP_VERSION ORDER BY s.STANDARD_ATTR_ID ) AS window_column FROM SUBNETS AS s JOIN NETWORKRBACS AS n ON n.OBJECT_ID = s.NETWORK_ID WHERE n.ACTION = 'access_as_shared' ), active_network_rbac AS ( SELECT n.name, n.status, n.admin_state_up, r.action, r.target_tenant, DENSE_RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY n.id ORDER BY n.id) AS window_column FROM networksecuritybindings b JOIN networks n ON b.network_id = n.id JOIN networkrbacs r ON n.id = r.object_id WHERE n.status = 'ACTIVE' ) SELECT anr.name AS network_name, anr.status AS network_status, anr.admin_state_up, anr.action AS rbac_action, anr.target_tenant AS rbac_target_tenant, anr.window_column AS network_dense_rank, ssr.subnet_name, ssr.subnet_cidr, ssr.window_column AS subnet_standard_attr_running_sum FROM active_network_rbac anr JOIN subnet_shared_rbac ssr ON ssr.rbac_target_tenant = anr.target_tenant AND anr.action = 'access_as_shared';

question: For the top 10 (port status, device owner) combinations with the most ports that are admin_state_up = 1, bound to a security group, and whose standard attribute resource type is 'ports', show the port status, device owner, count of such bound admin-up ports, the total number of ports for that status/owner with resource type 'ports', the earliest standard-attribute updated timestamp, the total security-group bindings and DNS records across those bound admin-up ports, along with the average bound admin-up port count across these top-10 combinations. Do not return any rounded answers.
sql: WITH inner_cte AS (WITH port_status_owner_stats AS ( SELECT p.STATUS AS port_status, p.DEVICE_OWNER AS device_owner, COUNT(p.ID) AS port_count, MIN(sa.UPDATED_AT) AS earliest_standard_attr_update FROM PORTS p JOIN STANDARDATTRIBUTES sa ON sa.ID = p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID WHERE sa.RESOURCE_TYPE = 'ports' GROUP BY p.STATUS, p.DEVICE_OWNER ), bound_admin_ports AS ( SELECT p.id AS port_id, p.tenant_id, p.name AS port_name, COUNT(sgpb.security_group_id) AS security_group_binding_count, SUM(CASE WHEN pd.port_id IS NULL THEN 0 ELSE 1 END) AS dns_record_count FROM SECURITYGROUPPORTBINDINGS sgpb JOIN PORTS p ON sgpb.port_id = p.id LEFT JOIN PORTDNSES pd ON p.id = pd.port_id WHERE p.admin_state_up = 1 GROUP BY p.id, p.tenant_id, p.name ), top10_status_owner_by_bound_ports AS ( SELECT p.STATUS AS port_status, p.DEVICE_OWNER AS device_owner, COUNT(DISTINCT p.ID) AS bound_admin_port_count FROM PORTS p JOIN STANDARDATTRIBUTES sa ON sa.ID = p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID JOIN SECURITYGROUPPORTBINDINGS sgpb ON sgpb.port_id = p.id WHERE sa.RESOURCE_TYPE = 'ports' AND p.admin_state_up = 1 GROUP BY p.STATUS, p.DEVICE_OWNER ORDER BY bound_admin_port_count DESC LIMIT 10 ) SELECT t.port_status, t.device_owner, t.bound_admin_port_count, psos.port_count AS total_ports_with_standard_attr_resource_type_ports, psos.earliest_standard_attr_update, SUM(bap.security_group_binding_count) AS total_security_group_bindings_across_bound_admin_ports, SUM(bap.dns_record_count) AS total_dns_records_across_bound_admin_ports FROM top10_status_owner_by_bound_ports t JOIN port_status_owner_stats psos ON psos.port_status = t.port_status AND ( (psos.device_owner = t.device_owner) OR (psos.device_owner IS NULL AND t.device_owner IS NULL) ) JOIN PORTS p ON p.STATUS = t.port_status AND ( (p.DEVICE_OWNER = t.device_owner) OR (p.DEVICE_OWNER IS NULL AND t.device_owner IS NULL) ) JOIN STANDARDATTRIBUTES sa ON sa.ID = p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID AND sa.RESOURCE_TYPE = 'ports' JOIN bound_admin_ports bap ON bap.port_id = p.id GROUP BY t.port_status, t.device_owner, t.bound_admin_port_count, psos.port_count, psos.earliest_standard_attr_update ORDER BY t.bound_admin_port_count DESC) SELECT i.port_status, i.device_owner, i.bound_admin_port_count, i.total_ports_with_standard_attr_resource_type_ports, i.earliest_standard_attr_update, i.total_security_group_bindings_across_bound_admin_ports, i.total_dns_records_across_bound_admin_ports, avg_stats.avg_bound_admin_port_count_across_top10 FROM inner_cte i JOIN (SELECT AVG(bound_admin_port_count) AS avg_bound_admin_port_count_across_top10 FROM inner_cte) AS avg_stats;
sub_questions: For each port status and device owner, considering only ports whose standard attribute resource type is 'ports', return the number of ports and the earliest (minimum) standard attribute updated timestamp.

STANDARDATTRIBUTES sa ON sa.ID = p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID WHERE sa.RESOURCE_TYPE = 'ports' GROUP BY p.STATUS, p.DEVICE_OWNER ), bound_admin_ports AS ( SELECT p.id AS port_id, p.tenant_id, p.name AS t.bound_admin_port_count, psos.port_count AS total_ports_with_standard_attr_resource_type_ports, psos.earliest_standard_attr_update, SUM(bap.security_group_binding_count) AS psos ON psos.port_status = t.port_status AND ( (psos.device_owner = t.device_owner) OR (psos.device_owner IS NULL AND t.device_owner IS NULL) ) JOIN PORTS p ON p.STATUS = t.port_status AND ( (p.DEVICE_OWNER = t.device_owner) OR (p.DEVICE_OWNER IS NULL AND t.device_owner IS NULL) ) JOIN STANDARDATTRIBUTES sa ON sa.ID = p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID AND sa.RESOURCE_TYPE = 'ports' JOIN bound_admin_ports bap ON bap.port_id = p.id GROUP BY t.port_status, t.device_owner, t.bound_admin_port_count, psos.port_count, psos.earliest_standard_attr_update ORDER BY t.bound_admin_port_count DESC;

question: For ACTIVE networks, use the existing logic to find networks that have an RBAC action of 'access_as_shared' and match them to subnets whose network is also shared to the same RBAC target tenant. Then, summarize the results by network status and whether the network is admin-up ('AdminUp' if admin_state_up = 1, 'AdminDown' otherwise), returning the status, admin-up label, and the total number of matched (network, subnet) rows, including subtotals per status and a grand total. Do not return any rounded answers.
sql: WITH inner_cte AS (WITH SharedSubnets AS ( SELECT s.NAME AS subnet_name, s.CIDR AS subnet_cidr, n.TARGET_TENANT AS rbac_target_tenant, SUM(s.STANDARD_ATTR_ID) OVER ( PARTITION BY s.IP_VERSION ORDER BY s.STANDARD_ATTR_ID ) AS window_column FROM SUBNETS AS s JOIN NETWORKRBACS AS n ON n.OBJECT_ID = s.NETWORK_ID WHERE n.ACTION = 'access_as_shared' ), ActiveNetworkRBACs AS ( SELECT n.name, n.status, n.admin_state_up, r.action, r.target_tenant, DENSE_RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY n.id ORDER BY n.id) AS window_column FROM networksecuritybindings b JOIN networks n ON b.network_id = n.id JOIN networkrbacs r ON n.id = r.object_id WHERE n.status = 'ACTIVE' ) SELECT anr.name AS network_name, anr.status AS network_status, anr.admin_state_up, anr.action AS rbac_action, anr.target_tenant AS rbac_target_tenant, ss.subnet_name, ss.subnet_cidr, ss.window_column AS subnet_std_attr_running_sum_by_ip_version, anr.window_column AS network_dense_rank_within_network FROM ActiveNetworkRBACs anr JOIN SharedSubnets ss ON ss.rbac_target_tenant = anr.target_tenant AND anr.action = 'access_as_shared' ORDER BY anr.name, ss.subnet_name), MatchSummary AS ( SELECT ic.network_status AS status, CASE WHEN ic.admin_state_up = 1 THEN 'AdminUp' ELSE 'AdminDown' END AS admin_state_label, COUNT(*) AS total_matches FROM inner_cte ic GROUP BY ic.network_status, admin_state_label ) SELECT CASE WHEN GROUPING(status) = 1 THEN 'GRAND TOTAL' ELSE status END AS status, CASE WHEN GROUPING(admin_state_label) = 1 AND GROUPING(status) = 0 THEN 'SUBTOTAL' ELSE admin_state_label END AS admin_state_label, SUM(total_matches) AS total_matches FROM MatchSummary GROUP BY status, admin_state_label WITH ROLLUP;

question: For each RBAC action, show the action, the average/variance/standard deviation (using STDDEV only and never STDDEV_POP) of IP version for its IP-version-4-only subnets, and the standard deviation (using STDDEV only and never STDDEV_POP) of IP version for its DHCP-enabled subnets (only keeping actions with more than 5 DHCP-enabled subnets). Also include subtotals per action and a grand total across all actions. Do not return any rounded answers.
sql: WITH inner_cte AS ( WITH Subq1 AS ( SELECT n.ACTION, AVG(s.IP_VERSION) AS avg_ip_version, VARIANCE(s.IP_VERSION) AS ip_version_variance, STDDEV(s.IP_VERSION) AS ip_version_stddev FROM NETWORKRBACS AS n JOIN SUBNETS AS s ON n.OBJECT_ID = s.NETWORK_ID WHERE s.IP_VERSION = 4 GROUP BY n.ACTION ORDER BY ip_version_variance DESC ), Subq2 AS ( SELECT n.ACTION, STDDEV(s.IP_VERSION) AS ip_version_stddev FROM NETWORKRBACS AS n JOIN SUBNETS AS s ON n.OBJECT_ID = s.NETWORK_ID WHERE s.ENABLE_DHCP = 1 GROUP BY n.ACTION HAVING COUNT(*) > 5 ORDER BY ip_version_stddev DESC ) SELECT s1.ACTION, s1.avg_ip_version, s1.ip_version_variance, s1.ip_version_stddev AS ip_version_stddev_ip4_only, s2.ip_version_stddev AS ip_version_stddev_dhcp_enabled_count_gt_5 FROM Subq1 s1 JOIN Subq2 s2 ON s1.ACTION = s2.ACTION ) SELECT CASE WHEN GROUPING(ACTION) = 1 THEN 'GRAND TOTAL' ELSE ACTION END AS action, AVG(avg_ip_version) AS avg_ip_version, AVG(ip_version_variance) AS ip_version_variance, AVG(ip_version_stddev_ip4_only) AS ip_version_stddev_ip4_only, AVG(ip_version_stddev_dhcp_enabled_count_gt_5) AS ip_version_stddev_dhcp_enabled_count_gt_5 FROM inner_cte GROUP BY ACTION WITH ROLLUP;
sub_questions: For each RBAC action, show the average, variance, and standard deviation of the subnet IP version (4 or 6) across subnets whose network is referenced by an RBAC entry.

question: For haproxy load balancers that are in ACTIVE provisioning status, list the load balancer name, ID, VIP address, provisioning status, operating status, the running average of the load balancer ID within the haproxy provider group ordered by load balancer name, and the total incoming bytes for that operating status. Also include the overall average of total incoming bytes across operating statuses (considering only ACTIVE load balancers) as a benchmark, and categorize each operating status as 'HIGH_BYTES_IN' (at least 50% above the benchmark), 'LOW_BYTES_IN' (at least 50% below the benchmark), or 'AVERAGE_BYTES_IN'. Keep only operating statuses whose total incoming bytes (across ACTIVE load balancers) exceed 1,000,000. Do not return any rounded answers.
sql: WITH inner_cte AS (WITH HapLoadBalancers AS (SELECT lb.NAME, lb.ID, lb.VIP_ADDRESS, lb.PROVISIONING_STATUS, lb.OPERATING_STATUS, AVG(lb.ID) OVER ( PARTITION BY pra.PROVIDER_NAME ORDER BY lb.NAME ) AS window_column FROM LBAAS_LOADBALANCERS AS lb JOIN PROVIDERRESOURCEASSOCIATIONS AS pra ON lb.ID = pra.RESOURCE_ID WHERE pra.PROVIDER_NAME = 'haproxy'), OperatingStatusBytesIn AS (SELECT lb.OPERATING_STATUS, SUM(s.BYTES_IN) AS total_bytes_in FROM LBAAS_LOADBALANCERS AS lb JOIN LBAAS_LOADBALANCER_STATISTICS AS s ON lb.ID = s.LOADBALANCER_ID WHERE lb.PROVISIONING_STATUS = 'ACTIVE' GROUP BY lb.OPERATING_STATUS HAVING SUM(s.BYTES_IN) > 1000000) SELECT hlb.NAME, hlb.ID, hlb.VIP_ADDRESS, hlb.PROVISIONING_STATUS, hlb.OPERATING_STATUS, hlb.window_column, osbi.total_bytes_in FROM HapLoadBalancers hlb JOIN OperatingStatusBytesIn osbi ON hlb.OPERATING_STATUS = osbi.OPERATING_STATUS WHERE hlb.PROVISIONING_STATUS = 'ACTIVE' ORDER BY hlb.NAME), AvgBytesInBenchmark AS (SELECT AVG(total_bytes_in) AS avg_total_bytes_in FROM (SELECT lb.OPERATING_STATUS, SUM(s.BYTES_IN) AS total_bytes_in FROM LBAAS_LOADBALANCERS AS lb JOIN LBAAS_LOADBALANCER_STATISTICS AS s ON lb.ID = s.LOADBALANCER_ID WHERE lb.PROVISIONING_STATUS = 'ACTIVE' GROUP BY lb.OPERATING_STATUS HAVING SUM(s.BYTES_IN) > 1000000) t) SELECT i.NAME, i.ID, i.VIP_ADDRESS, i.PROVISIONING_STATUS, i.OPERATING_STATUS, i.window_column, i.total_bytes_in, a.avg_total_bytes_in AS benchmark, CASE WHEN i.total_bytes_in > a.avg_total_bytes_in * 1.5 THEN 'HIGH_BYTES_IN' WHEN i.total_bytes_in < a.avg_total_bytes_in * 0.5 THEN 'LOW_BYTES_IN' ELSE 'AVERAGE_BYTES_IN' END AS bytes_in_category FROM inner_cte i CROSS JOIN AvgBytesInBenchmark a;
sub_questions: For load balancers provided by the “haproxy” provider, show the load balancer name, load balancer ID, VIP address, provisioning status, operating status, and the running average of the load balancer ID within each provider name group ordered by load balancer name.

For each load balancer operating status, show the operating status and the total number of incoming bytes across load balancers that are in ACTIVE provisioning status, keeping only operating statuses where the total incoming bytes exceed 1,000,000.

question: For each shared network (i.e., networks that have an RBAC action of 'access_as_shared'), find the network ID and the maximum route-count range (max routes per nexthop minus min routes per nexthop) among its IPv4 subnets, considering only subnet name/gateway IP groups where the maximum IP version is greater than 3. Do not return any rounded answers.
sql: WITH inner_cte AS (WITH route_metrics AS ( SELECT s.NAME AS subnet_name, MAX(route_count) - MIN(route_count) AS route_count_range, VARIANCE(route_count) AS route_count_variance, STDDEV(route_count) AS route_count_stddev FROM SUBNETS AS s JOIN ( SELECT sr.SUBNET_ID, COUNT(*) AS route_count FROM SUBNETROUTES AS sr GROUP BY sr.SUBNET_ID, sr.NEXTHOP ) AS route_stats ON s.ID = route_stats.SUBNET_ID WHERE s.IP_VERSION = 4 GROUP BY s.NAME ORDER BY route_count_range DESC ), shared_rbac_max_ip AS ( SELECT s.name, MAX(s.ip_version) AS max_ip_version, s.gateway_ip FROM NETWORKRBACS n JOIN SUBNETS s ON n.object_id = s.network_id WHERE n.action = 'access_as_shared' GROUP BY s.name, s.gateway_ip HAVING MAX(s.ip_version) > 3 ) SELECT rm.subnet_name, srm.gateway_ip, srm.max_ip_version, rm.route_count_range, rm.route_count_variance, rm.route_count_stddev FROM route_metrics rm JOIN shared_rbac_max_ip srm ON rm.subnet_name = srm.name ORDER BY rm.route_count_range DESC) SELECT s.network_id, MAX(inner_cte.route_count_range) AS max_route_count_range FROM inner_cte JOIN SUBNETS s ON s.name = inner_cte.subnet_name AND s.gateway_ip = inner_cte.gateway_ip GROUP BY s.network_id;
sub_questions: For each subnet name, show the range, variance, and standard deviation of the number of routes per subnet, considering only IPv4 subnets.

For each subnet name and its gateway IP, find the maximum IP version among subnets whose network has a RBAC action of 'access_as_shared', and only keep subnet name/gateway IP groups where that maximum IP version is greater than 3.

For subnet names that are IPv4 and belong to networks with an RBAC action of 'access_as_shared' (keeping only subnet name/gateway IP groups where the maximum IP version is greater than 3), list each subnet name and gateway IP along with the maximum IP version and the range, variance, and standard deviation of the number of routes per subnet.
