question: For IPv4 subnets, using the per-subnet route-count range/variance/standard-deviation and the dense-rank window (current row and 2 preceding rows) of the subnet’s standard attribute ordered by updated-at, list each subnet name and its statistics, and also include subtotals and a grand total of how many subnets fall under each window dense-rank value. Do not return any rounded answers.
sql: WITH inner_cte AS (WITH subnet_route_stats AS ( SELECT s.NAME AS subnet_name, MAX(route_count) - MIN(route_count) AS route_count_range, VARIANCE(route_count) AS route_count_variance, STDDEV(route_count) AS route_count_stddev FROM SUBNETS AS s JOIN ( SELECT sr.SUBNET_ID, COUNT(*) AS route_count FROM SUBNETROUTES AS sr GROUP BY sr.SUBNET_ID, sr.NEXTHOP ) AS route_stats ON s.ID = route_stats.SUBNET_ID WHERE s.IP_VERSION = 4 GROUP BY s.NAME ORDER BY route_count_range DESC ), subnet_attr_window_rank AS ( SELECT s.NAME, dense_rank() OVER ( ORDER BY sa.UPDATED_AT ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW ) AS window_column FROM SUBNETS AS s JOIN STANDARDATTRIBUTES AS sa ON sa.ID = s.STANDARD_ATTR_ID WHERE s.IP_VERSION = 4 ) SELECT srs.subnet_name, srs.route_count_range, srs.route_count_variance, srs.route_count_stddev, sawr.window_column FROM subnet_route_stats AS srs JOIN subnet_attr_window_rank AS sawr ON sawr.NAME = srs.subnet_name) SELECT CASE WHEN GROUPING(inner_cte.window_column) = 1 THEN 'GRAND TOTAL' ELSE CAST(inner_cte.window_column AS CHAR) END AS window_dense_rank, CASE WHEN GROUPING(inner_cte.subnet_name) = 1 AND GROUPING(inner_cte.window_column) = 0 THEN 'SUBTOTAL' ELSE inner_cte.subnet_name END AS subnet_name, COUNT(*) AS total_subnets FROM inner_cte GROUP BY inner_cte.window_column, inner_cte.subnet_name WITH ROLLUP;
sub_questions: For each subnet name, show the range, variance, and standard deviation of the number of routes per subnet, considering only IPv4 subnets.

For subnets whose IP version is 4, list each subnet name and the dense rank of its associated standard attribute ID when ordered by the standard attribute’s updated-at timestamp, using a window frame of the current row and the 2 preceding rows.

For IPv4 subnets, for each subnet name, return the range, variance, and standard deviation of the number of routes per subnet, along with the dense rank of its associated standard attribute ID when ordered by the standard attribute’s updated-at timestamp using a window frame of the current row and the 2 preceding rows.
sub_sqls: SELECT s.NAME AS subnet_name, MAX(route_count) - MIN(route_count) AS route_count_range, VARIANCE(route_count) AS route_count_variance, STDDEV(route_count) AS route_count_stddev FROM SUBNETS AS s JOIN ( SELECT sr.SUBNET_ID, COUNT(*) AS route_count FROM SUBNETROUTES AS sr GROUP BY sr.SUBNET_ID, sr.NEXTHOP ) AS route_stats ON s.ID = route_stats.SUBNET_ID WHERE s.IP_VERSION = 4 GROUP BY s.NAME ORDER BY route_count_range DESC;

WITH subnet_route_stats AS ( SELECT s.NAME AS subnet_name, MAX(route_count) - MIN(route_count) AS route_count_range, VARIANCE(route_count) AS route_count_variance, STDDEV(route_count) AS route_count_stddev FROM SUBNETS AS s JOIN ( SELECT sr.SUBNET_ID, COUNT(*) AS route_count FROM SUBNETROUTES AS sr GROUP BY sr.SUBNET_ID, sr.NEXTHOP ) AS route_stats ON s.ID = route_stats.SUBNET_ID WHERE s.IP_VERSION = 4 GROUP BY s.NAME ORDER BY route_count_range DESC ), subnet_attr_window_rank AS ( SELECT s.NAME, dense_rank() OVER ( ORDER BY sa.UPDATED_AT ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW ) AS window_column FROM SUBNETS AS s JOIN STANDARDATTRIBUTES AS sa ON sa.ID = s.STANDARD_ATTR_ID WHERE s.IP_VERSION = 4 ) SELECT srs.subnet_name, srs.route_count_range, srs.route_count_variance, srs.route_count_stddev, sawr.window_column FROM subnet_route_stats AS srs JOIN subnet_attr_window_rank AS sawr ON sawr.NAME = srs.subnet_name;

question: For each tenant that has at least 2 ports in DOWN status, return the tenant ID, the number of distinct DOWN ports, the average row-number window value computed by ordering allocated IP addresses (with a frame of 2 preceding rows and 1 following row), and the average dense-rank window value computed by ordering port-security settings (with a frame of the current row and 2 preceding rows). Also include the overall average DOWN-port count across all qualifying tenants as a benchmark, and categorize each tenant as 'HIGH_DOWN' (at least 50% above the benchmark), 'LOW_DOWN' (at least 50% below the benchmark), or 'AVERAGE_DOWN'. Do not return any rounded answers.
sql: WITH inner_cte AS (WITH PortSecurityWindow AS (SELECT p.id AS port_id, dense_rank() OVER ( ORDER BY psb.port_security_enabled ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW ) AS window_column FROM ports AS p JOIN portsecuritybindings AS psb ON p.id = psb.port_id WHERE p.status = 'DOWN'), PortIpBindingWindow AS (SELECT p.ID AS port_id, p.TENANT_ID AS tenant_id, b.HOST AS host, b.VIF_TYPE AS vif_type, ia.IP_ADDRESS AS ip_address, ROW_NUMBER() OVER ( ORDER BY ia.IP_ADDRESS ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND 1 FOLLOWING ) AS window_column FROM ML2_PORT_BINDINGS b JOIN PORTS p ON b.PORT_ID = p.ID JOIN IPALLOCATIONS ia ON p.ID = ia.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN') SELECT pibw.tenant_id, COUNT(DISTINCT pibw.port_id) AS down_port_count, AVG(pibw.window_column) AS avg_ip_row_number_window, AVG(psw.window_column) AS avg_port_security_dense_rank_window FROM PortIpBindingWindow pibw JOIN PortSecurityWindow psw ON pibw.port_id = psw.port_id WHERE pibw.tenant_id IS NOT NULL GROUP BY pibw.tenant_id HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT pibw.port_id) >= 2 ORDER BY down_port_count DESC, pibw.tenant_id), Benchmark AS ( SELECT AVG(down_port_count) AS avg_down_ports FROM inner_cte ) SELECT i.tenant_id, i.down_port_count, i.avg_ip_row_number_window, i.avg_port_security_dense_rank_window, b.avg_down_ports AS benchmark, CASE WHEN i.down_port_count > b.avg_down_ports * 1.5 THEN 'HIGH_DOWN' WHEN i.down_port_count < b.avg_down_ports * 0.5 THEN 'LOW_DOWN' ELSE 'AVERAGE_DOWN' END AS down_category FROM inner_cte i CROSS JOIN Benchmark b;
sub_questions: For ports whose status is DOWN, list each port ID and the dense rank of that port when ordering by its port-security setting (PORT_SECURITY_ENABLED), using a window frame that includes the current row and the 2 preceding rows.

For ports whose status is DOWN, list the port ID, tenant ID, host, VIF type, and allocated IP address, and assign row numbers ordered by IP address using a window frame of 2 preceding rows and 1 following row.

For each tenant that has at least 2 ports in DOWN status, return the tenant ID, the number of distinct DOWN ports, the average row-number window value computed by ordering allocated IP addresses (with a frame of 2 preceding rows and 1 following row), and the average dense-rank window value computed by ordering port-security settings (with a frame of the current row and 2 preceding rows).
sub_sqls: SELECT p.id AS port_id, dense_rank() OVER ( ORDER BY psb.port_security_enabled ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW ) AS window_column FROM ports AS p JOIN portsecuritybindings AS psb ON p.id = psb.port_id WHERE p.status = 'DOWN';

SELECT p.ID AS port_id, p.TENANT_ID AS tenant_id, b.HOST AS host, b.VIF_TYPE AS vif_type, ia.IP_ADDRESS AS ip_address, ROW_NUMBER() OVER ( ORDER BY ia.IP_ADDRESS ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND 1 FOLLOWING ) AS window_column FROM ML2_PORT_BINDINGS b JOIN PORTS p ON b.PORT_ID = p.ID JOIN IPALLOCATIONS ia ON p.ID = ia.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN';

WITH PortSecurityWindow AS (SELECT p.id AS port_id, dense_rank() OVER ( ORDER BY psb.port_security_enabled ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW ) AS window_column FROM ports AS p JOIN portsecuritybindings AS psb ON p.id = psb.port_id WHERE p.status = 'DOWN'), PortIpBindingWindow AS (SELECT p.ID AS port_id, p.TENANT_ID AS tenant_id, b.HOST AS host, b.VIF_TYPE AS vif_type, ia.IP_ADDRESS AS ip_address, ROW_NUMBER() OVER ( ORDER BY ia.IP_ADDRESS ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND 1 FOLLOWING ) AS window_column FROM ML2_PORT_BINDINGS b JOIN PORTS p ON b.PORT_ID = p.ID JOIN IPALLOCATIONS ia ON p.ID = ia.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN') SELECT pibw.tenant_id, COUNT(DISTINCT pibw.port_id) AS down_port_count, AVG(pibw.window_column) AS avg_ip_row_number_window, AVG(psw.window_column) AS avg_port_security_dense_rank_window FROM PortIpBindingWindow pibw JOIN PortSecurityWindow psw ON pibw.port_id = psw.port_id WHERE pibw.tenant_id IS NOT NULL GROUP BY pibw.tenant_id HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT pibw.port_id) >= 2 ORDER BY down_port_count DESC, pibw.tenant_id;

question: For ports with status DOWN, use the existing combined result (device-owner aggregates cross-joined to DOWN port details) as an inner result, then summarize it by port status and device owner to show the total number of rows produced and the minimum standard attribute ID. Include subtotals per port status and a grand total. Do not return any rounded answers.
sql: WITH inner_cte AS ( WITH PortStatusOwnerAgg AS (SELECT p.STATUS AS port_status, p.DEVICE_OWNER AS device_owner, COUNT(DISTINCT p.ID) AS port_count, MIN(p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID) AS min_standard_attr_id FROM PORTS p JOIN SECURITYGROUPPORTBINDINGS spb ON p.ID = spb.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' GROUP BY p.STATUS, p.DEVICE_OWNER), DownPortDetails AS (SELECT p.ID AS port_id, p.NAME AS port_name, p.MAC_ADDRESS AS mac_address, b.HOST AS binding_host, b.VIF_TYPE AS vif_type, RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY p.STATUS ORDER BY p.ID) AS window_column FROM PORTS p JOIN ML2_PORT_BINDINGS b ON p.ID = b.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN') SELECT psa.port_status, psa.device_owner, psa.port_count, psa.min_standard_attr_id, dpd.port_id, dpd.port_name, dpd.mac_address, dpd.binding_host, dpd.vif_type, dpd.window_column FROM PortStatusOwnerAgg psa CROSS JOIN DownPortDetails dpd ) SELECT CASE WHEN GROUPING(port_status) = 1 THEN 'GRAND TOTAL' ELSE port_status END AS port_status, CASE WHEN GROUPING(device_owner) = 1 AND GROUPING(port_status) = 0 THEN 'SUBTOTAL' WHEN GROUPING(device_owner) = 1 AND GROUPING(port_status) = 1 THEN 'SUBTOTAL' ELSE device_owner END AS device_owner, COUNT(*) AS total_rows_in_inner_result, MIN(min_standard_attr_id) AS min_standard_attr_id FROM inner_cte GROUP BY port_status, device_owner WITH ROLLUP;
sub_questions: For each port status and device owner, considering only ports that are bound to a security group, return the number of distinct ports and the minimum standard attribute ID.
For ports whose status is DOWN, show the port ID, port name, MAC address, the binding host, VIF type, and the rank of each port within its status group ordered by port ID.

question: For IPv4 subnets, show each subnet route (destination and next hop) with the subnet name and CIDR and the allocation pool’s first and last IP, plus the subnet’s average and variance of DNS nameserver order values; also include the overall average DNS order variance across all IPv4 subnets as a benchmark and classify each subnet as 'HIGH_VARIANCE' (at least 50% above benchmark), 'LOW_VARIANCE' (at least 50% below benchmark), or 'AVERAGE_VARIANCE'. Order results by DNS order variance (highest first). Do not return any rounded answers.
sql: WITH inner_cte AS (WITH DnsOrderStats AS (SELECT s.NAME AS subnet_name, AVG(d.ORDER) AS avg_dns_order, VARIANCE(d.ORDER) AS dns_order_variance FROM SUBNETS AS s JOIN DNSNAMESERVERS AS d ON s.ID = d.SUBNET_ID WHERE s.IP_VERSION = 4 GROUP BY s.NAME ORDER BY dns_order_variance DESC), RoutePoolDetails AS (SELECT r.DESTINATION, r.NEXTHOP, s.NAME AS subnet_name, s.CIDR AS subnet_cidr, p.FIRST_IP, p.LAST_IP, DENSE_RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY r.SUBNET_ID ORDER BY r.SUBNET_ID) AS window_column FROM SUBNETROUTES r JOIN SUBNETS s ON r.SUBNET_ID = s.ID JOIN IPALLOCATIONPOOLS p ON s.ID = p.SUBNET_ID WHERE s.IP_VERSION = 4) SELECT rpd.subnet_name, rpd.subnet_cidr, rpd.DESTINATION, rpd.NEXTHOP, rpd.FIRST_IP, rpd.LAST_IP, rpd.window_column, dos.avg_dns_order, dos.dns_order_variance FROM RoutePoolDetails rpd JOIN DnsOrderStats dos ON rpd.subnet_name = dos.subnet_name ORDER BY dos.dns_order_variance DESC, rpd.subnet_name, rpd.window_column), VarianceBenchmark AS (SELECT AVG(dns_order_variance) AS avg_dns_order_variance FROM inner_cte) SELECT i.subnet_name, i.subnet_cidr, i.DESTINATION, i.NEXTHOP, i.FIRST_IP, i.LAST_IP, i.window_column, i.avg_dns_order, i.dns_order_variance, vb.avg_dns_order_variance AS benchmark_dns_order_variance, CASE WHEN i.dns_order_variance > vb.avg_dns_order_variance * 1.5 THEN 'HIGH_VARIANCE' WHEN i.dns_order_variance < vb.avg_dns_order_variance * 0.5 THEN 'LOW_VARIANCE' ELSE 'AVERAGE_VARIANCE' END AS variance_category FROM inner_cte i CROSS JOIN VarianceBenchmark vb ORDER BY i.dns_order_variance DESC, i.subnet_name, i.window_column;

question: For ports whose status is DOWN, show the down port name, MAC address, admin_state_up flag, binding host, VIF type, and the average admin_state_up over a window of 2 preceding and 2 following rows (partitioned by VIF type and ordered by MAC address), along with the matching administratively up port’s name, MAC address, port security enabled flag, and its row number over a window of 2 preceding rows and 1 following row (ordered by MAC address), matching the two sets by MAC address; additionally, for each matched pair, include the deviation of the down port’s windowed average admin_state_up from the overall average of that windowed average across all down ports. Do not return any rounded answers.
sql: WITH inner_cte AS (WITH DownPortsWithBindings AS ( SELECT p.NAME, p.MAC_ADDRESS, p.ADMIN_STATE_UP, b.HOST, b.VIF_TYPE, AVG(p.ADMIN_STATE_UP) OVER ( PARTITION BY b.VIF_TYPE ORDER BY p.MAC_ADDRESS ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND 2 FOLLOWING ) AS window_column FROM PORTS AS p JOIN ML2_PORT_BINDINGS AS b ON p.ID = b.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' ORDER BY p.MAC_ADDRESS ), AdminUpPortsWithSecurity AS ( SELECT p.NAME AS port_name, p.MAC_ADDRESS AS mac_address, psb.PORT_SECURITY_ENABLED AS port_security_enabled, ROW_NUMBER() OVER ( ORDER BY p.MAC_ADDRESS ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND 1 FOLLOWING ) AS window_column FROM PORTS AS p JOIN PORTSECURITYBINDINGS AS psb ON p.ID = psb.PORT_ID WHERE p.ADMIN_STATE_UP = 1 ) SELECT dp.NAME AS down_port_name, dp.MAC_ADDRESS AS down_mac_address, dp.ADMIN_STATE_UP AS down_admin_state_up, dp.HOST AS binding_host, dp.VIF_TYPE AS vif_type, dp.window_column AS avg_admin_state_up_window_2p_2f, au.port_name AS admin_up_port_name, au.mac_address AS admin_up_mac_address, au.port_security_enabled, au.window_column AS row_number_window_2p_1f FROM DownPortsWithBindings dp JOIN AdminUpPortsWithSecurity au ON dp.MAC_ADDRESS = au.mac_address ORDER BY dp.MAC_ADDRESS), overall_avg AS (SELECT AVG(avg_admin_state_up_window_2p_2f) AS overall_avg_admin_state_up_window FROM inner_cte) SELECT i.down_port_name, i.down_mac_address, i.down_admin_state_up, i.binding_host, i.vif_type, i.avg_admin_state_up_window_2p_2f, i.admin_up_port_name, i.admin_up_mac_address, i.port_security_enabled, i.row_number_window_2p_1f, (i.avg_admin_state_up_window_2p_2f - oa.overall_avg_admin_state_up_window) AS deviation_from_overall_avg_windowed_admin_state_up FROM inner_cte i CROSS JOIN overall_avg oa ORDER BY i.down_mac_address;

question: For the tenants that have at least 2 ports in DOWN status, group the results by tenant and VIF type, and return the tenant ID, VIF type, the number of distinct DOWN ports, the average row-number window value computed by ordering allocated IP addresses (with a frame of 2 preceding rows and 1 following row), and the average dense-rank window value computed by ordering port-security settings (with a frame of the current row and 2 preceding rows). Include subtotals per tenant and a grand total. Do not return any rounded answers.
sql: WITH inner_cte AS (WITH PortSecurityWindow AS (SELECT p.id AS port_id, dense_rank() OVER ( ORDER BY psb.port_security_enabled ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW ) AS window_column FROM ports AS p JOIN portsecuritybindings AS psb ON p.id = psb.port_id WHERE p.status = 'DOWN'), PortIpBindingWindow AS (SELECT p.ID AS port_id, p.TENANT_ID AS tenant_id, b.HOST AS host, b.VIF_TYPE AS vif_type, ia.IP_ADDRESS AS ip_address, ROW_NUMBER() OVER ( ORDER BY ia.IP_ADDRESS ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND 1 FOLLOWING ) AS window_column FROM ML2_PORT_BINDINGS b JOIN PORTS p ON b.PORT_ID = p.ID JOIN IPALLOCATIONS ia ON p.ID = ia.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN') SELECT pibw.tenant_id, COUNT(DISTINCT pibw.port_id) AS down_port_count, AVG(pibw.window_column) AS avg_ip_row_number_window, AVG(psw.window_column) AS avg_port_security_dense_rank_window FROM PortIpBindingWindow pibw JOIN PortSecurityWindow psw ON pibw.port_id = psw.port_id WHERE pibw.tenant_id IS NOT NULL GROUP BY pibw.tenant_id HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT pibw.port_id) >= 2 ORDER BY down_port_count DESC, pibw.tenant_id) SELECT CASE WHEN GROUPING(p.tenant_id) = 1 THEN 'GRAND TOTAL' ELSE p.tenant_id END AS tenant_id, CASE WHEN GROUPING(b.vif_type) = 1 AND GROUPING(p.tenant_id) = 0 THEN 'SUBTOTAL' ELSE b.vif_type END AS vif_type, SUM(inner_cte.down_port_count) AS down_port_count, AVG(inner_cte.avg_ip_row_number_window) AS avg_ip_row_number_window, AVG(inner_cte.avg_port_security_dense_rank_window) AS avg_port_security_dense_rank_window FROM inner_cte JOIN ports p ON p.tenant_id = inner_cte.tenant_id JOIN ml2_port_bindings b ON b.port_id = p.id GROUP BY p.tenant_id, b.vif_type WITH ROLLUP;

question: For ACTIVE networks, return only those networks whose number of administratively-up ports on the same tenant/network is greater than the average administratively-up port count for ACTIVE networks within the same tenant. For each qualifying network, list the network’s ID, name, tenant ID, admin_state_up flag, MTU, and standard-attribute updated_at timestamp (with a row number per tenant ordered by network name), along with details of its administratively-up ports (port ID, host, VIF type, VNIC type, MAC address, port status, device owner, and the average standard attribute ID computed over a 2-preceding/2-following window partitioned by VIF type and ordered by standard attribute ID). Do not return any rounded answers.
sql: WITH inner_cte AS ( WITH AdminUpPorts AS ( SELECT b.PORT_ID, b.HOST, b.VIF_TYPE, b.VNIC_TYPE, p.TENANT_ID, p.NETWORK_ID, p.MAC_ADDRESS, p.STATUS, p.DEVICE_OWNER, AVG(p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID) OVER ( PARTITION BY b.VIF_TYPE ORDER BY p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND 2 FOLLOWING ) AS window_column FROM ML2_PORT_BINDINGS AS b JOIN PORTS AS p ON b.PORT_ID = p.ID JOIN PORTSECURITYBINDINGS AS psb ON p.ID = psb.PORT_ID WHERE p.ADMIN_STATE_UP = 1 ), ActiveNetworks AS ( SELECT n.ID AS network_id, n.NAME AS network_name, n.TENANT_ID AS tenant_id, n.ADMIN_STATE_UP AS admin_state_up, n.MTU AS mtu, sa.UPDATED_AT AS standard_attr_updated_at, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY n.TENANT_ID ORDER BY n.NAME) AS window_column FROM NETWORKS n JOIN STANDARDATTRIBUTES sa ON sa.ID = n.STANDARD_ATTR_ID WHERE n.STATUS = 'ACTIVE' ) SELECT an.network_id, an.network_name, an.tenant_id, an.admin_state_up, an.mtu, an.standard_attr_updated_at, an.window_column AS network_row_number_within_tenant, ap.PORT_ID, ap.HOST, ap.VIF_TYPE, ap.VNIC_TYPE, ap.MAC_ADDRESS, ap.STATUS AS port_status, ap.DEVICE_OWNER, ap.window_column AS avg_standard_attr_id_window_2_preceding_2_following FROM ActiveNetworks an JOIN AdminUpPorts ap ON ap.NETWORK_ID = an.network_id AND ap.TENANT_ID = an.tenant_id ), TenantActiveAdminUpPortCounts AS ( SELECT n.tenant_id, n.id AS network_id, COUNT(p.id) AS admin_up_port_count FROM NETWORKS n JOIN PORTS p ON p.network_id = n.id AND p.tenant_id = n.tenant_id WHERE n.status = 'ACTIVE' AND p.admin_state_up = 1 GROUP BY n.tenant_id, n.id ), TenantActiveAdminUpAverages AS ( SELECT tenant_id, AVG(admin_up_port_count) AS avg_admin_up_ports_per_active_network FROM TenantActiveAdminUpPortCounts GROUP BY tenant_id ) SELECT i.network_id, i.network_name, i.tenant_id, i.admin_state_up, i.mtu, i.standard_attr_updated_at, i.network_row_number_within_tenant, i.port_id, i.host, i.vif_type, i.vnic_type, i.mac_address, i.port_status, i.device_owner, i.avg_standard_attr_id_window_2_preceding_2_following FROM inner_cte i JOIN TenantActiveAdminUpPortCounts c ON c.tenant_id = i.tenant_id AND c.network_id = i.network_id JOIN TenantActiveAdminUpAverages a ON a.tenant_id = i.tenant_id WHERE c.admin_up_port_count > a.avg_admin_up_ports_per_active_network;

WITH AdminUpPorts AS ( SELECT b.PORT_ID, b.HOST, b.VIF_TYPE, b.VNIC_TYPE, p.TENANT_ID, p.NETWORK_ID, p.MAC_ADDRESS, p.STATUS, p.DEVICE_OWNER, AVG(p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID) OVER ( PARTITION BY b.VIF_TYPE ORDER BY p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND 2 FOLLOWING ) AS window_column FROM ML2_PORT_BINDINGS AS b JOIN PORTS AS p ON b.PORT_ID = p.ID JOIN PORTSECURITYBINDINGS AS psb ON p.ID = psb.PORT_ID WHERE p.ADMIN_STATE_UP = 1 ), ActiveNetworks AS ( SELECT n.ID AS network_id, n.NAME AS network_name, n.TENANT_ID AS tenant_id, n.ADMIN_STATE_UP AS admin_state_up, n.MTU AS mtu, sa.UPDATED_AT AS standard_attr_updated_at, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY n.TENANT_ID ORDER BY n.NAME) AS window_column FROM NETWORKS n JOIN STANDARDATTRIBUTES sa ON sa.ID = n.STANDARD_ATTR_ID WHERE n.STATUS = 'ACTIVE' ) SELECT an.network_id, an.network_name, an.tenant_id, an.admin_state_up, an.mtu, an.standard_attr_updated_at, an.window_column AS network_row_number_within_tenant, ap.PORT_ID, ap.HOST, ap.VIF_TYPE, ap.VNIC_TYPE, ap.MAC_ADDRESS, ap.STATUS AS port_status, ap.DEVICE_OWNER, ap.window_column AS avg_standard_attr_id_window_2_preceding_2_following FROM ActiveNetworks an JOIN AdminUpPorts ap ON ap.NETWORK_ID = an.network_id AND ap.TENANT_ID = an.tenant_id;

question: Across tenants, compute how many administratively up ports meet the criteria of being bound to at least one security group, having at least one port security binding, and having more than 75% of their port security bindings enabled. Return each tenant’s ID, the number of such qualifying ports, the average qualifying-port count across all tenants as a benchmark, and label each tenant as 'HIGH_USER' (at least 50% above average), 'LOW_USER' (at least 50% below average), or 'AVERAGE_USER'. Do not return any rounded answers.
sql: WITH inner_cte AS ( WITH PortSecurityGroupDNS AS ( SELECT p.id AS port_id, p.tenant_id, p.name AS port_name, COUNT(sgpb.security_group_id) AS security_group_binding_count, SUM(CASE WHEN pd.port_id IS NULL THEN 0 ELSE 1 END) AS dns_record_count FROM SECURITYGROUPPORTBINDINGS sgpb JOIN PORTS p ON sgpb.port_id = p.id LEFT JOIN PORTDNSES pd ON p.id = pd.port_id WHERE p.admin_state_up = 1 GROUP BY p.id, p.tenant_id, p.name ), PortSecurityBindings AS ( SELECT p.id AS port_id, p.tenant_id, p.mac_address, COUNT(psb.port_id) AS binding_count, SUM(CASE WHEN psb.port_security_enabled THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS port_security_enabled_total FROM ports p JOIN portsecuritybindings psb ON p.id = psb.port_id WHERE p.admin_state_up = 1 GROUP BY p.id, p.tenant_id, p.mac_address ) SELECT psgd.port_id, psgd.tenant_id, psgd.port_name, psb.mac_address, psgd.security_group_binding_count, psb.binding_count, psb.port_security_enabled_total, psgd.dns_record_count FROM PortSecurityGroupDNS psgd JOIN PortSecurityBindings psb ON psgd.port_id = psb.port_id WHERE (psb.port_security_enabled_total * 1.0 / psb.binding_count) > 0.75 ), TenantQualifyingPorts AS ( SELECT tenant_id, COUNT(port_id) AS qualifying_ports FROM inner_cte GROUP BY tenant_id ), AverageQualifyingPorts AS ( SELECT AVG(qualifying_ports) AS avg_qualifying_ports FROM TenantQualifyingPorts ) SELECT tqp.tenant_id, tqp.qualifying_ports, aqp.avg_qualifying_ports AS benchmark, CASE WHEN tqp.qualifying_ports > aqp.avg_qualifying_ports * 1.5 THEN 'HIGH_USER' WHEN tqp.qualifying_ports < aqp.avg_qualifying_ports * 0.5 THEN 'LOW_USER' ELSE 'AVERAGE_USER' END AS user_category FROM TenantQualifyingPorts tqp CROSS JOIN AverageQualifyingPorts aqp;

question: For ports bound to the security group ID 0008e629-5619-41e0-b86c-4eecfeaacb6c, list each port’s ID, status, allocated IP address, and the running sum of its standard attribute ID within its network (ordered by standard attribute ID), along with (for that same port status) the range, variance, and standard deviation (using STDDEV only and never STDDEV_POP) of the number of port security bindings per port, and the total number of ports in that security group having that status; additionally, include the average number of ports per status within that security group as a benchmark and categorize each port’s status as HIGH_STATUS (at least 50% above the benchmark), LOW_STATUS (at least 50% below the benchmark), or AVERAGE_STATUS. Do not return any rounded answers.
sql: WITH inner_cte AS ( WITH PortDetailsForSecurityGroup AS ( SELECT p.ID AS port_id, p.STATUS AS port_status, ia.IP_ADDRESS AS ip_address, SUM(p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID) OVER ( PARTITION BY p.NETWORK_ID ORDER BY p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID ) AS window_column FROM SECURITYGROUPPORTBINDINGS sgpb JOIN PORTS p ON sgpb.PORT_ID = p.ID JOIN IPALLOCATIONS ia ON p.ID = ia.PORT_ID WHERE sgpb.SECURITY_GROUP_ID = '0008e629-5619-41e0-b86c-4eecfeaacb6c' ), PortSecurityBindingStatsByStatus AS ( SELECT p.status, MAX(ps.binding_count) - MIN(ps.binding_count) AS binding_count_range, VARIANCE(ps.binding_count) AS binding_count_variance, STDDEV(ps.binding_count) AS binding_count_stddev FROM ports AS p JOIN ( SELECT p2.id AS port_id, COUNT(*) AS binding_count FROM ports AS p2 JOIN portsecuritybindings AS b ON p2.id = b.port_id GROUP BY p2.id ) AS ps ON p.id = ps.port_id GROUP BY p.status ORDER BY binding_count_range DESC ), SecurityGroupPortStatusCounts AS ( SELECT p.STATUS AS port_status, COUNT(DISTINCT p.ID) AS ports_in_security_group FROM SECURITYGROUPPORTBINDINGS sgpb JOIN PORTS p ON sgpb.PORT_ID = p.ID WHERE sgpb.SECURITY_GROUP_ID = '0008e629-5619-41e0-b86c-4eecfeaacb6c' GROUP BY p.STATUS ) SELECT pd.port_id, pd.port_status, pd.ip_address, pd.window_column, pss.binding_count_range, pss.binding_count_variance, pss.binding_count_stddev, sgc.ports_in_security_group FROM PortDetailsForSecurityGroup pd JOIN PortSecurityBindingStatsByStatus pss ON pd.port_status = pss.status JOIN SecurityGroupPortStatusCounts sgc ON pd.port_status = sgc.port_status ORDER BY pd.port_status, pd.window_column, pd.port_id ), StatusBenchmark AS ( SELECT AVG(ports_in_security_group) AS avg_ports_per_status FROM ( SELECT port_status, MAX(ports_in_security_group) AS ports_in_security_group FROM inner_cte GROUP BY port_status ) s ) SELECT i.port_id, i.port_status, i.ip_address, i.window_column, i.binding_count_range, i.binding_count_variance, i.binding_count_stddev, i.ports_in_security_group, sb.avg_ports_per_status AS benchmark, CASE WHEN i.ports_in_security_group > sb.avg_ports_per_status * 1.5 THEN 'HIGH_STATUS' WHEN i.ports_in_security_group < sb.avg_ports_per_status * 0.5 THEN 'LOW_STATUS' ELSE 'AVERAGE_STATUS' END AS status_category FROM inner_cte i CROSS JOIN StatusBenchmark sb ORDER BY i.port_status, i.window_column, i.port_id;

question: Among the top 10 tenants with the most ACTIVE networks, show each tenant’s ID, total number of ACTIVE networks, and whether the tenant has any IPv4 subnets whose route-count range is greater than 0 (based on per-subnet next-hop route counts). Do not return any rounded answers.
sql: WITH inner_cte AS (WITH SubnetRouteStats AS ( SELECT s.NAME AS subnet_name, MAX(route_count) - MIN(route_count) AS route_count_range, VARIANCE(route_count) AS route_count_variance, STDDEV(route_count) AS route_count_stddev FROM SUBNETS AS s JOIN ( SELECT sr.SUBNET_ID, COUNT(*) AS route_count FROM SUBNETROUTES AS sr GROUP BY sr.SUBNET_ID, sr.NEXTHOP ) AS route_stats ON s.ID = route_stats.SUBNET_ID WHERE s.IP_VERSION = 4 GROUP BY s.NAME ORDER BY route_count_range DESC ), ActiveNetworks AS ( SELECT n.ID AS network_id, n.NAME AS network_name, n.TENANT_ID AS tenant_id, n.ADMIN_STATE_UP AS admin_state_up, n.MTU AS mtu, sa.UPDATED_AT AS standard_attr_updated_at, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY n.TENANT_ID ORDER BY n.NAME) AS window_column FROM NETWORKS n JOIN STANDARDATTRIBUTES sa ON sa.ID = n.STANDARD_ATTR_ID WHERE n.STATUS = 'ACTIVE' ) SELECT an.tenant_id, an.network_id, an.network_name, an.admin_state_up, an.mtu, an.standard_attr_updated_at, an.window_column, srs.subnet_name, srs.route_count_range, srs.route_count_variance, srs.route_count_stddev FROM ActiveNetworks an JOIN SUBNETS s ON s.NETWORK_ID = an.network_id AND s.IP_VERSION = 4 JOIN SubnetRouteStats srs ON srs.subnet_name = s.NAME) SELECT i.tenant_id, COUNT(DISTINCT i.network_id) AS total_active_networks, CASE WHEN COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN i.route_count_range > 0 THEN i.subnet_name END) > 0 THEN 'Yes' ELSE 'No' END AS has_ipv4_subnet_with_nonzero_route_range FROM inner_cte i GROUP BY i.tenant_id ORDER BY total_active_networks DESC LIMIT 10;

question: For each tenant that has ports on host "drive-59", show the tenant ID, the number of distinct ports on that host, the number of those ports that are administratively up and have port security enabled (matched by MAC address), the secured-port ratio (secured ports divided by total drive-59 ports) rounded to 2 decimals, and also include the overall average secured-port ratio across all such tenants.
sql: WITH inner_cte AS ( WITH HostDrive59Ports AS ( SELECT b.PORT_ID, p.TENANT_ID, p.MAC_ADDRESS, SUM(p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID) OVER ( PARTITION BY b.VIF_TYPE ORDER BY p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID ) AS window_column FROM ML2_PORT_BINDINGS AS b JOIN PORTS AS p ON b.PORT_ID = p.ID JOIN PORTSECURITYBINDINGS AS psb ON p.ID = psb.PORT_ID WHERE b.HOST = 'drive-59' ), AdminUpPorts AS ( SELECT p.NAME AS port_name, p.MAC_ADDRESS AS mac_address, psb.PORT_SECURITY_ENABLED AS port_security_enabled, ROW_NUMBER() OVER ( ORDER BY p.MAC_ADDRESS ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND 1 FOLLOWING ) AS window_column FROM PORTS AS p JOIN PORTSECURITYBINDINGS AS psb ON p.ID = psb.PORT_ID WHERE p.ADMIN_STATE_UP = 1 ), Drive59AdminUpSummary AS ( SELECT h.TENANT_ID, COUNT(DISTINCT h.PORT_ID) AS drive59_port_count, COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN a.port_security_enabled = 1 THEN h.PORT_ID END) AS drive59_secured_port_count, ROUND( COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN a.port_security_enabled = 1 THEN h.PORT_ID END) * 1.0 / NULLIF(COUNT(DISTINCT h.PORT_ID), 0), 2 ) AS secured_port_ratio FROM HostDrive59Ports h JOIN AdminUpPorts a ON a.mac_address = h.MAC_ADDRESS GROUP BY h.TENANT_ID ) SELECT s.TENANT_ID, s.drive59_port_count, s.drive59_secured_port_count, s.secured_port_ratio FROM Drive59AdminUpSummary s ORDER BY s.secured_port_ratio DESC, s.drive59_port_count DESC ) SELECT inner_cte.TENANT_ID, inner_cte.drive59_port_count, inner_cte.drive59_secured_port_count, inner_cte.secured_port_ratio, avg_stats.avg_secured_port_ratio FROM inner_cte JOIN ( SELECT AVG(secured_port_ratio) AS avg_secured_port_ratio FROM inner_cte ) AS avg_stats ON 1 = 1 ORDER BY inner_cte.secured_port_ratio DESC, inner_cte.drive59_port_count DESC;

question: For active networks with admin_state_up = 1 that have at least one DOWN port, return the tenant ID, network ID, network name, admin_state_up flag, MTU, the network’s standard attribute updated_at timestamp, and the count of DOWN ports—only for those networks whose DOWN-port count is greater than the average DOWN-port count among all active admin_state_up = 1 networks. Do not return any rounded answers.
sql: WITH inner_cte AS ( WITH DownPorts AS ( SELECT p.ID AS port_id, p.TENANT_ID AS tenant_id, p.NAME AS port_name, p.NETWORK_ID AS network_id, p.MAC_ADDRESS AS mac_address, p.DEVICE_OWNER AS device_owner, ia.IP_ADDRESS AS ip_address, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY p.NETWORK_ID ORDER BY p.ID) AS window_column FROM PORTS p JOIN IPALLOCATIONS ia ON p.ID = ia.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' ), ActiveNetworks AS ( SELECT n.ID AS network_id, n.NAME AS network_name, n.TENANT_ID AS tenant_id, n.ADMIN_STATE_UP AS admin_state_up, n.MTU AS mtu, sa.UPDATED_AT AS standard_attr_updated_at, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY n.TENANT_ID ORDER BY n.NAME) AS window_column FROM NETWORKS n JOIN STANDARDATTRIBUTES sa ON sa.ID = n.STANDARD_ATTR_ID WHERE n.STATUS = 'ACTIVE' ) SELECT an.tenant_id, an.network_id, an.network_name, an.admin_state_up, an.mtu, an.standard_attr_updated_at, COUNT(DISTINCT dp.port_id) AS down_port_count FROM ActiveNetworks an LEFT JOIN DownPorts dp ON dp.network_id = an.network_id AND dp.tenant_id = an.tenant_id WHERE an.admin_state_up = 1 GROUP BY an.tenant_id, an.network_id, an.network_name, an.admin_state_up, an.mtu, an.standard_attr_updated_at HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT dp.port_id) > 0 ORDER BY down_port_count DESC, an.network_name ) , DownPortAverages AS ( SELECT AVG(down_port_count) AS avg_down_ports FROM inner_cte ) SELECT i.tenant_id, i.network_id, i.network_name, i.admin_state_up, i.mtu, i.standard_attr_updated_at, i.down_port_count FROM inner_cte i WHERE i.down_port_count > (SELECT avg_down_ports FROM DownPortAverages) ORDER BY i.down_port_count DESC, i.network_name;
sub_questions: For ports that are DOWN, list the port ID, tenant ID, port name, network ID, MAC address, device owner, and the allocated IP address, and assign row numbers within each network ordered by port ID.

For active networks, show the network ID, network name, tenant ID, admin_state_up flag, MTU, and the standard attribute updated_at timestamp, and assign row numbers within each tenant ordered by network name.

sub_sqls: SELECT p.ID AS port_id, p.TENANT_ID AS tenant_id, p.NAME AS port_name, p.NETWORK_ID AS network_id, p.MAC_ADDRESS AS mac_address, p.DEVICE_OWNER AS device_owner, ia.IP_ADDRESS AS ip_address, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY p.NETWORK_ID ORDER BY p.ID) AS window_column FROM PORTS p JOIN IPALLOCATIONS ia ON p.ID = ia.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN';

SELECT n.ID AS network_id, n.NAME AS network_name, n.TENANT_ID AS tenant_id, n.ADMIN_STATE_UP AS admin_state_up, n.MTU AS mtu, sa.UPDATED_AT AS standard_attr_updated_at, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY n.TENANT_ID ORDER BY n.NAME) AS window_column FROM NETWORKS n JOIN STANDARDATTRIBUTES sa ON sa.ID = n.STANDARD_ATTR_ID WHERE n.STATUS = 'ACTIVE';

WITH DownPorts AS ( SELECT p.ID AS port_id, p.TENANT_ID AS tenant_id, p.NAME AS port_name, p.NETWORK_ID AS network_id, p.MAC_ADDRESS AS mac_address, p.DEVICE_OWNER AS device_owner, ia.IP_ADDRESS AS ip_address, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY p.NETWORK_ID ORDER BY p.ID) AS window_column FROM PORTS p JOIN IPALLOCATIONS ia ON p.ID = ia.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' ), ActiveNetworks AS ( SELECT n.ID AS network_id, n.NAME AS network_name, n.TENANT_ID AS tenant_id, n.ADMIN_STATE_UP AS admin_state_up, n.MTU AS mtu, sa.UPDATED_AT AS standard_attr_updated_at, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY n.TENANT_ID ORDER BY n.NAME) AS window_column FROM NETWORKS n JOIN STANDARDATTRIBUTES sa ON sa.ID = n.STANDARD_ATTR_ID WHERE n.STATUS = 'ACTIVE' ) SELECT an.tenant_id, an.network_id, an.network_name, an.admin_state_up, an.mtu, an.standard_attr_updated_at, COUNT(DISTINCT dp.port_id) AS down_port_count FROM ActiveNetworks an LEFT JOIN DownPorts dp ON dp.network_id = an.network_id AND dp.tenant_id = an.tenant_id WHERE an.admin_state_up = 1 GROUP BY an.tenant_id, an.network_id, an.network_name, an.admin_state_up, an.mtu, an.standard_attr_updated_at HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT dp.port_id) > 0 ORDER BY down_port_count DESC, an.network_name;

question: For each tenant that has ports on host "drive-59", show the tenant ID, the number of distinct ports on that host, the number of those ports that are administratively up and have port security enabled (matched by MAC address), the secured-port ratio (secured ports divided by total drive-59 ports) rounded to 2 decimals, and the deviation of that tenant’s secured-port ratio from the average secured-port ratio across all such tenants.
sql: WITH inner_cte AS ( WITH HostDrive59Ports AS ( SELECT b.PORT_ID, p.TENANT_ID, p.MAC_ADDRESS, SUM(p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID) OVER ( PARTITION BY b.VIF_TYPE ORDER BY p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID ) AS window_column FROM ML2_PORT_BINDINGS AS b JOIN PORTS AS p ON b.PORT_ID = p.ID JOIN PORTSECURITYBINDINGS AS psb ON p.ID = psb.PORT_ID WHERE b.HOST = 'drive-59' ), AdminUpPorts AS ( SELECT p.NAME AS port_name, p.MAC_ADDRESS AS mac_address, psb.PORT_SECURITY_ENABLED AS port_security_enabled, ROW_NUMBER() OVER ( ORDER BY p.MAC_ADDRESS ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND 1 FOLLOWING ) AS window_column FROM PORTS AS p JOIN PORTSECURITYBINDINGS AS psb ON p.ID = psb.PORT_ID WHERE p.ADMIN_STATE_UP = 1 ), Drive59AdminUpSummary AS ( SELECT h.TENANT_ID, COUNT(DISTINCT h.PORT_ID) AS drive59_port_count, COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN a.port_security_enabled = 1 THEN h.PORT_ID END) AS drive59_secured_port_count, ROUND( COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN a.port_security_enabled = 1 THEN h.PORT_ID END) * 1.0 / NULLIF(COUNT(DISTINCT h.PORT_ID), 0), 2 ) AS secured_port_ratio FROM HostDrive59Ports h JOIN AdminUpPorts a ON a.mac_address = h.MAC_ADDRESS GROUP BY h.TENANT_ID ) SELECT s.TENANT_ID, s.drive59_port_count, s.drive59_secured_port_count, s.secured_port_ratio FROM Drive59AdminUpSummary s ORDER BY s.secured_port_ratio DESC, s.drive59_port_count DESC ), avg_cte AS ( SELECT AVG(secured_port_ratio) AS avg_secured_port_ratio FROM inner_cte ) SELECT i.TENANT_ID, i.drive59_port_count, i.drive59_secured_port_count, i.secured_port_ratio, (i.secured_port_ratio - a.avg_secured_port_ratio) AS deviation_from_avg_secured_port_ratio FROM inner_cte i CROSS JOIN avg_cte a ORDER BY deviation_from_avg_secured_port_ratio DESC, i.secured_port_ratio DESC, i.drive59_port_count DESC;

For ports that are administratively up, list the port name, MAC address, and port security status, and assign row numbers ordered by MAC address using a window frame of 2 preceding rows and 1 following row.

sub_sqls: SELECT b.PORT_ID, p.TENANT_ID, p.MAC_ADDRESS, SUM(p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID) OVER ( PARTITION BY b.VIF_TYPE ORDER BY p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID ) AS window_column FROM ML2_PORT_BINDINGS AS b JOIN PORTS AS p ON b.PORT_ID = p.ID JOIN PORTSECURITYBINDINGS AS psb ON p.ID = psb.PORT_ID WHERE b.HOST = 'drive-59';

WITH HostDrive59Ports AS ( SELECT b.PORT_ID, p.TENANT_ID, p.MAC_ADDRESS, SUM(p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID) OVER ( PARTITION BY b.VIF_TYPE ORDER BY p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID ) AS window_column FROM ML2_PORT_BINDINGS AS b JOIN PORTS AS p ON b.PORT_ID = p.ID JOIN PORTSECURITYBINDINGS AS psb ON p.ID = psb.PORT_ID WHERE b.HOST = 'drive-59' ), AdminUpPorts AS ( SELECT p.NAME AS port_name, p.MAC_ADDRESS AS mac_address, psb.PORT_SECURITY_ENABLED AS port_security_enabled, ROW_NUMBER() OVER ( ORDER BY p.MAC_ADDRESS ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND 1 FOLLOWING ) AS window_column FROM PORTS AS p JOIN PORTSECURITYBINDINGS AS psb ON p.ID = psb.PORT_ID WHERE p.ADMIN_STATE_UP = 1 ), Drive59AdminUpSummary AS ( SELECT h.TENANT_ID, COUNT(DISTINCT h.PORT_ID) AS drive59_port_count, COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN a.port_security_enabled = 1 THEN h.PORT_ID END) AS drive59_secured_port_count, ROUND( COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN a.port_security_enabled = 1 THEN h.PORT_ID END) * 1.0 / NULLIF(COUNT(DISTINCT h.PORT_ID), 0), 2 ) AS secured_port_ratio FROM HostDrive59Ports h JOIN AdminUpPorts a ON a.mac_address = h.MAC_ADDRESS GROUP BY h.TENANT_ID ) SELECT s.TENANT_ID, s.drive59_port_count, s.drive59_secured_port_count, s.secured_port_ratio FROM Drive59AdminUpSummary s ORDER BY s.secured_port_ratio DESC, s.drive59_port_count DESC;

question: For each IPv4 subnet stats row (either DNS nameserver ORDER stats or per-next-hop route-count stats), list the subnet name, network ID, the stats fields, the “reason” label, and the deviation of that row’s range value from the average range among rows with the same reason. Do not return any rounded answers.
sql: WITH inner_cte AS (WITH DnsOrderStats AS ( SELECT s.name AS subnet_name, MAX(d.ORDER) - MIN(d.ORDER) AS order_range, VARIANCE(d.ORDER) AS order_variance FROM SUBNETS AS s JOIN DNSNAMESERVERS AS d ON s.id = d.subnet_id WHERE s.ip_version = 4 GROUP BY s.name ORDER BY order_range DESC ), RouteCountStats AS ( SELECT s.NAME AS subnet_name, MAX(route_count) - MIN(route_count) AS route_count_range, VARIANCE(route_count) AS route_count_variance, STDDEV(route_count) AS route_count_stddev FROM SUBNETS AS s JOIN ( SELECT sr.SUBNET_ID, COUNT(*) AS route_count FROM SUBNETROUTES AS sr GROUP BY sr.SUBNET_ID, sr.NEXTHOP ) AS route_stats ON s.ID = route_stats.SUBNET_ID WHERE s.IP_VERSION = 4 GROUP BY s.NAME ORDER BY route_count_range DESC ), CombinedSubnetStats AS ( SELECT subnet_name, order_range, order_variance, NULL AS route_count_range, NULL AS route_count_variance, NULL AS route_count_stddev, 'DNS Nameserver Order Stats' AS reason FROM DnsOrderStats UNION ALL SELECT subnet_name, NULL AS order_range, NULL AS order_variance, route_count_range, route_count_variance, route_count_stddev, 'Route Count Stats' AS reason FROM RouteCountStats ) SELECT * FROM CombinedSubnetStats ORDER BY subnet_name, reason) , Enriched AS ( SELECT i.subnet_name, s.network_id, i.order_range, i.order_variance, i.route_count_range, i.route_count_variance, i.route_count_stddev, i.reason, CASE WHEN i.reason = 'DNS Nameserver Order Stats' THEN i.order_range ELSE i.route_count_range END AS range_value FROM inner_cte i JOIN subnets s ON s.name = i.subnet_name AND s.ip_version = 4 ), AvgByReason AS ( SELECT reason, AVG(range_value) AS avg_range_value FROM Enriched GROUP BY reason ) SELECT e.subnet_name, e.network_id, e.order_range, e.order_variance, e.route_count_range, e.route_count_variance, e.route_count_stddev, e.reason, (e.range_value - a.avg_range_value) AS deviation_from_avg_range_within_reason FROM Enriched e JOIN AvgByReason a ON e.reason = a.reason ORDER BY e.subnet_name, e.reason;

sub_sqls: SELECT s.name AS subnet_name, MAX(d.ORDER) - MIN(d.ORDER) AS order_range, VARIANCE(d.ORDER) AS order_variance FROM SUBNETS AS s JOIN DNSNAMESERVERS AS d ON s.id = d.subnet_id WHERE s.ip_version = 4 GROUP BY s.name ORDER BY order_range DESC;

WITH DnsOrderStats AS ( SELECT s.name AS subnet_name, MAX(d.ORDER) - MIN(d.ORDER) AS order_range, VARIANCE(d.ORDER) AS order_variance FROM SUBNETS AS s JOIN DNSNAMESERVERS AS d ON s.id = d.subnet_id WHERE s.ip_version = 4 GROUP BY s.name ORDER BY order_range DESC ), RouteCountStats AS ( SELECT s.NAME AS subnet_name, MAX(route_count) - MIN(route_count) AS route_count_range, VARIANCE(route_count) AS route_count_variance, STDDEV(route_count) AS route_count_stddev FROM SUBNETS AS s JOIN ( SELECT sr.SUBNET_ID, COUNT(*) AS route_count FROM SUBNETROUTES AS sr GROUP BY sr.SUBNET_ID, sr.NEXTHOP ) AS route_stats ON s.ID = route_stats.SUBNET_ID WHERE s.IP_VERSION = 4 GROUP BY s.NAME ORDER BY route_count_range DESC ), CombinedSubnetStats AS ( SELECT subnet_name, order_range, order_variance, NULL AS route_count_range, NULL AS route_count_variance, NULL AS route_count_stddev, 'DNS Nameserver Order Stats' AS reason FROM DnsOrderStats UNION ALL SELECT subnet_name, NULL AS order_range, NULL AS order_variance, route_count_range, route_count_variance, route_count_stddev, 'Route Count Stats' AS reason FROM RouteCountStats ) SELECT * FROM CombinedSubnetStats ORDER BY subnet_name, reason;

question: For ports whose status is DOWN, list each port’s ID and tenant ID along with its binding host and VIF type, allocated IP address (with a row number ordered by IP address using a window frame of 2 preceding rows and 1 following row), and the port’s MAC address with the running sum of standard attribute IDs within each resource type group ordered by standard attribute ID; additionally, for each tenant show the total number of distinct DOWN ports and the deviation of that tenant’s DOWN-port count from the average DOWN-port count across all tenants. Do not return any rounded answers.
sql: WITH inner_cte AS (WITH DownPortBindingIPs AS (SELECT p.ID AS port_id, p.TENANT_ID AS tenant_id, b.HOST AS host, b.VIF_TYPE AS vif_type, ia.IP_ADDRESS AS ip_address, ROW_NUMBER() OVER ( ORDER BY ia.IP_ADDRESS ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND 1 FOLLOWING ) AS window_column FROM ML2_PORT_BINDINGS b JOIN PORTS p ON b.PORT_ID = p.ID JOIN IPALLOCATIONS ia ON p.ID = ia.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN'), DownPortMacAttrSums AS (SELECT p.ID AS port_id, p.TENANT_ID AS tenant_id, p.MAC_ADDRESS AS mac_address, SUM(sa.ID) OVER ( PARTITION BY sa.RESOURCE_TYPE ORDER BY sa.ID ) AS window_column FROM PORTS p JOIN STANDARDATTRIBUTES sa ON sa.ID = p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN') SELECT d1.port_id, d1.tenant_id, d1.host, d1.vif_type, d1.ip_address, d1.window_column AS ip_row_number_window, d2.mac_address, d2.window_column AS standard_attr_running_sum_window FROM DownPortBindingIPs d1 JOIN DownPortMacAttrSums d2 ON d1.port_id = d2.port_id ORDER BY d1.tenant_id, d1.port_id, d1.ip_address), TenantDownPortCounts AS (SELECT p.tenant_id, COUNT(DISTINCT p.id) AS down_ports FROM PORTS p WHERE p.status = 'DOWN' GROUP BY p.tenant_id), AverageTenantDownPortCounts AS (SELECT AVG(down_ports) AS avg_down_ports FROM TenantDownPortCounts) SELECT i.port_id, i.tenant_id, i.host, i.vif_type, i.ip_address, i.ip_row_number_window, i.mac_address, i.standard_attr_running_sum_window, t.down_ports AS tenant_down_port_count, (t.down_ports - a.avg_down_ports) AS deviation_from_avg_tenant_down_port_count FROM inner_cte i JOIN TenantDownPortCounts t ON t.tenant_id = i.tenant_id CROSS JOIN AverageTenantDownPortCounts a ORDER BY i.tenant_id, i.port_id, i.ip_address;

WITH DownPortBindingIPs AS (SELECT p.ID AS port_id, p.TENANT_ID AS tenant_id, b.HOST AS host, b.VIF_TYPE AS vif_type, ia.IP_ADDRESS AS ip_address, ROW_NUMBER() OVER ( ORDER BY ia.IP_ADDRESS ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND 1 FOLLOWING ) AS window_column FROM ML2_PORT_BINDINGS b JOIN PORTS p ON b.PORT_ID = p.ID JOIN IPALLOCATIONS ia ON p.ID = ia.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN'), DownPortMacAttrSums AS (SELECT p.ID AS port_id, p.TENANT_ID AS tenant_id, p.MAC_ADDRESS AS mac_address, SUM(sa.ID) OVER ( PARTITION BY sa.RESOURCE_TYPE ORDER BY sa.ID ) AS window_column FROM PORTS p JOIN STANDARDATTRIBUTES sa ON sa.ID = p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN') SELECT d1.port_id, d1.tenant_id, d1.host, d1.vif_type, d1.ip_address, d1.window_column AS ip_row_number_window, d2.mac_address, d2.window_column AS standard_attr_running_sum_window FROM DownPortBindingIPs d1 JOIN DownPortMacAttrSums d2 ON d1.port_id = d2.port_id ORDER BY d1.tenant_id, d1.port_id, d1.ip_address;

question: From the top 10 tenants (among those with at least 2 DOWN ports) ranked by the number of distinct DOWN ports, show each tenant’s ID, the distinct DOWN port count, the average row-number window value computed by ordering allocated IP addresses (frame: 2 preceding to 1 following), the average dense-rank window value computed by ordering port-security settings (frame: 2 preceding to current row), and whether the tenant has any ports bound to a host (i.e., any ML2 port binding exists). Do not return any rounded answers.
sql: WITH inner_cte AS ( WITH PortSecurityWindow AS (SELECT p.id AS port_id, dense_rank() OVER ( ORDER BY psb.port_security_enabled ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW ) AS window_column FROM ports AS p JOIN portsecuritybindings AS psb ON p.id = psb.port_id WHERE p.status = 'DOWN'), PortIpBindingWindow AS (SELECT p.ID AS port_id, p.TENANT_ID AS tenant_id, b.HOST AS host, b.VIF_TYPE AS vif_type, ia.IP_ADDRESS AS ip_address, ROW_NUMBER() OVER ( ORDER BY ia.IP_ADDRESS ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND 1 FOLLOWING ) AS window_column FROM ML2_PORT_BINDINGS b JOIN PORTS p ON b.PORT_ID = p.ID JOIN IPALLOCATIONS ia ON p.ID = ia.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN') SELECT pibw.tenant_id, COUNT(DISTINCT pibw.port_id) AS down_port_count, AVG(pibw.window_column) AS avg_ip_row_number_window, AVG(psw.window_column) AS avg_port_security_dense_rank_window FROM PortIpBindingWindow pibw JOIN PortSecurityWindow psw ON pibw.port_id = psw.port_id WHERE pibw.tenant_id IS NOT NULL GROUP BY pibw.tenant_id HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT pibw.port_id) >= 2 ORDER BY down_port_count DESC, pibw.tenant_id ) SELECT i.tenant_id, i.down_port_count, i.avg_ip_row_number_window, i.avg_port_security_dense_rank_window, CASE WHEN COUNT(DISTINCT b.port_id) > 0 THEN 'Yes' ELSE 'No' END AS has_any_port_binding FROM inner_cte i LEFT JOIN ports p ON p.tenant_id = i.tenant_id LEFT JOIN ml2_port_bindings b ON b.port_id = p.id GROUP BY i.tenant_id, i.down_port_count, i.avg_ip_row_number_window, i.avg_port_security_dense_rank_window ORDER BY i.down_port_count DESC, i.tenant_id LIMIT 10;

sub_sqls: SELECT p.id AS port_id, dense_rank() OVER ( ORDER BY psb.port_security_enabled ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW ) AS window_column FROM ports AS p JOIN portsecuritybindings AS psb ON p.id = psb.port_id WHERE p.status = 'DOWN';

SELECT p.ID AS port_id, p.TENANT_ID AS tenant_id, b.HOST AS host, b.VIF_TYPE AS vif_type, ia.IP_ADDRESS AS ip_address, ROW_NUMBER() OVER ( ORDER BY ia.IP_ADDRESS ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND 1 FOLLOWING ) AS window_column FROM ML2_PORT_BINDINGS b JOIN PORTS p ON b.PORT_ID = p.ID JOIN IPALLOCATIONS ia ON p.ID = ia.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN';

WITH PortSecurityWindow AS (SELECT p.id AS port_id, dense_rank() OVER ( ORDER BY psb.port_security_enabled ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW ) AS window_column FROM ports AS p JOIN portsecuritybindings AS psb ON p.id = psb.port_id WHERE p.status = 'DOWN'), PortIpBindingWindow AS (SELECT p.ID AS port_id, p.TENANT_ID AS tenant_id, b.HOST AS host, b.VIF_TYPE AS vif_type, ia.IP_ADDRESS AS ip_address, ROW_NUMBER() OVER ( ORDER BY ia.IP_ADDRESS ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND 1 FOLLOWING ) AS window_column FROM ML2_PORT_BINDINGS b JOIN PORTS p ON b.PORT_ID = p.ID JOIN IPALLOCATIONS ia ON p.ID = ia.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN') SELECT pibw.tenant_id, COUNT(DISTINCT pibw.port_id) AS down_port_count, AVG(pibw.window_column) AS avg_ip_row_number_window, AVG(psw.window_column) AS avg_port_security_dense_rank_window FROM PortIpBindingWindow pibw JOIN PortSecurityWindow psw ON pibw.port_id = psw.port_id WHERE pibw.tenant_id IS NOT NULL GROUP BY pibw.tenant_id HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT pibw.port_id) >= 2 ORDER BY down_port_count DESC, pibw.tenant_id;

question: For ports that are DOWN, list each port’s ID, tenant ID, name, network ID, MAC address, admin state, status, device owner, and security group ID, along with (1) the rank of the port within its security group when ordered by port ID and (2) the minimum admin_state_up value over a window of 3 preceding and 1 following row ordered by port ID. Do not repeat the security group ID if it is the same as the previous row, and include a subtotal row per security group showing the total number of DOWN ports in that security group. Do not return any rounded answers.
sql: WITH inner_cte AS ( WITH subq1 AS ( SELECT p.id AS port_id, p.tenant_id, p.mac_address, sgpb.security_group_id, RANK() OVER ( PARTITION BY sgpb.security_group_id ORDER BY p.id ) AS window_column FROM SECURITYGROUPPORTBINDINGS AS sgpb JOIN PORTS AS p ON sgpb.port_id = p.id JOIN PORTSECURITYBINDINGS AS psb ON p.id = psb.port_id WHERE p.status = 'DOWN' ), subq2 AS ( SELECT p.NAME, p.NETWORK_ID, p.MAC_ADDRESS, p.ADMIN_STATE_UP, p.STATUS, p.DEVICE_OWNER, s.SECURITY_GROUP_ID, MIN(p.ADMIN_STATE_UP) OVER ( ORDER BY p.ID ROWS BETWEEN 3 PRECEDING AND 1 FOLLOWING ) AS window_column FROM PORTS AS p JOIN SECURITYGROUPPORTBINDINGS AS s ON p.ID = s.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' ) SELECT subq1.port_id, subq1.tenant_id, subq2.name AS port_name, subq2.network_id, subq1.mac_address, subq2.admin_state_up, subq2.status, subq2.device_owner, subq1.security_group_id, subq1.window_column AS port_rank_within_security_group_by_port_id, subq2.window_column AS min_admin_state_up_in_3_preceding_1_following_by_port_id FROM subq1 JOIN subq2 ON subq1.security_group_id = subq2.security_group_id AND subq1.mac_address = subq2.mac_address ORDER BY subq1.security_group_id, subq1.window_column, subq1.port_id ) SELECT CASE WHEN LAG(security_group_id) OVER (ORDER BY security_group_id_sort, port_rank_within_security_group_by_port_id, port_id) = security_group_id THEN NULL ELSE security_group_id END AS security_group_id, port_id, tenant_id, port_name, network_id, mac_address, admin_state_up, status, device_owner, port_rank_within_security_group_by_port_id, min_admin_state_up_in_3_preceding_1_following_by_port_id, down_ports_in_security_group FROM ( SELECT CASE WHEN GROUPING(security_group_id) = 1 THEN 'zzz' ELSE security_group_id END AS security_group_id_sort, CASE WHEN GROUPING(security_group_id) = 1 THEN 'TOTAL' ELSE security_group_id END AS security_group_id, port_id, tenant_id, port_name, network_id, mac_address, admin_state_up, status, device_owner, port_rank_within_security_group_by_port_id, min_admin_state_up_in_3_preceding_1_following_by_port_id, COUNT(*) AS down_ports_in_security_group FROM inner_cte GROUP BY security_group_id, port_id, tenant_id, port_name, network_id, mac_address, admin_state_up, status, device_owner, port_rank_within_security_group_by_port_id, min_admin_state_up_in_3_preceding_1_following_by_port_id WITH ROLLUP ) AS tbltmp ORDER BY security_group_id_sort, port_rank_within_security_group_by_port_id, port_id;

question: For ports whose status is DOWN, return only those ports whose rank within the DOWN status group (ordered by port ID) is greater than the average of those ranks across all DOWN ports; list the port ID, tenant ID, MAC address, the running sum of standard attribute IDs within each standard attribute resource type (ordered by standard attribute ID), plus the port name, binding host, VIF type, and the port’s rank. Do not return any rounded answers.
sql: WITH inner_cte AS ( WITH DownPortsStdAttrWindow AS ( SELECT p.ID AS port_id, p.TENANT_ID AS tenant_id, p.MAC_ADDRESS AS mac_address, SUM(sa.ID) OVER ( PARTITION BY sa.RESOURCE_TYPE ORDER BY sa.ID ) AS window_column FROM PORTS p JOIN STANDARDATTRIBUTES sa ON sa.ID = p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' ), DownPortsBindingRank AS ( SELECT p.ID AS port_id, p.NAME AS port_name, p.MAC_ADDRESS AS mac_address, b.HOST AS binding_host, b.VIF_TYPE AS vif_type, RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY p.STATUS ORDER BY p.ID) AS window_column FROM PORTS p JOIN ML2_PORT_BINDINGS b ON p.ID = b.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' ) SELECT s.port_id, s.tenant_id, s.mac_address, s.window_column AS running_sum_standard_attr_ids_within_resource_type, b.port_name, b.binding_host, b.vif_type, b.window_column AS rank_within_down_status_by_port_id FROM DownPortsStdAttrWindow s JOIN DownPortsBindingRank b ON s.port_id = b.port_id AND s.mac_address = b.mac_address ) SELECT port_id, tenant_id, mac_address, running_sum_standard_attr_ids_within_resource_type, port_name, binding_host, vif_type, rank_within_down_status_by_port_id FROM inner_cte WHERE rank_within_down_status_by_port_id > (SELECT AVG(rank_within_down_status_by_port_id) FROM inner_cte);

question: For each network, using the combined list of administratively-up ports (including those with status DOWN) from the prior result set, find the network ID and the maximum of the per-port window metric (admin-up window average standard attribute ID for “Admin State Up” rows, or down-window average port ID for “Status DOWN” rows) observed among ports in that network. Do not return any rounded answers.
sql: WITH inner_cte AS (WITH AdminUpPorts AS (SELECT b.PORT_ID, b.HOST, b.VIF_TYPE, b.VNIC_TYPE, p.TENANT_ID, p.NETWORK_ID, p.MAC_ADDRESS, p.STATUS, p.DEVICE_OWNER, AVG(p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID) OVER ( PARTITION BY b.VIF_TYPE ORDER BY p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND 2 FOLLOWING ) AS window_column FROM ML2_PORT_BINDINGS AS b JOIN PORTS AS p ON b.PORT_ID = p.ID JOIN PORTSECURITYBINDINGS AS psb ON p.ID = psb.PORT_ID WHERE p.ADMIN_STATE_UP = 1), DownPortsWithIPs AS (SELECT p.ID AS port_id, p.NAME AS port_name, p.MAC_ADDRESS AS mac_address, ia.IP_ADDRESS AS ip_address, ia.SUBNET_ID AS subnet_id, AVG(p.ID) OVER (PARTITION BY p.ID ORDER BY ia.IP_ADDRESS) AS window_column FROM PORTS p JOIN IPALLOCATIONS ia ON p.ID = ia.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' ORDER BY ia.IP_ADDRESS), CombinedPorts AS ( SELECT a.PORT_ID AS port_id, a.HOST, a.VIF_TYPE, a.VNIC_TYPE, a.TENANT_ID, a.NETWORK_ID, a.MAC_ADDRESS, a.STATUS, a.DEVICE_OWNER, a.window_column AS admin_up_window_avg_standard_attr_id, NULL AS port_name, NULL AS ip_address, NULL AS subnet_id, NULL AS down_window_avg_port_id, 'Admin State Up' AS reason FROM AdminUpPorts a UNION ALL SELECT d.port_id, NULL AS HOST, NULL AS VIF_TYPE, NULL AS VNIC_TYPE, p.TENANT_ID, p.NETWORK_ID, d.mac_address AS MAC_ADDRESS, p.STATUS, p.DEVICE_OWNER, NULL AS admin_up_window_avg_standard_attr_id, d.port_name, d.ip_address, d.subnet_id, d.window_column AS down_window_avg_port_id, 'Status DOWN' AS reason FROM DownPortsWithIPs d JOIN PORTS p ON p.ID = d.port_id WHERE p.ADMIN_STATE_UP = 1 ) SELECT * FROM CombinedPorts ORDER BY port_id, reason) , NetworkPortWindowMetric AS ( SELECT p.network_id, p.id AS port_id, MAX( COALESCE(inner_cte.admin_up_window_avg_standard_attr_id, inner_cte.down_window_avg_port_id) ) AS port_window_metric FROM inner_cte JOIN PORTS p ON p.id = inner_cte.port_id GROUP BY p.network_id, p.id ) SELECT network_id, MAX(port_window_metric) AS max_port_window_metric FROM NetworkPortWindowMetric GROUP BY network_id;

WITH AdminUpPorts AS (SELECT b.PORT_ID, b.HOST, b.VIF_TYPE, b.VNIC_TYPE, p.TENANT_ID, p.NETWORK_ID, p.MAC_ADDRESS, p.STATUS, p.DEVICE_OWNER, AVG(p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID) OVER ( PARTITION BY b.VIF_TYPE ORDER BY p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND 2 FOLLOWING ) AS window_column FROM ML2_PORT_BINDINGS AS b JOIN PORTS AS p ON b.PORT_ID = p.ID JOIN PORTSECURITYBINDINGS AS psb ON p.ID = psb.PORT_ID WHERE p.ADMIN_STATE_UP = 1), DownPortsWithIPs AS (SELECT p.ID AS port_id, p.NAME AS port_name, p.MAC_ADDRESS AS mac_address, ia.IP_ADDRESS AS ip_address, ia.SUBNET_ID AS subnet_id, AVG(p.ID) OVER (PARTITION BY p.ID ORDER BY ia.IP_ADDRESS) AS window_column FROM PORTS p JOIN IPALLOCATIONS ia ON p.ID = ia.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' ORDER BY ia.IP_ADDRESS), CombinedPorts AS ( SELECT a.PORT_ID AS port_id, a.HOST, a.VIF_TYPE, a.VNIC_TYPE, a.TENANT_ID, a.NETWORK_ID, a.MAC_ADDRESS, a.STATUS, a.DEVICE_OWNER, a.window_column AS admin_up_window_avg_standard_attr_id, NULL AS port_name, NULL AS ip_address, NULL AS subnet_id, NULL AS down_window_avg_port_id, 'Admin State Up' AS reason FROM AdminUpPorts a UNION ALL SELECT d.port_id, NULL AS HOST, NULL AS VIF_TYPE, NULL AS VNIC_TYPE, p.TENANT_ID, p.NETWORK_ID, d.mac_address AS MAC_ADDRESS, p.STATUS, p.DEVICE_OWNER, NULL AS admin_up_window_avg_standard_attr_id, d.port_name, d.ip_address, d.subnet_id, d.window_column AS down_window_avg_port_id, 'Status DOWN' AS reason FROM DownPortsWithIPs d JOIN PORTS p ON p.ID = d.port_id WHERE p.ADMIN_STATE_UP = 1 ) SELECT * FROM CombinedPorts ORDER BY port_id, reason;

question: Among device owners that have DOWN ports bound to a security group, list the top 10 device owners by distinct DOWN port count, showing the device owner, distinct port count, minimum standard attribute ID, the variance of standard attribute IDs for DOWN ports that have an IP allocation, and the number of distinct networks those DOWN ports span. Do not return any rounded answers.
sql: WITH inner_cte AS ( WITH PortSecurityGroupStats AS ( SELECT p.STATUS AS port_status, p.DEVICE_OWNER AS device_owner, COUNT(DISTINCT p.ID) AS port_count, MIN(p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID) AS min_standard_attr_id FROM PORTS p JOIN SECURITYGROUPPORTBINDINGS spb ON p.ID = spb.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' GROUP BY p.STATUS, p.DEVICE_OWNER ), PortStatusStdAttrVariance AS ( SELECT p.STATUS, VARIANCE(p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID) AS standard_attr_id_variance FROM PORTS AS p JOIN IPALLOCATIONS AS ia ON p.ID = ia.PORT_ID WHERE p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID IS NOT NULL GROUP BY p.STATUS ORDER BY standard_attr_id_variance DESC ) SELECT psgs.port_status, psgs.device_owner, psgs.port_count, psgs.min_standard_attr_id, pssav.standard_attr_id_variance FROM PortSecurityGroupStats psgs JOIN PortStatusStdAttrVariance pssav ON psgs.port_status = pssav.STATUS ORDER BY psgs.port_status, psgs.device_owner ) SELECT i.device_owner, i.port_count, i.min_standard_attr_id, i.standard_attr_id_variance, COUNT(DISTINCT p.NETWORK_ID) AS distinct_networks FROM inner_cte i JOIN PORTS p ON p.DEVICE_OWNER = i.device_owner AND p.STATUS = i.port_status JOIN SECURITYGROUPPORTBINDINGS spb ON p.ID = spb.PORT_ID GROUP BY i.device_owner, i.port_count, i.min_standard_attr_id, i.standard_attr_id_variance ORDER BY i.port_count DESC LIMIT 10;

WITH PortSecurityGroupStats AS ( SELECT p.STATUS AS port_status, p.DEVICE_OWNER AS device_owner, COUNT(DISTINCT p.ID) AS port_count, MIN(p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID) AS min_standard_attr_id FROM PORTS p JOIN SECURITYGROUPPORTBINDINGS spb ON p.ID = spb.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' GROUP BY p.STATUS, p.DEVICE_OWNER ), PortStatusStdAttrVariance AS ( SELECT p.STATUS, VARIANCE(p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID) AS standard_attr_id_variance FROM PORTS AS p JOIN IPALLOCATIONS AS ia ON p.ID = ia.PORT_ID WHERE p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID IS NOT NULL GROUP BY p.STATUS ORDER BY standard_attr_id_variance DESC ) SELECT psgs.port_status, psgs.device_owner, psgs.port_count, psgs.min_standard_attr_id, pssav.standard_attr_id_variance FROM PortSecurityGroupStats psgs JOIN PortStatusStdAttrVariance pssav ON psgs.port_status = pssav.STATUS ORDER BY psgs.port_status, psgs.device_owner;

question: For each network that has at least one DOWN port bound to a security group, find the network ID and the maximum (across its ports) of the per-port row number computed by ordering allocated IP addresses with a window frame of 2 preceding rows and 1 following row, using the DOWN-port details and status/device-owner security-group summary as the inner result. Do not return any rounded answers.
sql: WITH inner_cte AS (WITH port_status_owner_sg_summary AS ( SELECT p.STATUS AS port_status, p.DEVICE_OWNER AS device_owner, COUNT(DISTINCT p.ID) AS port_count, MIN(p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID) AS min_standard_attr_id FROM PORTS p JOIN SECURITYGROUPPORTBINDINGS spb ON p.ID = spb.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' GROUP BY p.STATUS, p.DEVICE_OWNER ), down_ports_with_ip_window AS ( SELECT p.ID AS port_id, p.TENANT_ID AS tenant_id, b.HOST AS host, b.VIF_TYPE AS vif_type, ia.IP_ADDRESS AS ip_address, ROW_NUMBER() OVER ( ORDER BY ia.IP_ADDRESS ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND 1 FOLLOWING ) AS window_column FROM ML2_PORT_BINDINGS b JOIN PORTS p ON b.PORT_ID = p.ID JOIN IPALLOCATIONS ia ON p.ID = ia.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' ) SELECT d.port_id, d.tenant_id, d.host, d.vif_type, d.ip_address, d.window_column, s.port_status, s.device_owner, s.port_count, s.min_standard_attr_id FROM down_ports_with_ip_window d JOIN PORTS p ON p.ID = d.port_id JOIN port_status_owner_sg_summary s ON s.port_status = p.STATUS AND s.device_owner = p.DEVICE_OWNER) SELECT p.NETWORK_ID AS network_id, MAX(i.window_column) AS max_ip_row_number FROM inner_cte i JOIN PORTS p ON p.ID = i.port_id JOIN SECURITYGROUPPORTBINDINGS spb ON spb.PORT_ID = p.ID GROUP BY p.NETWORK_ID;

WITH port_status_owner_sg_summary AS ( SELECT p.STATUS AS port_status, p.DEVICE_OWNER AS device_owner, COUNT(DISTINCT p.ID) AS port_count, MIN(p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID) AS min_standard_attr_id FROM PORTS p JOIN SECURITYGROUPPORTBINDINGS spb ON p.ID = spb.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' GROUP BY p.STATUS, p.DEVICE_OWNER ), down_ports_with_ip_window AS ( SELECT p.ID AS port_id, p.TENANT_ID AS tenant_id, b.HOST AS host, b.VIF_TYPE AS vif_type, ia.IP_ADDRESS AS ip_address, ROW_NUMBER() OVER ( ORDER BY ia.IP_ADDRESS ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND 1 FOLLOWING ) AS window_column FROM ML2_PORT_BINDINGS b JOIN PORTS p ON b.PORT_ID = p.ID JOIN IPALLOCATIONS ia ON p.ID = ia.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' ) SELECT d.port_id, d.tenant_id, d.host, d.vif_type, d.ip_address, d.window_column, s.port_status, s.device_owner, s.port_count, s.min_standard_attr_id FROM down_ports_with_ip_window d JOIN PORTS p ON p.ID = d.port_id JOIN port_status_owner_sg_summary s ON s.port_status = p.STATUS AND s.device_owner = p.DEVICE_OWNER;

question: For DOWN ports that are bound to a security group, show the same per-device-owner and VIF-type statistics as before, but also include subtotals per device owner and a grand total. Do not repeat the device owner label when it is the same as the previous row. Do not return any rounded answers.
sql: WITH inner_cte AS (WITH PortStatusOwnerStats AS (SELECT p.STATUS AS port_status, p.DEVICE_OWNER AS device_owner, COUNT(DISTINCT p.ID) AS port_count, MIN(p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID) AS min_standard_attr_id FROM PORTS p JOIN SECURITYGROUPPORTBINDINGS spb ON p.ID = spb.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' GROUP BY p.STATUS, p.DEVICE_OWNER), DownPortWindowDetails AS (SELECT p.NAME, p.MAC_ADDRESS, p.ADMIN_STATE_UP, b.HOST, b.VIF_TYPE, AVG(p.ADMIN_STATE_UP) OVER ( PARTITION BY b.VIF_TYPE ORDER BY p.MAC_ADDRESS ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND 2 FOLLOWING ) AS window_column FROM PORTS AS p JOIN ML2_PORT_BINDINGS AS b ON p.ID = b.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' ORDER BY p.MAC_ADDRESS), VifTypePortCounts AS ( SELECT b.VIF_TYPE AS vif_type, COUNT(DISTINCT p.ID) AS down_ports_with_sg_count FROM PORTS p JOIN ML2_PORT_BINDINGS b ON p.ID = b.PORT_ID JOIN SECURITYGROUPPORTBINDINGS spb ON p.ID = spb.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' GROUP BY b.VIF_TYPE ) SELECT psos.port_status, psos.device_owner, psos.port_count, psos.min_standard_attr_id, dpwd.VIF_TYPE, vpc.down_ports_with_sg_count, AVG(dpwd.window_column) AS avg_window_admin_state_up_for_vif_type FROM PortStatusOwnerStats psos JOIN PORTS p ON p.STATUS = psos.port_status AND p.DEVICE_OWNER = psos.device_owner JOIN SECURITYGROUPPORTBINDINGS spb ON spb.PORT_ID = p.ID JOIN DownPortWindowDetails dpwd ON dpwd.MAC_ADDRESS = p.MAC_ADDRESS JOIN VifTypePortCounts vpc ON vpc.vif_type = dpwd.VIF_TYPE GROUP BY psos.port_status, psos.device_owner, psos.port_count, psos.min_standard_attr_id, dpwd.VIF_TYPE, vpc.down_ports_with_sg_count ORDER BY psos.port_count DESC, dpwd.VIF_TYPE) SELECT CASE WHEN LAG(device_owner) OVER (ORDER BY device_owner_sort, device_owner, vif_type) = device_owner THEN NULL ELSE device_owner END AS device_owner, port_status, vif_type, port_count, min_standard_attr_id, down_ports_with_sg_count, avg_window_admin_state_up_for_vif_type FROM ( SELECT CASE WHEN GROUPING(device_owner) = 1 THEN 'zzz' ELSE device_owner END AS device_owner_sort, CASE WHEN GROUPING(device_owner) = 1 THEN 'TOTAL' ELSE device_owner END AS device_owner, port_status, vif_type, SUM(port_count) AS port_count, MIN(min_standard_attr_id) AS min_standard_attr_id, MAX(down_ports_with_sg_count) AS down_ports_with_sg_count, AVG(avg_window_admin_state_up_for_vif_type) AS avg_window_admin_state_up_for_vif_type FROM inner_cte GROUP BY device_owner, port_status, vif_type WITH ROLLUP ) AS tbltmp ORDER BY device_owner_sort, device_owner, vif_type;
sub_questions: For each port status and device owner, considering only ports that are bound to a security group, return the number of distinct ports and the minimum standard attribute ID.

For ports that are DOWN, show the port name, MAC address, admin_state_up flag, binding host, VIF type, and the average admin_state_up in a window of 2 preceding and 2 following rows partitioned by VIF type and ordered by MAC address.

For DOWN ports that are bound to a security group, for each device owner and VIF type, show the port status, device owner, number of distinct ports, minimum standard attribute ID, the number of DOWN ports with a security-group binding for that VIF type, and the average (by VIF type) of the 2-preceding/2-following windowed admin_state_up value ordered by MAC address.
sub_sqls: SELECT p.STATUS AS port_status, p.DEVICE_OWNER AS device_owner, COUNT(DISTINCT p.ID) AS port_count, MIN(p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID) AS min_standard_attr_id FROM PORTS p JOIN SECURITYGROUPPORTBINDINGS spb ON p.ID = spb.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' GROUP BY p.STATUS, p.DEVICE_OWNER;

SELECT p.NAME, p.MAC_ADDRESS, p.ADMIN_STATE_UP, b.HOST, b.VIF_TYPE, AVG(p.ADMIN_STATE_UP) OVER ( PARTITION BY b.VIF_TYPE ORDER BY p.MAC_ADDRESS ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND 2 FOLLOWING ) AS window_column FROM PORTS AS p JOIN ML2_PORT_BINDINGS AS b ON p.ID = b.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' ORDER BY p.MAC_ADDRESS;

WITH PortStatusOwnerStats AS (SELECT p.STATUS AS port_status, p.DEVICE_OWNER AS device_owner, COUNT(DISTINCT p.ID) AS port_count, MIN(p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID) AS min_standard_attr_id FROM PORTS p JOIN SECURITYGROUPPORTBINDINGS spb ON p.ID = spb.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' GROUP BY p.STATUS, p.DEVICE_OWNER), DownPortWindowDetails AS (SELECT p.NAME, p.MAC_ADDRESS, p.ADMIN_STATE_UP, b.HOST, b.VIF_TYPE, AVG(p.ADMIN_STATE_UP) OVER ( PARTITION BY b.VIF_TYPE ORDER BY p.MAC_ADDRESS ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND 2 FOLLOWING ) AS window_column FROM PORTS AS p JOIN ML2_PORT_BINDINGS AS b ON p.ID = b.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' ORDER BY p.MAC_ADDRESS), VifTypePortCounts AS ( SELECT b.VIF_TYPE AS vif_type, COUNT(DISTINCT p.ID) AS down_ports_with_sg_count FROM PORTS p JOIN ML2_PORT_BINDINGS b ON p.ID = b.PORT_ID JOIN SECURITYGROUPPORTBINDINGS spb ON p.ID = spb.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' GROUP BY b.VIF_TYPE ) SELECT psos.port_status, psos.device_owner, psos.port_count, psos.min_standard_attr_id, dpwd.VIF_TYPE, vpc.down_ports_with_sg_count, AVG(dpwd.window_column) AS avg_window_admin_state_up_for_vif_type FROM PortStatusOwnerStats psos JOIN PORTS p ON p.STATUS = psos.port_status AND p.DEVICE_OWNER = psos.device_owner JOIN SECURITYGROUPPORTBINDINGS spb ON spb.PORT_ID = p.ID JOIN DownPortWindowDetails dpwd ON dpwd.MAC_ADDRESS = p.MAC_ADDRESS JOIN VifTypePortCounts vpc ON vpc.vif_type = dpwd.VIF_TYPE GROUP BY psos.port_status, psos.device_owner, psos.port_count, psos.min_standard_attr_id, dpwd.VIF_TYPE, vpc.down_ports_with_sg_count ORDER BY psos.port_count DESC, dpwd.VIF_TYPE;

question: For DOWN ports that have an IP allocation, show rollups of how many such ports exist per binding host and VIF type. Include subtotals per host and a grand total, while also reporting the maximum variance of the port standard attribute ID observed for each host within the same DOWN+allocated-IP set. Do not return any rounded answers.
sql: WITH inner_cte AS ( WITH DownPortsWithWindow AS ( SELECT p.ID AS port_id, p.TENANT_ID AS tenant_id, b.HOST AS host, b.VIF_TYPE AS vif_type, ia.IP_ADDRESS AS ip_address, ROW_NUMBER() OVER ( ORDER BY ia.IP_ADDRESS ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND 1 FOLLOWING ) AS window_column FROM ML2_PORT_BINDINGS b JOIN PORTS p ON b.PORT_ID = p.ID JOIN IPALLOCATIONS ia ON p.ID = ia.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' ), HostStandardAttrVariance AS ( SELECT b.HOST, VARIANCE(p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID) AS standard_attr_id_variance FROM ML2_PORT_BINDINGS AS b JOIN PORTS AS p ON b.PORT_ID = p.ID JOIN IPALLOCATIONS AS ia ON p.ID = ia.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' AND ia.PORT_ID IS NOT NULL GROUP BY b.HOST ORDER BY standard_attr_id_variance DESC ) SELECT dpw.port_id, dpw.tenant_id, dpw.host, dpw.vif_type, dpw.ip_address, dpw.window_column, hsv.standard_attr_id_variance FROM DownPortsWithWindow dpw JOIN HostStandardAttrVariance hsv ON dpw.host = hsv.HOST ORDER BY hsv.standard_attr_id_variance DESC, dpw.ip_address ), HostVifCounts AS ( SELECT i.host, i.vif_type, COUNT(DISTINCT i.port_id) AS total_ports, MAX(i.standard_attr_id_variance) AS host_standard_attr_id_variance FROM inner_cte i GROUP BY i.host, i.vif_type ) SELECT CASE WHEN GROUPING(host) = 1 THEN 'GRAND TOTAL' ELSE host END AS host, CASE WHEN GROUPING(vif_type) = 1 AND GROUPING(host) = 0 THEN 'SUBTOTAL' WHEN GROUPING(vif_type) = 1 AND GROUPING(host) = 1 THEN 'GRAND TOTAL' ELSE vif_type END AS vif_type, SUM(total_ports) AS total_ports, MAX(host_standard_attr_id_variance) AS host_standard_attr_id_variance FROM HostVifCounts GROUP BY host, vif_type WITH ROLLUP;
sub_questions: For ports whose status is DOWN, list the port ID, tenant ID, host, VIF type, and allocated IP address, and assign row numbers ordered by IP address using a window frame of 2 preceding rows and 1 following row.
For each port binding host, show the host name and the variance of the port standard attribute ID, considering only ports whose status is 'DOWN' and that have an IP allocation.

For ports with status 'DOWN' that have an IP allocation, list each port’s ID, tenant ID, binding host, VIF type, allocated IP address, and the row number ordered by IP address using a window frame of 2 preceding rows and 1 following row, along with the variance of the port standard attribute ID for that same host.
sub_sqls: SELECT p.ID AS port_id, p.TENANT_ID AS tenant_id, b.HOST AS host, b.VIF_TYPE AS vif_type, ia.IP_ADDRESS AS ip_address, ROW_NUMBER() OVER ( ORDER BY ia.IP_ADDRESS ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND 1 FOLLOWING ) AS window_column FROM ML2_PORT_BINDINGS b JOIN PORTS p ON b.PORT_ID = p.ID JOIN IPALLOCATIONS ia ON p.ID = ia.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN';

SELECT b.HOST, VARIANCE(p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID) AS standard_attr_id_variance FROM ML2_PORT_BINDINGS AS b JOIN PORTS AS p ON b.PORT_ID = p.ID JOIN IPALLOCATIONS AS ia ON p.ID = ia.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' AND ia.PORT_ID IS NOT NULL GROUP BY b.HOST ORDER BY standard_attr_id_variance DESC;

WITH DownPortsWithWindow AS ( SELECT p.ID AS port_id, p.TENANT_ID AS tenant_id, b.HOST AS host, b.VIF_TYPE AS vif_type, ia.IP_ADDRESS AS ip_address, ROW_NUMBER() OVER ( ORDER BY ia.IP_ADDRESS ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND 1 FOLLOWING ) AS window_column FROM ML2_PORT_BINDINGS b JOIN PORTS p ON b.PORT_ID = p.ID JOIN IPALLOCATIONS ia ON p.ID = ia.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' ), HostStandardAttrVariance AS ( SELECT b.HOST, VARIANCE(p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID) AS standard_attr_id_variance FROM ML2_PORT_BINDINGS AS b JOIN PORTS AS p ON b.PORT_ID = p.ID JOIN IPALLOCATIONS AS ia ON p.ID = ia.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' AND ia.PORT_ID IS NOT NULL GROUP BY b.HOST ORDER BY standard_attr_id_variance DESC ) SELECT dpw.port_id, dpw.tenant_id, dpw.host, dpw.vif_type, dpw.ip_address, dpw.window_column, hsv.standard_attr_id_variance FROM DownPortsWithWindow dpw JOIN HostStandardAttrVariance hsv ON dpw.host = hsv.HOST ORDER BY hsv.standard_attr_id_variance DESC, dpw.ip_address;

question: For IPv4 subnets, using the detailed subnet-and-route listing as a base, summarize how many result rows fall under each DHCP enabled flag and route presence category (label as 'Has Routes' when a subnet has at least one associated route row, otherwise 'No Routes'). Include subtotals per DHCP flag and a grand total. Do not return any rounded answers.
sql: WITH inner_cte AS (WITH SubnetDetails AS (SELECT s.NAME, s.TENANT_ID, s.NETWORK_ID, s.IP_VERSION, s.CIDR, s.GATEWAY_IP, s.ENABLE_DHCP, p.FIRST_IP, p.LAST_IP, MAX(s.STANDARD_ATTR_ID) OVER ( ORDER BY s.ID ROWS BETWEEN CURRENT ROW AND 2 FOLLOWING ) AS max_standard_attr_id_next2 FROM SUBNETS AS s JOIN IPALLOCATIONPOOLS AS p ON s.ID = p.SUBNET_ID WHERE s.IP_VERSION = 4), SubnetRouteDetails AS (SELECT r.DESTINATION, r.NEXTHOP, s.NAME AS subnet_name, s.CIDR AS subnet_cidr, p.FIRST_IP, p.LAST_IP, DENSE_RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY r.SUBNET_ID ORDER BY r.SUBNET_ID) AS window_column FROM SUBNETROUTES r JOIN SUBNETS s ON r.SUBNET_ID = s.ID JOIN IPALLOCATIONPOOLS p ON s.ID = p.SUBNET_ID WHERE s.IP_VERSION = 4) SELECT sd.NAME AS subnet_name, sd.TENANT_ID, sd.NETWORK_ID, sd.IP_VERSION, sd.CIDR, sd.GATEWAY_IP, sd.ENABLE_DHCP, sd.FIRST_IP AS allocation_first_ip, sd.LAST_IP AS allocation_last_ip, sd.max_standard_attr_id_next2, srd.DESTINATION AS route_destination, srd.NEXTHOP AS route_nexthop, srd.window_column AS route_dense_rank_within_subnet FROM SubnetDetails sd LEFT JOIN SubnetRouteDetails srd ON sd.NAME = srd.subnet_name AND sd.CIDR = srd.subnet_cidr AND sd.FIRST_IP = srd.FIRST_IP AND sd.LAST_IP = srd.LAST_IP ORDER BY sd.NAME, srd.window_column, srd.DESTINATION), RoutePresenceSummary AS (SELECT ic.ENABLE_DHCP, CASE WHEN ic.route_destination IS NOT NULL THEN 'Has Routes' ELSE 'No Routes' END AS route_presence, COUNT(*) AS total_rows FROM inner_cte ic GROUP BY ic.ENABLE_DHCP, route_presence) SELECT CASE WHEN GROUPING(ENABLE_DHCP) = 1 THEN 'GRAND TOTAL' ELSE CAST(ENABLE_DHCP AS CHAR) END AS enable_dhcp, CASE WHEN GROUPING(route_presence) = 1 AND GROUPING(ENABLE_DHCP) = 0 THEN 'SUBTOTAL' ELSE route_presence END AS route_presence, SUM(total_rows) AS total_rows FROM RoutePresenceSummary GROUP BY ENABLE_DHCP, route_presence WITH ROLLUP;

Also show any associated subnet routes (destination and next hop) and the dense-rank value within each subnet for those routes.
