SELECT r.DESTINATION, r.NEXTHOP, s.NAME AS subnet_name, s.CIDR AS subnet_cidr, p.FIRST_IP, p.LAST_IP, DENSE_RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY r.SUBNET_ID ORDER BY r.SUBNET_ID) AS window_column FROM SUBNETROUTES r JOIN SUBNETS s ON r.SUBNET_ID = s.ID JOIN IPALLOCATIONPOOLS p ON s.ID = p.SUBNET_ID WHERE s.IP_VERSION = 4

WITH SubnetDetails AS (SELECT s.NAME, s.TENANT_ID, s.NETWORK_ID, s.IP_VERSION, s.CIDR, s.GATEWAY_IP, s.ENABLE_DHCP, p.FIRST_IP, p.LAST_IP, MAX(s.STANDARD_ATTR_ID) OVER ( ORDER BY s.ID ROWS BETWEEN CURRENT ROW AND 2 FOLLOWING ) AS max_standard_attr_id_next2 FROM SUBNETS AS s JOIN IPALLOCATIONPOOLS AS p ON s.ID = p.SUBNET_ID WHERE s.IP_VERSION = 4), SubnetRouteDetails AS (SELECT r.DESTINATION, r.NEXTHOP, s.NAME AS subnet_name, s.CIDR AS subnet_cidr, p.FIRST_IP, p.LAST_IP, DENSE_RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY r.SUBNET_ID ORDER BY r.SUBNET_ID) AS window_column FROM SUBNETROUTES r JOIN SUBNETS s ON r.SUBNET_ID = s.ID JOIN IPALLOCATIONPOOLS p ON s.ID = p.SUBNET_ID WHERE s.IP_VERSION = 4) SELECT sd.NAME AS subnet_name, sd.TENANT_ID, sd.NETWORK_ID, sd.IP_VERSION, sd.CIDR, sd.GATEWAY_IP, sd.ENABLE_DHCP, sd.FIRST_IP AS allocation_first_ip, sd.LAST_IP AS allocation_last_ip, sd.max_standard_attr_id_next2, srd.DESTINATION AS route_destination, srd.NEXTHOP AS route_nexthop, srd.window_column AS route_dense_rank_within_subnet FROM SubnetDetails sd LEFT JOIN SubnetRouteDetails srd ON sd.NAME = srd.subnet_name AND sd.CIDR = srd.subnet_cidr AND sd.FIRST_IP = srd.FIRST_IP AND sd.LAST_IP = srd.LAST_IP ORDER BY sd.NAME, srd.window_column, srd.DESTINATION;

question: For active networks, list each tenant’s networks (with a row number per tenant ordered by network name) and, for the ports on those networks whose standard attribute resource type is 'ports', show the port status and device owner along with the number of ports and the earliest standard-attribute updated timestamp for that status/owner; additionally, return only those rows where the port_count is greater than the average port_count for the same port_status across all status/owner groups. Do not return any rounded answers.
sql: WITH inner_cte AS (WITH PortStatusOwnerStats AS (SELECT p.STATUS AS port_status, p.DEVICE_OWNER AS device_owner, COUNT(p.ID) AS port_count, MIN(sa.UPDATED_AT) AS earliest_standard_attr_update FROM PORTS p JOIN STANDARDATTRIBUTES sa ON sa.ID = p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID WHERE sa.RESOURCE_TYPE = 'ports' GROUP BY p.STATUS, p.DEVICE_OWNER), ActiveTenantNetworks AS (SELECT n.ID AS network_id, n.NAME AS network_name, n.TENANT_ID AS tenant_id, n.ADMIN_STATE_UP AS admin_state_up, n.MTU AS mtu, sa.UPDATED_AT AS standard_attr_updated_at, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY n.TENANT_ID ORDER BY n.NAME) AS window_column FROM NETWORKS n JOIN STANDARDATTRIBUTES sa ON sa.ID = n.STANDARD_ATTR_ID WHERE n.STATUS = 'ACTIVE'), ActiveTenantPortStatusOwnerStats AS ( SELECT atn.tenant_id, atn.network_id, atn.network_name, atn.admin_state_up, atn.mtu, atn.standard_attr_updated_at, atn.window_column, psos.port_status, psos.device_owner, psos.port_count, psos.earliest_standard_attr_update FROM ActiveTenantNetworks atn JOIN PORTS p ON p.NETWORK_ID = atn.network_id JOIN PortStatusOwnerStats psos ON psos.port_status = p.STATUS AND psos.device_owner = p.DEVICE_OWNER JOIN STANDARDATTRIBUTES sa_p ON sa_p.ID = p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID WHERE sa_p.RESOURCE_TYPE = 'ports' GROUP BY atn.tenant_id, atn.network_id, atn.network_name, atn.admin_state_up, atn.mtu, atn.standard_attr_updated_at, atn.window_column, psos.port_status, psos.device_owner, psos.port_count, psos.earliest_standard_attr_update ) SELECT * FROM ActiveTenantPortStatusOwnerStats ORDER BY tenant_id, window_column, network_id, port_status, device_owner) , StatusAverages AS ( SELECT port_status, AVG(port_count) AS avg_port_count FROM ( SELECT psos.port_status, psos.device_owner, psos.port_count FROM PORTS p JOIN STANDARDATTRIBUTES sa ON sa.ID = p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID JOIN ( SELECT p2.STATUS AS port_status, p2.DEVICE_OWNER AS device_owner, COUNT(p2.ID) AS port_count FROM PORTS p2 JOIN STANDARDATTRIBUTES sa2 ON sa2.ID = p2.STANDARD_ATTR_ID WHERE sa2.RESOURCE_TYPE = 'ports' GROUP BY p2.STATUS, p2.DEVICE_OWNER ) psos ON psos.port_status = p.STATUS AND psos.device_owner = p.DEVICE_OWNER WHERE sa.RESOURCE_TYPE = 'ports' GROUP BY psos.port_status, psos.device_owner, psos.port_count ) grouped_counts GROUP BY port_status ) SELECT i.* FROM inner_cte i JOIN StatusAverages sa ON sa.port_status = i.port_status WHERE i.port_count > sa.avg_port_count ORDER BY i.tenant_id, i.window_column, i.network_id, i.port_status, i.device_owner;

SELECT n.ID AS network_id, n.NAME AS network_name, n.TENANT_ID AS tenant_id, n.ADMIN_STATE_UP AS admin_state_up, n.MTU AS mtu, sa.UPDATED_AT AS standard_attr_updated_at, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY n.TENANT_ID ORDER BY n.NAME) AS window_column FROM NETWORKS n JOIN STANDARDATTRIBUTES sa ON sa.ID = n.STANDARD_ATTR_ID WHERE n.STATUS = 'ACTIVE';

WITH PortStatusOwnerStats AS (SELECT p.STATUS AS port_status, p.DEVICE_OWNER AS device_owner, COUNT(p.ID) AS port_count, MIN(sa.UPDATED_AT) AS earliest_standard_attr_update FROM PORTS p JOIN STANDARDATTRIBUTES sa ON sa.ID = p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID WHERE sa.RESOURCE_TYPE = 'ports' GROUP BY p.STATUS, p.DEVICE_OWNER), ActiveTenantNetworks AS (SELECT n.ID AS network_id, n.NAME AS network_name, n.TENANT_ID AS tenant_id, n.ADMIN_STATE_UP AS admin_state_up, n.MTU AS mtu, sa.UPDATED_AT AS standard_attr_updated_at, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY n.TENANT_ID ORDER BY n.NAME) AS window_column FROM NETWORKS n JOIN STANDARDATTRIBUTES sa ON sa.ID = n.STANDARD_ATTR_ID WHERE n.STATUS = 'ACTIVE'), ActiveTenantPortStatusOwnerStats AS ( SELECT atn.tenant_id, atn.network_id, atn.network_name, atn.admin_state_up, atn.mtu, atn.standard_attr_updated_at, atn.window_column, psos.port_status, psos.device_owner, psos.port_count, psos.earliest_standard_attr_update FROM ActiveTenantNetworks atn JOIN PORTS p ON p.NETWORK_ID = atn.network_id JOIN PortStatusOwnerStats psos ON psos.port_status = p.STATUS AND psos.device_owner = p.DEVICE_OWNER JOIN STANDARDATTRIBUTES sa_p ON sa_p.ID = p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID WHERE sa_p.RESOURCE_TYPE = 'ports' GROUP BY atn.tenant_id, atn.network_id, atn.network_name, atn.admin_state_up, atn.mtu, atn.standard_attr_updated_at, atn.window_column, psos.port_status, psos.device_owner, psos.port_count, psos.earliest_standard_attr_update ) SELECT * FROM ActiveTenantPortStatusOwnerStats ORDER BY tenant_id, window_column, network_id, port_status, device_owner;

question: For IPv4 subnets whose routes have next hop 10.30.19.197/8, list each subnet route’s destination and next hop along with the subnet name and CIDR and the allocation pool’s first and last IP (including a dense rank per subnet), and also show the subnet-level range and variance of allocation pool starting IPs (FIRST_IP) for that subnet; additionally, compute the average FIRST_IP range across these subnets as a benchmark and categorize each subnet as 'HIGH_SPREAD' (at least 50% above average), 'LOW_SPREAD' (at least 50% below average), or 'AVERAGE_SPREAD'. Do not return any rounded answers.
sql: WITH inner_cte AS (WITH FirstIpStatsBySubnet AS ( SELECT s.NAME AS subnet_name, MAX(p.FIRST_IP) - MIN(p.FIRST_IP) AS first_ip_range, VARIANCE(p.FIRST_IP) AS first_ip_variance FROM SUBNETROUTES r JOIN SUBNETS s ON r.SUBNET_ID = s.ID JOIN IPALLOCATIONPOOLS p ON s.ID = p.SUBNET_ID WHERE r.NEXTHOP = '10.30.19.197/8' GROUP BY s.NAME ORDER BY first_ip_range DESC ), SubnetRoutePoolDetails AS ( SELECT r.DESTINATION, r.NEXTHOP, s.NAME AS subnet_name, s.CIDR AS subnet_cidr, p.FIRST_IP, p.LAST_IP, DENSE_RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY r.SUBNET_ID ORDER BY r.SUBNET_ID) AS window_column FROM SUBNETROUTES r JOIN SUBNETS s ON r.SUBNET_ID = s.ID JOIN IPALLOCATIONPOOLS p ON s.ID = p.SUBNET_ID WHERE s.IP_VERSION = 4 ), CombinedSubnetResults AS ( SELECT d.subnet_name, d.subnet_cidr, d.DESTINATION, d.NEXTHOP, d.FIRST_IP, d.LAST_IP, d.window_column, s.first_ip_range, s.first_ip_variance FROM SubnetRoutePoolDetails d JOIN FirstIpStatsBySubnet s ON d.subnet_name = s.subnet_name WHERE d.NEXTHOP = '10.30.19.197/8' ) SELECT * FROM CombinedSubnetResults ORDER BY subnet_name, DESTINATION, FIRST_IP), AvgFirstIpRange AS (SELECT AVG(first_ip_range) AS avg_first_ip_range FROM inner_cte) SELECT i.subnet_name, i.subnet_cidr, i.DESTINATION, i.NEXTHOP, i.FIRST_IP, i.LAST_IP, i.window_column, i.first_ip_range, i.first_ip_variance, a.avg_first_ip_range AS benchmark, CASE WHEN i.first_ip_range > a.avg_first_ip_range * 1.5 THEN 'HIGH_SPREAD' WHEN i.first_ip_range < a.avg_first_ip_range * 0.5 THEN 'LOW_SPREAD' ELSE 'AVERAGE_SPREAD' END AS spread_category FROM inner_cte i CROSS JOIN AvgFirstIpRange a ORDER BY i.subnet_name, i.DESTINATION, i.FIRST_IP;
sub_questions: For each subnet name, calculate the range and variance of the allocation pool starting IP addresses (FIRST_IP) across that subnet’s IP allocation pools, considering only routes whose next hop is 10.30.19.197/8.

Show each subnet route’s destination and next hop together with the subnet name and CIDR, plus the allocation pool’s first and last IP. Also include a dense rank within each subnet (partitioned by subnet ID) ordered by the subnet ID. Only include IPv4 subnets.

For IPv4 subnets whose routes have next hop 10.30.19.197/8, list each subnet route’s destination and next hop along with the subnet name and CIDR and the allocation pool’s first and last IP (including a dense rank per subnet), and also show the subnet-level range and variance of allocation pool starting IPs (FIRST_IP) for that subnet.
sub_sqls: SELECT s.NAME AS subnet_name, MAX(p.FIRST_IP) - MIN(p.FIRST_IP) AS first_ip_range, VARIANCE(p.FIRST_IP) AS first_ip_variance FROM SUBNETROUTES r JOIN SUBNETS s ON r.SUBNET_ID = s.ID JOIN IPALLOCATIONPOOLS p ON s.ID = p.SUBNET_ID WHERE r.NEXTHOP = '10.30.19.197/8' GROUP BY s.NAME ORDER BY first_ip_range DESC;

SELECT r.DESTINATION, r.NEXTHOP, s.NAME AS subnet_name, s.CIDR AS subnet_cidr, p.FIRST_IP, p.LAST_IP, DENSE_RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY r.SUBNET_ID ORDER BY r.SUBNET_ID) AS window_column FROM SUBNETROUTES r JOIN SUBNETS s ON r.SUBNET_ID = s.ID JOIN IPALLOCATIONPOOLS p ON s.ID = p.SUBNET_ID WHERE s.IP_VERSION = 4

WITH FirstIpStatsBySubnet AS ( SELECT s.NAME AS subnet_name, MAX(p.FIRST_IP) - MIN(p.FIRST_IP) AS first_ip_range, VARIANCE(p.FIRST_IP) AS first_ip_variance FROM SUBNETROUTES r JOIN SUBNETS s ON r.SUBNET_ID = s.ID JOIN IPALLOCATIONPOOLS p ON s.ID = p.SUBNET_ID WHERE r.NEXTHOP = '10.30.19.197/8' GROUP BY s.NAME ORDER BY first_ip_range DESC ), SubnetRoutePoolDetails AS ( SELECT r.DESTINATION, r.NEXTHOP, s.NAME AS subnet_name, s.CIDR AS subnet_cidr, p.FIRST_IP, p.LAST_IP, DENSE_RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY r.SUBNET_ID ORDER BY r.SUBNET_ID) AS window_column FROM SUBNETROUTES r JOIN SUBNETS s ON r.SUBNET_ID = s.ID JOIN IPALLOCATIONPOOLS p ON s.ID = p.SUBNET_ID WHERE s.IP_VERSION = 4 ), CombinedSubnetResults AS ( SELECT d.subnet_name, d.subnet_cidr, d.DESTINATION, d.NEXTHOP, d.FIRST_IP, d.LAST_IP, d.window_column, s.first_ip_range, s.first_ip_variance FROM SubnetRoutePoolDetails d JOIN FirstIpStatsBySubnet s ON d.subnet_name = s.subnet_name WHERE d.NEXTHOP = '10.30.19.197/8' ) SELECT * FROM CombinedSubnetResults ORDER BY subnet_name, DESTINATION, FIRST_IP;

question: For each binding host, find the host name and the highest total number of times port security is enabled across any single port on that host—considering only ports that are DOWN but administratively up, and only including ports where port security is enabled at least once. Do not return any rounded answers.
sql: WITH inner_cte AS (WITH DownPortsWithBindings AS (SELECT p.ID AS port_id, p.NAME AS port_name, p.MAC_ADDRESS AS mac_address, b.HOST AS binding_host, b.VIF_TYPE AS vif_type, RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY p.STATUS ORDER BY p.ID) AS window_column FROM PORTS p JOIN ML2_PORT_BINDINGS b ON p.ID = b.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN'), AdminUpPortSecurityStats AS (SELECT p.id AS port_id, p.tenant_id, p.mac_address, COUNT(psb.port_id) AS binding_count, SUM(CASE WHEN psb.port_security_enabled THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS port_security_enabled_total FROM ports p JOIN portsecuritybindings psb ON p.id = psb.port_id WHERE p.admin_state_up = 1 GROUP BY p.id, p.tenant_id, p.mac_address) SELECT d.port_id, d.port_name, d.mac_address, d.binding_host, d.vif_type, d.window_column, a.tenant_id, a.binding_count, a.port_security_enabled_total FROM DownPortsWithBindings d JOIN AdminUpPortSecurityStats a ON d.port_id = a.port_id WHERE a.port_security_enabled_total > 0 ORDER BY a.port_security_enabled_total DESC, d.port_id), HostPortSecurity AS ( SELECT binding_host, port_id, MAX(port_security_enabled_total) AS port_security_enabled_total FROM inner_cte GROUP BY binding_host, port_id ) SELECT binding_host, MAX(port_security_enabled_total) AS max_port_security_enabled_total FROM HostPortSecurity GROUP BY binding_host;
sub_questions: For ports whose status is DOWN, show the port ID, port name, MAC address, the binding host, VIF type, and the rank of each port within its status group ordered by port ID.

For each port that is administratively up, list the port ID, tenant ID, MAC address, the number of port security bindings on that port, and the total number of times port security is enabled across those bindings.

For ports that are DOWN but also administratively up, return the port ID, port name, MAC address, binding host, VIF type, the port’s rank within the DOWN status group (ordered by port ID), the tenant ID, the number of port security bindings on the port, and the total number of times port security is enabled across those bindings—only including ports where port security is enabled at least once.

SELECT p.id AS port_id, p.tenant_id, p.mac_address, COUNT(psb.port_id) AS binding_count, SUM(CASE WHEN psb.port_security_enabled THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS port_security_enabled_total FROM ports p JOIN portsecuritybindings psb ON p.id = psb.port_id WHERE p.admin_state_up = 1 GROUP BY p.id, p.tenant_id, p.mac_address;

WITH DownPortsWithBindings AS (SELECT p.ID AS port_id, p.NAME AS port_name, p.MAC_ADDRESS AS mac_address, b.HOST AS binding_host, b.VIF_TYPE AS vif_type, RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY p.STATUS ORDER BY p.ID) AS window_column FROM PORTS p JOIN ML2_PORT_BINDINGS b ON p.ID = b.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN'), AdminUpPortSecurityStats AS (SELECT p.id AS port_id, p.tenant_id, p.mac_address, COUNT(psb.port_id) AS binding_count, SUM(CASE WHEN psb.port_security_enabled THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS port_security_enabled_total FROM ports p JOIN portsecuritybindings psb ON p.id = psb.port_id WHERE p.admin_state_up = 1 GROUP BY p.id, p.tenant_id, p.mac_address) SELECT d.port_id, d.port_name, d.mac_address, d.binding_host, d.vif_type, d.window_column, a.tenant_id, a.binding_count, a.port_security_enabled_total FROM DownPortsWithBindings d JOIN AdminUpPortSecurityStats a ON d.port_id = a.port_id WHERE a.port_security_enabled_total > 0 ORDER BY a.port_security_enabled_total DESC, d.port_id;

question: For IPv4 subnets that belong to networks with an RBAC action of 'access_as_shared', group results by the RBAC target tenant and DHCP enabled flag, and list the RBAC target tenant, DHCP flag, the number of distinct subnets, and the average of the per-subnet max-to-running-sum ratio (rounded to 2 decimals). Include subtotals per RBAC target tenant and a grand total.
sql: WITH inner_cte AS ( WITH Subq1 AS ( SELECT s.NAME AS subnet_name, s.CIDR AS subnet_cidr, n.TARGET_TENANT AS rbac_target_tenant, SUM(s.STANDARD_ATTR_ID) OVER ( PARTITION BY s.IP_VERSION ORDER BY s.STANDARD_ATTR_ID ) AS window_column FROM SUBNETS AS s JOIN NETWORKRBACS AS n ON n.OBJECT_ID = s.NETWORK_ID WHERE n.ACTION = 'access_as_shared' ), Subq2 AS ( SELECT s.NAME, s.TENANT_ID, s.NETWORK_ID, s.IP_VERSION, s.CIDR, s.GATEWAY_IP, s.ENABLE_DHCP, p.FIRST_IP, p.LAST_IP, MAX(s.STANDARD_ATTR_ID) OVER ( ORDER BY s.ID ROWS BETWEEN CURRENT ROW AND 2 FOLLOWING ) AS max_standard_attr_id_next2 FROM SUBNETS AS s JOIN IPALLOCATIONPOOLS AS p ON s.ID = p.SUBNET_ID WHERE s.IP_VERSION = 4 ) SELECT q2.NAME AS subnet_name, q2.CIDR AS subnet_cidr, q2.TENANT_ID AS subnet_tenant_id, q2.NETWORK_ID AS subnet_network_id, q2.IP_VERSION AS ip_version, q2.GATEWAY_IP AS gateway_ip, q2.ENABLE_DHCP AS enable_dhcp, q2.FIRST_IP AS allocation_pool_first_ip, q2.LAST_IP AS allocation_pool_last_ip, q1.rbac_target_tenant, q1.window_column AS running_sum_standard_attr_id_within_ip_version, q2.max_standard_attr_id_next2, ROUND(q2.max_standard_attr_id_next2 / NULLIF(q1.window_column, 0), 2) AS max_to_running_sum_ratio FROM Subq2 q2 JOIN Subq1 q1 ON q1.subnet_name = q2.NAME AND q1.subnet_cidr = q2.CIDR ORDER BY max_to_running_sum_ratio DESC ) , Agg AS ( SELECT rbac_target_tenant, enable_dhcp, COUNT(DISTINCT subnet_name) AS distinct_subnets, ROUND(AVG(max_to_running_sum_ratio), 2) AS avg_max_to_running_sum_ratio FROM inner_cte GROUP BY rbac_target_tenant, enable_dhcp ) SELECT CASE WHEN GROUPING(rbac_target_tenant) = 1 THEN 'GRAND TOTAL' ELSE rbac_target_tenant END AS rbac_target_tenant, CASE WHEN GROUPING(enable_dhcp) = 1 AND GROUPING(rbac_target_tenant) = 0 THEN 'SUBTOTAL' WHEN GROUPING(enable_dhcp) = 1 AND GROUPING(rbac_target_tenant) = 1 THEN 'ALL' ELSE CAST(enable_dhcp AS CHAR) END AS enable_dhcp, SUM(distinct_subnets) AS distinct_subnets, ROUND(AVG(avg_max_to_running_sum_ratio), 2) AS avg_max_to_running_sum_ratio FROM Agg GROUP BY rbac_target_tenant, enable_dhcp WITH ROLLUP;

For each subnet, show the subnet name, tenant ID, network ID, IP version, CIDR, gateway IP, DHCP enabled flag, the allocation pool’s first IP and last IP, and the maximum subnet standard attribute ID considering the current row and the next 2 rows when ordered by subnet ID.

For IPv4 subnets that belong to networks with an RBAC action of 'access_as_shared', list each subnet’s name and CIDR along with its tenant ID, network ID, gateway IP, DHCP enabled flag, allocation pool first/last IP, the RBAC target tenant, the running sum of subnet standard attribute IDs within the IP version group, the maximum subnet standard attribute ID over the current row and next 2 rows (ordered by subnet ID), and the ratio of that maximum to the running sum (rounded to 2 decimals).
sub_sqls: SELECT s.NAME AS subnet_name, s.CIDR AS subnet_cidr, n.TARGET_TENANT AS rbac_target_tenant, SUM(s.STANDARD_ATTR_ID) OVER ( PARTITION BY s.IP_VERSION ORDER BY s.STANDARD_ATTR_ID ) AS window_column FROM SUBNETS AS s JOIN NETWORKRBACS AS n ON n.OBJECT_ID = s.NETWORK_ID WHERE n.ACTION = 'access_as_shared';

SELECT s.NAME, s.TENANT_ID, s.NETWORK_ID, s.IP_VERSION, s.CIDR, s.GATEWAY_IP, s.ENABLE_DHCP, p.FIRST_IP, p.LAST_IP, MAX(s.STANDARD_ATTR_ID) OVER ( ORDER BY s.ID ROWS BETWEEN CURRENT ROW AND 2 FOLLOWING ) AS max_standard_attr_id_next2 FROM SUBNETS AS s JOIN IPALLOCATIONPOOLS AS p ON s.ID = p.SUBNET_ID WHERE s.IP_VERSION = 4;

WITH Subq1 AS ( SELECT s.NAME AS subnet_name, s.CIDR AS subnet_cidr, n.TARGET_TENANT AS rbac_target_tenant, SUM(s.STANDARD_ATTR_ID) OVER ( PARTITION BY s.IP_VERSION ORDER BY s.STANDARD_ATTR_ID ) AS window_column FROM SUBNETS AS s JOIN NETWORKRBACS AS n ON n.OBJECT_ID = s.NETWORK_ID WHERE n.ACTION = 'access_as_shared' ), Subq2 AS ( SELECT s.NAME, s.TENANT_ID, s.NETWORK_ID, s.IP_VERSION, s.CIDR, s.GATEWAY_IP, s.ENABLE_DHCP, p.FIRST_IP, p.LAST_IP, MAX(s.STANDARD_ATTR_ID) OVER ( ORDER BY s.ID ROWS BETWEEN CURRENT ROW AND 2 FOLLOWING ) AS max_standard_attr_id_next2 FROM SUBNETS AS s JOIN IPALLOCATIONPOOLS AS p ON s.ID = p.SUBNET_ID WHERE s.IP_VERSION = 4 ) SELECT q2.NAME AS subnet_name, q2.CIDR AS subnet_cidr, q2.TENANT_ID AS subnet_tenant_id, q2.NETWORK_ID AS subnet_network_id, q2.IP_VERSION AS ip_version, q2.GATEWAY_IP AS gateway_ip, q2.ENABLE_DHCP AS enable_dhcp, q2.FIRST_IP AS allocation_pool_first_ip, q2.LAST_IP AS allocation_pool_last_ip, q1.rbac_target_tenant, q1.window_column AS running_sum_standard_attr_id_within_ip_version, q2.max_standard_attr_id_next2, ROUND(q2.max_standard_attr_id_next2 / NULLIF(q1.window_column, 0), 2) AS max_to_running_sum_ratio FROM Subq2 q2 JOIN Subq1 q1 ON q1.subnet_name = q2.NAME AND q1.subnet_cidr = q2.CIDR ORDER BY max_to_running_sum_ratio DESC;

question: For ports with status = 'DOWN', return only those ports whose standard attribute ID is greater than the average standard attribute ID among all DOWN ports with the same VIF type. For each such port, list the port ID, tenant ID, host, VIF type, allocated IP address, the row number ordered by IP address using a window frame of 2 preceding rows and 1 following row, the port’s MAC address, and the running sum of standard attribute IDs within each resource type group ordered by standard attribute ID. Do not return any rounded answers.
sql: WITH inner_cte AS ( WITH DownPortBindingsAndIPs AS ( SELECT p.ID AS port_id, p.TENANT_ID AS tenant_id, b.HOST AS host, b.VIF_TYPE AS vif_type, ia.IP_ADDRESS AS ip_address, ROW_NUMBER() OVER ( ORDER BY ia.IP_ADDRESS ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND 1 FOLLOWING ) AS window_column FROM ML2_PORT_BINDINGS b JOIN PORTS p ON b.PORT_ID = p.ID JOIN IPALLOCATIONS ia ON p.ID = ia.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' ), DownPortsMacAndStdAttrRunningSum AS ( SELECT p.ID AS port_id, p.TENANT_ID AS tenant_id, p.MAC_ADDRESS AS mac_address, SUM(sa.ID) OVER ( PARTITION BY sa.RESOURCE_TYPE ORDER BY sa.ID ) AS window_column FROM PORTS p JOIN STANDARDATTRIBUTES sa ON sa.ID = p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' ) SELECT d1.port_id, d1.tenant_id, d1.host, d1.vif_type, d1.ip_address, d1.window_column AS ip_row_number_window, d2.mac_address, d2.window_column AS stdattr_id_running_sum_window FROM DownPortBindingsAndIPs d1 JOIN DownPortsMacAndStdAttrRunningSum d2 ON d1.port_id = d2.port_id AND d1.tenant_id = d2.tenant_id ), VifTypeAverages AS ( SELECT b.VIF_TYPE AS vif_type, AVG(sa.ID) AS avg_stdattr_id FROM PORTS p JOIN ML2_PORT_BINDINGS b ON b.PORT_ID = p.ID JOIN STANDARDATTRIBUTES sa ON sa.ID = p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' GROUP BY b.VIF_TYPE ) SELECT i.port_id, i.tenant_id, i.host, i.vif_type, i.ip_address, i.ip_row_number_window, i.mac_address, i.stdattr_id_running_sum_window FROM inner_cte i JOIN PORTS p ON p.ID = i.port_id JOIN STANDARDATTRIBUTES sa ON sa.ID = p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID WHERE sa.ID > (SELECT v.avg_stdattr_id FROM VifTypeAverages v WHERE v.vif_type = i.vif_type);

For ports whose status is DOWN, show the port ID, tenant ID, and MAC address, along with the running sum of the standard attribute IDs within each resource type group ordered by standard attribute ID.

For ports with status = 'DOWN', list each port’s port ID and tenant ID along with its host, VIF type, allocated IP address, the row number ordered by IP address using a window frame of 2 preceding rows and 1 following row, and also the port’s MAC address plus the running sum of standard attribute IDs within each resource type group ordered by standard attribute ID.

SELECT p.ID AS port_id, p.TENANT_ID AS tenant_id, p.MAC_ADDRESS AS mac_address, SUM(sa.ID) OVER ( PARTITION BY sa.RESOURCE_TYPE ORDER BY sa.ID ) AS window_column FROM PORTS p JOIN STANDARDATTRIBUTES sa ON sa.ID = p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN';

WITH DownPortBindingsAndIPs AS ( SELECT p.ID AS port_id, p.TENANT_ID AS tenant_id, b.HOST AS host, b.VIF_TYPE AS vif_type, ia.IP_ADDRESS AS ip_address, ROW_NUMBER() OVER ( ORDER BY ia.IP_ADDRESS ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND 1 FOLLOWING ) AS window_column FROM ML2_PORT_BINDINGS b JOIN PORTS p ON b.PORT_ID = p.ID JOIN IPALLOCATIONS ia ON p.ID = ia.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' ), DownPortsMacAndStdAttrRunningSum AS ( SELECT p.ID AS port_id, p.TENANT_ID AS tenant_id, p.MAC_ADDRESS AS mac_address, SUM(sa.ID) OVER ( PARTITION BY sa.RESOURCE_TYPE ORDER BY sa.ID ) AS window_column FROM PORTS p JOIN STANDARDATTRIBUTES sa ON sa.ID = p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' ) SELECT d1.port_id, d1.tenant_id, d1.host, d1.vif_type, d1.ip_address, d1.window_column AS ip_row_number_window, d2.mac_address, d2.window_column AS stdattr_id_running_sum_window FROM DownPortBindingsAndIPs d1 JOIN DownPortsMacAndStdAttrRunningSum d2 ON d1.port_id = d2.port_id AND d1.tenant_id = d2.tenant_id;

question: For ACTIVE networks, find those that have an RBAC action of 'access_as_shared' and match them to subnets whose network is also shared to the same RBAC target tenant. Return the network name, status, admin_state_up, RBAC action and target tenant, along with the subnet name and CIDR, the running sum of subnet standard attribute IDs within each IP version group (ordered by standard attribute ID), and the dense rank within each network. Additionally, include the network standard attribute ID and filter to only rows where the subnet running-sum is greater than 50,000. Do not return any rounded answers.
sql: WITH inner_cte AS (WITH SharedSubnets AS ( SELECT s.NAME AS subnet_name, s.CIDR AS subnet_cidr, n.TARGET_TENANT AS rbac_target_tenant, SUM(s.STANDARD_ATTR_ID) OVER ( PARTITION BY s.IP_VERSION ORDER BY s.STANDARD_ATTR_ID ) AS window_column FROM SUBNETS AS s JOIN NETWORKRBACS AS n ON n.OBJECT_ID = s.NETWORK_ID WHERE n.ACTION = 'access_as_shared' ), ActiveNetworkRBACs AS ( SELECT n.name, n.status, n.admin_state_up, r.action, r.target_tenant, DENSE_RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY n.id ORDER BY n.id) AS window_column FROM networksecuritybindings b JOIN networks n ON b.network_id = n.id JOIN networkrbacs r ON n.id = r.object_id WHERE n.status = 'ACTIVE' ) SELECT anr.name AS network_name, anr.status AS network_status, anr.admin_state_up, anr.action AS rbac_action, anr.target_tenant AS rbac_target_tenant, ss.subnet_name, ss.subnet_cidr, ss.window_column AS subnet_std_attr_running_sum_by_ip_version, anr.window_column AS network_dense_rank_within_network FROM ActiveNetworkRBACs anr JOIN SharedSubnets ss ON ss.rbac_target_tenant = anr.target_tenant AND anr.action = 'access_as_shared' ORDER BY anr.name, ss.subnet_name) SELECT i.network_name, i.network_status, i.admin_state_up, i.rbac_action, i.rbac_target_tenant, i.subnet_name, i.subnet_cidr, i.subnet_std_attr_running_sum_by_ip_version, i.network_dense_rank_within_network, n.standard_attr_id AS network_standard_attr_id FROM inner_cte i JOIN networks n ON n.name = i.network_name WHERE i.subnet_std_attr_running_sum_by_ip_version > 50000 ORDER BY i.network_name, i.subnet_name;

WITH SharedSubnets AS ( SELECT s.NAME AS subnet_name, s.CIDR AS subnet_cidr, n.TARGET_TENANT AS rbac_target_tenant, SUM(s.STANDARD_ATTR_ID) OVER ( PARTITION BY s.IP_VERSION ORDER BY s.STANDARD_ATTR_ID ) AS window_column FROM SUBNETS AS s JOIN NETWORKRBACS AS n ON n.OBJECT_ID = s.NETWORK_ID WHERE n.ACTION = 'access_as_shared' ), ActiveNetworkRBACs AS ( SELECT n.name, n.status, n.admin_state_up, r.action, r.target_tenant, DENSE_RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY n.id ORDER BY n.id) AS window_column FROM networksecuritybindings b JOIN networks n ON b.network_id = n.id JOIN networkrbacs r ON n.id = r.object_id WHERE n.status = 'ACTIVE' ) SELECT anr.name AS network_name, anr.status AS network_status, anr.admin_state_up, anr.action AS rbac_action, anr.target_tenant AS rbac_target_tenant, ss.subnet_name, ss.subnet_cidr, ss.window_column AS subnet_std_attr_running_sum_by_ip_version, anr.window_column AS network_dense_rank_within_network FROM ActiveNetworkRBACs anr JOIN SharedSubnets ss ON ss.rbac_target_tenant = anr.target_tenant AND anr.action = 'access_as_shared' ORDER BY anr.name, ss.subnet_name;

question: Return the same combined list as before (default external networks plus port-count summary rows), and for every row also show the deviation of its metric_value from the overall average metric_value across the entire combined result set. Do not return any rounded answers.
sql: WITH inner_cte AS (WITH PortStatusOwnerStats AS ( SELECT p.STATUS AS port_status, p.DEVICE_OWNER AS device_owner, COUNT(p.ID) AS port_count, MIN(sa.UPDATED_AT) AS earliest_standard_attr_update FROM PORTS p JOIN STANDARDATTRIBUTES sa ON sa.ID = p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID WHERE sa.RESOURCE_TYPE = 'ports' GROUP BY p.STATUS, p.DEVICE_OWNER ), DefaultExternalNetworks AS ( SELECT e.NETWORK_ID, n.NAME, n.STATUS, n.ADMIN_STATE_UP, AVG(n.ADMIN_STATE_UP) OVER (PARTITION BY n.STATUS ORDER BY n.NAME) AS window_column FROM EXTERNALNETWORKS e JOIN NETWORKS n ON e.NETWORK_ID = n.ID WHERE e.IS_DEFAULT = 0 ), CombinedResults AS ( SELECT den.NETWORK_ID AS entity_id, den.NAME AS entity_name, den.STATUS AS status, den.ADMIN_STATE_UP AS admin_state_up, den.window_column AS metric_value, 'Default External Network' AS record_type FROM DefaultExternalNetworks den UNION ALL SELECT NULL AS entity_id, NULL AS entity_name, psos.port_status AS status, NULL AS admin_state_up, psos.port_count AS metric_value, 'Port Count by Status/Owner (ports resource_type)' AS record_type FROM PortStatusOwnerStats psos ) SELECT record_type, entity_id, entity_name, status, admin_state_up, metric_value FROM CombinedResults ORDER BY record_type, status, entity_name, entity_id), avg_metrics AS ( SELECT AVG(metric_value) AS avg_metric_value FROM inner_cte ) SELECT i.record_type, i.entity_id, i.entity_name, i.status, i.admin_state_up, i.metric_value, (i.metric_value - a.avg_metric_value) AS deviation_from_overall_avg_metric_value FROM inner_cte i CROSS JOIN avg_metrics a ORDER BY i.record_type, i.status, i.entity_name, i.entity_id;
sub_questions: For each port status and device owner, considering only ports whose standard attribute resource type is 'ports', return the number of ports and the earliest (minimum) standard attribute updated timestamp.

For external networks that are marked as default (is_default = 0), list the network ID, the network name, status, admin_state_up flag, and the average admin_state_up within each status group ordered by network name.

Return a single combined list that (1) shows each external network with IS_DEFAULT = 0 including its network id, name, status, admin_state_up, and the status-partitioned running average of admin_state_up ordered by network name, and (2) appends port summary rows for STANDARDATTRIBUTES.RESOURCE_TYPE = 'ports' giving the port status and the corresponding port count (grouped by port status and device owner), with all rows labeled by a record type and ordered by record type, status, and network name/id.

i.allowed_ip_address) AS distinct_allowed_ip_count, SUM(COALESCE(i.port_security_enabled_total, 0)) AS port_security_enabled_total FROM inner_cte i JOIN PortAdminStatus pas ON pas.port_id = i.port_id question: For the RBAC action access_as_shared, show the action together with (1) the variance of subnet IP version (IPv4 vs IPv6) across subnets on the referenced networks, and (2) the overall average, range (max minus min), and variance of subnet IP version (considering only subnets with IP version 4 or 6) for networks referenced by RBAC entries with that same action; additionally, include whether any of those referenced networks have at least one IPv6 subnet (Yes/No). Do not return any rounded answers.
sql: WITH inner_cte AS (WITH RbacSharedIpVersionVariance AS (SELECT n.ACTION, VARIANCE(s.IP_VERSION) AS ip_version_variance FROM NETWORKRBACS AS n JOIN SUBNETS AS s ON n.OBJECT_ID = s.NETWORK_ID WHERE n.ACTION = 'access_as_shared' GROUP BY n.ACTION ORDER BY ip_version_variance DESC), RbacIpVersionStats AS (SELECT n.ACTION AS rbac_action, AVG(s.IP_VERSION) AS avg_ip_version, MAX(s.IP_VERSION) - MIN(s.IP_VERSION) AS ip_version_range, VARIANCE(s.IP_VERSION) AS ip_version_variance FROM NETWORKRBACS AS n JOIN SUBNETS AS s ON n.OBJECT_ID = s.NETWORK_ID WHERE s.IP_VERSION IN (4, 6) GROUP BY n.ACTION ORDER BY ip_version_range DESC) SELECT rs.ACTION AS rbac_action, rs.ip_version_variance AS shared_action_ip_version_variance, ris.avg_ip_version, ris.ip_version_range, ris.ip_version_variance AS overall_ip_version_variance FROM RbacSharedIpVersionVariance rs JOIN RbacIpVersionStats ris ON rs.ACTION = ris.rbac_action ORDER BY rs.ip_version_variance DESC) SELECT i.rbac_action, i.shared_action_ip_version_variance, i.avg_ip_version, i.ip_version_range, i.overall_ip_version_variance, CASE WHEN COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN s2.IP_VERSION = 6 THEN s2.ID END) > 0 THEN 'Yes' ELSE 'No' END AS has_any_ipv6_subnet_on_referenced_networks FROM inner_cte i JOIN NETWORKRBACS n2 ON n2.ACTION = i.rbac_action JOIN SUBNETS s2 ON s2.NETWORK_ID = n2.OBJECT_ID GROUP BY i.rbac_action, i.shared_action_ip_version_variance, i.avg_ip_version, i.ip_version_range, i.overall_ip_version_variance ORDER BY i.shared_action_ip_version_variance DESC;

question: For ports that are DOWN, list the port name, network ID, MAC address, admin state, status, device owner, the bound security group ID, and the minimum admin_state_up value in a window of 3 preceding and 1 following row ordered by port ID, along with (for the DOWN status) the coefficient of variation (using STDDEV only and never STDDEV_POP) (standard deviation (using STDDEV only and never STDDEV_POP) divided by average) of the length of allocated IP address strings for ports that have port security enabled; additionally, for each returned DOWN port, include the number of allocated IP addresses on that port and the deviation of that count from the average allocated-IP count across all DOWN ports in the result. Do not return any rounded answers.
sql: WITH inner_cte AS (WITH PortStatusIPLenCV AS (SELECT p.status, STDDEV(LENGTH(ia.ip_address)) / NULLIF(AVG(LENGTH(ia.ip_address)), 0) AS coefficient_of_variation FROM portsecuritybindings psb JOIN ports p ON psb.port_id = p.id JOIN ipallocations ia ON p.id = ia.port_id WHERE psb.port_security_enabled = 1 GROUP BY p.status HAVING AVG(LENGTH(ia.ip_address)) > 0 ORDER BY coefficient_of_variation DESC), DownPortsWithSecurityGroup AS (SELECT p.NAME, p.NETWORK_ID, p.MAC_ADDRESS, p.ADMIN_STATE_UP, p.STATUS, p.DEVICE_OWNER, s.SECURITY_GROUP_ID, MIN(p.ADMIN_STATE_UP) OVER ( ORDER BY p.ID ROWS BETWEEN 3 PRECEDING AND 1 FOLLOWING ) AS window_column FROM PORTS AS p JOIN SECURITYGROUPPORTBINDINGS AS s ON p.ID = s.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN') SELECT d.NAME, d.NETWORK_ID, d.MAC_ADDRESS, d.ADMIN_STATE_UP, d.STATUS, d.DEVICE_OWNER, d.SECURITY_GROUP_ID, d.window_column, cv.coefficient_of_variation AS status_ip_length_coefficient_of_variation FROM DownPortsWithSecurityGroup d JOIN PortStatusIPLenCV cv ON d.STATUS = cv.status ORDER BY cv.coefficient_of_variation DESC, d.NAME), DownPortIpCounts AS ( SELECT p.id AS port_id, COUNT(DISTINCT ia.ip_address) AS allocated_ip_count FROM ports p JOIN inner_cte i ON p.name = i.name AND p.network_id = i.network_id AND p.mac_address = i.mac_address AND p.admin_state_up = i.admin_state_up AND p.status = i.status AND p.device_owner = i.device_owner LEFT JOIN ipallocations ia ON ia.port_id = p.id GROUP BY p.id ), AvgDownPortIpCounts AS ( SELECT AVG(allocated_ip_count) AS avg_allocated_ip_count FROM DownPortIpCounts ) SELECT i.NAME, i.NETWORK_ID, i.MAC_ADDRESS, i.ADMIN_STATE_UP, i.STATUS, i.DEVICE_OWNER, i.SECURITY_GROUP_ID, i.window_column, i.status_ip_length_coefficient_of_variation, dpc.allocated_ip_count, (dpc.allocated_ip_count - adpc.avg_allocated_ip_count) AS deviation_from_avg_allocated_ip_count FROM inner_cte i JOIN ports p ON p.name = i.name AND p.network_id = i.network_id AND p.mac_address = i.mac_address AND p.admin_state_up = i.admin_state_up AND p.status = i.status AND p.device_owner = i.device_owner JOIN DownPortIpCounts dpc ON dpc.port_id = p.id CROSS JOIN AvgDownPortIpCounts adpc ORDER BY i.status_ip_length_coefficient_of_variation DESC, i.NAME;

question: Using the per-port details for administratively up ports that have at least one IP allocation (port ID, tenant ID, MAC address, port name, port security enabled status, the window row number ordered by MAC address with a frame of 2 preceding rows and 1 following row, the number of IP allocations, and the number of rows with a non-null subnet ID), compute the average IP allocation count across all returned ports as a benchmark and classify each port as 'HIGH_IP_ALLOC' (at least 50% more than average), 'LOW_IP_ALLOC' (at least 50% less than average), or 'AVERAGE_IP_ALLOC'. Return all original columns plus the benchmark and category. Do not return any rounded answers.
sql: WITH inner_cte AS (WITH PortIpAllocSummary AS (SELECT p.id AS port_id, p.tenant_id, p.mac_address, COUNT(ia.ip_address) AS ip_allocation_count, SUM(CASE WHEN ia.subnet_id IS NOT NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS subnet_id_rows FROM ports p JOIN portsecuritybindings psb ON psb.port_id = p.id JOIN ipallocations ia ON ia.port_id = p.id WHERE p.admin_state_up = 1 AND ia.ip_address IS NOT NULL GROUP BY p.id, p.tenant_id, p.mac_address), PortSecurityWindow AS (SELECT p.NAME AS port_name, p.MAC_ADDRESS AS mac_address, psb.PORT_SECURITY_ENABLED AS port_security_enabled, ROW_NUMBER() OVER ( ORDER BY p.MAC_ADDRESS ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND 1 FOLLOWING ) AS window_column FROM PORTS AS p JOIN PORTSECURITYBINDINGS AS psb ON p.ID = psb.PORT_ID WHERE p.ADMIN_STATE_UP = 1), CombinedPortDetails AS ( SELECT s.port_id, s.tenant_id, s.mac_address, w.port_name, w.port_security_enabled, w.window_column, s.ip_allocation_count, s.subnet_id_rows FROM PortIpAllocSummary s JOIN PortSecurityWindow w ON w.mac_address = s.mac_address ) SELECT * FROM CombinedPortDetails ORDER BY tenant_id, mac_address, port_id), AvgIpAlloc AS (SELECT AVG(ip_allocation_count) AS avg_ip_allocation_count FROM inner_cte) SELECT i.port_id, i.tenant_id, i.mac_address, i.port_name, i.port_security_enabled, i.window_column, i.ip_allocation_count, i.subnet_id_rows, a.avg_ip_allocation_count AS benchmark, CASE WHEN i.ip_allocation_count > a.avg_ip_allocation_count * 1.5 THEN 'HIGH_IP_ALLOC' WHEN i.ip_allocation_count < a.avg_ip_allocation_count * 0.5 THEN 'LOW_IP_ALLOC' ELSE 'AVERAGE_IP_ALLOC' END AS ip_alloc_category FROM inner_cte i CROSS JOIN AvgIpAlloc a ORDER BY i.tenant_id, i.mac_address, i.port_id;

question: For each IPv4 subnet that has at least one DNS nameserver entry, show the subnet name, tenant ID, network ID, IP version, CIDR, gateway IP, DHCP enabled flag, allocation pool first IP and last IP, the maximum subnet standard attribute ID over the current subnet and the next 2 subnets by subnet ID, and also (per network) the maximum pool-count range across subnet names in that network, ordered by that network-level maximum range descending. Do not return any rounded answers.
sql: WITH inner_cte AS ( WITH SubnetPoolStatsByName AS ( SELECT s.name AS subnet_name, MAX(pool_count) - MIN(pool_count) AS pool_count_range, VARIANCE(pool_count) AS pool_count_variance, STDDEV(pool_count) AS pool_count_stddev FROM subnets AS s JOIN dnsnameservers AS d ON d.subnet_id = s.id JOIN ( SELECT s2.id AS subnet_id, COUNT(*) AS pool_count FROM subnets AS s2 JOIN ipallocationpools AS p ON p.subnet_id = s2.id GROUP BY s2.id, p.id ) AS pool_stats ON pool_stats.subnet_id = s.id GROUP BY s.name ORDER BY pool_count_range DESC ), SubnetDetailsWithWindowMax AS ( SELECT s.NAME, s.TENANT_ID, s.NETWORK_ID, s.IP_VERSION, s.CIDR, s.GATEWAY_IP, s.ENABLE_DHCP, p.FIRST_IP, p.LAST_IP, MAX(s.STANDARD_ATTR_ID) OVER ( ORDER BY s.ID ROWS BETWEEN CURRENT ROW AND 2 FOLLOWING ) AS max_standard_attr_id_next2 FROM SUBNETS AS s JOIN IPALLOCATIONPOOLS AS p ON s.ID = p.SUBNET_ID WHERE s.IP_VERSION = 4 ), DnsSubnetNames AS ( SELECT DISTINCT s.name AS subnet_name FROM subnets s JOIN dnsnameservers d ON d.subnet_id = s.id ) SELECT sd.NAME AS subnet_name, sd.TENANT_ID, sd.NETWORK_ID, sd.IP_VERSION, sd.CIDR, sd.GATEWAY_IP, sd.ENABLE_DHCP, sd.FIRST_IP, sd.LAST_IP, sd.max_standard_attr_id_next2, sp.pool_count_range, sp.pool_count_variance, sp.pool_count_stddev FROM SubnetDetailsWithWindowMax sd JOIN SubnetPoolStatsByName sp ON sd.NAME = sp.subnet_name JOIN DnsSubnetNames dn ON sd.NAME = dn.subnet_name ORDER BY sp.pool_count_range DESC, sd.NAME ), NetworkMaxPoolRange AS ( SELECT s.network_id, MAX(ic.pool_count_range) AS max_pool_count_range_in_network FROM inner_cte ic JOIN subnets s ON s.name = ic.subnet_name GROUP BY s.network_id ) SELECT ic.subnet_name, ic.tenant_id, ic.network_id, ic.ip_version, ic.cidr, ic.gateway_ip, ic.enable_dhcp, ic.first_ip, ic.last_ip, ic.max_standard_attr_id_next2, ic.pool_count_range, ic.pool_count_variance, ic.pool_count_stddev, nmr.max_pool_count_range_in_network FROM inner_cte ic JOIN NetworkMaxPoolRange nmr ON nmr.network_id = ic.network_id ORDER BY nmr.max_pool_count_range_in_network DESC, ic.pool_count_range DESC, ic.subnet_name;

For each subnet, show the subnet name, tenant ID, network ID, IP version, CIDR, gateway IP, DHCP enabled flag, the allocation pool’s first IP and last IP, and the maximum subnet standard attribute ID considering the current row and the next 2 rows when ordered by subnet ID.

For each IPv4 subnet that has at least one DNS nameserver entry, show the subnet name, tenant ID, network ID, IP version, CIDR, gateway IP, DHCP enabled flag, allocation pool first IP and last IP, the maximum subnet standard attribute ID over the current subnet and the next 2 subnets by subnet ID, and also the range, variance, and standard deviation of the number of IP allocation pools per subnet (grouped by subnet name), ordered by the pool-count range descending.
sub_sqls: SELECT s.name AS subnet_name, MAX(pool_count) - MIN(pool_count) AS pool_count_range, VARIANCE(pool_count) AS pool_count_variance, STDDEV(pool_count) AS pool_count_stddev FROM subnets AS s JOIN dnsnameservers AS d ON d.subnet_id = s.id JOIN ( SELECT s2.id AS subnet_id, COUNT(*) AS pool_count FROM subnets AS s2 JOIN ipallocationpools AS p ON p.subnet_id = s2.id GROUP BY s2.id, p.id ) AS pool_stats ON pool_stats.subnet_id = s.id GROUP BY s.name ORDER BY pool_count_range DESC;

SELECT s.NAME, s.TENANT_ID, s.NETWORK_ID, s.IP_VERSION, s.CIDR, s.GATEWAY_IP, s.ENABLE_DHCP, p.FIRST_IP, p.LAST_IP, MAX(s.STANDARD_ATTR_ID) OVER ( ORDER BY s.ID ROWS BETWEEN CURRENT ROW AND 2 FOLLOWING ) AS max_standard_attr_id_next2 FROM SUBNETS AS s JOIN IPALLOCATIONPOOLS AS p ON s.ID = p.SUBNET_ID WHERE s.IP_VERSION = 4;

WITH SubnetPoolStatsByName AS ( SELECT s.name AS subnet_name, MAX(pool_count) - MIN(pool_count) AS pool_count_range, VARIANCE(pool_count) AS pool_count_variance, STDDEV(pool_count) AS pool_count_stddev FROM subnets AS s JOIN dnsnameservers AS d ON d.subnet_id = s.id JOIN ( SELECT s2.id AS subnet_id, COUNT(*) AS pool_count FROM subnets AS s2 JOIN ipallocationpools AS p ON p.subnet_id = s2.id GROUP BY s2.id, p.id ) AS pool_stats ON pool_stats.subnet_id = s.id GROUP BY s.name ORDER BY pool_count_range DESC ), SubnetDetailsWithWindowMax AS ( SELECT s.NAME, s.TENANT_ID, s.NETWORK_ID, s.IP_VERSION, s.CIDR, s.GATEWAY_IP, s.ENABLE_DHCP, p.FIRST_IP, p.LAST_IP, MAX(s.STANDARD_ATTR_ID) OVER ( ORDER BY s.ID ROWS BETWEEN CURRENT ROW AND 2 FOLLOWING ) AS max_standard_attr_id_next2 FROM SUBNETS AS s JOIN IPALLOCATIONPOOLS AS p ON s.ID = p.SUBNET_ID WHERE s.IP_VERSION = 4 ), DnsSubnetNames AS ( SELECT DISTINCT s.name AS subnet_name FROM subnets s JOIN dnsnameservers d ON d.subnet_id = s.id ) SELECT sd.NAME AS subnet_name, sd.TENANT_ID, sd.NETWORK_ID, sd.IP_VERSION, sd.CIDR, sd.GATEWAY_IP, sd.ENABLE_DHCP, sd.FIRST_IP, sd.LAST_IP, sd.max_standard_attr_id_next2, sp.pool_count_range, sp.pool_count_variance, sp.pool_count_stddev FROM SubnetDetailsWithWindowMax sd JOIN SubnetPoolStatsByName sp ON sd.NAME = sp.subnet_name JOIN DnsSubnetNames dn ON sd.NAME = dn.subnet_name ORDER BY sp.pool_count_range DESC, sd.NAME;

question: For IPv4 subnets that belong to networks with an RBAC action of 'access_as_shared', return only those subnets whose max-to-running-sum ratio (maximum subnet standard attribute ID over the current row and next 2 rows, divided by the running sum of subnet standard attribute IDs within the IP version group, rounded to 2 decimals) is greater than the average of that same ratio across all such subnets; list the subnet’s name and CIDR along with its tenant ID, network ID, gateway IP, DHCP enabled flag, allocation pool first/last IP, the RBAC target tenant, the running sum, the max-over-next-2 value, and the ratio.
sql: WITH inner_cte AS ( WITH Subq1 AS ( SELECT s.NAME AS subnet_name, s.CIDR AS subnet_cidr, n.TARGET_TENANT AS rbac_target_tenant, SUM(s.STANDARD_ATTR_ID) OVER ( PARTITION BY s.IP_VERSION ORDER BY s.STANDARD_ATTR_ID ) AS window_column FROM SUBNETS AS s JOIN NETWORKRBACS AS n ON n.OBJECT_ID = s.NETWORK_ID WHERE n.ACTION = 'access_as_shared' ), Subq2 AS ( SELECT s.NAME, s.TENANT_ID, s.NETWORK_ID, s.IP_VERSION, s.CIDR, s.GATEWAY_IP, s.ENABLE_DHCP, p.FIRST_IP, p.LAST_IP, MAX(s.STANDARD_ATTR_ID) OVER ( ORDER BY s.ID ROWS BETWEEN CURRENT ROW AND 2 FOLLOWING ) AS max_standard_attr_id_next2 FROM SUBNETS AS s JOIN IPALLOCATIONPOOLS AS p ON s.ID = p.SUBNET_ID WHERE s.IP_VERSION = 4 ) SELECT q2.NAME AS subnet_name, q2.CIDR AS subnet_cidr, q2.TENANT_ID AS subnet_tenant_id, q2.NETWORK_ID AS subnet_network_id, q2.IP_VERSION AS ip_version, q2.GATEWAY_IP AS gateway_ip, q2.ENABLE_DHCP AS enable_dhcp, q2.FIRST_IP AS allocation_pool_first_ip, q2.LAST_IP AS allocation_pool_last_ip, q1.rbac_target_tenant, q1.window_column AS running_sum_standard_attr_id_within_ip_version, q2.max_standard_attr_id_next2, ROUND(q2.max_standard_attr_id_next2 / NULLIF(q1.window_column, 0), 2) AS max_to_running_sum_ratio FROM Subq2 q2 JOIN Subq1 q1 ON q1.subnet_name = q2.NAME AND q1.subnet_cidr = q2.CIDR ORDER BY max_to_running_sum_ratio DESC ) SELECT subnet_name, subnet_cidr, subnet_tenant_id, subnet_network_id, ip_version, gateway_ip, enable_dhcp, allocation_pool_first_ip, allocation_pool_last_ip, rbac_target_tenant, running_sum_standard_attr_id_within_ip_version, max_standard_attr_id_next2, max_to_running_sum_ratio FROM inner_cte WHERE max_to_running_sum_ratio > (SELECT AVG(max_to_running_sum_ratio) FROM inner_cte) ORDER BY max_to_running_sum_ratio DESC;

For IPv4 subnets that belong to networks with an RBAC action of 'access_as_shared', list each subnet’s name and CIDR along with its tenant ID, network ID, gateway IP, DHCP enabled flag, allocation pool first/last IP, the RBAC target tenant, the running sum of subnet standard attribute IDs within the IP version group, the maximum subnet standard attribute ID over the current row and next 2 rows (ordered by subnet ID), and the ratio of that maximum to the running sum (rounded to 2 decimals).

SELECT s.NAME, s.TENANT_ID, s.NETWORK_ID, s.IP_VERSION, s.CIDR, s.GATEWAY_IP, s.ENABLE_DHCP, p.FIRST_IP, p.LAST_IP, MAX(s.STANDARD_ATTR_ID) OVER ( ORDER BY s.ID ROWS BETWEEN CURRENT ROW AND 2 FOLLOWING ) AS max_standard_attr_id_next2 FROM SUBNETS AS s JOIN IPALLOCATIONPOOLS AS p ON s.ID = p.SUBNET_ID WHERE s.IP_VERSION = 4;

WITH Subq1 AS ( SELECT s.NAME AS subnet_name, s.CIDR AS subnet_cidr, n.TARGET_TENANT AS rbac_target_tenant, SUM(s.STANDARD_ATTR_ID) OVER ( PARTITION BY s.IP_VERSION ORDER BY s.STANDARD_ATTR_ID ) AS window_column FROM SUBNETS AS s JOIN NETWORKRBACS AS n ON n.OBJECT_ID = s.NETWORK_ID WHERE n.ACTION = 'access_as_shared' ), Subq2 AS ( SELECT s.NAME, s.TENANT_ID, s.NETWORK_ID, s.IP_VERSION, s.CIDR, s.GATEWAY_IP, s.ENABLE_DHCP, p.FIRST_IP, p.LAST_IP, MAX(s.STANDARD_ATTR_ID) OVER ( ORDER BY s.ID ROWS BETWEEN CURRENT ROW AND 2 FOLLOWING ) AS max_standard_attr_id_next2 FROM SUBNETS AS s JOIN IPALLOCATIONPOOLS AS p ON s.ID = p.SUBNET_ID WHERE s.IP_VERSION = 4 ) SELECT q2.NAME AS subnet_name, q2.CIDR AS subnet_cidr, q2.TENANT_ID AS subnet_tenant_id, q2.NETWORK_ID AS subnet_network_id, q2.IP_VERSION AS ip_version, q2.GATEWAY_IP AS gateway_ip, q2.ENABLE_DHCP AS enable_dhcp, q2.FIRST_IP AS allocation_pool_first_ip, q2.LAST_IP AS allocation_pool_last_ip, q1.rbac_target_tenant, q1.window_column AS running_sum_standard_attr_id_within_ip_version, q2.max_standard_attr_id_next2, ROUND(q2.max_standard_attr_id_next2 / NULLIF(q1.window_column, 0), 2) AS max_to_running_sum_ratio FROM Subq2 q2 JOIN Subq1 q1 ON q1.subnet_name = q2.NAME AND q1.subnet_cidr = q2.CIDR ORDER BY max_to_running_sum_ratio DESC;

question: For IPv4 subnets that have both subnet routes and DNS nameservers with a positive average nameserver order, show the route-count range, variance, and standard deviation (using STDDEV only and never STDDEV_POP) (based on routes per next hop) and the coefficient of variation (using STDDEV only and never STDDEV_POP) of DNS nameserver order values, and also include subtotals and a grand total across all qualifying subnets, ordered by the route-count range descending. Do not return any rounded answers.
sql: WITH inner_cte AS ( WITH q1 AS ( SELECT s.NAME AS subnet_name, MAX(route_count) - MIN(route_count) AS route_count_range, VARIANCE(route_count) AS route_count_variance, STDDEV(route_count) AS route_count_stddev FROM SUBNETS AS s JOIN ( SELECT sr.SUBNET_ID, COUNT(*) AS route_count FROM SUBNETROUTES AS sr GROUP BY sr.SUBNET_ID, sr.NEXTHOP ) AS route_stats ON s.ID = route_stats.SUBNET_ID WHERE s.IP_VERSION = 4 GROUP BY s.NAME ORDER BY route_count_range DESC ), q2 AS ( SELECT s.name AS subnet_name, STDDEV(d.ORDER) / NULLIF(AVG(d.ORDER), 0) AS coefficient_of_variation FROM subnets AS s JOIN dnsnameservers AS d ON d.subnet_id = s.id JOIN ipallocationpools AS p ON p.subnet_id = s.id WHERE s.ip_version = 4 GROUP BY s.name HAVING AVG(d.ORDER) > 0 ORDER BY coefficient_of_variation DESC ) SELECT q1.subnet_name, q1.route_count_range, q1.route_count_variance, q1.route_count_stddev, q2.coefficient_of_variation FROM q1 JOIN q2 ON q1.subnet_name = q2.subnet_name ORDER BY q1.route_count_range DESC ) SELECT CASE WHEN GROUPING(inner_cte.subnet_name) = 1 THEN 'GRAND TOTAL' ELSE inner_cte.subnet_name END AS subnet_name, SUM(inner_cte.route_count_range) AS route_count_range, AVG(inner_cte.route_count_variance) AS route_count_variance, AVG(inner_cte.route_count_stddev) AS route_count_stddev, AVG(inner_cte.coefficient_of_variation) AS coefficient_of_variation FROM inner_cte GROUP BY inner_cte.subnet_name WITH ROLLUP ORDER BY CASE WHEN GROUPING(inner_cte.subnet_name) = 1 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END, route_count_range DESC;

WITH q1 AS ( SELECT s.NAME AS subnet_name, MAX(route_count) - MIN(route_count) AS route_count_range, VARIANCE(route_count) AS route_count_variance, STDDEV(route_count) AS route_count_stddev FROM SUBNETS AS s JOIN ( SELECT sr.SUBNET_ID, COUNT(*) AS route_count FROM SUBNETROUTES AS sr GROUP BY sr.SUBNET_ID, sr.NEXTHOP ) AS route_stats ON s.ID = route_stats.SUBNET_ID WHERE s.IP_VERSION = 4 GROUP BY s.NAME ORDER BY route_count_range DESC ), q2 AS ( SELECT s.name AS subnet_name, STDDEV(d.ORDER) / NULLIF(AVG(d.ORDER), 0) AS coefficient_of_variation FROM subnets AS s JOIN dnsnameservers AS d ON d.subnet_id = s.id JOIN ipallocationpools AS p ON p.subnet_id = s.id WHERE s.ip_version = 4 GROUP BY s.name HAVING AVG(d.ORDER) > 0 ORDER BY coefficient_of_variation DESC ) SELECT q1.subnet_name, q1.route_count_range, q1.route_count_variance, q1.route_count_stddev, q2.coefficient_of_variation FROM q1 JOIN q2 ON q1.subnet_name = q2.subnet_name ORDER BY q1.route_count_range DESC;

question: Using the DOWN-port details query as an inner CTE, list the top 10 tenants with the most DOWN ports. For each of these tenants, show the tenant ID, total number of DOWN ports, and whether any of their DOWN ports have an ML2 port binding with VIF type 'ovs'. Do not return any rounded answers.
sql: WITH inner_cte AS ( WITH DownPortStandardAttrWindow AS ( SELECT p.ID AS port_id, p.TENANT_ID AS tenant_id, p.MAC_ADDRESS AS mac_address, SUM(sa.ID) OVER ( PARTITION BY sa.RESOURCE_TYPE ORDER BY sa.ID ) AS window_column FROM PORTS p JOIN STANDARDATTRIBUTES sa ON sa.ID = p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' ), DownPortBindingRank AS ( SELECT p.ID AS port_id, p.NAME AS port_name, p.MAC_ADDRESS AS mac_address, b.HOST AS binding_host, b.VIF_TYPE AS vif_type, RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY p.STATUS ORDER BY p.ID) AS window_column FROM PORTS p JOIN ML2_PORT_BINDINGS b ON p.ID = b.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' ) SELECT dpsaw.port_id, dpsaw.tenant_id, dpbr.port_name, dpsaw.mac_address, dpbr.binding_host, dpbr.vif_type, dpsaw.window_column AS standard_attr_id_running_sum_within_resource_type, dpbr.window_column AS port_rank_within_down_status FROM DownPortStandardAttrWindow dpsaw JOIN DownPortBindingRank dpbr ON dpsaw.port_id = dpbr.port_id AND dpsaw.mac_address = dpbr.mac_address ORDER BY dpsaw.port_id ) SELECT i.tenant_id, COUNT(DISTINCT i.port_id) AS total_down_ports, CASE WHEN SUM(CASE WHEN i.vif_type = 'ovs' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) > 0 THEN 'Yes' ELSE 'No' END AS has_ovs_vif_type_on_any_down_port FROM inner_cte i GROUP BY i.tenant_id ORDER BY total_down_ports DESC LIMIT 10;

For ports whose status is DOWN, show the port ID, port name, MAC address, the binding host, VIF type, and the rank of each port within its status group ordered by port ID.

For ports whose status is DOWN, show each port’s ID, tenant ID, port name, MAC address, binding host, and VIF type, along with (1) the running sum of standard attribute IDs within each standard attribute resource type group ordered by standard attribute ID and (2) the port’s rank within the DOWN status group ordered by port ID.

SELECT p.ID AS port_id, p.NAME AS port_name, p.MAC_ADDRESS AS mac_address, b.HOST AS binding_host, b.VIF_TYPE AS vif_type, RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY p.STATUS ORDER BY p.ID) AS window_column FROM PORTS p JOIN ML2_PORT_BINDINGS b ON p.ID = b.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN';

WITH DownPortStandardAttrWindow AS ( SELECT p.ID AS port_id, p.TENANT_ID AS tenant_id, p.MAC_ADDRESS AS mac_address, SUM(sa.ID) OVER ( PARTITION BY sa.RESOURCE_TYPE ORDER BY sa.ID ) AS window_column FROM PORTS p JOIN STANDARDATTRIBUTES sa ON sa.ID = p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' ), DownPortBindingRank AS ( SELECT p.ID AS port_id, p.NAME AS port_name, p.MAC_ADDRESS AS mac_address, b.HOST AS binding_host, b.VIF_TYPE AS vif_type, RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY p.STATUS ORDER BY p.ID) AS window_column FROM PORTS p JOIN ML2_PORT_BINDINGS b ON p.ID = b.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' ) SELECT dpsaw.port_id, dpsaw.tenant_id, dpbr.port_name, dpsaw.mac_address, dpbr.binding_host, dpbr.vif_type, dpsaw.window_column AS standard_attr_id_running_sum_within_resource_type, dpbr.window_column AS port_rank_within_down_status FROM DownPortStandardAttrWindow dpsaw JOIN DownPortBindingRank dpbr ON dpsaw.port_id = dpbr.port_id AND dpsaw.mac_address = dpbr.mac_address ORDER BY dpsaw.port_id;

question: Using the DOWN-port result set from the existing query as an inner CTE, for each VIF type return the VIF type and the maximum number of distinct device owners observed among DOWN ports in that VIF type (where device owners come from the port-status/device-owner aggregation and VIF types come from the windowed DOWN-port set). Do not return any rounded answers.
sql: WITH inner_cte AS (WITH PortStatusOwnerAgg AS ( SELECT p.STATUS AS port_status, p.DEVICE_OWNER AS device_owner, COUNT(DISTINCT p.ID) AS port_count, MIN(p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID) AS min_standard_attr_id FROM PORTS p JOIN SECURITYGROUPPORTBINDINGS spb ON p.ID = spb.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' GROUP BY p.STATUS, p.DEVICE_OWNER ), DownPortsWindow AS ( SELECT p.NAME, p.MAC_ADDRESS, p.ADMIN_STATE_UP, b.HOST, b.VIF_TYPE, AVG(p.ADMIN_STATE_UP) OVER ( PARTITION BY b.VIF_TYPE ORDER BY p.MAC_ADDRESS ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND 2 FOLLOWING ) AS window_column FROM PORTS AS p JOIN ML2_PORT_BINDINGS AS b ON p.ID = b.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' ORDER BY p.MAC_ADDRESS ) SELECT psa.port_status, psa.device_owner, psa.port_count, psa.min_standard_attr_id, dpw.VIF_TYPE, COUNT(*) AS down_ports_in_vif_type, AVG(dpw.window_column) AS avg_window_admin_state_up FROM PortStatusOwnerAgg psa CROSS JOIN DownPortsWindow dpw GROUP BY psa.port_status, psa.device_owner, psa.port_count, psa.min_standard_attr_id, dpw.VIF_TYPE) SELECT VIF_TYPE, MAX(distinct_device_owners) AS max_distinct_device_owners FROM (SELECT VIF_TYPE, COUNT(DISTINCT device_owner) AS distinct_device_owners FROM inner_cte GROUP BY VIF_TYPE) t GROUP BY VIF_TYPE;

For ports that are DOWN, show the port name, MAC address, admin_state_up flag, binding host, VIF type, and the average admin_state_up in a window of 2 preceding and 2 following rows partitioned by VIF type and ordered by MAC address.

sub_sqls: SELECT p.STATUS AS port_status, p.DEVICE_OWNER AS device_owner, COUNT(DISTINCT p.ID) AS port_count, MIN(p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID) AS min_standard_attr_id FROM PORTS p JOIN SECURITYGROUPPORTBINDINGS spb ON p.ID = spb.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' GROUP BY p.STATUS, p.DEVICE_OWNER;

SELECT p.NAME, p.MAC_ADDRESS, p.ADMIN_STATE_UP, b.HOST, b.VIF_TYPE, AVG(p.ADMIN_STATE_UP) OVER ( PARTITION BY b.VIF_TYPE ORDER BY p.MAC_ADDRESS ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND 2 FOLLOWING ) AS window_column FROM PORTS AS p JOIN ML2_PORT_BINDINGS AS b ON p.ID = b.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' ORDER BY p.MAC_ADDRESS;

WITH PortStatusOwnerAgg AS ( SELECT p.STATUS AS port_status, p.DEVICE_OWNER AS device_owner, COUNT(DISTINCT p.ID) AS port_count, MIN(p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID) AS min_standard_attr_id FROM PORTS p JOIN SECURITYGROUPPORTBINDINGS spb ON p.ID = spb.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' GROUP BY p.STATUS, p.DEVICE_OWNER ), DownPortsWindow AS ( SELECT p.NAME, p.MAC_ADDRESS, p.ADMIN_STATE_UP, b.HOST, b.VIF_TYPE, AVG(p.ADMIN_STATE_UP) OVER ( PARTITION BY b.VIF_TYPE ORDER BY p.MAC_ADDRESS ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND 2 FOLLOWING ) AS window_column FROM PORTS AS p JOIN ML2_PORT_BINDINGS AS b ON p.ID = b.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' ORDER BY p.MAC_ADDRESS ) SELECT psa.port_status, psa.device_owner, psa.port_count, psa.min_standard_attr_id, dpw.VIF_TYPE, COUNT(*) AS down_ports_in_vif_type, AVG(dpw.window_column) AS avg_window_admin_state_up FROM PortStatusOwnerAgg psa CROSS JOIN DownPortsWindow dpw GROUP BY psa.port_status, psa.device_owner, psa.port_count, psa.min_standard_attr_id, dpw.VIF_TYPE;

question: Using the same counts of distinct tenants with ACTIVE networks and distinct tenants with ports bound to host "drive-59", categorize the result by whether the ACTIVE network is admin-up ("Admin Up") or admin-down ("Admin Down"). Return the admin state category, the two tenant counts, and include subtotals and a grand total. Do not return any rounded answers.
sql: WITH inner_cte AS ( WITH active_networks AS ( SELECT n.ID AS network_id, n.NAME AS network_name, n.TENANT_ID AS tenant_id, n.ADMIN_STATE_UP AS admin_state_up, n.MTU AS mtu, sa.UPDATED_AT AS standard_attr_updated_at, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY n.TENANT_ID ORDER BY n.NAME) AS window_column FROM NETWORKS n JOIN STANDARDATTRIBUTES sa ON sa.ID = n.STANDARD_ATTR_ID WHERE n.STATUS = 'ACTIVE' ), drive59_ports AS ( SELECT b.PORT_ID, p.TENANT_ID, p.MAC_ADDRESS, SUM(p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID) OVER ( PARTITION BY b.VIF_TYPE ORDER BY p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID ) AS window_column FROM ML2_PORT_BINDINGS AS b JOIN PORTS AS p ON b.PORT_ID = p.ID JOIN PORTSECURITYBINDINGS AS psb ON p.ID = psb.PORT_ID WHERE b.HOST = 'drive-59' ) SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT an.tenant_id) AS tenants_with_active_networks, COUNT(DISTINCT dp.tenant_id) AS tenants_with_ports_on_drive59 FROM active_networks an CROSS JOIN drive59_ports dp ) , AdminStateCounts AS ( SELECT CASE WHEN an.admin_state_up = 1 THEN 'Admin Up' ELSE 'Admin Down' END AS admin_state_category, COUNT(DISTINCT an.tenant_id) AS tenants_with_active_networks, COUNT(DISTINCT dp.tenant_id) AS tenants_with_ports_on_drive59 FROM NETWORKS n JOIN STANDARDATTRIBUTES sa ON sa.ID = n.STANDARD_ATTR_ID JOIN ( SELECT n.ID AS network_id, n.TENANT_ID AS tenant_id, n.ADMIN_STATE_UP AS admin_state_up FROM NETWORKS n JOIN STANDARDATTRIBUTES sa ON sa.ID = n.STANDARD_ATTR_ID WHERE n.STATUS = 'ACTIVE' ) an ON an.network_id = n.ID CROSS JOIN ( SELECT p.TENANT_ID AS tenant_id FROM ML2_PORT_BINDINGS b JOIN PORTS p ON b.PORT_ID = p.ID JOIN PORTSECURITYBINDINGS psb ON p.ID = psb.PORT_ID WHERE b.HOST = 'drive-59' ) dp GROUP BY admin_state_category ) SELECT CASE WHEN GROUPING(admin_state_category) = 1 THEN 'GRAND TOTAL' ELSE admin_state_category END AS admin_state_category, SUM(tenants_with_active_networks) AS tenants_with_active_networks, SUM(tenants_with_ports_on_drive59) AS tenants_with_ports_on_drive59 FROM AdminStateCounts GROUP BY admin_state_category WITH ROLLUP;

question: For each port status that appears in both result sets, return the port status along with (1) the coefficient of variation (using STDDEV only and never STDDEV_POP) of ports’ standard attribute IDs for ports that have both a security group port binding and a port security binding, and (2) the coefficient of variation (using STDDEV only and never STDDEV_POP) of the allocated IP address string lengths for ports with port security enabled; additionally, only keep statuses where more than 75% of the distinct ports in that status have at least one IP allocation. Do not return any rounded answers.
sql: WITH inner_cte AS (WITH StdAttrIdCV_ByStatus AS ( SELECT p.status, STDDEV(p.standard_attr_id) / NULLIF(AVG(p.standard_attr_id), 0) AS coefficient_of_variation FROM securitygroupportbindings AS sgpb JOIN ports AS p ON sgpb.port_id = p.id JOIN portsecuritybindings AS psb ON p.id = psb.port_id GROUP BY p.status HAVING AVG(p.standard_attr_id) > 0 ORDER BY coefficient_of_variation DESC ), IpAddressLenCV_ByStatus AS ( SELECT p.status, STDDEV(LENGTH(ia.ip_address)) / NULLIF(AVG(LENGTH(ia.ip_address)), 0) AS coefficient_of_variation FROM portsecuritybindings psb JOIN ports p ON psb.port_id = p.id JOIN ipallocations ia ON p.id = ia.port_id WHERE psb.port_security_enabled = 1 GROUP BY p.status HAVING AVG(LENGTH(ia.ip_address)) > 0 ORDER BY coefficient_of_variation DESC ) SELECT s1.status, s1.coefficient_of_variation AS std_attr_id_coefficient_of_variation, s2.coefficient_of_variation AS ip_address_length_coefficient_of_variation FROM StdAttrIdCV_ByStatus s1 JOIN IpAddressLenCV_ByStatus s2 ON s1.status = s2.status) SELECT i.status, i.std_attr_id_coefficient_of_variation, i.ip_address_length_coefficient_of_variation FROM inner_cte i JOIN ports p ON p.status = i.status LEFT JOIN ipallocations ia ON ia.port_id = p.id GROUP BY i.status, i.std_attr_id_coefficient_of_variation, i.ip_address_length_coefficient_of_variation HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN ia.ip_address IS NOT NULL THEN p.id END) * 1.0 / NULLIF(COUNT(DISTINCT p.id), 0) > 0.75;

question: For ports with status DOWN, list each port’s ID, tenant ID, host, VIF type, allocated IP address, and its row number ordered by IP address (using a window frame of 2 preceding rows and 1 following row). Also include the corresponding summary for that port’s status and device owner considering only ports bound to a security group (distinct port count and minimum standard attribute ID), and add the average of these per-(status, device owner) port counts across all such DOWN groups. Do not return any rounded answers.
sql: WITH inner_cte AS (WITH port_status_owner_sg_summary AS ( SELECT p.STATUS AS port_status, p.DEVICE_OWNER AS device_owner, COUNT(DISTINCT p.ID) AS port_count, MIN(p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID) AS min_standard_attr_id FROM PORTS p JOIN SECURITYGROUPPORTBINDINGS spb ON p.ID = spb.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' GROUP BY p.STATUS, p.DEVICE_OWNER ), down_ports_with_ip_window AS ( SELECT p.ID AS port_id, p.TENANT_ID AS tenant_id, b.HOST AS host, b.VIF_TYPE AS vif_type, ia.IP_ADDRESS AS ip_address, ROW_NUMBER() OVER ( ORDER BY ia.IP_ADDRESS ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND 1 FOLLOWING ) AS window_column FROM ML2_PORT_BINDINGS b JOIN PORTS p ON b.PORT_ID = p.ID JOIN IPALLOCATIONS ia ON p.ID = ia.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' ) SELECT d.port_id, d.tenant_id, d.host, d.vif_type, d.ip_address, d.window_column, s.port_status, s.device_owner, s.port_count, s.min_standard_attr_id FROM down_ports_with_ip_window d JOIN PORTS p ON p.ID = d.port_id JOIN port_status_owner_sg_summary s ON s.port_status = p.STATUS AND s.device_owner = p.DEVICE_OWNER) SELECT i.port_id, i.tenant_id, i.host, i.vif_type, i.ip_address, i.window_column, i.port_status, i.device_owner, i.port_count, i.min_standard_attr_id, avg_counts.avg_port_count_across_down_status_owner_groups FROM inner_cte i JOIN ( SELECT AVG(port_count) AS avg_port_count_across_down_status_owner_groups FROM ( SELECT p.STATUS AS port_status, p.DEVICE_OWNER AS device_owner, COUNT(DISTINCT p.ID) AS port_count FROM PORTS p JOIN SECURITYGROUPPORTBINDINGS spb ON p.ID = spb.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' GROUP BY p.STATUS, p.DEVICE_OWNER ) AS sub ) AS avg_counts ON 1 = 1;

question: For ports that are DOWN, return the port ID, tenant ID, MAC address, and the running sum of the port’s standard attribute ID within each security group (ordered by standard attribute ID), and for those same MAC addresses also show the administratively up port name, port security enabled status, and the row number ordered by MAC address using a window frame of 2 preceding rows and 1 following row. Additionally, group the results by whether the port is in an “External” or “Internal” security-group category (treat security groups whose ID starts with '000' as “External”, otherwise “Internal”), and include subtotals per category and a grand total of matched MAC addresses. Do not return any rounded answers.
sql: WITH inner_cte AS (WITH down_ports_sg_running_sum AS ( SELECT p.ID AS port_id, p.TENANT_ID AS tenant_id, p.MAC_ADDRESS AS mac_address, SUM(p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID) OVER ( PARTITION BY sgpb.SECURITY_GROUP_ID ORDER BY p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID ) AS window_column FROM SECURITYGROUPPORTBINDINGS AS sgpb JOIN PORTS AS p ON sgpb.PORT_ID = p.ID JOIN PORTSECURITYBINDINGS AS psb ON p.ID = psb.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' ), admin_up_ports_rownum AS ( SELECT p.NAME AS port_name, p.MAC_ADDRESS AS mac_address, psb.PORT_SECURITY_ENABLED AS port_security_enabled, ROW_NUMBER() OVER ( ORDER BY p.MAC_ADDRESS ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND 1 FOLLOWING ) AS window_column FROM PORTS AS p JOIN PORTSECURITYBINDINGS AS psb ON p.ID = psb.PORT_ID WHERE p.ADMIN_STATE_UP = 1 ) SELECT d.port_id, d.tenant_id, d.mac_address, d.window_column AS down_ports_running_sum_standard_attr_id_within_security_group, a.port_name, a.port_security_enabled, a.window_column AS admin_up_ports_row_number_by_mac FROM down_ports_sg_running_sum d JOIN admin_up_ports_rownum a ON d.mac_address = a.mac_address), mac_externality AS ( SELECT i.mac_address, CASE WHEN MAX(CASE WHEN sgpb.security_group_id LIKE '000%' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) = 1 THEN 'External' ELSE 'Internal' END AS external_status FROM inner_cte i JOIN ports p ON p.mac_address = i.mac_address JOIN securitygroupportbindings sgpb ON sgpb.port_id = p.id GROUP BY i.mac_address ), counts AS ( SELECT me.external_status, COUNT(DISTINCT me.mac_address) AS total_macs FROM mac_externality me GROUP BY me.external_status ) SELECT CASE WHEN GROUPING(external_status) = 1 THEN 'GRAND TOTAL' ELSE external_status END AS external_status, SUM(total_macs) AS total_macs FROM counts GROUP BY external_status WITH ROLLUP;

question: For each network, list the network ID, total number of ports that are (1) DOWN with an allocated IP address and a row number within their network (ordered by port ID) and (2) bound to at least one security group with admin_state_up = 1, along with the average number of DNS records per such port. Do not repeat the network ID if it is the same as the previous row. Include a final TOTAL row across all networks. Do not return any rounded answers.
sql: WITH inner_cte AS (WITH AdminUpBoundPorts AS ( SELECT p.id AS port_id, p.tenant_id, p.name AS port_name, COUNT(sgpb.security_group_id) AS security_group_binding_count, SUM(CASE WHEN pd.port_id IS NULL THEN 0 ELSE 1 END) AS dns_record_count FROM SECURITYGROUPPORTBINDINGS sgpb JOIN PORTS p ON sgpb.port_id = p.id LEFT JOIN PORTDNSES pd ON p.id = pd.port_id WHERE p.admin_state_up = 1 GROUP BY p.id, p.tenant_id, p.name ), DownPortsWithIPs AS ( SELECT p.ID AS port_id, p.TENANT_ID AS tenant_id, p.NAME AS port_name, p.NETWORK_ID AS network_id, p.MAC_ADDRESS AS mac_address, p.DEVICE_OWNER AS device_owner, ia.IP_ADDRESS AS ip_address, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY p.NETWORK_ID ORDER BY p.ID) AS window_column FROM PORTS p JOIN IPALLOCATIONS ia ON p.ID = ia.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' ) SELECT d.network_id, d.window_column AS down_port_row_number_in_network, d.port_id, d.tenant_id, d.port_name, d.mac_address, d.device_owner, d.ip_address, a.security_group_binding_count, a.dns_record_count FROM DownPortsWithIPs d JOIN AdminUpBoundPorts a ON d.port_id = a.port_id ORDER BY d.network_id, d.window_column, d.port_id) SELECT CASE WHEN LAG(network_id) OVER (ORDER BY network_id_sort, network_id) = network_id THEN NULL ELSE network_id END AS network_id, total_ports, avg_dns_records_per_port FROM ( SELECT CASE WHEN GROUPING(i.network_id) = 1 THEN 'zzz' ELSE i.network_id END AS network_id_sort, CASE WHEN GROUPING(i.network_id) = 1 THEN 'TOTAL' ELSE i.network_id END AS network_id, COUNT(DISTINCT i.port_id) AS total_ports, AVG(i.dns_record_count) AS avg_dns_records_per_port FROM inner_cte i GROUP BY i.network_id WITH ROLLUP ) AS tbltmp ORDER BY network_id_sort;

Do not return any rounded answers.
sql: WITH inner_cte AS ( WITH down_ports_bindings AS ( SELECT p.NAME, p.MAC_ADDRESS, p.ADMIN_STATE_UP, b.HOST, b.VIF_TYPE, AVG(p.ADMIN_STATE_UP) OVER ( PARTITION BY b.VIF_TYPE ORDER BY p.MAC_ADDRESS ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND 2 FOLLOWING ) AS window_column FROM PORTS AS p JOIN ML2_PORT_BINDINGS AS b ON p.ID = b.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' ORDER BY p.MAC_ADDRESS ), down_ports_ipallocs AS ( SELECT p.ID AS port_id, p.NAME AS port_name, p.MAC_ADDRESS AS mac_address, ia.IP_ADDRESS AS ip_address, ia.SUBNET_ID AS subnet_id, AVG(p.ID) OVER (PARTITION BY p.ID ORDER BY ia.IP_ADDRESS) AS window_column FROM PORTS p JOIN IPALLOCATIONS ia ON p.ID = ia.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' ORDER BY ia.IP_ADDRESS ) SELECT dpi.port_id, dpi.port_name, dpi.mac_address, dpb.ADMIN_STATE_UP, dpb.HOST, dpb.VIF_TYPE, dpi.ip_address, dpi.subnet_id, dpb.window_column AS avg_admin_state_up_window_2_pre_2_fol_by_vif_type, dpi.window_column AS avg_port_id_by_port_id_ordered_by_ip FROM down_ports_ipallocs dpi JOIN down_ports_bindings dpb ON dpi.port_name = dpb.NAME AND dpi.mac_address = dpb.MAC_ADDRESS ORDER BY dpi.ip_address ) SELECT i.port_id, i.port_name, i.mac_address, i.admin_state_up, i.host, i.vif_type, i.ip_address, i.subnet_id, i.avg_admin_state_up_window_2_pre_2_fol_by_vif_type, i.avg_port_id_by_port_id_ordered_by_ip, vif_stats.total_down_ports_for_vif_type, avg_vif_stats.avg_down_ports_across_vif_types FROM inner_cte AS i JOIN ( SELECT vif_type, COUNT(*) AS total_down_ports_for_vif_type FROM inner_cte GROUP BY vif_type ) AS vif_stats ON i.vif_type = vif_stats.vif_type JOIN ( SELECT AVG(down_port_count) AS avg_down_ports_across_vif_types FROM ( SELECT COUNT(*) AS down_port_count FROM inner_cte GROUP BY vif_type ) AS sub ) AS avg_vif_stats ON 1 = 1 ORDER BY i.ip_address;

question: For each RBAC action that is access_as_shared, list the action along with (1) the variance of subnet IP version (IPv4 vs IPv6) across subnets on the referenced networks, and (2) the overall average, range (max minus min), and variance of subnet IP version (considering only subnets with IP version 4 or 6) for networks referenced by RBAC entries with that same action; also include the average DHCP-enabled flag across those same subnets (treating ENABLE_DHCP as 0/1). Do not return any rounded answers.
sql: WITH inner_cte AS ( WITH RbacSharedIpVersionVariance AS (SELECT n.ACTION, VARIANCE(s.IP_VERSION) AS ip_version_variance FROM NETWORKRBACS AS n JOIN SUBNETS AS s ON n.OBJECT_ID = s.NETWORK_ID WHERE n.ACTION = 'access_as_shared' GROUP BY n.ACTION ORDER BY ip_version_variance DESC), RbacIpVersionStats AS (SELECT n.ACTION AS rbac_action, AVG(s.IP_VERSION) AS avg_ip_version, MAX(s.IP_VERSION) - MIN(s.IP_VERSION) AS ip_version_range, VARIANCE(s.IP_VERSION) AS ip_version_variance FROM NETWORKRBACS AS n JOIN SUBNETS AS s ON n.OBJECT_ID = s.NETWORK_ID WHERE s.IP_VERSION IN (4, 6) GROUP BY n.ACTION ORDER BY ip_version_range DESC) SELECT rs.ACTION AS rbac_action, rs.ip_version_variance AS shared_action_ip_version_variance, ris.avg_ip_version, ris.ip_version_range, ris.ip_version_variance AS overall_ip_version_variance FROM RbacSharedIpVersionVariance rs JOIN RbacIpVersionStats ris ON rs.ACTION = ris.rbac_action ORDER BY rs.ip_version_variance DESC ), dhcp_stats AS ( SELECT n.ACTION AS rbac_action, AVG(CAST(s.ENABLE_DHCP AS FLOAT)) AS avg_enable_dhcp FROM NETWORKRBACS AS n JOIN SUBNETS AS s ON n.OBJECT_ID = s.NETWORK_ID WHERE n.ACTION = 'access_as_shared' GROUP BY n.ACTION ) SELECT i.rbac_action, i.shared_action_ip_version_variance, i.avg_ip_version, i.ip_version_range, i.overall_ip_version_variance, d.avg_enable_dhcp FROM inner_cte AS i JOIN dhcp_stats AS d ON i.rbac_action = d.rbac_action ORDER BY i.shared_action_ip_version_variance DESC;

question: For ports with status equal to 'DOWN', return the same port/IP details (port ID, tenant ID, port name, network ID, MAC address, device owner, allocated IP address, subnet ID, the average port ID within each port ID group ordered by IP address, and the row number within each network ordered by port ID), but only for networks whose number of DOWN ports is greater than the average number of DOWN ports per network. Do not return any rounded answers.
sql: WITH inner_cte AS ( WITH DownPortIpWindow AS ( SELECT p.ID AS port_id, p.NAME AS port_name, p.MAC_ADDRESS AS mac_address, ia.IP_ADDRESS AS ip_address, ia.SUBNET_ID AS subnet_id, AVG(p.ID) OVER (PARTITION BY p.ID ORDER BY ia.IP_ADDRESS) AS window_column FROM PORTS p JOIN IPALLOCATIONS ia ON p.ID = ia.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' ORDER BY ia.IP_ADDRESS ), DownPortNetworkRowNum AS ( SELECT p.ID AS port_id, p.TENANT_ID AS tenant_id, p.NAME AS port_name, p.NETWORK_ID AS network_id, p.MAC_ADDRESS AS mac_address, p.DEVICE_OWNER AS device_owner, ia.IP_ADDRESS AS ip_address, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY p.NETWORK_ID ORDER BY p.ID) AS window_column FROM PORTS p JOIN IPALLOCATIONS ia ON p.ID = ia.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' ) SELECT dpiw.port_id, dpnr.tenant_id, dpiw.port_name, dpnr.network_id, dpiw.mac_address, dpnr.device_owner, dpiw.ip_address, dpiw.subnet_id, dpiw.window_column AS avg_port_id_within_port_id_group_by_ip, dpnr.window_column AS row_number_within_network_by_port_id FROM DownPortIpWindow dpiw JOIN DownPortNetworkRowNum dpnr ON dpiw.port_id = dpnr.port_id AND dpiw.ip_address = dpnr.ip_address ORDER BY dpnr.network_id, dpnr.window_column, dpiw.ip_address ), NetworkDownPortCounts AS ( SELECT p.NETWORK_ID AS network_id, COUNT(DISTINCT p.ID) AS total_down_ports FROM PORTS p JOIN IPALLOCATIONS ia ON p.ID = ia.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' GROUP BY p.NETWORK_ID ) SELECT i.port_id, i.tenant_id, i.port_name, i.network_id, i.mac_address, i.device_owner, i.ip_address, i.subnet_id, i.avg_port_id_within_port_id_group_by_ip, i.row_number_within_network_by_port_id FROM inner_cte i JOIN NetworkDownPortCounts ndpc ON i.network_id = ndpc.network_id WHERE ndpc.total_down_ports > (SELECT AVG(total_down_ports) FROM NetworkDownPortCounts) ORDER BY i.network_id, i.row_number_within_network_by_port_id, i.ip_address;

question: Among the ports returned by the existing “DOWN ports on host drive-59” window/running-sum analysis, list the top 10 tenants with the most such ports, showing each tenant’s ID, the total number of matching ports, and whether any of those ports have a port-security binding. sql: WITH inner_cte AS ( WITH DownPortsWindow AS ( SELECT p.NAME, p.MAC_ADDRESS, p.ADMIN_STATE_UP, b.HOST, b.VIF_TYPE, AVG(p.ADMIN_STATE_UP) OVER ( PARTITION BY b.VIF_TYPE ORDER BY p.MAC_ADDRESS ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND 2 FOLLOWING ) AS window_column FROM PORTS AS p JOIN ML2_PORT_BINDINGS AS b ON p.ID = b.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' ORDER BY p.MAC_ADDRESS ), Drive59PortsRunningSum AS ( SELECT b.PORT_ID, p.TENANT_ID, p.MAC_ADDRESS, SUM(p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID) OVER ( PARTITION BY b.VIF_TYPE ORDER BY p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID ) AS window_column FROM ML2_PORT_BINDINGS AS b JOIN PORTS AS p ON b.PORT_ID = p.ID JOIN PORTSECURITYBINDINGS AS psb ON p.ID = psb.PORT_ID WHERE b.HOST = 'drive-59' ), DownDrive59PortDetails AS ( SELECT dpw.NAME, dpw.MAC_ADDRESS, dpw.ADMIN_STATE_UP, dpw.HOST, dpw.VIF_TYPE, dpw.window_column AS down_ports_avg_admin_state_up_window, d59.PORT_ID, d59.TENANT_ID, d59.window_column AS drive59_running_sum_standard_attr_id FROM DownPortsWindow dpw JOIN Drive59PortsRunningSum d59 ON dpw.MAC_ADDRESS = d59.MAC_ADDRESS WHERE dpw.HOST = 'drive-59' ) SELECT * FROM DownDrive59PortDetails ORDER BY VIF_TYPE, MAC_ADDRESS, PORT_ID ) SELECT i.tenant_id, COUNT(DISTINCT i.port_id) AS total_ports, CASE WHEN COUNT(DISTINCT psb.port_id) > 0 THEN 'Yes' ELSE 'No' END AS has_port_security_binding FROM inner_cte i LEFT JOIN PORTS p ON p.id = i.port_id LEFT JOIN PORTSECURITYBINDINGS psb ON psb.port_id = p.id GROUP BY i.tenant_id ORDER BY total_ports DESC LIMIT 10;

Do not return any rounded answers.
sql: WITH inner_cte AS ( WITH HostPortMaxAttr AS ( SELECT b.HOST, MAX(p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID) AS max_standard_attr_id, p.STATUS FROM ML2_PORT_BINDINGS b JOIN PORTS p ON b.PORT_ID = p.ID JOIN ALLOWEDADDRESSPAIRS a ON p.ID = a.PORT_ID WHERE a.IP_ADDRESS = '10.232.210.41/8' GROUP BY b.HOST, p.STATUS HAVING MAX(p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID) > 1 ), StatusAttrVariance AS ( SELECT p.STATUS, VARIANCE(p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID) AS standard_attr_id_variance FROM PORTS AS p JOIN IPALLOCATIONS AS ia ON p.ID = ia.PORT_ID WHERE p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID IS NOT NULL GROUP BY p.STATUS ORDER BY standard_attr_id_variance DESC ) SELECT hpma.HOST, hpma.STATUS, hpma.max_standard_attr_id, sav.standard_attr_id_variance FROM HostPortMaxAttr hpma JOIN StatusAttrVariance sav ON hpma.STATUS = sav.STATUS ) SELECT i.HOST, i.STATUS, i.max_standard_attr_id, i.standard_attr_id_variance, CASE WHEN COUNT(DISTINCT ia.PORT_ID) > 0 THEN 'Yes' ELSE 'No' END AS has_ip_allocation_in_group FROM inner_cte i JOIN ML2_PORT_BINDINGS b ON i.HOST = b.HOST JOIN PORTS p ON b.PORT_ID = p.ID AND p.STATUS = i.STATUS LEFT JOIN IPALLOCATIONS ia ON p.ID = ia.PORT_ID GROUP BY i.HOST, i.STATUS, i.max_standard_attr_id, i.standard_attr_id_variance;

sql: WITH inner_cte AS ( WITH DownPortsBySecurityGroup AS ( SELECT p.ID AS port_id, p.TENANT_ID AS tenant_id, p.MAC_ADDRESS AS mac_address, SUM(p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID) OVER ( PARTITION BY sgpb.SECURITY_GROUP_ID ORDER BY p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID ) AS window_column FROM SECURITYGROUPPORTBINDINGS AS sgpb JOIN PORTS AS p ON sgpb.PORT_ID = p.ID JOIN PORTSECURITYBINDINGS AS psb ON p.ID = psb.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' ), Drive59PortsByVifType AS ( SELECT b.PORT_ID, p.TENANT_ID, p.MAC_ADDRESS, SUM(p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID) OVER ( PARTITION BY b.VIF_TYPE ORDER BY p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID ) AS window_column FROM ML2_PORT_BINDINGS AS b JOIN PORTS AS p ON b.PORT_ID = p.ID JOIN PORTSECURITYBINDINGS AS psb ON p.ID = psb.PORT_ID WHERE b.HOST = 'drive-59' ), CombinedPorts AS ( SELECT port_id, tenant_id, mac_address, window_column, 'DOWN (by Security Group)' AS reason FROM DownPortsBySecurityGroup UNION ALL SELECT PORT_ID AS port_id, TENANT_ID AS tenant_id, MAC_ADDRESS AS mac_address, window_column, 'Host drive-59 (by VIF Type)' AS reason FROM Drive59PortsByVifType ) SELECT port_id, tenant_id, mac_address, window_column, reason FROM CombinedPorts ORDER BY tenant_id, port_id ) SELECT inner_cte.tenant_id, COUNT(DISTINCT inner_cte.port_id) AS total_ports_in_combined_set, CASE WHEN SUM(CASE WHEN inner_cte.reason = 'Host drive-59 (by VIF Type)' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) > 0 THEN 'Yes' ELSE 'No' END AS has_drive59_ports FROM inner_cte GROUP BY inner_cte.tenant_id ORDER BY total_ports_in_combined_set DESC LIMIT 10;
