question: For IPv4 subnets that belong to networks with an RBAC action of 'access_as_shared', return the subnet name, CIDR, RBAC target tenant, the running sum of subnet standard attribute IDs within each IP version group ordered by standard attribute ID, and the dense rank of the subnet’s standard attribute ID ordered by the standard attribute updated-at timestamp (using the current row and 2 preceding rows). Do not return any rounded answers.
sql: WITH SharedRbacSubnets AS ( SELECT s.NAME AS subnet_name, s.CIDR AS subnet_cidr, n.TARGET_TENANT AS rbac_target_tenant, SUM(s.STANDARD_ATTR_ID) OVER ( PARTITION BY s.IP_VERSION ORDER BY s.STANDARD_ATTR_ID ) AS window_column FROM SUBNETS AS s JOIN NETWORKRBACS AS n ON n.OBJECT_ID = s.NETWORK_ID WHERE n.ACTION = 'access_as_shared' ), IPv4SubnetDenseRanks AS ( SELECT s.NAME, dense_rank() OVER ( ORDER BY sa.UPDATED_AT ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW ) AS window_column FROM SUBNETS AS s JOIN STANDARDATTRIBUTES AS sa ON sa.ID = s.STANDARD_ATTR_ID WHERE s.IP_VERSION = 4 ) SELECT srs.subnet_name, srs.subnet_cidr, srs.rbac_target_tenant, srs.window_column AS running_sum_standard_attr_id_within_ip_version, idr.window_column AS dense_rank_by_standardattribute_updated_at_for_ipv4 FROM SharedRbacSubnets AS srs JOIN IPv4SubnetDenseRanks AS idr ON idr.NAME = srs.subnet_name;

question: For ports that are DOWN but also administratively up, return the port ID, port name, MAC address, binding host, VIF type, the port’s rank within the DOWN status group (ordered by port ID), the tenant ID, the number of port security bindings on the port, and the total number of times port security is enabled across those bindings—only including ports where port security is enabled at least once. Do not return any rounded answers.
sql: WITH DownPortsWithBindings AS (SELECT p.ID AS port_id, p.NAME AS port_name, p.MAC_ADDRESS AS mac_address, b.HOST AS binding_host, b.VIF_TYPE AS vif_type, RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY p.STATUS ORDER BY p.ID) AS window_column FROM PORTS p JOIN ML2_PORT_BINDINGS b ON p.ID = b.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN'), AdminUpPortSecurityStats AS (SELECT p.id AS port_id, p.tenant_id, p.mac_address, COUNT(psb.port_id) AS binding_count, SUM(CASE WHEN psb.port_security_enabled THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS port_security_enabled_total FROM ports p JOIN portsecuritybindings psb ON p.id = psb.port_id WHERE p.admin_state_up = 1 GROUP BY p.id, p.tenant_id, p.mac_address) SELECT d.port_id, d.port_name, d.mac_address, d.binding_host, d.vif_type, d.window_column, a.tenant_id, a.binding_count, a.port_security_enabled_total FROM DownPortsWithBindings d JOIN AdminUpPortSecurityStats a ON d.port_id = a.port_id WHERE a.port_security_enabled_total > 0 ORDER BY a.port_security_enabled_total DESC, d.port_id;

question: For DOWN ports, considering only the first 3 ports per network (by port ID), show for each tenant and VIF type the number of such DOWN ports and the average of the 2-preceding/2-following admin_state_up window metric (partitioned by VIF type and ordered by MAC address). sql: WITH PortBindingsWindow AS ( SELECT p.NAME, p.MAC_ADDRESS, p.ADMIN_STATE_UP, b.HOST, b.VIF_TYPE, AVG(p.ADMIN_STATE_UP) OVER ( PARTITION BY b.VIF_TYPE ORDER BY p.MAC_ADDRESS ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND 2 FOLLOWING ) AS window_column FROM PORTS AS p JOIN ML2_PORT_BINDINGS AS b ON p.ID = b.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' ORDER BY p.MAC_ADDRESS ), DownPortsWithIPs AS ( SELECT p.ID AS port_id, p.TENANT_ID AS tenant_id, p.NAME AS port_name, p.NETWORK_ID AS network_id, p.MAC_ADDRESS AS mac_address, p.DEVICE_OWNER AS device_owner, ia.IP_ADDRESS AS ip_address, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY p.NETWORK_ID ORDER BY p.ID) AS window_column FROM PORTS p JOIN IPALLOCATIONS ia ON p.ID = ia.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' ) SELECT dpi.tenant_id, pbw.VIF_TYPE, COUNT(*) AS down_port_count, AVG(pbw.window_column) AS avg_admin_state_up_window_2_pre_2_fol FROM DownPortsWithIPs dpi JOIN PortBindingsWindow pbw ON dpi.mac_address = pbw.MAC_ADDRESS WHERE dpi.window_column <= 3 GROUP BY dpi.tenant_id, pbw.VIF_TYPE ORDER BY down_port_count DESC, avg_admin_state_up_window_2_pre_2_fol DESC;

question: For ports with status DOWN, return (1) the number of distinct DOWN ports that are bound to a security group and the minimum standard attribute ID for each device owner, and (2) the DOWN port details (port ID, port name, MAC address, binding host, VIF type, and the rank within the DOWN status group ordered by port ID), output together in one result set. Do not return any rounded answers.
sql: WITH PortStatusOwnerAgg AS (SELECT p.STATUS AS port_status, p.DEVICE_OWNER AS device_owner, COUNT(DISTINCT p.ID) AS port_count, MIN(p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID) AS min_standard_attr_id FROM PORTS p JOIN SECURITYGROUPPORTBINDINGS spb ON p.ID = spb.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' GROUP BY p.STATUS, p.DEVICE_OWNER), DownPortDetails AS (SELECT p.ID AS port_id, p.NAME AS port_name, p.MAC_ADDRESS AS mac_address, b.HOST AS binding_host, b.VIF_TYPE AS vif_type, RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY p.STATUS ORDER BY p.ID) AS window_column FROM PORTS p JOIN ML2_PORT_BINDINGS b ON p.ID = b.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN') SELECT psa.port_status, psa.device_owner, psa.port_count, psa.min_standard_attr_id, dpd.port_id, dpd.port_name, dpd.mac_address, dpd.binding_host, dpd.vif_type, dpd.window_column FROM PortStatusOwnerAgg psa CROSS JOIN DownPortDetails dpd;

sql: WITH port_status_owner_sg_summary AS ( SELECT p.STATUS AS port_status, p.DEVICE_OWNER AS device_owner, COUNT(DISTINCT p.ID) AS port_count, MIN(p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID) AS min_standard_attr_id FROM PORTS p JOIN SECURITYGROUPPORTBINDINGS spb ON p.ID = spb.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' GROUP BY p.STATUS, p.DEVICE_OWNER ), down_ports_with_ip_window AS ( SELECT p.ID AS port_id, p.TENANT_ID AS tenant_id, b.HOST AS host, b.VIF_TYPE AS vif_type, ia.IP_ADDRESS AS ip_address, ROW_NUMBER() OVER ( ORDER BY ia.IP_ADDRESS ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND 1 FOLLOWING ) AS window_column FROM ML2_PORT_BINDINGS b JOIN PORTS p ON b.PORT_ID = p.ID JOIN IPALLOCATIONS ia ON p.ID = ia.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' ) SELECT d.port_id, d.tenant_id, d.host, d.vif_type, d.ip_address, d.window_column, s.port_status, s.device_owner, s.port_count, s.min_standard_attr_id FROM down_ports_with_ip_window d JOIN PORTS p ON p.ID = d.port_id JOIN port_status_owner_sg_summary s ON s.port_status = p.STATUS AND s.device_owner = p.DEVICE_OWNER;

question: From the top 10 port binding hosts with the highest variance in port standard attribute ID (considering only ports with status 'DOWN' that have an IP allocation), display each host name and its variance, along with the port status, device owner, number of distinct security-group-bound ports, and the minimum standard attribute ID for 'DOWN' ports by device owner. sql: WITH sq1 AS ( SELECT p.STATUS AS port_status, p.DEVICE_OWNER AS device_owner, COUNT(DISTINCT p.ID) AS port_count, MIN(p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID) AS min_standard_attr_id FROM PORTS p JOIN SECURITYGROUPPORTBINDINGS spb ON p.ID = spb.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' GROUP BY p.STATUS, p.DEVICE_OWNER ), sq2 AS ( SELECT b.HOST, VARIANCE(p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID) AS standard_attr_id_variance FROM ML2_PORT_BINDINGS AS b JOIN PORTS AS p ON b.PORT_ID = p.ID JOIN IPALLOCATIONS AS ia ON p.ID = ia.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' AND ia.PORT_ID IS NOT NULL GROUP BY b.HOST ORDER BY standard_attr_id_variance DESC ), top_hosts AS ( SELECT HOST, standard_attr_id_variance FROM sq2 ORDER BY standard_attr_id_variance DESC LIMIT 10 ) SELECT th.HOST, th.standard_attr_id_variance, sq1.port_status, sq1.device_owner, sq1.port_count, sq1.min_standard_attr_id FROM top_hosts th CROSS JOIN sq1 ORDER BY th.standard_attr_id_variance DESC, sq1.port_count DESC;
sub_questions: For each port status and device owner, considering only ports that are bound to a security group, return the number of distinct ports and the minimum standard attribute ID.
For each port binding host, show the host name and the variance of the port standard attribute ID, considering only ports whose status is 'DOWN' and that have an IP allocation.
sub_sqls: SELECT p.STATUS AS port_status, p.DEVICE_OWNER AS device_owner, COUNT(DISTINCT p.ID) AS port_count, MIN(p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID) AS min_standard_attr_id FROM PORTS p JOIN SECURITYGROUPPORTBINDINGS spb ON p.ID = spb.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' GROUP BY p.STATUS, p.DEVICE_OWNER;

SELECT b.HOST, VARIANCE(p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID) AS standard_attr_id_variance FROM ML2_PORT_BINDINGS AS b JOIN PORTS AS p ON b.PORT_ID = p.ID JOIN IPALLOCATIONS AS ia ON p.ID = ia.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' AND ia.PORT_ID IS NOT NULL GROUP BY b.HOST ORDER BY standard_attr_id_variance DESC;

question: For load balancers associated with the 'haproxy' provider, for each operating status that has more than 1 such load balancer, return the operating status, the total number of 'haproxy' load balancers in that status, and how many of those load balancers have a maximum admin_state_up value of 1. Do not return any rounded answers.
sql: WITH haproxy_status_counts AS ( SELECT lb.OPERATING_STATUS, COUNT(*) AS total_loadbalancers FROM LBAAS_LOADBALANCERS AS lb JOIN PROVIDERRESOURCEASSOCIATIONS AS pra ON lb.ID = pra.RESOURCE_ID WHERE pra.PROVIDER_NAME = 'haproxy' GROUP BY lb.OPERATING_STATUS HAVING COUNT(*) > 1 ), haproxy_admin_up_lbs AS ( SELECT lb.name AS loadbalancer_name, MAX(lb.admin_state_up) AS max_admin_state_up, lb.operating_status FROM LBAAS_LOADBALANCERS lb JOIN PROVIDERRESOURCEASSOCIATIONS pra ON lb.id = pra.resource_id WHERE pra.provider_name = 'haproxy' GROUP BY lb.name, lb.operating_status HAVING MAX(lb.admin_state_up) = 1 ) SELECT hsc.OPERATING_STATUS, hsc.total_loadbalancers, COUNT(hal.loadbalancer_name) AS admin_up_loadbalancers_in_status FROM haproxy_status_counts hsc LEFT JOIN haproxy_admin_up_lbs hal ON hal.operating_status = hsc.OPERATING_STATUS GROUP BY hsc.OPERATING_STATUS, hsc.total_loadbalancers;
sub_questions: For each load balancer operating status, show the operating status and the total number of load balancers that are associated with the “haproxy” provider, only including statuses where the total count of such load balancers is greater than 1.

For each load balancer that is associated with the provider named 'haproxy', return the load balancer name, the highest admin_state_up value, and the load balancer operating status, keeping only those groups where the highest admin_state_up value is 1.
sub_sqls: SELECT lb.OPERATING_STATUS, COUNT(*) AS total_loadbalancers FROM LBAAS_LOADBALANCERS AS lb JOIN PROVIDERRESOURCEASSOCIATIONS AS pra ON lb.ID = pra.RESOURCE_ID WHERE pra.PROVIDER_NAME = 'haproxy' GROUP BY lb.OPERATING_STATUS HAVING COUNT(*) > 1;

SELECT lb.name AS loadbalancer_name, MAX(lb.admin_state_up) AS max_admin_state_up, lb.operating_status FROM LBAAS_LOADBALANCERS lb JOIN PROVIDERRESOURCEASSOCIATIONS pra ON lb.id = pra.resource_id WHERE pra.provider_name = 'haproxy' GROUP BY lb.name, lb.operating_status HAVING MAX(lb.admin_state_up) = 1;

question: For each device owner among ports with status 'DOWN' that are bound to a security group, list the port status, device owner, number of distinct ports, and minimum standard attribute ID; also include (for that same status) the coefficient of variation (using STDDEV only and never STDDEV_POP) of standard attribute IDs among ports that have both a security group port binding and a port security binding, and compute the ratio of the minimum standard attribute ID to that coefficient of variation (using STDDEV only and never STDDEV_POP).
sql: WITH StatusVariation AS ( SELECT p.status, STDDEV(p.standard_attr_id) / NULLIF(AVG(p.standard_attr_id), 0) AS coefficient_of_variation FROM securitygroupportbindings AS sgpb JOIN ports AS p ON sgpb.port_id = p.id JOIN portsecuritybindings AS psb ON p.id = psb.port_id GROUP BY p.status HAVING AVG(p.standard_attr_id) > 0 ORDER BY coefficient_of_variation DESC ), DownPortsByOwner AS ( SELECT p.STATUS AS port_status, p.DEVICE_OWNER AS device_owner, COUNT(DISTINCT p.ID) AS port_count, MIN(p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID) AS min_standard_attr_id FROM PORTS p JOIN SECURITYGROUPPORTBINDINGS spb ON p.ID = spb.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' GROUP BY p.STATUS, p.DEVICE_OWNER ) SELECT dpo.port_status, dpo.device_owner, dpo.port_count, dpo.min_standard_attr_id, sv.coefficient_of_variation, ROUND(dpo.min_standard_attr_id / NULLIF(sv.coefficient_of_variation, 0), 2) AS min_attr_id_per_variation FROM DownPortsByOwner dpo JOIN StatusVariation sv ON dpo.port_status = sv.status ORDER BY min_attr_id_per_variation DESC;
sub_questions: For each port status, show the status and the coefficient of variation of the ports’ standard attribute IDs, considering only ports that have a security group port binding and a port security binding.
For each port status and device owner, considering only ports that are bound to a security group, return the number of distinct ports and the minimum standard attribute ID.
sub_sqls: SELECT p.status, STDDEV(p.standard_attr_id) / NULLIF(AVG(p.standard_attr_id), 0) AS coefficient_of_variation FROM securitygroupportbindings AS sgpb JOIN ports AS p ON sgpb.port_id = p.id JOIN portsecuritybindings AS psb ON p.id = psb.port_id GROUP BY p.status HAVING AVG(p.standard_attr_id) > 0 ORDER BY coefficient_of_variation DESC;

SELECT p.STATUS AS port_status, p.DEVICE_OWNER AS device_owner, COUNT(DISTINCT p.ID) AS port_count, MIN(p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID) AS min_standard_attr_id FROM PORTS p JOIN SECURITYGROUPPORTBINDINGS spb ON p.ID = spb.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' GROUP BY p.STATUS, p.DEVICE_OWNER;

question: For IPv4 subnets, list each subnet route (destination and next hop) along with the subnet name and CIDR and the allocation pool’s first and last IP, and also include the subnet’s average and variance of DNS nameserver order values; order results by the DNS order variance (highest first). Do not return any rounded answers.
sql: WITH DnsOrderStats AS (SELECT s.NAME AS subnet_name, AVG(d.ORDER) AS avg_dns_order, VARIANCE(d.ORDER) AS dns_order_variance FROM SUBNETS AS s JOIN DNSNAMESERVERS AS d ON s.ID = d.SUBNET_ID WHERE s.IP_VERSION = 4 GROUP BY s.NAME ORDER BY dns_order_variance DESC), RoutePoolDetails AS (SELECT r.DESTINATION, r.NEXTHOP, s.NAME AS subnet_name, s.CIDR AS subnet_cidr, p.FIRST_IP, p.LAST_IP, DENSE_RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY r.SUBNET_ID ORDER BY r.SUBNET_ID) AS window_column FROM SUBNETROUTES r JOIN SUBNETS s ON r.SUBNET_ID = s.ID JOIN IPALLOCATIONPOOLS p ON s.ID = p.SUBNET_ID WHERE s.IP_VERSION = 4) SELECT rpd.subnet_name, rpd.subnet_cidr, rpd.DESTINATION, rpd.NEXTHOP, rpd.FIRST_IP, rpd.LAST_IP, rpd.window_column, dos.avg_dns_order, dos.dns_order_variance FROM RoutePoolDetails rpd JOIN DnsOrderStats dos ON rpd.subnet_name = dos.subnet_name ORDER BY dos.dns_order_variance DESC, rpd.subnet_name, rpd.window_column;
sub_questions: For each subnet (by subnet name), calculate the average and variance of the DNS nameserver order values for DNS entries associated with that subnet, considering only IPv4 subnets.

Show each subnet route’s destination and next hop together with the subnet name and CIDR, plus the allocation pool’s first and last IP. Also include a dense rank within each subnet (partitioned by subnet ID) ordered by the subnet ID. Only include IPv4 subnets.
sub_sqls: SELECT s.NAME AS subnet_name, AVG(d.ORDER) AS avg_dns_order, VARIANCE(d.ORDER) AS dns_order_variance FROM SUBNETS AS s JOIN DNSNAMESERVERS AS d ON s.ID = d.SUBNET_ID WHERE s.IP_VERSION = 4 GROUP BY s.NAME ORDER BY dns_order_variance DESC;

SELECT r.DESTINATION, r.NEXTHOP, s.NAME AS subnet_name, s.CIDR AS subnet_cidr, p.FIRST_IP, p.LAST_IP, DENSE_RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY r.SUBNET_ID ORDER BY r.SUBNET_ID) AS window_column FROM SUBNETROUTES r JOIN SUBNETS s ON r.SUBNET_ID = s.ID JOIN IPALLOCATIONPOOLS p ON s.ID = p.SUBNET_ID WHERE s.IP_VERSION = 4

question: For IPv4 subnets that have routes with next hop 10.30.19.197/8, list each route’s destination and next hop along with the subnet name and CIDR, the allocation pool’s first and last IP, and the dense-rank within each subnet; also include, per subnet name, the range and variance of allocation-pool starting IPs (FIRST_IP) across that subnet’s allocation pools. Do not return any rounded answers.
sql: WITH FirstIpStatsBySubnet AS ( SELECT s.NAME AS subnet_name, MAX(p.FIRST_IP) - MIN(p.FIRST_IP) AS first_ip_range, VARIANCE(p.FIRST_IP) AS first_ip_variance FROM SUBNETROUTES r JOIN SUBNETS s ON r.SUBNET_ID = s.ID JOIN IPALLOCATIONPOOLS p ON s.ID = p.SUBNET_ID WHERE r.NEXTHOP = '10.30.19.197/8' GROUP BY s.NAME ORDER BY first_ip_range DESC ), SubnetRoutePoolDetails AS ( SELECT r.DESTINATION, r.NEXTHOP, s.NAME AS subnet_name, s.CIDR AS subnet_cidr, p.FIRST_IP, p.LAST_IP, DENSE_RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY r.SUBNET_ID ORDER BY r.SUBNET_ID) AS window_column FROM SUBNETROUTES r JOIN SUBNETS s ON r.SUBNET_ID = s.ID JOIN IPALLOCATIONPOOLS p ON s.ID = p.SUBNET_ID WHERE s.IP_VERSION = 4 ), SubnetRoutePoolDetailsFiltered AS ( SELECT * FROM SubnetRoutePoolDetails WHERE NEXTHOP = '10.30.19.197/8' ) SELECT srpd.subnet_name, srpd.subnet_cidr, srpd.DESTINATION, srpd.NEXTHOP, srpd.FIRST_IP, srpd.LAST_IP, srpd.window_column, fips.first_ip_range, fips.first_ip_variance FROM SubnetRoutePoolDetailsFiltered srpd JOIN FirstIpStatsBySubnet fips ON srpd.subnet_name = fips.subnet_name ORDER BY fips.first_ip_range DESC, srpd.subnet_name, srpd.DESTINATION;
sub_questions: For each subnet name, calculate the range and variance of the allocation pool starting IP addresses (FIRST_IP) across that subnet’s IP allocation pools, considering only routes whose next hop is 10.30.19.197/8.

Show each subnet route’s destination and next hop together with the subnet name and CIDR, plus the allocation pool’s first and last IP. Also include a dense rank within each subnet (partitioned by subnet ID) ordered by the subnet ID. Only include IPv4 subnets.
sub_sqls: SELECT s.NAME AS subnet_name, MAX(p.FIRST_IP) - MIN(p.FIRST_IP) AS first_ip_range, VARIANCE(p.FIRST_IP) AS first_ip_variance FROM SUBNETROUTES r JOIN SUBNETS s ON r.SUBNET_ID = s.ID JOIN IPALLOCATIONPOOLS p ON s.ID = p.SUBNET_ID WHERE r.NEXTHOP = '10.30.19.197/8' GROUP BY s.NAME ORDER BY first_ip_range DESC;

SELECT r.DESTINATION, r.NEXTHOP, s.NAME AS subnet_name, s.CIDR AS subnet_cidr, p.FIRST_IP, p.LAST_IP, DENSE_RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY r.SUBNET_ID ORDER BY r.SUBNET_ID) AS window_column FROM SUBNETROUTES r JOIN SUBNETS s ON r.SUBNET_ID = s.ID JOIN IPALLOCATIONPOOLS p ON s.ID = p.SUBNET_ID WHERE s.IP_VERSION = 4

question: For each port that is administratively up (admin_state_up = 1) and is bound to a security group, list the port ID, tenant ID, port name, MAC address, the number of security group bindings, the total number of DNS records associated with the port, the number of port security bindings, and the total number of times port security is enabled across those bindings. Do not return any rounded answers.
sql: WITH SecurityGroupBoundPorts AS ( SELECT p.id AS port_id, p.tenant_id, p.name AS port_name, COUNT(sgpb.security_group_id) AS security_group_binding_count, SUM(CASE WHEN pd.port_id IS NULL THEN 0 ELSE 1 END) AS dns_record_count FROM SECURITYGROUPPORTBINDINGS sgpb JOIN PORTS p ON sgpb.port_id = p.id LEFT JOIN PORTDNSES pd ON p.id = pd.port_id WHERE p.admin_state_up = 1 GROUP BY p.id, p.tenant_id, p.name ), PortSecurityBindingsSummary AS ( SELECT p.id AS port_id, p.tenant_id, p.mac_address, COUNT(psb.port_id) AS binding_count, SUM(CASE WHEN psb.port_security_enabled THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS port_security_enabled_total FROM ports p JOIN portsecuritybindings psb ON p.id = psb.port_id WHERE p.admin_state_up = 1 GROUP BY p.id, p.tenant_id, p.mac_address ), CombinedPortDetails AS ( SELECT sg.port_id, sg.tenant_id, sg.port_name, ps.mac_address, sg.security_group_binding_count, sg.dns_record_count, ps.binding_count AS port_security_binding_count, ps.port_security_enabled_total FROM SecurityGroupBoundPorts sg JOIN PortSecurityBindingsSummary ps ON sg.port_id = ps.port_id ) SELECT port_id, tenant_id, port_name, mac_address, security_group_binding_count, dns_record_count, port_security_binding_count, port_security_enabled_total FROM CombinedPortDetails ORDER BY tenant_id, port_id;
sub_questions: For each port that is bound to a security group and has admin_state_up = 1, list the port ID, tenant ID, port name, and the number of security group bindings for that port along with the total number of DNS records associated with the port.

For each port that is administratively up, list the port ID, tenant ID, MAC address, the number of port security bindings on that port, and the total number of times port security is enabled across those bindings.
sub_sqls: SELECT p.id AS port_id, p.tenant_id, p.name AS port_name, COUNT(sgpb.security_group_id) AS security_group_binding_count, SUM(CASE WHEN pd.port_id IS NULL THEN 0 ELSE 1 END) AS dns_record_count FROM SECURITYGROUPPORTBINDINGS sgpb JOIN PORTS p ON sgpb.port_id = p.id LEFT JOIN PORTDNSES pd ON p.id = pd.port_id WHERE p.admin_state_up = 1 GROUP BY p.id, p.tenant_id, p.name;

SELECT p.id AS port_id, p.tenant_id, p.mac_address, COUNT(psb.port_id) AS binding_count, SUM(CASE WHEN psb.port_security_enabled THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS port_security_enabled_total FROM ports p JOIN portsecuritybindings psb ON p.id = psb.port_id WHERE p.admin_state_up = 1 GROUP BY p.id, p.tenant_id, p.mac_address;

question: For networks that are marked as default external networks (IS_DEFAULT = 0), list each network’s ID, tenant, name, status, admin state, MTU, and the tenant’s minimum MTU, but only for port status/device owner groups (considering only ports whose standard attribute resource type is 'ports') where the group’s port count is greater than 75% of that tenant’s total port count; also return the group’s port status, device owner, port count, and earliest standard attribute updated timestamp. Do not return any rounded answers.
sql: WITH PortStatusOwnerStats AS (SELECT p.STATUS AS port_status, p.DEVICE_OWNER AS device_owner, COUNT(p.ID) AS port_count, MIN(sa.UPDATED_AT) AS earliest_standard_attr_update FROM PORTS p JOIN STANDARDATTRIBUTES sa ON sa.ID = p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID WHERE sa.RESOURCE_TYPE = 'ports' GROUP BY p.STATUS, p.DEVICE_OWNER), DefaultExternalNetworks AS (SELECT e.NETWORK_ID, e.IS_DEFAULT, n.TENANT_ID, n.NAME, n.STATUS, n.ADMIN_STATE_UP, n.MTU, n.STANDARD_ATTR_ID, MIN(n.MTU) OVER (PARTITION BY n.TENANT_ID ORDER BY n.TENANT_ID) AS window_column FROM EXTERNALNETWORKS e JOIN NETWORKS n ON e.NETWORK_ID = n.ID WHERE e.IS_DEFAULT = 0), TenantPortCounts AS ( SELECT n.TENANT_ID, COUNT(p.ID) AS tenant_port_count FROM NETWORKS n JOIN PORTS p ON p.NETWORK_ID = n.ID JOIN STANDARDATTRIBUTES sa ON sa.ID = p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID WHERE sa.RESOURCE_TYPE = 'ports' GROUP BY n.TENANT_ID ) SELECT den.NETWORK_ID, den.TENANT_ID, den.NAME AS network_name, den.STATUS AS network_status, den.ADMIN_STATE_UP, den.MTU, den.window_column AS tenant_min_mtu, tpc.tenant_port_count, pso.port_status, pso.device_owner, pso.port_count, pso.earliest_standard_attr_update FROM DefaultExternalNetworks den JOIN TenantPortCounts tpc ON tpc.TENANT_ID = den.TENANT_ID CROSS JOIN PortStatusOwnerStats pso WHERE pso.port_count > (0.75 * tpc.tenant_port_count);
sub_questions: For each port status and device owner, considering only ports whose standard attribute resource type is 'ports', return the number of ports and the earliest (minimum) standard attribute updated timestamp.

For networks that are marked as default external networks, show the network ID, whether it is default, the tenant ID, network name, status, admin state up flag, MTU, standard attribute ID, and the minimum MTU within each tenant (partitioned and ordered by tenant ID).
sub_sqls: SELECT p.STATUS AS port_status, p.DEVICE_OWNER AS device_owner, COUNT(p.ID) AS port_count, MIN(sa.UPDATED_AT) AS earliest_standard_attr_update FROM PORTS p JOIN STANDARDATTRIBUTES sa ON sa.ID = p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID WHERE sa.RESOURCE_TYPE = 'ports' GROUP BY p.STATUS, p.DEVICE_OWNER;

SELECT e.NETWORK_ID, e.IS_DEFAULT, n.TENANT_ID, n.NAME, n.STATUS, n.ADMIN_STATE_UP, n.MTU, n.STANDARD_ATTR_ID, MIN(n.MTU) OVER (PARTITION BY n.TENANT_ID ORDER BY n.TENANT_ID) AS window_column FROM EXTERNALNETWORKS e JOIN NETWORKS n ON e.NETWORK_ID = n.ID WHERE e.IS_DEFAULT = 0;

question: For default external networks (IS_DEFAULT = 0) that are ACTIVE, show the default flag, the total number of distinct active external networks, the average dense rank within the default-flag group ordered by network ID, and the average dense rank ordered by RBAC action (using a window frame of the current row and the 2 preceding rows). Do not return any rounded answers.
sql: WITH ExternalActiveNetworks AS ( SELECT t0.NETWORK_ID, t0.IS_DEFAULT, t1.NAME, t1.STATUS, DENSE_RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY t0.IS_DEFAULT ORDER BY t0.NETWORK_ID) AS window_column FROM EXTERNALNETWORKS t0 JOIN NETWORKS t1 ON t0.NETWORK_ID = t1.ID WHERE t1.STATUS = 'ACTIVE' ), DefaultExternalNetworkRbacRanks AS ( SELECT n.NAME, dense_rank() OVER ( ORDER BY r.ACTION ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW ) AS window_column FROM EXTERNALNETWORKS e JOIN NETWORKS n ON e.NETWORK_ID = n.ID JOIN NETWORKRBACS r ON n.ID = r.OBJECT_ID WHERE e.IS_DEFAULT = 0 ) SELECT ean.IS_DEFAULT, COUNT(DISTINCT ean.NETWORK_ID) AS Active_External_Networks, AVG(ean.window_column * 1.0) AS Avg_Dense_Rank_By_NetworkId_Within_DefaultFlag, AVG(denrr.window_column * 1.0) AS Avg_Dense_Rank_By_Rbac_Action_For_Default_External_Networks FROM ExternalActiveNetworks ean LEFT JOIN DefaultExternalNetworkRbacRanks denrr ON ean.NAME = denrr.NAME WHERE ean.IS_DEFAULT = 0 GROUP BY ean.IS_DEFAULT ORDER BY Active_External_Networks DESC;
sub_questions: Show each external network’s ID, whether it is the default external network, the network name, and the network status, along with a dense rank within each default-flag group ordered by the network ID.

For networks that are marked as default external networks (IS_DEFAULT = 0), list the network name and the dense rank of each network when ordered by the RBAC action, using a window frame of the current row and the 2 preceding rows.
sub_sqls: SELECT t0.NETWORK_ID, t0.IS_DEFAULT, t1.NAME, t1.STATUS, DENSE_RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY t0.IS_DEFAULT ORDER BY t0.NETWORK_ID) AS window_column FROM EXTERNALNETWORKS t0 JOIN NETWORKS t1 ON t0.NETWORK_ID = t1.ID WHERE t1.STATUS = 'ACTIVE';

SELECT n.NAME, dense_rank() OVER ( ORDER BY r.ACTION ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW ) AS window_column FROM EXTERNALNETWORKS e JOIN NETWORKS n ON e.NETWORK_ID = n.ID JOIN NETWORKRBACS r ON n.ID = r.OBJECT_ID WHERE e.IS_DEFAULT = 0;

question: For DOWN ports, list the port ID, tenant ID, port name, network ID, MAC address, device owner, allocated IP address, and the row number within each network (ordered by port ID), along with the DOWN-status range, variance, and standard deviation (using STDDEV only and never STDDEV_POP) of port security binding counts per port (considering only ports with at least one binding) and the total number of DOWN ports in the same network. Do not return any rounded answers.
sql: WITH DownPortsWithIPs AS ( SELECT p.ID AS port_id, p.TENANT_ID AS tenant_id, p.NAME AS port_name, p.NETWORK_ID AS network_id, p.MAC_ADDRESS AS mac_address, p.DEVICE_OWNER AS device_owner, ia.IP_ADDRESS AS ip_address, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY p.NETWORK_ID ORDER BY p.ID) AS window_column FROM PORTS p JOIN IPALLOCATIONS ia ON p.ID = ia.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' ), PortSecurityBindingStatsByStatus AS ( SELECT p.status, MAX(ps.binding_count) - MIN(ps.binding_count) AS binding_count_range, VARIANCE(ps.binding_count) AS binding_count_variance, STDDEV(ps.binding_count) AS binding_count_stddev FROM ports AS p JOIN ( SELECT p2.id AS port_id, COUNT(*) AS binding_count FROM ports AS p2 JOIN portsecuritybindings AS b ON p2.id = b.port_id GROUP BY p2.id ) AS ps ON p.id = ps.port_id GROUP BY p.status ORDER BY binding_count_range DESC ), DownPortCountsByNetwork AS ( SELECT network_id, COUNT(DISTINCT port_id) AS down_port_count FROM DownPortsWithIPs GROUP BY network_id ) SELECT d.port_id, d.tenant_id, d.port_name, d.network_id, d.mac_address, d.device_owner, d.ip_address, d.window_column, ps.status, ps.binding_count_range, ps.binding_count_variance, ps.binding_count_stddev, c.down_port_count FROM DownPortsWithIPs d JOIN PortSecurityBindingStatsByStatus ps ON ps.status = 'DOWN' JOIN DownPortCountsByNetwork c ON d.network_id = c.network_id ORDER BY d.network_id, d.window_column;
sub_questions: For ports that are DOWN, list the port ID, tenant ID, port name, network ID, MAC address, device owner, and the allocated IP address, and assign row numbers within each network ordered by port ID.

For each port status, report the status and the range, variance, and standard deviation of the number of port security bindings per port (considering only ports that have at least one port security binding).
sub_sqls: SELECT p.ID AS port_id, p.TENANT_ID AS tenant_id, p.NAME AS port_name, p.NETWORK_ID AS network_id, p.MAC_ADDRESS AS mac_address, p.DEVICE_OWNER AS device_owner, ia.IP_ADDRESS AS ip_address, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY p.NETWORK_ID ORDER BY p.ID) AS window_column FROM PORTS p JOIN IPALLOCATIONS ia ON p.ID = ia.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN';

SELECT p.status, MAX(ps.binding_count) - MIN(ps.binding_count) AS binding_count_range, VARIANCE(ps.binding_count) AS binding_count_variance, STDDEV(ps.binding_count) AS binding_count_stddev FROM ports AS p JOIN ( SELECT p2.id AS port_id, COUNT(*) AS binding_count FROM ports AS p2 JOIN portsecuritybindings AS b ON p2.id = b.port_id GROUP BY p2.id ) AS ps ON p.id = ps.port_id GROUP BY p.status ORDER BY binding_count_range DESC;

question: For ports that are DOWN, show the port ID, tenant ID, and MAC address with the running sum of the port’s standard attribute ID within each security group, and also include (for the same MAC address) the administratively-up port name, port security status, and the row number ordered by MAC address using a window frame of 2 preceding rows and 1 following row. Do not return any rounded answers.
sql: WITH DownPortsBySecurityGroup AS (SELECT p.ID AS port_id, p.TENANT_ID AS tenant_id, p.MAC_ADDRESS AS mac_address, SUM(p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID) OVER ( PARTITION BY sgpb.SECURITY_GROUP_ID ORDER BY p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID ) AS window_column FROM SECURITYGROUPPORTBINDINGS AS sgpb JOIN PORTS AS p ON sgpb.PORT_ID = p.ID JOIN PORTSECURITYBINDINGS AS psb ON p.ID = psb.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN'), AdminUpPortsSecurity AS (SELECT p.NAME AS port_name, p.MAC_ADDRESS AS mac_address, psb.PORT_SECURITY_ENABLED AS port_security_enabled, ROW_NUMBER() OVER ( ORDER BY p.MAC_ADDRESS ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND 1 FOLLOWING ) AS window_column FROM PORTS AS p JOIN PORTSECURITYBINDINGS AS psb ON p.ID = psb.PORT_ID WHERE p.ADMIN_STATE_UP = 1) SELECT dpsg.port_id, dpsg.tenant_id, dpsg.mac_address, dpsg.window_column AS down_ports_running_sum_standard_attr_id, aups.port_name, aups.port_security_enabled, aups.window_column AS admin_up_ports_row_number FROM DownPortsBySecurityGroup dpsg JOIN AdminUpPortsSecurity aups ON dpsg.mac_address = aups.mac_address ORDER BY dpsg.port_id;
sub_questions: For ports that are DOWN, show the port ID, tenant ID, and MAC address, along with the running sum of the port’s standard attribute ID within each security group, ordered by standard attribute ID.

For ports that are administratively up, list the port name, MAC address, and port security status, and assign row numbers ordered by MAC address using a window frame of 2 preceding rows and 1 following row.
sub_sqls: SELECT p.ID AS port_id, p.TENANT_ID AS tenant_id, p.MAC_ADDRESS AS mac_address, SUM(p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID) OVER ( PARTITION BY sgpb.SECURITY_GROUP_ID ORDER BY p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID ) AS window_column FROM SECURITYGROUPPORTBINDINGS AS sgpb JOIN PORTS AS p ON sgpb.PORT_ID = p.ID JOIN PORTSECURITYBINDINGS AS psb ON p.ID = psb.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN';

SELECT p.NAME AS port_name, p.MAC_ADDRESS AS mac_address, psb.PORT_SECURITY_ENABLED AS port_security_enabled, ROW_NUMBER() OVER ( ORDER BY p.MAC_ADDRESS ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND 1 FOLLOWING ) AS window_column FROM PORTS AS p JOIN PORTSECURITYBINDINGS AS psb ON p.ID = psb.PORT_ID WHERE p.ADMIN_STATE_UP = 1;

question: For DOWN ports, for each device owner where the ports are bound to a security group, return the distinct port count and the minimum standard attribute ID, and also include (for the same port status) the variance of standard attribute IDs across ports that have an IP allocation. Do not return any rounded answers.
sql: WITH PortSecurityGroupStats AS ( SELECT p.STATUS AS port_status, p.DEVICE_OWNER AS device_owner, COUNT(DISTINCT p.ID) AS port_count, MIN(p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID) AS min_standard_attr_id FROM PORTS p JOIN SECURITYGROUPPORTBINDINGS spb ON p.ID = spb.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' GROUP BY p.STATUS, p.DEVICE_OWNER ), PortStatusStdAttrVariance AS ( SELECT p.STATUS, VARIANCE(p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID) AS standard_attr_id_variance FROM PORTS AS p JOIN IPALLOCATIONS AS ia ON p.ID = ia.PORT_ID WHERE p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID IS NOT NULL GROUP BY p.STATUS ORDER BY standard_attr_id_variance DESC ) SELECT psgs.port_status, psgs.device_owner, psgs.port_count, psgs.min_standard_attr_id, pssav.standard_attr_id_variance FROM PortSecurityGroupStats psgs JOIN PortStatusStdAttrVariance pssav ON psgs.port_status = pssav.STATUS ORDER BY psgs.port_status, psgs.device_owner;

SELECT p.STATUS, VARIANCE(p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID) AS standard_attr_id_variance FROM PORTS AS p JOIN IPALLOCATIONS AS ia ON p.ID = ia.PORT_ID WHERE p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID IS NOT NULL GROUP BY p.STATUS ORDER BY standard_attr_id_variance DESC;

question: For the top 10 (port status, device owner) combinations with the most ports that are admin_state_up = 1, bound to a security group, and whose standard attribute resource type is 'ports', show the port status, device owner, count of such bound admin-up ports, the total number of ports for that status/owner with resource type 'ports', the earliest standard-attribute updated timestamp, and the total security-group bindings and DNS records across those bound admin-up ports. Do not return any rounded answers.
sql: WITH port_status_owner_stats AS ( SELECT p.STATUS AS port_status, p.DEVICE_OWNER AS device_owner, COUNT(p.ID) AS port_count, MIN(sa.UPDATED_AT) AS earliest_standard_attr_update FROM PORTS p JOIN STANDARDATTRIBUTES sa ON sa.ID = p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID WHERE sa.RESOURCE_TYPE = 'ports' GROUP BY p.STATUS, p.DEVICE_OWNER ), bound_admin_ports AS ( SELECT p.id AS port_id, p.tenant_id, p.name AS port_name, COUNT(sgpb.security_group_id) AS security_group_binding_count, SUM(CASE WHEN pd.port_id IS NULL THEN 0 ELSE 1 END) AS dns_record_count FROM SECURITYGROUPPORTBINDINGS sgpb JOIN PORTS p ON sgpb.port_id = p.id LEFT JOIN PORTDNSES pd ON p.id = pd.port_id WHERE p.admin_state_up = 1 GROUP BY p.id, p.tenant_id, p.name ), top10_status_owner_by_bound_ports AS ( SELECT p.STATUS AS port_status, p.DEVICE_OWNER AS device_owner, COUNT(DISTINCT p.ID) AS bound_admin_port_count FROM PORTS p JOIN STANDARDATTRIBUTES sa ON sa.ID = p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID JOIN SECURITYGROUPPORTBINDINGS sgpb ON sgpb.port_id = p.id WHERE sa.RESOURCE_TYPE = 'ports' AND p.admin_state_up = 1 GROUP BY p.STATUS, p.DEVICE_OWNER ORDER BY bound_admin_port_count DESC LIMIT 10 ) SELECT t.port_status, t.device_owner, t.bound_admin_port_count, psos.port_count AS total_ports_with_standard_attr_resource_type_ports, psos.earliest_standard_attr_update, SUM(bap.security_group_binding_count) AS total_security_group_bindings_across_bound_admin_ports, SUM(bap.dns_record_count) AS total_dns_records_across_bound_admin_ports FROM top10_status_owner_by_bound_ports t JOIN port_status_owner_stats psos ON psos.port_status = t.port_status AND ( (psos.device_owner = t.device_owner) OR (psos.device_owner IS NULL AND t.device_owner IS NULL) ) JOIN PORTS p ON p.STATUS = t.port_status AND ( (p.DEVICE_OWNER = t.device_owner) OR (p.DEVICE_OWNER IS NULL AND t.device_owner IS NULL) ) JOIN STANDARDATTRIBUTES sa ON sa.ID = p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID AND sa.RESOURCE_TYPE = 'ports' JOIN bound_admin_ports bap ON bap.port_id = p.id GROUP BY t.port_status, t.device_owner, t.bound_admin_port_count, psos.port_count, psos.earliest_standard_attr_update ORDER BY t.bound_admin_port_count DESC;

question: For ports that are DOWN, list the port name, MAC address, admin_state_up flag, binding host, VIF type, and the average admin_state_up over a window of 2 preceding and 2 following rows (partitioned by VIF type and ordered by MAC address), and also include the DOWN-status range, variance, and standard deviation (using STDDEV only and never STDDEV_POP) of the number of port security bindings per port (considering only ports with at least one port security binding). Do not return any rounded answers.
sql: WITH down_ports_window AS ( SELECT p.NAME, p.MAC_ADDRESS, p.ADMIN_STATE_UP, b.HOST, b.VIF_TYPE, AVG(p.ADMIN_STATE_UP) OVER ( PARTITION BY b.VIF_TYPE ORDER BY p.MAC_ADDRESS ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND 2 FOLLOWING ) AS window_column FROM PORTS AS p JOIN ML2_PORT_BINDINGS AS b ON p.ID = b.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' ORDER BY p.MAC_ADDRESS ), status_binding_stats AS ( SELECT p.status, MAX(ps.binding_count) - MIN(ps.binding_count) AS binding_count_range, VARIANCE(ps.binding_count) AS binding_count_variance, STDDEV(ps.binding_count) AS binding_count_stddev FROM ports AS p JOIN ( SELECT p2.id AS port_id, COUNT(*) AS binding_count FROM ports AS p2 JOIN portsecuritybindings AS b ON p2.id = b.port_id GROUP BY p2.id ) AS ps ON p.id = ps.port_id GROUP BY p.status ORDER BY binding_count_range DESC ) SELECT dpw.NAME, dpw.MAC_ADDRESS, dpw.ADMIN_STATE_UP, dpw.HOST, dpw.VIF_TYPE, dpw.window_column, sbs.status, sbs.binding_count_range, sbs.binding_count_variance, sbs.binding_count_stddev FROM down_ports_window AS dpw CROSS JOIN status_binding_stats AS sbs WHERE sbs.status = 'DOWN' ORDER BY dpw.MAC_ADDRESS;

sql: WITH subq1 AS ( SELECT p.STATUS AS port_status, p.DEVICE_OWNER AS device_owner, COUNT(DISTINCT p.ID) AS port_count, MIN(p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID) AS min_standard_attr_id FROM PORTS p JOIN SECURITYGROUPPORTBINDINGS spb ON p.ID = spb.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' GROUP BY p.STATUS, p.DEVICE_OWNER ), subq2 AS ( SELECT p.NAME, p.NETWORK_ID, p.MAC_ADDRESS, p.ADMIN_STATE_UP, p.STATUS, p.DEVICE_OWNER, s.SECURITY_GROUP_ID, MIN(p.ADMIN_STATE_UP) OVER ( ORDER BY p.ID ROWS BETWEEN 3 PRECEDING AND 1 FOLLOWING ) AS window_column FROM PORTS AS p JOIN SECURITYGROUPPORTBINDINGS AS s ON p.ID = s.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' ) SELECT subq1.port_status, subq1.device_owner, subq1.port_count, subq1.min_standard_attr_id, subq2.NAME AS port_name, subq2.NETWORK_ID, subq2.MAC_ADDRESS, subq2.ADMIN_STATE_UP, subq2.SECURITY_GROUP_ID, subq2.window_column FROM subq1 JOIN subq2 ON subq1.port_status = subq2.STATUS AND subq1.device_owner = subq2.DEVICE_OWNER ORDER BY subq1.port_count DESC, subq1.device_owner, subq2.NETWORK_ID, subq2.NAME;

sql: WITH DownPortsWithBindings AS (SELECT p.NAME, p.MAC_ADDRESS, p.ADMIN_STATE_UP, b.HOST, b.VIF_TYPE, AVG(p.ADMIN_STATE_UP) OVER ( PARTITION BY b.VIF_TYPE ORDER BY p.MAC_ADDRESS ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND 2 FOLLOWING ) AS window_column FROM PORTS AS p JOIN ML2_PORT_BINDINGS AS b ON p.ID = b.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' ORDER BY p.MAC_ADDRESS), DownPortsWithSecurityGroups AS (SELECT p.NAME, p.NETWORK_ID, p.MAC_ADDRESS, p.ADMIN_STATE_UP, p.STATUS, p.DEVICE_OWNER, s.SECURITY_GROUP_ID, MIN(p.ADMIN_STATE_UP) OVER ( ORDER BY p.ID ROWS BETWEEN 3 PRECEDING AND 1 FOLLOWING ) AS window_column FROM PORTS AS p JOIN SECURITYGROUPPORTBINDINGS AS s ON p.ID = s.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN') SELECT dpb.NAME AS port_name, dpsg.NETWORK_ID, dpb.MAC_ADDRESS, dpb.ADMIN_STATE_UP, dpsg.STATUS, dpsg.DEVICE_OWNER, dpb.HOST AS binding_host, dpb.VIF_TYPE, dpsg.SECURITY_GROUP_ID AS bound_security_group_id, dpb.window_column AS avg_admin_state_up_viftype_mac_window, dpsg.window_column AS min_admin_state_up_portid_window FROM DownPortsWithBindings dpb JOIN DownPortsWithSecurityGroups dpsg ON dpb.NAME = dpsg.NAME AND dpb.MAC_ADDRESS = dpsg.MAC_ADDRESS AND dpb.ADMIN_STATE_UP = dpsg.ADMIN_STATE_UP ORDER BY dpb.MAC_ADDRESS;

sql: WITH SecurityGroupBoundPorts AS ( SELECT p.ID AS port_id, p.STATUS AS port_status, ia.IP_ADDRESS AS ip_address, SUM(p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID) OVER ( PARTITION BY p.NETWORK_ID ORDER BY p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID ) AS window_column FROM SECURITYGROUPPORTBINDINGS sgpb JOIN PORTS p ON sgpb.PORT_ID = p.ID JOIN IPALLOCATIONS ia ON p.ID = ia.PORT_ID WHERE sgpb.SECURITY_GROUP_ID = '0008e629-5619-41e0-b86c-4eecfeaacb6c' ), AdminUpPortSecurityStats AS ( SELECT p.id AS port_id, p.tenant_id, p.mac_address, COUNT(psb.port_id) AS binding_count, SUM(CASE WHEN psb.port_security_enabled THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS port_security_enabled_total FROM ports p JOIN portsecuritybindings psb ON p.id = psb.port_id WHERE p.admin_state_up = 1 GROUP BY p.id, p.tenant_id, p.mac_address ) SELECT sg.port_id, sg.port_status, sg.ip_address, sg.window_column, aup.tenant_id, aup.mac_address, aup.binding_count, aup.port_security_enabled_total FROM SecurityGroupBoundPorts sg JOIN AdminUpPortSecurityStats aup ON sg.port_id = aup.port_id ORDER BY sg.port_id;

sql: WITH SecurityGroupAndDnsByPort AS ( SELECT p.id AS port_id, p.tenant_id, p.name AS port_name, COUNT(sgpb.security_group_id) AS security_group_binding_count, SUM(CASE WHEN pd.port_id IS NULL THEN 0 ELSE 1 END) AS dns_record_count FROM SECURITYGROUPPORTBINDINGS sgpb JOIN PORTS p ON sgpb.port_id = p.id LEFT JOIN PORTDNSES pd ON p.id = pd.port_id WHERE p.admin_state_up = 1 GROUP BY p.id, p.tenant_id, p.name ), DownPortBindings AS ( SELECT p.ID AS port_id, p.NAME AS port_name, p.MAC_ADDRESS AS mac_address, b.HOST AS binding_host, b.VIF_TYPE AS vif_type, RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY p.STATUS ORDER BY p.ID) AS window_column FROM PORTS p JOIN ML2_PORT_BINDINGS b ON p.ID = b.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' ) SELECT sgd.port_id, sgd.tenant_id, sgd.port_name, sgd.security_group_binding_count, sgd.dns_record_count, dpb.mac_address, dpb.binding_host, dpb.vif_type, dpb.window_column FROM SecurityGroupAndDnsByPort sgd JOIN DownPortBindings dpb ON sgd.port_id = dpb.port_id;

question: For allowed address pairs on the port with ID `25d421c1-c76d-4c26-9550-9f871a1d5034` (restricted to ports that are administratively up), list the allowed address pair MAC address, allowed address pair IP address, port ID, the security group ID bound to that port, the running average of the port’s standard attribute ID within the port ordered by allowed address pair IP address, the tenant ID and port MAC address, the number of port security bindings, the total number of times port security is enabled across those bindings, and the normalized port-security-enabled ratio (enabled total divided by binding count).
sql: WITH AllowedPairsAndSecurityGroups AS ( SELECT aap.MAC_ADDRESS AS allowed_mac_address, aap.IP_ADDRESS AS allowed_ip_address, p.ID AS port_id, sgpb.SECURITY_GROUP_ID AS security_group_id, AVG(p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID) OVER ( PARTITION BY p.ID ORDER BY aap.IP_ADDRESS ) AS window_column FROM SECURITYGROUPPORTBINDINGS AS sgpb JOIN PORTS AS p ON sgpb.PORT_ID = p.ID JOIN ALLOWEDADDRESSPAIRS AS aap ON p.ID = aap.PORT_ID WHERE p.ID = '25d421c1-c76d-4c26-9550-9f871a1d5034' ORDER BY aap.IP_ADDRESS ), AdminUpPortSecurityStats AS ( SELECT p.id AS port_id, p.tenant_id, p.mac_address, COUNT(psb.port_id) AS binding_count, SUM(CASE WHEN psb.port_security_enabled THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS port_security_enabled_total FROM ports p JOIN portsecuritybindings psb ON p.id = psb.port_id WHERE p.admin_state_up = 1 GROUP BY p.id, p.tenant_id, p.mac_address ) SELECT apsg.allowed_mac_address, apsg.allowed_ip_address, apsg.port_id, apsg.security_group_id, apsg.window_column, aup.tenant_id, aup.mac_address AS port_mac_address, aup.binding_count, aup.port_security_enabled_total, ROUND(aup.port_security_enabled_total / NULLIF(aup.binding_count, 0), 2) AS normalized_port_security_enabled_ratio FROM AllowedPairsAndSecurityGroups apsg JOIN AdminUpPortSecurityStats aup ON aup.port_id = apsg.port_id WHERE apsg.port_id = '25d421c1-c76d-4c26-9550-9f871a1d5034' ORDER BY normalized_port_security_enabled_ratio DESC, apsg.allowed_ip_address;

question: For ports whose standard attribute resource type is 'ports' and that are in status 'DOWN' with an IP allocation, list each port status, device owner, and binding host along with (a) the total number of ports and the earliest standard-attribute updated timestamp for that same status/owner group, and (b) the variance of STANDARD_ATTR_ID for that host. Do not return any rounded answers.
sql: WITH PortStatusOwnerStats AS (SELECT p.STATUS AS port_status, p.DEVICE_OWNER AS device_owner, COUNT(p.ID) AS port_count, MIN(sa.UPDATED_AT) AS earliest_standard_attr_update FROM PORTS p JOIN STANDARDATTRIBUTES sa ON sa.ID = p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID WHERE sa.RESOURCE_TYPE = 'ports' GROUP BY p.STATUS, p.DEVICE_OWNER), HostStandardAttrVariance AS (SELECT b.HOST, VARIANCE(p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID) AS standard_attr_id_variance FROM ML2_PORT_BINDINGS AS b JOIN PORTS AS p ON b.PORT_ID = p.ID JOIN IPALLOCATIONS AS ia ON p.ID = ia.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' AND ia.PORT_ID IS NOT NULL GROUP BY b.HOST ORDER BY standard_attr_id_variance DESC), DownPortsWithIPAndPortsResourceType AS ( SELECT p.STATUS AS port_status, p.DEVICE_OWNER AS device_owner, b.HOST FROM PORTS p JOIN STANDARDATTRIBUTES sa ON sa.ID = p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID JOIN IPALLOCATIONS ia ON p.ID = ia.PORT_ID JOIN ML2_PORT_BINDINGS b ON b.PORT_ID = p.ID WHERE sa.RESOURCE_TYPE = 'ports' AND p.STATUS = 'DOWN' AND ia.PORT_ID IS NOT NULL ) SELECT d.port_status, d.device_owner, psos.port_count, psos.earliest_standard_attr_update, d.host, hsav.standard_attr_id_variance FROM DownPortsWithIPAndPortsResourceType d JOIN PortStatusOwnerStats psos ON psos.port_status = d.port_status AND psos.device_owner = d.device_owner JOIN HostStandardAttrVariance hsav ON hsav.HOST = d.host ORDER BY d.port_status, d.device_owner, hsav.standard_attr_id_variance DESC, d.host;

sql: WITH SG_Bound_Ports AS ( SELECT p.ID AS port_id, p.STATUS AS port_status, ia.IP_ADDRESS AS ip_address, SUM(p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID) OVER ( PARTITION BY p.NETWORK_ID ORDER BY p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID ) AS window_column FROM SECURITYGROUPPORTBINDINGS sgpb JOIN PORTS p ON sgpb.PORT_ID = p.ID JOIN IPALLOCATIONS ia ON p.ID = ia.PORT_ID WHERE sgpb.SECURITY_GROUP_ID = '0008e629-5619-41e0-b86c-4eecfeaacb6c' ), Down_Ports_DenseRank AS ( SELECT p.id AS port_id, dense_rank() OVER ( ORDER BY psb.port_security_enabled ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW ) AS window_column FROM ports AS p JOIN portsecuritybindings AS psb ON p.id = psb.port_id WHERE p.status = 'DOWN' ) SELECT sbp.port_id, sbp.port_status, sbp.ip_address, sbp.window_column AS running_sum_standard_attr_id_within_network, dpdr.window_column AS dense_rank_by_port_security_for_down_ports FROM SG_Bound_Ports sbp JOIN Down_Ports_DenseRank dpdr ON sbp.port_id = dpdr.port_id WHERE sbp.port_status = 'DOWN' ORDER BY sbp.port_id;

sql: WITH PortDetailsForSecurityGroup AS ( SELECT p.ID AS port_id, p.STATUS AS port_status, ia.IP_ADDRESS AS ip_address, SUM(p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID) OVER ( PARTITION BY p.NETWORK_ID ORDER BY p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID ) AS window_column FROM SECURITYGROUPPORTBINDINGS sgpb JOIN PORTS p ON sgpb.PORT_ID = p.ID JOIN IPALLOCATIONS ia ON p.ID = ia.PORT_ID WHERE sgpb.SECURITY_GROUP_ID = '0008e629-5619-41e0-b86c-4eecfeaacb6c' ), PortSecurityBindingStatsByStatus AS ( SELECT p.status, MAX(ps.binding_count) - MIN(ps.binding_count) AS binding_count_range, VARIANCE(ps.binding_count) AS binding_count_variance, STDDEV(ps.binding_count) AS binding_count_stddev FROM ports AS p JOIN ( SELECT p2.id AS port_id, COUNT(*) AS binding_count FROM ports AS p2 JOIN portsecuritybindings AS b ON p2.id = b.port_id GROUP BY p2.id ) AS ps ON p.id = ps.port_id GROUP BY p.status ORDER BY binding_count_range DESC ), SecurityGroupPortStatusCounts AS ( SELECT p.STATUS AS port_status, COUNT(DISTINCT p.ID) AS ports_in_security_group FROM SECURITYGROUPPORTBINDINGS sgpb JOIN PORTS p ON sgpb.PORT_ID = p.ID WHERE sgpb.SECURITY_GROUP_ID = '0008e629-5619-41e0-b86c-4eecfeaacb6c' GROUP BY p.STATUS ) SELECT pd.port_id, pd.port_status, pd.ip_address, pd.window_column, pss.binding_count_range, pss.binding_count_variance, pss.binding_count_stddev, sgc.ports_in_security_group FROM PortDetailsForSecurityGroup pd JOIN PortSecurityBindingStatsByStatus pss ON pd.port_status = pss.status JOIN SecurityGroupPortStatusCounts sgc ON pd.port_status = sgc.port_status ORDER BY pd.port_status, pd.window_column, pd.port_id;

sql: WITH PortStatusOwnerStandardAttrAgg AS ( SELECT p.STATUS AS port_status, p.DEVICE_OWNER AS device_owner, COUNT(p.ID) AS port_count, MIN(sa.UPDATED_AT) AS earliest_standard_attr_update FROM PORTS p JOIN STANDARDATTRIBUTES sa ON sa.ID = p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID WHERE sa.RESOURCE_TYPE = 'ports' GROUP BY p.STATUS, p.DEVICE_OWNER ), AdminUpPortSecurityWindow AS ( SELECT p.NAME AS port_name, p.MAC_ADDRESS AS mac_address, psb.PORT_SECURITY_ENABLED AS port_security_enabled, ROW_NUMBER() OVER ( ORDER BY p.MAC_ADDRESS ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND 1 FOLLOWING ) AS window_column FROM PORTS AS p JOIN PORTSECURITYBINDINGS AS psb ON p.ID = psb.PORT_ID WHERE p.ADMIN_STATE_UP = 1 ) SELECT a.port_name, a.mac_address, a.port_security_enabled, a.window_column, s.port_status, s.device_owner, s.port_count, s.earliest_standard_attr_update FROM AdminUpPortSecurityWindow a JOIN PORTS p ON p.MAC_ADDRESS = a.mac_address JOIN STANDARDATTRIBUTES sa ON sa.ID = p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID JOIN PortStatusOwnerStandardAttrAgg s ON s.port_status = p.STATUS AND s.device_owner = p.DEVICE_OWNER WHERE sa.RESOURCE_TYPE = 'ports' ORDER BY a.mac_address, a.window_column;

sql: WITH down_ports_security_groups AS ( SELECT p.ID AS port_id, p.TENANT_ID AS tenant_id, p.MAC_ADDRESS AS mac_address, SUM(p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID) OVER ( PARTITION BY sgpb.SECURITY_GROUP_ID ORDER BY p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID ) AS window_column FROM SECURITYGROUPPORTBINDINGS AS sgpb JOIN PORTS AS p ON sgpb.PORT_ID = p.ID JOIN PORTSECURITYBINDINGS AS psb ON p.ID = psb.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' ), down_ports_ip_allocations AS ( SELECT p.ID AS port_id, p.NAME AS port_name, p.MAC_ADDRESS AS mac_address, ia.IP_ADDRESS AS ip_address, ia.SUBNET_ID AS subnet_id, AVG(p.ID) OVER (PARTITION BY p.ID ORDER BY ia.IP_ADDRESS) AS window_column FROM PORTS p JOIN IPALLOCATIONS ia ON p.ID = ia.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' ORDER BY ia.IP_ADDRESS ) SELECT dpsg.port_id, dpsg.tenant_id, dpsg.mac_address, dpsg.window_column AS security_group_running_sum_standard_attr_id, dpia.port_name, dpia.ip_address, dpia.subnet_id, dpia.window_column AS avg_port_id_over_ip_order FROM down_ports_security_groups dpsg JOIN down_ports_ip_allocations dpia ON dpia.port_id = dpsg.port_id AND dpia.mac_address = dpsg.mac_address;

sql: WITH DownPorts AS (SELECT p.ID AS port_id, p.NAME AS port_name, p.MAC_ADDRESS AS mac_address, b.HOST AS binding_host, b.VIF_TYPE AS vif_type, RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY p.STATUS ORDER BY p.ID) AS window_column FROM PORTS p JOIN ML2_PORT_BINDINGS b ON p.ID = b.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN'), ActiveNetworks AS (SELECT n.ID AS network_id, n.NAME AS network_name, n.TENANT_ID AS tenant_id, n.ADMIN_STATE_UP AS admin_state_up, n.MTU AS mtu, sa.UPDATED_AT AS standard_attr_updated_at, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY n.TENANT_ID ORDER BY n.NAME) AS window_column FROM NETWORKS n JOIN STANDARDATTRIBUTES sa ON sa.ID = n.STANDARD_ATTR_ID WHERE n.STATUS = 'ACTIVE') SELECT an.tenant_id, an.network_id, an.network_name, an.admin_state_up, an.mtu, an.standard_attr_updated_at, an.window_column AS network_row_number_within_tenant, dp.port_id, dp.port_name, dp.mac_address, dp.binding_host, dp.vif_type, dp.window_column AS port_rank_within_down_status FROM ActiveNetworks an JOIN PORTS p ON p.NETWORK_ID = an.network_id AND p.STATUS = 'DOWN' JOIN DownPorts dp ON dp.port_id = p.ID ORDER BY an.tenant_id, an.window_column, dp.port_id;

sql: WITH DownPortsWithSecurityGroupRank AS (SELECT p.id AS port_id, p.tenant_id, p.mac_address, sgpb.security_group_id, RANK() OVER ( PARTITION BY sgpb.security_group_id ORDER BY p.id ) AS window_column FROM SECURITYGROUPPORTBINDINGS AS sgpb JOIN PORTS AS p ON sgpb.port_id = p.id JOIN PORTSECURITYBINDINGS AS psb ON p.id = psb.port_id WHERE p.status = 'DOWN'), Drive59PortsWithRunningStdAttrSum AS (SELECT b.PORT_ID, p.TENANT_ID, p.MAC_ADDRESS, SUM(p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID) OVER ( PARTITION BY b.VIF_TYPE ORDER BY p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID ) AS window_column FROM ML2_PORT_BINDINGS AS b JOIN PORTS AS p ON b.PORT_ID = p.ID JOIN PORTSECURITYBINDINGS AS psb ON p.ID = psb.PORT_ID WHERE b.HOST = 'drive-59') SELECT d.port_id, d.tenant_id, d.mac_address, d.security_group_id, d.window_column AS security_group_port_rank, r.window_column AS running_std_attr_id_sum_within_vif_type FROM DownPortsWithSecurityGroupRank d JOIN Drive59PortsWithRunningStdAttrSum r ON d.port_id = r.PORT_ID ORDER BY d.security_group_id, d.port_id;

sql: WITH DownPortsBySecurityGroup AS ( SELECT p.ID AS port_id, p.TENANT_ID AS tenant_id, p.MAC_ADDRESS AS mac_address, SUM(p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID) OVER ( PARTITION BY sgpb.SECURITY_GROUP_ID ORDER BY p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID ) AS window_column FROM SECURITYGROUPPORTBINDINGS AS sgpb JOIN PORTS AS p ON sgpb.PORT_ID = p.ID JOIN PORTSECURITYBINDINGS AS psb ON p.ID = psb.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' ), PortsInGivenSecurityGroup AS ( SELECT p.ID AS port_id, p.STATUS AS port_status, ia.IP_ADDRESS AS ip_address, SUM(p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID) OVER ( PARTITION BY p.NETWORK_ID ORDER BY p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID ) AS window_column FROM SECURITYGROUPPORTBINDINGS sgpb JOIN PORTS p ON sgpb.PORT_ID = p.ID JOIN IPALLOCATIONS ia ON p.ID = ia.PORT_ID WHERE sgpb.SECURITY_GROUP_ID = '0008e629-5619-41e0-b86c-4eecfeaacb6c' ), DownPortsInGivenSecurityGroup AS ( SELECT dpsg.port_id, dpsg.tenant_id, dpsg.mac_address, pisg.port_status, pisg.ip_address, dpsg.window_column AS down_ports_sg_running_sum_standard_attr_id, pisg.window_column AS sg_ports_network_running_sum_standard_attr_id FROM DownPortsBySecurityGroup dpsg JOIN PortsInGivenSecurityGroup pisg ON dpsg.port_id = pisg.port_id ) SELECT port_id, tenant_id, mac_address, port_status, ip_address, down_ports_sg_running_sum_standard_attr_id, sg_ports_network_running_sum_standard_attr_id FROM DownPortsInGivenSecurityGroup;

question: For IPv4 subnets whose routes have next hop 10.30.19.197/8, list each subnet route’s destination and next hop along with the subnet name and CIDR and the allocation pool’s first and last IP (including a dense rank per subnet), and also show the subnet-level range and variance of allocation pool starting IPs (FIRST_IP) for that subnet. sql: WITH FirstIpStatsBySubnet AS ( SELECT s.NAME AS subnet_name, MAX(p.FIRST_IP) - MIN(p.FIRST_IP) AS first_ip_range, VARIANCE(p.FIRST_IP) AS first_ip_variance FROM SUBNETROUTES r JOIN SUBNETS s ON r.SUBNET_ID = s.ID JOIN IPALLOCATIONPOOLS p ON s.ID = p.SUBNET_ID WHERE r.NEXTHOP = '10.30.19.197/8' GROUP BY s.NAME ORDER BY first_ip_range DESC ), SubnetRoutePoolDetails AS ( SELECT r.DESTINATION, r.NEXTHOP, s.NAME AS subnet_name, s.CIDR AS subnet_cidr, p.FIRST_IP, p.LAST_IP, DENSE_RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY r.SUBNET_ID ORDER BY r.SUBNET_ID) AS window_column FROM SUBNETROUTES r JOIN SUBNETS s ON r.SUBNET_ID = s.ID JOIN IPALLOCATIONPOOLS p ON s.ID = p.SUBNET_ID WHERE s.IP_VERSION = 4 ), CombinedSubnetResults AS ( SELECT d.subnet_name, d.subnet_cidr, d.DESTINATION, d.NEXTHOP, d.FIRST_IP, d.LAST_IP, d.window_column, s.first_ip_range, s.first_ip_variance FROM SubnetRoutePoolDetails d JOIN FirstIpStatsBySubnet s ON d.subnet_name = s.subnet_name WHERE d.NEXTHOP = '10.30.19.197/8' ) SELECT * FROM CombinedSubnetResults ORDER BY subnet_name, DESTINATION, FIRST_IP;

question: For each port that is both (1) DOWN with an allocated IP address and a row number within its network (ordered by port ID) and (2) bound to a security group with admin_state_up = 1, list the network ID, the per-network row number, port ID, tenant ID, port name, MAC address, device owner, allocated IP address, the number of security group bindings for the port, and the total number of DNS records associated with the port.
